subject: St. Francis de Sales, bishop, half-length, in a white lace rochet and violet mozzetta with a gold pectoral cross; he holds a book in one hand and in the other the Sacred Heart of Jesus crowned with thorns, with a small flame. Background: Annecy, its blue lake and the Savoy Alps.

subject: St. Agatha, virgin and martyr, half-length, in a noble Roman gown with a red veil over her head, holding a martyr's palm and a small martyr's crown; iron tongs held modestly at her side. Background: Catania by the sea with Mount Etna smoking gently behind.
face: A young noblewoman of about twenty with long fair golden hair under the red veil, a serene oval face, large dark eyes and a composed, steadfast expression.

subject: St. Maximilian Kolbe, half-length, in the dark grey-black Conventual Franciscan habit with a short cape and white cord, holding a rosary and a Miraculous Medal; above him in the sky the Immaculata offers two crowns, one white and one red. Background: a Polish friary with a wooden chapel (Niepokalanów).
face: A man in his early forties, balding with close-cropped dark hair, a long dark-brown beard narrowing to a point, small round wire-rimmed spectacles, a straight nose, an earnest gentle gaze.

subject: St. Faustina Kowalska, half-length, in the black habit and black veil of the Sisters of Our Lady of Mercy with a white band framing the face and a white collar, a crucifix on a cord; she holds a small framed Divine Mercy image (Christ in a white robe, pale and red rays streaming from his heart, no lettering) against her breast. Background: a Polish convent with a small church and trees (Kraków-Łagiewniki).
face: A woman of about thirty with a round, open face, fair skin with a light dusting of freckles, reddish-gold eyebrows, light grey-green eyes, a straight nose, a calm steady gaze and a faint gentle smile.

subject: St. Padre Pio of Pietrelcina, half-length, in the brown Capuchin habit with hood and white cord; brown fingerless half-mittens on both hands covering the palms; he holds a rosary and a small crucifix. Background: the Gargano hills and the small friary church of Santa Maria delle Grazie at San Giovanni Rotondo.
face: A man of about sixty with short thick white hair receding from a high forehead, a full rounded white beard of medium length, strong dark eyebrows, deep-set dark eyes and a warm, faintly amused half-smile, eyes slightly lowered.

subject: Pope St. Leo the Great, half-length, wearing the papal tiara and a gold embroidered cope over an alb, holding a papal triple cross; his right hand raised in blessing. Background: the Roman countryside with an aqueduct and, in the sky, Sts. Peter and Paul holding swords.
face: A heavy-set, clean-shaven man of about sixty with a full, rounded face, a strong jaw, dark eyes and a calm, commanding yet kindly expression.

subject: St. Ignatius of Antioch, bishop and martyr, half-length, in red martyr's chasuble with a white pallium marked with black crosses; he holds a closed book (his letters) and a martyr's palm; two calm lions at his feet. Background: the Colosseum in Rome under a blue sky.
face: An old man of about seventy, bald on the crown with a fringe of grey hair, a long grey beard narrowing to a point, a lean ascetic face, a steady upward gaze. The beard is grey and tapering, not broad and white.

subject: Sts. Perpetua and Felicity, two young women martyrs side by side, half-length, each holding a martyr's palm. Perpetua on the left in a Roman matron's stola and palla with a jewelled diadem over a white veil; Felicity on the right in a plain tunic and plain veil. Behind them in the sky, a slender golden ladder rising to heaven. Background: a Roman amphitheatre by the sea at Carthage.
face: Perpetua: about twenty-two, dark hair bound up under a white veil, a composed oval face and a direct, fearless gaze. Felicity: slightly younger, a simpler rounder face, dark hair under a plain veil, a gentle lowered gaze. The two faces clearly different.

subject: St. Martin of Tours as a young Roman cavalry officer in armour, on a white horse, cutting his red military cloak in half with his sword to give half to a poor beggar wrapped in rags beside the horse. Background: the stone city gate of Amiens in winter snow.
face: A young man of about twenty, clean-shaven, with fair wavy hair cut to the jaw, a kind face, his gaze lowered to the beggar.

face: A small, thin, clean-shaven old priest of about seventy with long snow-white hair falling to his collar, a high pale smooth forehead, a narrow gentle face, deep-set luminous eyes raised in prayer.

face: A young man of about twenty, clean-shaven, with FAIR BLOND straight-to-wavy hair cut to the jaw (not brown, not tight curls), a kind face, his gaze lowered to the beggar.

subject: Half-length: a Nahua man in a plain white cotton tunic, with a coarse cream-coloured maguey-fibre tilma knotted at his right shoulder; with both hands he holds the tilma open in front of him, and on it is the image of Our Lady of Guadalupe (the rose-pink robe, blue-green mantle with gold stars, sunburst and crescent), while red and pink Castilian roses spill from its folds. Background: the rocky hill of Tepeyac at a December dawn, with nopal cactus and scrub, and the lake and valley of Mexico beyond.
face: An Indigenous Mexican man in his mid-fifties with warm copper-brown skin, straight black hair falling to the shoulders, a thin black moustache and a short, sparse black beard on the chin, high cheekbones, dark almond-shaped eyes and a humble, wondering gaze turned down toward the image.

subject: Half-length: a peasant girl of the Roman countryside in a plain white blouse with rolled sleeves, a dark skirt and a white apron, holding a bunch of white lilies against her breast and a martyr's palm; a small halo of light, no wound shown. Background: the flat farmland of the Pontine marshes at Le Ferriere near Nettuno, the old farmhouse La Cascina Antica with its outside stair, and a line of the sea on the horizon.
face: A girl of eleven, visibly a child, with a round, soft face, a lightly sun-warmed complexion, long, wavy chestnut-brown hair parted in the middle and loosely tied back, large dark-brown eyes and a serene, trusting gaze; no crown, no veil.

subject: Half-length: the black habit of the Canossian Daughters of Charity with the round black bonnet gathered in soft ruffles and tied under the chin, a white collar band, and on her breast the Canossian medal of Our Lady of Sorrows on a cord; her hands folded over a small crucifix; a broken iron chain lying at the lower edge of the window. Background: Schio in the Veneto, the Canossian convent with its church, and the green Pre-Alps behind the town.
face: A Sudanese woman of about fifty with deep dark-brown skin, a round, full face, a broad nose and full lips, large, gentle dark eyes and a warm, open smile; no marks on the face.

subject: Half-length: a priest in a plain black cassock with a white Roman collar, a small crucifix in one hand and a rosary in the other, turned three-quarters toward the viewer. Background: Madrid, where he founded Opus Dei in 1928: low brick houses and a church dome under a clear Castilian sky, with people at their daily work in the street below, kept small.
face: A robust, clean-shaven priest of about sixty-five with a broad, round face and full cheeks, dark hair greying at the temples, combed straight back from a high forehead, dark eyes behind heavy dark-rimmed rectangular spectacles, and a wide, cheerful smile.

subject: Half-length: white cassock, red velvet mozzetta, a red stole embroidered in gold with figures of saints, and on his head the red velvet camauro trimmed with white ermine, which he revived; a gold pectoral cross, a rosary in one hand and the other resting on an open Gospel book. Background: his birthplace, Sotto il Monte in the hills of Bergamo, with a village church tower, farmhouses and the foothills of the Alps.
face: A stout, heavy-set man of about eighty, clean-shaven, with a large round face, full cheeks and a double chin, a broad, prominent nose, small twinkling dark-brown eyes creased with laughter lines, and a broad, kindly smile.

subject: Half-length, the vigorous pope of the early 1980s: white cassock with the short white shoulder cape (pellegrina), white zucchetto, a gold pectoral cross on a cord; his right hand raised in blessing, his left holding the tall silver papal staff topped by a crucifix of the bent, suffering Christ (the Scorzelli ferula). Background: Kraków seen across the Vistula, Wawel Hill with the cathedral and castle, and the Tatra mountains faint on the horizon.

Background: the harbour of Alexandria with the Pharos lighthouse and white colonnades by the sea.

Background: Cologne, with the twin spires of the cathedral above the rooftops and the Rhine.
face: A woman of about fifty with an oval, pale face, strong straight dark eyebrows, deep-set dark-brown eyes, a long straight nose and full, closed lips; a serious, thoughtful, steady gaze with a faint gentleness about the mouth.

Background: Smyrna, its harbour and the hill of Mount Pagos, under a clear sky.
face: A very old man of about eighty-five with a full head of soft, thin, silvery-white hair falling to the nape (not bald), a short, neat, rounded snow-white beard, a lean, gentle face with a quiet smile and eyes raised to heaven.

Background: the Egyptian desert by the Red Sea mountains, a cave mouth, a spring and a few date palms.
face: A very old but hale man with a lean, deeply sun-browned face, the black hood framing it so that no hair shows, a medium-length grey-white beard parted at the chin into two points, bushy white brows and clear, bright, undimmed eyes with a calm gaze.

subject: St. Scholastica, virgin and abbess, half-length, in the black Benedictine habit with a black veil and a white wimple, holding the open Rule of St. Benedict and an abbess's crozier; a shining white dove rises from her toward heaven. Background: Monte Cassino, the abbey on its mountain top, seen from the valley below with gathering rain clouds on one side.
face: A woman of about forty with a soft, round, fair face, grey-blue eyes, gently arched light-brown brows, rosy cheeks and a warm, quiet smile; her gaze is lifted a little upward.

subject: Sts. Basil the Great and Gregory Nazianzen, two Greek bishops half-length side by side, both with haloes, inside the arched window. Left, Basil in a dark green-gold phelonion with the white omophorion marked with black crosses, holding an unrolled scroll of the Divine Liturgy. Right, Gregory in a rose-red phelonion with the same white omophorion, holding a closed jewelled Gospel book against his chest. Background: Cappadocia, the rocky hills and fairy-chimney rocks near Caesarea, with snow-capped Mount Argaeus in the distance.
face: Basil: a lean, ascetic man in his late forties with thick dark hair only threaded with grey, high-arched black brows, a long, narrow face with hollow cheeks and a long black beard narrowing to a point; a grave, searching gaze. Gregory: an older man of about sixty, bald on the whole crown with a short fringe at the sides, a broad, full, square-cut beard of smoky dark grey streaked with black, heavy grey-black brows and a gentle, meditative look; not a white beard.

subject: Sts. Martha, Mary and Lazarus, three figures half-length side by side, all with haloes, all inside the arched window. Centre, Lazarus, a little behind his sisters, in a plain off-white robe with a linen cloth over one shoulder, his hand on his heart. Right, Mary in a deep-blue mantle over a pale gown, an open scroll of the Scriptures in her hands. Background: the village of Bethany on the slope of the Mount of Olives, a stone house with a vine at the door, Jerusalem faint in the distance.
face: Martha: a woman of about thirty-five, strong and wholesome, with a round face, rosy cheeks, chestnut hair tucked under the head-cloth, steady brown eyes and a frank, kindly look toward the viewer. Mary: a younger woman of about twenty-five, with a delicate oval face, dark hair smoothly parted under the blue mantle, large dark eyes lowered to the scroll and a still, listening expression. Lazarus: a lean man of about forty with a pale, gaunt, gentle face, short straight black hair, a close-trimmed black beard and dark eyes raised in quiet gratitude; not curly-haired, not long-haired.
verdict: rejected (Mary in blue mantle and veil read as the Virgin; Lazarus a stock face)

subject: St. John Bosco, priest, half-length, in a black Piedmontese cassock with a small white collar, one arm around the shoulder of a smiling boy of about twelve in a jacket, holding a rosary in his other hand; above them, small in the sky, an image of Mary Help of Christians. Background: Turin, the domed Basilica of Mary Help of Christians at Valdocco with the Alps beyond.
face: A sturdy man of about fifty with a square, clean-shaven face, broad high cheekbones, thick wavy dark-brown hair with the first grey, brushed back from the forehead, lively dark eyes and a broad, warm, fatherly smile.

subject: St. Hildegard of Bingen, abbess, half-length, in the black Benedictine habit with a black veil over a white wimple, an abbess's crozier resting against her shoulder; she holds a wax writing tablet and a stylus, and golden tongues of fire descend from an opening in the sky onto her head. Background: the Rhine at Bingen, with the abbey of Rupertsberg above the river and vine-covered hills.
face: A woman of about sixty-five with a long, noble, narrow face, a strong straight nose, fine lines at the eyes, thin silver-grey brows, deep-set brown eyes raised upward toward the light, and firm, composed lips.

subject: Pope St. Pius X, half-length, in the white papal cassock and white zucchetto with a red mozzetta, a red stole and a gold pectoral cross on a cord; he holds a small golden ciborium and raises a white Host toward a little girl of about seven in a white First Communion veil, who kneels at the lower edge with folded hands. Background: the Vatican gardens with the dome of St. Peter's in the distance.
face: A man of about seventy with a broad, handsome, open face and strong clear-cut features, clean-shaven, thick short silver-white hair under the white zucchetto, clear light eyes under straight brows and a kind, winning smile.

subject: Two figures side by side, half-length. Andrew Kim Taegon, the first Korean priest, in a white hanbok and white durumagi coat with a red priest's stole, a black horsehair gat tied under the chin, holding a closed book and a martyr's palm, as in the 1920 portrait. Beside him Paul Chong Hasang, the lay leader, in a pale grey-blue durumagi and the same black gat, holding a small crucifix and a palm. Background: the bank of the Han River near Seoul at Saenamteo, with low hills, pines and the tiled roofs of a Joseon town.
face: Andrew: a slender Korean man of twenty-five with a smooth oval face, fine black brows, narrow dark eyes, a thin black moustache and a small tuft of beard on the chin, black hair gathered up under the gat, and a serene, direct gaze. Paul: a sturdier Korean layman of about forty-five, a broader face with lines at the eyes, a fuller short black beard with moustache, and a warm, earnest gaze.
verdict: superseded (face lines lacked bone structure; regenerated)

subject: Half-length, a lay philosopher, not a cleric: a long blue-grey philosopher's cloak (pallium) draped over one shoulder above a plain ochre tunic, no vestments. He holds an open scroll or a book (his Apology) in one hand and a martyr's palm in the other. Background: Rome under a clear sky, a colonnaded portico in the foreground and the Palatine and a temple front beyond.
face: A man of about sixty with thick, wavy salt-and-pepper hair brushed back from a high forehead to the nape, a full, broad, square-cut beard, dark streaked with grey, heavy dark brows, deep-set eyes and a searching, thoughtful gaze.
verdict: superseded (face lines lacked bone structure; regenerated)

subject: Two figures side by side, half-length. Charles Lwanga, the chief of the royal pages, standing tall in a long white kanzu with a russet bark-cloth mantle knotted on one shoulder, a martyr's palm in one hand and a rosary, his other hand resting protectively on the shoulder of the boy Kizito. Kizito, the youngest of the martyrs, a head shorter, in a plain white kanzu, hands joined in prayer, looking up at Charles. Background: the shore of Lake Victoria at Munyonyo, with banana groves and the round thatched houses of the Buganda court. No fire, no execution.
face: Charles: a tall, athletic Muganda man of about twenty-five, chestnut-brown skin, close-cropped black hair, clean-shaven, a handsome oval face with high cheekbones, a broad, calm brow and a steady, protective gaze. Kizito: a boy of thirteen, smaller and rounder in the face, dark-brown skin, close-cropped hair, large bright eyes and an eager, trusting look.
verdict: superseded (face lines lacked bone structure; regenerated)

subject: Half-length missionary bishop in a white mitre, a green chasuble with the pallium, holding a crozier and a book pierced through by a sword, the blade passing cleanly through the closed book (no blood). At his side, the felled trunk of the great oak of Geismar with an axe resting against it. Background: the wooded hills of Hesse with a small wooden oratory built from the oak's timber.
face: A sturdy Anglo-Saxon man of about fifty with a broad, ruddy, weathered face, fair flaxen hair cut short below the mitre, a short, square-trimmed flaxen beard flecked with grey, clear blue eyes and a resolute, open gaze.
verdict: superseded (face lines lacked bone structure; regenerated)

subject: Two half-length figures side by side, as on the Philip and James card. Left, Pope Cornelius, bareheaded as in the Trastevere mosaic, in a red chasuble over an alb with the white pallium marked with crosses, holding a tall triple papal cross and a curved horn (his attribute, from cornu). Right, Bishop Cyprian of Carthage, bareheaded, in a red cope with a gold border over an alb, holding a closed book (his treatise on the unity of the Church) against his chest and a martyr's palm. Background split behind them: on Cornelius's side the Roman campagna with the Appian Way lined with cypresses; on Cyprian's side the bay of Carthage with the sea and low white North African buildings. Keep both figures inside the arched window.
face: Cornelius: a man of about sixty, bald on the crown with a close fringe of grey hair, a short, neat grey beard, large dark almond eyes, a long straight nose and a calm, grave face. Cyprian: a man of about fifty with a warm olive-brown North African complexion, thick, tightly curled black hair, a full black beard parted into two points at the chin, dark eyes and an expression both grave and serene.
verdict: superseded (face lines lacked bone structure; regenerated)

subject: Half-length Byzantine-rite archbishop in a gold brocade sakkos with a white omophorion marked with large crosses, a round jewelled crown-mitre, an enkolpion on his chest, holding a hand cross and a martyr's palm. Background: Polotsk on the bank of the Western Dvina, with the white Cathedral of Holy Wisdom and its twin towers above the river.
face: A lean man of about forty with a long, narrow, ascetic face, hollow cheeks, deep-set dark eyes, a straight nose, a dark-brown moustache and a full dark-brown beard of medium length squared at the chin, and a steady, gentle gaze.
verdict: superseded (face lines lacked bone structure; regenerated)

subject: Sts. Martha, Mary and Lazarus, three figures half-length side by side, all with haloes, all inside the arched window. Left, Martha in a russet-red gown with a white head-cloth and a bunch of keys at her girdle, holding a small earthenware jug. Centre, Lazarus, a little behind his sisters, in a plain off-white robe with a linen cloth over one shoulder, his hand on his heart. Right, Mary of Bethany with her long dark hair loose and uncovered (NO veil, NO blue mantle: she must not look like the Virgin Mary), in a rose-coloured gown with a green cloak, holding a small alabaster jar of ointment. Background: the village of Bethany on the slope of the Mount of Olives, a stone house with a vine at the door, Jerusalem faint in the distance.
face: Martha: a woman of about thirty-five, strong and wholesome, with a round face, rosy cheeks, chestnut hair tucked under the head-cloth, steady brown eyes and a frank, kindly look toward the viewer. Mary: a younger woman of about twenty-five, with a delicate oval face, long dark wavy hair loose over her shoulders, large dark eyes lowered to the alabaster jar and a still, listening expression. Lazarus: a lean man of about fifty with a pale, gaunt, gentle face, receding short grey-streaked black hair, clean-shaven and dark eyes raised in quiet gratitude; not curly-haired, not long-haired.

subject: Two figures side by side, half-length. Paul Miki, a Japanese Jesuit, in a plain black cassock with a narrow standing collar, holding a crucifix against his chest and a martyr's palm; behind his shoulder the upright of a plain wooden cross. Beside him the boy Louis Ibaraki in a simple pale-blue kimono with a dark hakama, hands joined, looking up. Background: Nishizaka hill above Nagasaki in winter, pines, the bay with a Portuguese carrack, Japanese tiled roofs; on a distant slope a small line of plain crosses, too small for any figures.
face: Paul: a Japanese man of about thirty-three, clean-shaven, short-cropped black hair, a lean oval face with high cheekbones, fine straight brows, narrow dark eyes and lips slightly parted as if preaching, his gaze raised. Louis: a Japanese boy of twelve with round cheeks, glossy black hair tied back in a short tail, bright eager eyes and a small, joyful smile.
verdict: superseded (face lines lacked bone structure; regenerated)

subject: Two figures side by side, half-length. Andrew Dung-Lac, a Vietnamese priest, in a long dark áo dài-style tunic under a white surplice with a red stole, a black khăn đóng turban, holding a martyr's palm and a small crucifix. Beside him his fellow priest Peter Thi, beheaded with him, in the same dress with a dark-blue khăn đóng, holding a rosary and a palm. face: Andrew: a Vietnamese man of about forty-four with a lean, high-cheekboned face, a warm golden complexion, clean-shaven, black hair under the khăn đóng, calm dark almond eyes and a gentle, resolute expression. Peter: an elderly Vietnamese priest of about seventy-six, thin and slightly stooped, with a sparse white moustache and a wispy white chin beard, deep lines around kind, narrowed eyes.

subject: Half-length bishop in a tall white-and-gold jewelled mitre, a red chasuble over an alb, gloved hands holding a crozier and a sword held upright by the hilt, blade clean. Optional and small at the lower edge: Piotr rising from his grave in a white shroud, hands joined, as the witness raised by the bishop. Background: Kraków with Wawel hill, its cathedral and castle above the Vistula, and the small church on the Skałka rock by the river.
face: A man of about fifty, clean-shaven, with a full, broad face, heavy-lidded dark eyes lowered in thought, a straight nose, short dark hair greying at the temples below the mitre, and a grave, gentle expression.
verdict: superseded (face lines lacked bone structure; regenerated)

subject: Half-length bishop in a white mitre with gold bands, a red chasuble over an alb, holding a crozier and a large closed book (Against Heresies) with a small cross on its cover. Background: Lyon at the meeting of the Rhône and the Saône, the hill of Fourvière with its basilica and the ruins of the Roman theatre on the slope.
face: A man of about sixty with a long, narrow face and a high forehead, straight ash-brown hair to the ears, a long, straight ash-brown beard falling to the chest and silvering at the chin, light grey eyes and a gentle, peaceable gaze.
verdict: superseded (face lines lacked bone structure; regenerated)

subject: St. Teresa Benedicta of the Cross (Edith Stein), half-length, in the brown habit of a Discalced Carmelite with a black veil, white wimple and the white Carmelite mantle; she holds a plain wooden cross against her breast and a closed book in her other hand, with a martyr's palm beside her. Background: Cologne, with the twin spires of the cathedral above the rooftops and the Rhine.
face: A mature woman of about forty-seven (NOT a young girl): a strong, broad, square-jawed face with high cheekbones, thick dark straight eyebrows, deep-set dark intelligent eyes, a straight nose and full, composed lips; a grave, thoughtful, scholarly expression with a faint gentle warmth. She must look clearly older and more serious than Thérèse and Teresa of Ávila.

subject: St. Polycarp, bishop and martyr, half-length, bareheaded, in a white chasuble with a narrow red pallium, holding a Gospel book and a martyr's palm; behind him a tall arch of golden flames curves over him like a ship's sail filled with wind, leaving him untouched and serene. Background: Smyrna, its harbour and the hill of Mount Pagos, under a clear sky.
face: A very old man of about eighty-five with a SMALL, HEART-SHAPED face: wide cheekbones tapering to a small pointed chin, round rosy apple cheeks, a small short upturned nose, small bright eyes crinkled by a gentle smile, a short upper lip; a full head of soft thin silvery-white hair falling to the nape (not bald); a short, neat, rounded snow-white beard; eyes raised to heaven with a quiet smile.
verdict: rejected (face good, but frame and rendering drifted: other borders, oil-painting look)

subject: Half-length: a Nahua man in a plain white cotton tunic, with a coarse cream-coloured maguey-fibre tilma knotted at his right shoulder; with both hands he holds the tilma open in front of him, and on it is the image of Our Lady of Guadalupe (the rose-pink robe, blue-green mantle with gold stars, sunburst and crescent), while red and pink Castilian roses spill from its folds. Background: the rocky hill of Tepeyac at a December dawn, with nopal cactus and scrub, and the lake and valley of Mexico beyond.
face: A Nahua man of about fifty-seven with a broad, high-cheekboned indigenous face, warm brown skin, straight black hair cut in a thick fringe across the forehead and falling straight to the jaw, CLEAN-SHAVEN (no beard, no moustache), dark gentle eyes lowered in humble wonder. He must not resemble Christ.

subject: St. Anthony the Abbot, half-length, in a coarse grey-brown tunic under a black hooded mantle, the hood drawn up over his head, a blue tau cross on the shoulder of the mantle; he leans on a tall T-shaped (tau) staff hung with a small bell and holds an open book; a small pink pig at the lower edge. Background: the Egyptian desert by the Red Sea mountains, a cave mouth, a spring and a few date palms.
face: A very old but hale hermit with a TRIANGULAR face: broad weathered brow, very prominent high cheekbones, sunken temples, a narrow pointed chin under the beard; small deep-set eyes narrowed as against the desert sun with deep crow's-feet; a short, broad, slightly flattened nose; a wide thin mouth. Deeply sun-browned skin. The black hood frames the face so no hair shows; a medium-length grey-white beard parted at the chin into two points; bushy white brows; a calm, bright gaze.

subject: Sts. Basil the Great and Gregory Nazianzen, two Greek bishops half-length side by side, both with haloes, inside the arched window. Left, Basil in a dark green-gold phelonion with the white omophorion marked with black crosses, holding an unrolled scroll of the Divine Liturgy. Right, Gregory in a rose-red phelonion with the same white omophorion, holding a closed jewelled Gospel book against his chest. Background: Cappadocia, the rocky hills and fairy-chimney rocks near Caesarea, with snow-capped Mount Argaeus in the distance.
face: Two clearly different people. Basil: a lean ascetic man in his late forties; a LONG, NARROW face with a high forehead, a long thin aquiline nose with a pronounced bridge, close-set deep-set dark eyes under high-arched black brows, hollow cheeks, thin lips; thick dark hair threaded with grey; a long black beard narrowing to a point. Gregory: a man of about sixty with a BROAD, ROUND, FLESHY face, a short wide nose with a rounded tip, large wide-set soft eyes with heavy lids, full cheeks and a full lower lip; bald crown with a short fringe at the sides; a broad square-cut smoky dark-grey beard; a gentle, meditative look.

subject: St. Polycarp, bishop and martyr, half-length, bareheaded, in a white chasuble with a narrow red pallium, holding a Gospel book and a martyr's palm; behind him a tall arch of golden flames curves over him like a ship's sail filled with wind, leaving him untouched and serene. Background: Smyrna, its harbour and the hill of Mount Pagos, under a clear sky.
face: A very old man of about eighty-five with a SMALL, HEART-SHAPED face: wide cheekbones tapering to a small pointed chin, round rosy apple cheeks, a small short upturned nose, small bright eyes crinkled by a gentle smile, a short upper lip; a full head of soft thin silvery-white hair falling to the nape (not bald); a short, neat, rounded snow-white beard; eyes raised to heaven with a quiet smile.

subject: Half-length Byzantine-rite archbishop in a gold brocade sakkos with a white omophorion marked with large crosses, a round jewelled crown-mitre, an enkolpion on his chest, holding a hand cross and a martyr's palm. Background: Polotsk on the bank of the Western Dvina, with the white Cathedral of Holy Wisdom and its twin towers above the river.
face: A lean man of about forty with a long, narrow, ascetic face — a narrow forehead, a thin, long, straight nose with a narrow bridge, large dark eyes under straight, dark, level brows, angular cheekbones over hollow cheeks, a narrow jaw and thin lips; a dark-brown moustache and a full dark-brown beard of medium length squared at the chin, and a steady, gentle gaze.

subject: Half-length bishop in a tall white-and-gold jewelled mitre, a red chasuble over an alb, gloved hands holding a crozier and a sword held upright by the hilt, blade clean. Optional and small at the lower edge: Piotr rising from his grave in a white shroud, hands joined, as the witness raised by the bishop. Background: Kraków with Wawel hill, its cathedral and castle above the Vistula, and the small church on the Skałka rock by the river.
face: A man of about fifty with a full, pear-shaped face — narrow at the temples and widening to heavy, low cheeks and a broad, rounded jaw; a short, straight nose with a broad bridge; heavy-lidded dark eyes under thick, low, almost horizontal brows; a small, full-lipped, closed mouth; clean-shaven, short dark hair greying at the temples below the mitre, the eyes lowered in thought, and a grave, gentle expression.

subject: Two figures side by side, half-length. Paul Miki, a Japanese Jesuit, in a plain black cassock with a narrow standing collar, holding a crucifix against his chest and a martyr's palm; behind his shoulder the upright of a plain wooden cross. Beside him the boy Louis Ibaraki in a simple pale-blue kimono with a dark hakama, hands joined, looking up. Background: Nishizaka hill above Nagasaki in winter, pines, the bay with a Portuguese carrack, Japanese tiled roofs; on a distant slope a small line of plain crosses, too small for any figures.
face: Paul: a Japanese man of about thirty-three with a lean, long face — a high forehead, high, flat cheekbones, a slim, straight nose with a low bridge, narrow single-lidded dark eyes under fine straight brows and a firm, narrow chin; clean-shaven, short-cropped black hair, lips slightly parted as if preaching, his gaze raised. Louis: a Japanese boy of twelve with a flat, round little face — plump round cheeks, a tiny snub nose, narrow crescent eyes that nearly close as he smiles, thin arched brows and a small pointed chin; glossy black hair tied back in a short tail and a small, joyful smile.

subject: Two figures side by side, half-length. Andrew Dung-Lac, a Vietnamese priest, in a long dark áo dài-style tunic under a white surplice with a red stole, a black khăn đóng turban, holding a martyr's palm and a small crucifix. Beside him his fellow priest Peter Thi, beheaded with him, in the same dress with a dark-blue khăn đóng, holding a rosary and a palm. Background: the outskirts of Hanoi near the Cầu Giấy gate, rice paddies, bamboo groves, a river and a village church with curved tiled roofs.
face: Andrew: a Vietnamese man of about forty-four with a warm golden complexion and a lean, long-jawed face — high, prominent cheekbones over slightly hollow cheeks, a straight nose with a flat bridge and wide nostrils, calm dark almond eyes under straight, thick black brows, a long, firm jaw and a wide, thin-lipped mouth; clean-shaven, black hair under the khăn đóng, and a gentle, resolute expression. Peter: an elderly Vietnamese priest of about seventy-six, thin and slightly stooped, with a small, narrow face under a high, domed forehead — a small, low-bridged nose, narrow eyes deeply creased at the corners, sparse white brows, hollow cheeks, a small rounded chin and a thin, kind mouth; a sparse white moustache and a wispy white chin beard.

Andrew Kim Taegon, the first Korean priest, in a white hanbok and white durumagi coat with a red priest's stole, a black horsehair gat tied under the chin, holding a closed book and a martyr's palm, as in the 1920 portrait. Background: the bank of the Han River near Seoul at Saenamteo, with low hills, pines and the tiled roofs of a Joseon town.
face: Andrew: a slender Korean man of twenty-five with a smooth, soft oval face, wider at the cheeks — a short nose with a low bridge, narrow almond eyes with single lids tilted slightly up at the outer corners, fine black brows, full, soft cheekbones, a small rounded chin and a small closed mouth; a thin black moustache and a small tuft of beard on the chin, black hair gathered up under the gat, and a serene, direct gaze. Paul: a sturdier Korean layman of about forty-five with a broad, square face — wide, flat cheekbones, a short, broad nose with a flat bridge, small narrow eyes with lines at the corners under thick straight brows, a strong, wide jaw and a full, wide mouth; a fuller short black beard with moustache, and a warm, earnest gaze.

subject: Two figures side by side, half-length. Charles Lwanga, the chief of the royal pages, standing tall in a long white kanzu with a russet bark-cloth mantle knotted on one shoulder, a martyr's palm in one hand and a rosary, his other hand resting protectively on the shoulder of the boy Kizito. Kizito, the youngest of the martyrs, a head shorter, in a plain white kanzu, hands joined in prayer, looking up at Charles. Background: the shore of Lake Victoria at Munyonyo, with banana groves and the round thatched houses of the Buganda court. No fire, no execution.
face: Charles: a tall, athletic Muganda man of about twenty-five with chestnut-brown skin and a long, sculpted face — a broad, high forehead, high, chiselled cheekbones, a broad, straight nose with rounded nostrils, large, wide-set dark eyes under straight brows, a firm, square chin and full, well-defined lips; close-cropped black hair, clean-shaven, and a steady, protective gaze. Kizito: a boy of thirteen, smaller, with dark-brown skin and a small, round face — full cheeks, a short button nose, large, round bright eyes under soft arched brows, a small rounded chin and a wide mouth; close-cropped hair and an eager, trusting look.

subject: Half-length missionary bishop in a white mitre, a green chasuble with the pallium, holding a crozier and a book pierced through by a sword, the blade passing cleanly through the closed book (no blood). At his side, the felled trunk of the great oak of Geismar with an axe resting against it. Background: the wooded hills of Hesse with a small wooden oratory built from the oak's timber.
face: A sturdy Anglo-Saxon man of about fifty with a broad, flat-planed, ruddy, weathered face, widest at the cheekbones, with a wide, blunt jaw; a short snub nose; small, clear blue, slightly hooded eyes; faint flaxen brows; a wide, straight mouth; fair flaxen hair cut short below the mitre, a short, square-trimmed flaxen beard flecked with grey, and a resolute, open gaze.

subject: Half-length, a lay philosopher, not a cleric: a long blue-grey philosopher's cloak (pallium) draped over one shoulder above a plain ochre tunic, no vestments. He holds an open scroll or a book (his Apology) in one hand and a martyr's palm in the other. Background: Rome under a clear sky, a colonnaded portico in the foreground and the Palatine and a temple front beyond.
face: A man of about sixty with a large, broad, oblong face and a high forehead over a jutting brow ridge; a strong Roman nose with a pronounced hump at the bridge; deep-set eyes under heavy dark brows; broad cheekbones; a strong, deep jaw; a wide mouth with a full lower lip; thick, wavy salt-and-pepper hair brushed back from the forehead to the nape, a full, broad, square-cut beard, dark streaked with grey, and a searching, thoughtful gaze.

subject: Half-length bishop in a white mitre with gold bands, a red chasuble over an alb, holding a crozier and a large closed book (Against Heresies) with a small cross on its cover. Background: Lyon at the meeting of the Rhône and the Saône, the hill of Fourvière with its basilica and the ruins of the Roman theatre on the slope.
face: A man of about sixty with a long, narrow face and a high, domed forehead; a long nose with a softly rounded tip; pale grey eyes set wide apart under sparse, level ash-brown brows; smooth, flat cheeks; a long chin; a small, soft mouth; straight ash-brown hair to the ears, a long, straight ash-brown beard falling to the chest and silvering at the chin, and a gentle, peaceable gaze.

subject: Two half-length figures side by side, as on the Philip and James card. Left, Pope Cornelius, bareheaded as in the Trastevere mosaic, in a red chasuble over an alb with the white pallium marked with crosses, holding a tall triple papal cross and a curved horn (his attribute, from cornu). Right, Bishop Cyprian of Carthage, bareheaded, in a red cope with a gold border over an alb, holding a closed book (his treatise on the unity of the Church) against his chest and a martyr's palm. Background split behind them: on Cornelius's side the Roman campagna with the Appian Way lined with cypresses; on Cyprian's side the bay of Carthage with the sea and low white North African buildings. Keep both figures inside the arched window.
face: Cornelius: a man of about sixty with a long, rectangular face — a broad, flat forehead and a straight-edged jaw; a long, straight nose with a narrow ridge; large dark almond eyes set rather close under level grey brows; flat cheeks; a flat, square chin; a small, thin-lipped mouth; bald on the crown with a close fringe of grey hair, a short, neat grey beard and a calm, grave look. Cyprian: a man of about fifty with a warm olive-brown North African complexion and a diamond-shaped face — a narrow forehead, wide, angular, jutting cheekbones and a narrow chin; a strong, high-bridged nose with flared nostrils; large, round dark eyes under thick, low, straight black brows; a full, wide mouth; thick, tightly curled black hair, a full black beard parted into two points at the chin, and an expression both grave and serene.

subject: A young early pope, half-length, without a tiara: white vestments with a plain white pallium marked with black crosses, holding a golden chalice with the Host above it, and a small silver holy-water vessel with an aspergillum beside him (he is credited with the blessing of water with salt). A martyr's palm. Behind him, the Via Nomentana outside Rome, lined with umbrella pines and ancient tombs.
face: A clean-shaven young man of about thirty with a smooth oval face — a long, straight nose running down from the brow on a narrow bridge, large dark almond-shaped eyes under high, arched brows, smooth cheekbones, a small rounded chin and a small, full mouth; short chestnut hair combed forward in a straight fringe, and a serene, open gaze. Straight hair, not curls.

subject: An early pope, half-length, without a tiara: a deep-red chasuble and over it a plain white woollen pallium marked with black crosses. He holds a book (the tradition that he wrote the acts of St. Peter) and a martyr's palm. Behind him, his birthplace, Volterra in Etruria: a walled hill town of stone towers above rolling Tuscan hills.
face: A man of about fifty with a broad, hexagonal face — a low, wide forehead and wide, flat cheekbones angling to a broad jaw; a straight, wide nose with a blunt tip; wide-set, round dark eyes under thick, gently arched brows; a rounded chin under the beard; a straight, full mouth; dark hair greying at the temples and receding at the brow, a full, rounded salt-and-pepper beard of medium length, and a steady, gentle gaze. Beard neither white nor tapering.

subject: A young Roman noblewoman, half-length, in a moss-green gown with a dark wine-coloured mantle, a string of pearls bound in her hair. In one hand a small glass phial of healing ointment (her Greek title, Deliverer from Potions, and her care for Christians in prison), in the other a martyr's palm; a small flame glows in a bowl at her side for her death by fire. Behind her, Sirmium on the broad river Sava in the Pannonian plain, with Roman walls and poplars.
face: A young woman of about twenty-five with a fair, narrow, diamond-shaped face — high cheekbones, a slim nose with a slightly upturned tip, wide-set grey eyes under fine, straight light brows, a narrow pointed chin and a small, full mouth; light auburn hair braided and coiled at the nape under a pearl fillet (not loose, no veil), and a composed, compassionate gaze.

subject: An aged early pope, half-length, without a tiara: a gold chasuble with a plain white pallium marked with black crosses, his right hand raised in blessing, his left holding a simple staff topped with a cross, a martyr's palm at his side. Behind him, the Vatican hill above the Tiber, where he was buried beside St. Peter, with umbrella pines and the Roman skyline.
face: A lean old man of about seventy with a narrow, bony face — a broad, bony forehead, sharp, high cheekbones, a short, sharp, straight nose, small, very bright eyes set close together under bristling, upswept grey brows, a long, jutting chin under the beard and a thin mouth with a long upper lip; close-cropped silver hair, a long silver-grey beard divided into two points at the end, and a kind gaze. Not broad, not rounded, not heavy-set.

subject: A Roman officer of high rank, half-length: a bronze cuirass, a crimson military cloak fastened at the shoulder, and a light iron chain hanging from one wrist (his two years in prison). In one hand a folded letter sealed with a cross (his letters to Anastasia), in the other a martyr's palm. Behind him, the lagoon and shore of Aquileia on the Adriatic, where he was beheaded and his body thrown into the sea, with low marshes and a Roman town wall.
face: A man of about forty-five with a compact, square face and a low forehead — a nose with a flattened bridge and a broad tip; narrow, wide-set dark eyes under straight, low brows; wide, flat cheekbones; a strong, wide jaw with a dimpled chin; a thin, firm mouth; close-cropped iron-grey hair, a short, square-trimmed black beard streaked with grey, and a calm, resolute gaze. Clearly older and heavier-built than George and Martin.

subject: A French priest, half-length, in a black soutane and a black mantle with the white two-tailed rabat (bands) at the throat. One hand rests on the shoulder of a small schoolboy in a plain coat who holds an open primer; the other points gently upward. A slate and a book lie on a school desk beside him. Behind him, the city of Reims with the Gothic west front and towers of Reims Cathedral, where he was a canon.
face: A clean-shaven man of about sixty with an oval face and full cheeks — a long, straight nose with a fine ridge, round dark-brown eyes under softly arched brows, a rounded chin with a small dimple and a small, curved mouth in a gentle, kindly half-smile; soft grey hair brushed back and falling to the collar. Not thin or wasted, and the hair grey rather than snow-white.

subject: Two early bishops side by side, half-length. Left, Timothy: a white chlamys-like chasuble with a plain white pallium, holding a closed codex of Paul's letters against his chest. Right, Titus: a deep-red chasuble with a white pallium, one hand raised in blessing, the other on a bishop's staff with a simple cross. No mitres. Behind them, Ephesus: the great marble theatre on the hillside and the colonnaded harbour street running down to the sea, with a small ship bound for Crete on the horizon.
face: Timothy (left): a slender young man of about twenty-five with a slim, narrow face and a gently pointed chin — a slender, straight nose, gentle, slightly hooded hazel eyes, thin, faintly arched brows, smooth cheeks and a soft, small mouth; short straight light-brown hair with a soft fringe, a sparse, short, fair-brown beard rounded along the jaw, and a gentle, slightly lowered gaze. Titus (right): a clean-shaven man of about forty-five with a square face — a broad, flat forehead, a short, straight nose with a broad bridge, narrow, deep-set dark eyes under thick straight black brows that nearly meet, flat cheeks, a strong square jaw and a wide, thin-lipped mouth; olive complexion, black hair cut short in a straight Roman fringe with grey at the temples, and a steady, direct gaze. Not a beardless youth, not the thirties man with brown curls.

subject: A small, elderly nun, half-length, in a white cotton sari bordered with three blue stripes (one broad, two narrow), draped over her head and shoulders, a small wooden crucifix pinned at her left shoulder and a rosary in her joined hands. Beside her, a small sick child wrapped in a white cloth rests against her arm. Behind her, Kolkata: the Home of the Pure Heart (Nirmal Hriday) at Kalighat, with palms and the river in soft evening light.
face: A small woman of about seventy, slightly stooped, with a small face broad at the cheekbones and tapering to a firm, pointed chin — a strong nose curving slightly downward, deep-set, hooded brown eyes under thin, low brows, prominent cheekbones and a wide, thin-lipped mouth in a warm, gentle smile; the face softly lined with age. Idealise the wrinkles into a few soft lines.

subject: Two brothers side by side, half-length, holding between them an unrolled parchment scroll written with the letters of the Slavonic alphabet. Left, Cyril: a monk in a black habit and a black monastic hood covering his head, a small cross on a cord. Right, Methodius: an archbishop in a gold chasuble with a white pallium and a white mitre, holding a Gospel book and a staff with a double-barred cross. Behind them, the green valley of the Morava river in Moravia with wooded hills and a small round stone church.
face: Cyril (left): a thin, pale, scholarly man of about forty with an inverted-triangle face — a tall, broad forehead under the monastic hood narrowing sharply to the chin; a long, slender, slightly hooked nose; large, dark, prominent, intelligent eyes under straight black brows; smooth, flat cheeks; a small, thin mouth; a long, narrow black beard and a calm, inward gaze. Methodius (right): a man of about sixty with a broad, heavy, trapezoid face, wider at the jaw than at the brow — a large nose with a broad, fleshy, rounded tip; small, kind eyes creased at the corners under heavy dark eyebrows; full cheeks; a heavy jaw under the beard; a full mouth; a long, full iron-grey beard with darker streaks and a kindly, fatherly gaze. Methodius's beard is grey, not white.
verdict: rejected (scroll showed made-up Cyrillic letters; no text on cards)

subject: Two Roman brothers side by side, half-length, officers of the imperial household in white tunics with purple stripes and white mantles fastened at the shoulder, each holding a martyr's palm; the elder, John, also holds a jewelled martyr's crown. Behind them, the Caelian Hill in Rome: the Romanesque bell tower and arcaded porch of the basilica of Sts. John and Paul, built over their house, among cypresses.
face: John (left, the elder): a man of about forty with a broad, heavy-jawed, rectangular face — a thick, straight nose, small dark eyes set close under a heavy, straight brow ridge, flat cheekbones, a wide, squared chin under the beard and a straight, firm mouth; close-cropped black hair, a short, neatly trimmed black beard and a grave, steady gaze. Paul (right): a clean-shaven man of about twenty-eight with a narrower face and a delicate, pointed chin — a small, straight nose, large light-brown eyes under high, arched brows, smooth cheeks and a soft, full mouth; short light-brown hair combed forward in a straight Roman fringe and a gentle expression. John's hair is straight and cropped, not curly.

subject: A bishop in a red chasuble with a gold orphrey, a jewelled white-and-gold mitre and a crozier resting in the crook of his arm, half-length, holding before him two tall lit candles crossed in a saltire and tied with a red ribbon, as in the blessing of throats. At his side a young mother presents a small boy who touches his throat. Small birds perched near him and a gentle deer at the edge of the scene recall his cave. Behind, the rocky hills of Sebaste in Cappadocia with a cave mouth, and the walled town below.
face: A man of about forty-five, clean-shaven, with a short, wide, rounded face and ruddy apple cheeks — a short, straight nose, large, round blue-grey eyes under light, arched brows, a small, neat chin and a bow-shaped mouth; light-brown hair showing under the mitre, and a gentle smile turned down toward the boy.
verdict: rejected (frame drifted; mother in blue mantle and white veil with child read as the Virgin and Child)

subject: A Jesuit in a plain black soutane with a black sash and a small crucifix on a cord, half-length, bending slightly forward with a long wooden staff in his right hand, tracing Latin verses in the wet sand of the beach; a small book held to his chest with the other hand. Behind him the wide pale beach of Iperoig (Ubatuba) at dawn, rows of verses written in the sand, gentle surf, seagulls, green forested hills of the Serra do Mar, a simple wooden cross on the dunes. Keep the scene inside the arched window.
face: A lean man of about thirty, slight and a little stooped, with an olive, sun-tanned complexion and a face broad at the forehead and narrowing to a small, pointed chin — a long, thin, straight nose, blue-grey eyes set rather close under light, slightly arched brows, hollow cheeks under modest cheekbones and a wide mouth; short straight dark-brown hair, a sparse, thin dark beard along the jaw (not full), and eyes lowered to the sand with a cheerful, kindly half-smile.

subject: A Roman noblewoman in the simple black tunic of the Oblates of Tor de' Specchi with a long plain white veil falling to her shoulders (no wimple, no scapular), half-length, holding an open book of hours in one hand and a small basket of bread for the poor on her arm. Beside her, small and luminous, her guardian angel: a child of about nine with long golden hair in a white deacon's dalmatic, one hand on her shoulder. Behind, the Roman Forum with the Romanesque bell tower of Santa Maria Nova (Santa Francesca Romana) and the Colosseum in soft light.
face: A woman of about forty-five with an olive Roman complexion and a broad-cheeked, rounded-square face with a firm, rounded jaw — a straight Roman nose continuing the line of the brow, large, dark, heavy-lashed eyes under fine dark eyebrows, full cheekbones and a full, serene, faintly smiling mouth; the eyes lifted a little toward the angel.

subject: Inside the small whitewashed colonial chapel of Nossa Senhora das Candeias at the Engenho Cunhaú, half-length: in front, the old priest Fr. André de Soveral in a white Mass chasuble at a simple altar, raising the white Host in the elevation with both hands, candles on the altar. Beside him, slightly behind, the layman St. Mateus Moreira in the plain linen shirt and dark jacket of a 17th-century Brazilian farmer, kneeling in adoration with hands joined. Both have martyrs' palms nearby. Through the open chapel door, sugar-cane fields, coconut palms and the green coast of Rio Grande do Norte. Peaceful, no soldiers, no violence.
face: André: an old priest of about seventy-three, clean-shaven, with a weathered, sun-browned, bony face, wide at the high cheekbones and narrowing to a long, square chin — a big, straight nose with a broad bridge, deep-set dark eyes under bushy white eyebrows and a firm, full-lipped mouth; a bald crown with a short fringe of white hair, the eyes lifted to the Host. Mateus: a sturdy man of about forty with weathered olive skin and a wide, short face with a broad, low forehead — a straight nose with a broad, rounded tip, round, wide-open dark eyes under thick, level black brows, heavy cheekbones, a rounded jaw and a wide, full mouth; short black hair, a neat black moustache and short chin beard, and a fervent upward gaze.

subject: An early pope, half-length, without a tiara: a deep-red chasuble and over it a plain white woollen pallium marked with black crosses. He holds a book (the tradition that he wrote the acts of St. Peter) and a martyr's palm. Behind him, his birthplace, Volterra in Etruria: a walled hill town of stone towers above rolling Tuscan hills.
face: A man of about fifty with a broad, hexagonal face — a low, wide forehead and wide, flat cheekbones angling to a broad jaw; a straight, wide nose with a blunt tip; wide-set, round dark eyes under thick, gently arched brows; a rounded chin under the beard; a straight, full mouth; dark hair greying at the temples and receding at the brow, a full, rounded salt-and-pepper beard of medium length, and a steady, gentle gaze. Beard neither white nor tapering.

subject: A deacon in a rich crimson-and-gold brocade dalmatic over a white alb, half-length, holding a martyr's palm and a closed red book; behind his shoulder the X-shaped wooden rack (two crossed beams), and at the lower edge a round grey millstone. Two black ravens: one perched on the millstone, one in flight. Behind, a harbour at sunset with a small medieval ship under sail with a raven at its prow, the walls and towers of Valencia on the shore and the sea beyond.
face: A young man of about twenty-two, clean-shaven, with a pale, full oval face, wide at the cheekbones — a straight nose with a narrow bridge, heavy-lidded brown eyes under thin, level brows, a small rounded chin and a small, closed mouth; straight chestnut-brown hair parted in the middle and falling thickly to the jaw, covering the ears (no fringe, no tonsure, no curls), the eyes gently lowered in grave recollection.

subject: A pope in a white-and-gold cope with a jewelled morse over an alb, wearing a papal tiara, half-length, one hand raised in blessing and the other holding a closed book; a small white dove with a soft glow alighting on or just above his tiara, recalling his election. A martyr's palm at his side. Behind, a Roman landscape of the third century: the Appian Way with cypresses and umbrella pines and the entrance to the catacomb of St. Callixtus.
face: A lean, clean-shaven man of about sixty-five with a long, fine-boned face — a thin nose with a high, narrow bridge and a slight hump, gentle downcast grey-blue eyes with drooping outer lids under fine brows sloping down at the ends, fine cheekbones over hollow cheeks, a long, narrow chin and a small, thin mouth; thick, short silver hair showing below the tiara, and a humble, quiet expression.

subject: A Franciscan lay brother in a brown habit with a hood and white knotted cord, half-length, holding up the fold of his habit with both hands; the fold is full of red and pink roses, where he had hidden loaves for the poor (the miracle of the bread turned into flowers). A wooden rosary at the cord. No Child Jesus. Behind him the cloister garden of the friary of Santa Maria di Gesù above Palermo, with lemon trees, a stone arcade and Monte Pellegrino and the bay in the distance.
face: An Afro-Sicilian man of about sixty with deep ebony-brown skin and a broad, full face with a wide, square jaw and a short chin — rounded cheekbones that lift when he smiles, a broad, flat-bridged nose, dark eyes narrowed with laughter lines under thick, straight brows, and full lips; close-cropped tightly curled black hair greying at the temples around a small Franciscan tonsure, clean-shaven, and the eyes lowered to the roses with a broad, warm smile.

subject: Two brothers side by side, half-length, holding between them an unrolled parchment scroll whose writing is only faint, illegible ornamental strokes (no readable letters of any alphabet). Left, Cyril: a monk in a black habit and a black monastic hood covering his head, a small cross on a cord. Right, Methodius: an archbishop in a gold chasuble with a white pallium and a white mitre, holding a Gospel book and a staff with a double-barred cross. Behind them, the green valley of the Morava river in Moravia with wooded hills and a small round stone church.
face: Cyril (left): a thin, pale, scholarly man of about forty with an inverted-triangle face — a tall, broad forehead under the monastic hood narrowing sharply to the chin; a long, slender, slightly hooked nose; large, dark, prominent, intelligent eyes under straight black brows; smooth, flat cheeks; a small, thin mouth; a long, narrow black beard and a calm, inward gaze. Methodius (right): a man of about sixty with a broad, heavy, trapezoid face, wider at the jaw than at the brow — a large nose with a broad, fleshy, rounded tip; small, kind eyes creased at the corners under heavy dark eyebrows; full cheeks; a heavy jaw under the beard; a full mouth; a long, full iron-grey beard with darker streaks and a kindly, fatherly gaze. Methodius's beard is grey, not white.

subject: A woman in the dark brown habit and mantle of a Franciscan tertiary with a white knotted cord, a white linen veil and wimple framing her face, half-length, one arm around a little girl in a simple dress to whom she shows an open catechism. In the sky above, her vision: a golden ladder rising into the clouds with small white-veiled virgins ascending it among angels. Behind, the shore of Lake Garda at Desenzano with its small harbour, olive trees and the mountains across the water.
face: A slender woman of about sixty with a fine-boned, heart-shaped face — a wide, smooth forehead, high, soft cheekbones and a small, pointed chin; a small, straight nose with a delicate tip; warm dark-brown eyes slightly downturned at the outer corners, with soft lines at their corners; thin, dark, arched brows; a small mouth; fair skin, and a tender, motherly smile as she looks down at the child.

subject: A Franciscan friar in a dark greyish-brown habit with a hood and white knotted cord, half-length, seated at a small table, rolling a tiny slip of paper into a pill; beside him a small dish of the little rolled paper pills, an open breviary, a quill and inkpot. On the wall or above him a small image of the Immaculate Conception. Behind him, through an arch, the white colonial church and convent of the Mosteiro da Luz in São Paulo with its bell tower, palm trees and a blue sky.
face: A sturdy man of about sixty, clean-shaven, with a full, round face — soft, low cheekbones, a long, slender, straight nose, small almond-shaped dark eyes turned slightly up at the outer corners under thick, straight dark brows, a small rounded chin and a small mouth in a warm, quiet smile; a thick crown of short greying dark hair around the Franciscan tonsure, and a kindly gaze.

subject: A young early pope, half-length, without a tiara: white vestments with a plain white pallium marked with black crosses, holding a golden chalice with the Host above it, and a small silver holy-water vessel with an aspergillum beside him (he is credited with the blessing of water with salt). A martyr's palm. Behind him, the Via Nomentana outside Rome, lined with umbrella pines and ancient tombs.
face: A clean-shaven young man of about thirty with a smooth oval face — a long, straight nose running down from the brow on a narrow bridge, large dark almond-shaped eyes under high, arched brows, smooth cheekbones, a small rounded chin and a small, full mouth; short chestnut hair combed forward in a straight fringe, and a serene, open gaze. Straight hair, not curls.

subject: Two Jesuits in black soutanes on the deck of a sailing ship at sea, half-length. In front, Bl. Ignatius de Azevedo holds up before him with both hands a framed copy of the icon of Our Lady of St. Luke (Salus Populi Romani: the Virgin in a dark blue mantle holding the Child). Just behind his shoulder, one young companion, a teenage Jesuit novice, hands joined in prayer, looking up. Both hold martyrs' palms or have them nearby. Behind them the mast, rigging and a red-cross sail of the ship Santiago, a calm blue Atlantic and the green volcanic cliffs of La Palma (Tazacorte) on the horizon. No weapons, no violence. Keep the scene inside the arched window.
face: Ignatius: a nobleman of about forty-four with a long, lean face, a high forehead and a long, straight-sided jaw — a long nose drooping slightly at the tip, wide-set, earnest dark eyes under strongly arched dark brows, high, narrow cheekbones and a firm mouth with a full lower lip; receding dark hair, a full dark-brown beard of medium length touched with grey, and eyes raised toward the icon. The companion: a slender boy of about seventeen with a fresh, broad-cheeked face — a short, slightly upturned nose, large, clear light eyes under straight fair brows, a square, cleft chin and a wide, eager mouth; beardless, with short fair-brown hair and an ardent look.
verdict: rejected (too like ignatius_loyola: balding Jesuit with pointed dark beard)

subject: A Hospitaller brother in a plain, coarse dark grey-brown habit of rough wool with a hood lying on the shoulders, girded with a cord, half-length, walking barefoot. In his right hand he holds up a pomegranate crowned with a small cross (the arms of Granada, his attribute); over his left shoulder hang two small alms baskets on a cord. Behind him the city of Granada at dusk: the red walls and towers of the Alhambra on the hill, the snow of the Sierra Nevada, and an arched hospital doorway with a lamp. Keep the scene inside the arched window.
face: A lean, ascetic Portuguese-Spanish man of about fifty with an olive complexion and a long, angular face — a high, bare forehead with a pronounced baldness over the crown and short dark hair only at the sides and back, a long, straight nose with a slight hook at the bridge, dark, deep-set eyes under strongly arched dark brows, sharp, angular cheekbones over hollow cheeks, a narrow mouth; a thin dark moustache and a short, sparse dark beard only on the chin, and eyes lowered with grave compassion.

subject: A French missionary priest in a worn black cassock with white bands (rabat) at the collar, bareheaded, half-length; a large rosary hangs from his belt, a crucifix is held to his chest in his right hand, and in his left he carries a small painted wooden statuette of the Virgin and Child. A plain pilgrim's staff leans against his shoulder. Behind him the flat green countryside of the Vendée and Brittany: hedged fields, a small granite church, and on a low hill a great wooden Calvary with a crowd of tiny figures building it (Pontchâteau). Keep the scene inside the arched window.
face: A tall, robust man of about forty, clean-shaven, with ruddy cheeks and a LONG face — a broad, high forehead, a strong aquiline nose, large, lively dark eyes lowered modestly, dark, straight brows, firm cheekbones, a wide, gentle mouth and a rather long chin; chestnut hair cut very short, lying flat and falling a little onto the top of the forehead; a look of grandeur and goodness together.

subject: A small, slight Franciscan Observant friar in a grey-brown habit with a hood lying on the shoulders and a white knotted cord, half-length, holding up before him with both hands a wooden tablet bearing a golden sun: a flaming disc with wavy rays on a deep blue ground (a plain radiant disc, with NO letters, monogram or lettering on it). Behind him Siena: the shell-shaped Piazza del Campo, the Palazzo Pubblico with the tall Torre del Mangia, and Tuscan hills. Keep the scene inside the arched window.
face: A small, gaunt man of about sixty-three, clean-shaven, with a thin, pointed face — a smooth, rounded bald crown with a thin fringe of short grey hair, a long, fine nose curving slightly down at the tip, large, heavy-lidded pale-brown eyes lowered in gentle concentration, sunken cheeks under prominent cheekbones, a small, thin-lipped mouth drawn slightly inward and a prominent, upward-curving chin; a mild, kindly, recollected expression.

subject: An Eastern bishop in a pale blue phelonion with a white omophorion marked with large black crosses, half-length, bareheaded, teaching: his right hand raised in blessing, his left holding an open book of his catecheses against his chest. Behind him Jerusalem in the morning: the domed rotunda of the Anastasis (the Holy Sepulchre), the stone houses of the city and the Mount of Olives with olive trees. Keep the scene inside the arched window.
face: A vigorous man of about sixty-five with a wide, rectangular face — a strong, flat brow and a broad, square-set jaw under the beard; a broad, straight nose; wide-set grey eyes under bushy, dark-grey brows; flat, broad cheekbones; a firm, wide mouth; short iron-grey hair receding high at the temples with a small tuft left at the front; a thick, ROUNDED beard of iron-grey streaked with dark hair, trimmed to a rounded edge at the collarbone (not white, not long, not pointed); a steady, kindly teacher's gaze toward the viewer.

subject: A hermit of the Minims in a coarse, dark brown-black habit with the HOOD UP over the head and a short rounded capuce over the shoulders, a knotted cord at the waist, half-length, leaning on a rough knotted wooden staff with his right hand. In his left hand he holds up a golden sun disc with straight rays (the CHARITAS emblem, shown as a plain radiant disc with NO letters or lettering). Behind him the rocky Calabrian coast at Paola above the Strait of Messina, a small stone hermitage among chestnut trees, and across the blue water the hills of Sicily with Etna faint in the distance. Keep the scene inside the arched window.
face: A very old but wiry hermit of about seventy-five with a narrow, weathered face seen in the shadow of the hood — a high, bony forehead, a long, prominent hooked nose, small, deep-set, piercing dark eyes under thin, drooping grey brows, high, sharp cheekbones over deeply hollow cheeks, a thin mouth; no hair visible under the hood; a long, thin, wispy grey-white beard that parts into two strands at the tip, and eyes looking steadily out from under the hood.

subject: A Dominican friar in the white habit and white scapular under a black cappa (cloak), half-length, preaching: his right forefinger raised high toward heaven, his left hand holding a closed book against his side; a pair of large, soft white-and-gold angel WINGS rises from his shoulders behind him (the Angel of the Apocalypse). A small flame of light above his head. Behind him Valencia: the Gothic cathedral with the octagonal Micalet bell tower, palm trees and orange groves. Keep the wings and the scene inside the arched window.
face: A man of about sixty, clean-shaven, with a long, full oval face and a smooth, broad forehead — a long, straight nose with a fleshy, rounded tip, large dark, heavy-lidded eyes under high, rounded arched brows, full, smooth cheeks, a small, firm mouth and a full, rounded chin; greying dark hair in a thick Dominican corona around the shaven crown; an intent, earnest gaze toward the viewer.

subject: A bishop in a red chasuble with a gold orphrey, a jewelled white-and-gold mitre and a crozier resting in the crook of his arm, half-length, holding before him two tall lit candles crossed in a saltire and tied with a red ribbon, as in the blessing of throats. At his side a young peasant mother in a plain brown dress and a russet head-scarf (NOT blue, NOT a white veil: she must not resemble the Virgin Mary) presents a small boy of about eight who touches his throat. Small birds perched near him and a gentle deer at the edge of the scene recall his cave. The whole scene stays inside the inner arched gold-edged window, with the same gold border and vine borders as the reference cards. Behind, the rocky hills of Sebaste in Cappadocia with a cave mouth, and the walled town below.
face: A man of about forty-five, clean-shaven, with a short, wide, rounded face and ruddy apple cheeks — a short, straight nose, large, round blue-grey eyes under light, arched brows, a small, neat chin and a bow-shaped mouth; light-brown hair showing under the mitre, and a gentle smile turned down toward the boy.

subject: A pope dressed ALL IN WHITE: a white cassock of the Dominican white he kept as pope, a white shoulder cape and a white zucchetto, a gold pectoral cross, half-length; a long rosary of dark beads wound in his joined hands, which hold a small crucifix. Behind him a window of the Vatican palace open onto the Roman sky, the hills of Rome and, far beyond, a calm sea with a few distant galleys (Lepanto, 1571). No red. Keep the scene inside the arched window.
face: A thin, ascetic man of about sixty-six with a gaunt, long face — a bald, high, bony forehead under the zucchetto, a long, prominent aquiline nose with a sharp bridge, dark, deep-set eyes under heavy, arched grey brows, hollow cheeks under high cheekbones; a full WHITE beard of medium length, trimmed square below the chin, with a white moustache; a grave, prayerful gaze lowered toward the rosary.

subject: A Benedictine monk in a black cowl with wide sleeves, half-length, seated at a slanted wooden writing desk, writing with a quill in an open vellum manuscript; an inkhorn and a few bound books beside him, a candle. Behind him, through the window, the stone monastery church of Jarrow on the River Tyne, green Northumbrian fields and a grey-blue sea sky. Keep the scene inside the arched window.
face: A man of about sixty, clean-shaven, with a broad, flat-planed oval face — a wide forehead, a short, slightly upturned nose, pale blue eyes with fine crow's-feet under sandy-grey, softly arched brows, full, soft cheeks, a thin, wide mouth with a faint smile and a small rounded chin; a monastic tonsure with a neat ring of fair hair turned grey; eyes lowered to the page.

subject: A Benedictine monk-archbishop in a black monastic cowl with a white woollen pallium marked with black crosses over his shoulders, bareheaded, half-length, holding a gilded archbishop's crosier in his left hand and an open manuscript book in his right, looking up from it in thought. Behind him Canterbury: the pale stone cathedral with its towers, green Kentish fields and a cloister arcade. Keep the scene inside the arched window.
face: A man of about seventy with a long, high-domed head and a long, bony face — a very high, receding forehead with a deep brow, a strong, prominent aquiline nose with a high bridge, deep-set, pale eyes under a heavy brow ridge with thin grey brows, hollow cheeks, a long upper lip and a jutting chin; thin, straight grey hair left long behind the ears, falling to the nape; a very short, close-cropped grey beard along the jaw and chin (not full); a quiet, thoughtful gaze lifted from the book.

subject: Two Mexican priests side by side, half-length, both in black cassocks with a white Roman collar. Christopher (left, the elder) holds a small crucifix to his chest and a rosary in his hand; Agustín Caloca (right, the younger) holds a closed breviary and a martyr's palm. Calm and prayerful, no wounds or violence. Behind them the dry hills of northern Jalisco with scattered huisache trees and nopal cactus, the whitewashed adobe church of Totatiche with its bell tower, and a clear blue sky. Keep both figures and the scene inside the arched window.
face: Christopher (left): a Mexican mestizo man of about fifty-eight with a warm brown complexion and a broad, full, square-jawed face — a wide forehead, thick, wavy black hair greying a little, combed up and back in a wave, a broad nose with a rounded tip, heavy-lidded dark eyes under thick, straight black brows, full cheeks, full lips, clean-shaven; a calm, serious, fatherly gaze toward the viewer. Agustín (right): a slim young man of about twenty-nine with a light-brown complexion and a narrow oval face — thick, dark hair cut short and parted at the side, a straight, slender nose, dark eyes under straight, level brows, ears set out a little, a small mouth and a narrow chin, clean-shaven; a gentle, earnest gaze. The two must look clearly different in age and build.

subject: A king, half-length, wearing the Holy Crown of Hungary (gold band with enamel plaques, pendants at the sides and a bent cross on top) and a dark-red, bell-shaped mantle embroidered in gold like his coronation mantle over a blue tunic; he holds a golden orb in one hand and a tall double-barred (apostolic) cross in the other. Behind him the basilica of Esztergom with its great dome on its hill above the wide Danube, green hills beyond. Keep the scene inside the arched window.
face: A man of about sixty with a SQUARE, heavy-boned face — a wide, low forehead, flat, broad cheekbones, a strong straight nose with a high bridge, deep-set grey eyes under heavy, straight brows, a wide mouth under a drooping moustache and a broad jaw; shoulder-length straight light-brown hair streaked with grey under the crown, a long, full, grey-streaked beard cut square at the bottom, and a grave, resolute gaze to one side.

subject: A Visitation nun, half-length, in the black habit with a black veil over a white linen band, a wide, square white pleated guimpe covering the neck and chest, and a silver cross on her breast; she holds a small book of the Rule against her chest with one hand and a small red heart marked with the golden monogram IHS in the other. Behind her the Visitation monastery at Annecy, a plain cloister arcade and garden with the green Semnoz mountain beyond; no lake. Keep the scene inside the arched window; no lettering besides the initial.
face: A woman of about fifty-five with a BROAD OVAL face, full in the lower cheeks — a long, straight nose with a slightly rounded tip, wide-set clear grey-blue eyes under fine, lightly arched brows, smooth rounded cheekbones, thin, closed lips with a faint, knowing smile and a firm, rounded chin; fair skin with fine lines at the eyes, hair hidden by the veil, and a steady, kindly gaze toward the viewer.

subject: A bishop, half-length, in a gold-embroidered red cope over a white alb, a white mitre and a gilded crozier held in one hand; in the other he holds up a small silver reliquary with two glass ampoules of dark-red blood. Behind him the Bay of Naples with Mount Vesuvius and a thin plume of smoke, the city along the shore. Keep the scene inside the arched window; no gore.
face: A man of about forty with an ANGULAR face — a square forehead, prominent, sharply cut cheekbones, a straight Roman nose, dark, intense eyes under straight dark brows, a firm mouth and a strong jaw with a small cleft chin; olive southern-Italian skin, short dark hair curling under the mitre, clean-shaven, and a calm, resolute gaze lifted slightly upward.

subject: Two figures side by side, half-length. Left: a Jesuit priest in a worn black soutane and black cloak, a small crucifix on a cord at his chest, offering a clay cup of water with both hands. Right: a young West African man standing upright and dignified at his side, a length of clean white linen draped over one shoulder, his hand resting on the Jesuit's arm as he receives the cup; both are equals in the frame, no chains, no suffering shown. Behind them the harbour of Cartagena de Indias with its stone sea walls, a sailing ship at anchor and palm trees. Keep both figures inside the arched window.
face: Peter Claver (left): a lean man of about fifty with a TRIANGULAR face — a broad forehead and temples tapering past hollow cheeks to a narrow, pointed chin; a long, prominent aquiline nose, deep-set dark eyes under thin, straight dark brows, a thin-lipped, gentle mouth; clean-shaven, short black hair receding at the temples, eyes lowered to the man with compassion. The African man (right): about twenty-five, with deep dark-brown skin and a smooth OVAL face — high, rounded cheekbones, a broad, flat-bridged nose, large dark eyes under full brows, full lips set in a calm, grave expression, a firm chin; short, tightly curled black hair, clean-shaven, and a steady, self-possessed gaze toward the priest.

subject: A Theatine priest in a plain black cassock cinched with a black cincture, a white surplice over it, half-length, holding the Christ Child in his arms; the Child, partly wrapped in a white cloth, reaches up and touches his beard, and the saint bends his head tenderly toward him. A few ears of golden wheat at the lower edge of the window. Behind him the basilica of Santa Maria Maggiore in Rome with its Romanesque bell tower, under a clear winter-evening sky. Keep the scene inside the arched window.
face: A man of about fifty with a ROUND face and soft, full cheeks — a short, straight nose with a rounded tip, large, beautiful dark-brown eyes under gently arched dark brows, low, soft cheekbones, a small, sweet, full-lipped mouth and a rounded chin; short dark-brown hair thinning at the crown, a short, close, rounded dark beard threaded with grey, and his gaze lowered to the Child with a tender smile.

subject: Two twin physicians side by side, half-length, alike in dress. Cosmas (left) in a red tunic under a green mantle, holding a glass flask of medicine up in one hand and a green palm in the other; Damian (right) in a green tunic under a red mantle, holding a small open wooden box of ointments and a green palm. Behind them the Roman Forum with the round Temple of Romulus and the church of Santi Cosma e Damiano, columns and umbrella pines. Keep both figures inside the arched window.
face: Twin Syrian-Arab brothers of about thirty with warm olive-brown skin and the same dark almond eyes and gently aquiline nose, yet distinguishable. Cosmas (left): a broader, SQUARE-JAWED face with full cheeks and a wide mouth, heavier straight brows, short tightly waved black hair, and a short, sparse black beard along the jaw; he looks at the viewer. Damian (right): a narrower, HEART-SHAPED face — wide at the cheekbones, tapering to a small pointed chin — with finer arched brows, a smaller mouth, black hair a little longer and wavy to the ears, only a faint moustache and a wisp of beard at the chin; he looks toward his brother.

subject: Two Jesuits in black soutanes on the deck of a sailing ship at sea, half-length. In front, Bl. Ignatius de Azevedo holds up before him with both hands a framed copy of the icon of Our Lady of St. Luke (Salus Populi Romani: the Virgin in a dark blue mantle holding the Child). Just behind his shoulder, one young companion, a teenage Jesuit novice, hands joined in prayer, looking up. Both hold martyrs' palms or have them nearby. Behind them the mast, rigging and a red-cross sail of the ship Santiago, a calm blue Atlantic and the green volcanic cliffs of La Palma (Tazacorte) on the horizon. No weapons, no violence.
