Keep the scene inside the arched window.
face: Inácio: a noble Portuguese priest of about forty-three with a BROAD, full, rounded-square face and wide cheekbones, a short straight nose, wide-set warm dark eyes under straight dark brows, a full mouth; THICK wavy dark-brown hair with a full hairline (not receding, not balding), and a FULL, ROUNDED dark-brown beard (not pointed, not a goatee); a steady, luminous upward gaze. He must look clearly different from St. Ignatius of Loyola (balding, lean, short pointed beard). The companion: a slender boy of about seventeen with a fresh, broad-cheeked face — a short, slightly upturned nose, large, clear light eyes under straight fair brows, a square, cleft chin and a wide, eager mouth; beardless, with short fair-brown hair and an ardent look.
verdict: rejected: drawn with a saint's halo; a Blessed has rays

subject: A king, half-length, in a royal-blue mantle sown with small gold fleurs-de-lis and lined with ermine over a simple grey tunic, a slender gold crown of fleurs-de-lis on his head; he holds in both hands the Crown of Thorns resting on a small cushion inside a gold and crystal reliquary. Behind him the Sainte-Chapelle in Paris with its tall stained-glass windows and slender spire, the Seine and the Île de la Cité. Keep the scene inside the arched window.
face: A tall, slender man of about forty with a LONG, NARROW oval face — a high, smooth forehead, a fine, straight, slender nose, wide-set light-blue eyes under pale, level brows, slightly hollow cheeks under fine cheekbones, a small gentle mouth and a long, narrow chin; clean-shaven, straight ash-blond hair with the first grey, cut level at the jaw under the crown, and a serene, gracious gaze lowered to the relic.

subject: A layman, half-length, in a white, collarless, long-sleeved camisa de chino of light fabric and dark trousers, his hands clasped at his chest around a wooden rosary, a green palm of martyrdom in the crook of his arm. Behind him the church of Binondo in Manila with its white octagonal Chinese-style bell tower, the Pasig river with bancas, and palm trees. A single figure; his companions are not shown. Keep the scene inside the arched window.
face: A Filipino-Chinese man of about forty with warm golden-tan skin and a ROUND-SQUARE face — wide, flat cheekbones, a broad, low-bridged nose, dark almond eyes with a slight epicanthic fold under thick, straight black brows, a gentle full mouth and a rounded jaw; short straight black hair combed to the side, clean-shaven, and a quiet, steadfast gaze lifted slightly upward.

subject: A cardinal, half-length, in a scarlet mozzetta over a scarlet cassock with a white collar band and a red biretta, a plain pectoral cross; he holds a thick closed book (his Controversies) against his chest with one hand and a quill in the other. Behind him the Collegio Romano and the church of Sant'Ignazio in Rome, ochre façades under a clear sky. Keep the scene inside the arched window.
face: A small, lean man of about seventy with a LONG, RECTANGULAR face — a broad, high forehead, a long, straight, prominent nose, deep-set dark eyes with heavy lids under arched grey brows, sunken cheeks under strong cheekbones and a narrow jaw; grey hair at the temples under the biretta, a trimmed grey moustache and a short, pointed grey goatee, and a mild, penetrating gaze toward the viewer.

subject: A duke, half-length, in mail and a dark-red surcoat with a short ermine-lined mantle, a red ducal cap with an ermine brim and a small gold circlet; he holds a lance with a white pennant bearing a black eagle in one hand and rests the other on a shield bearing the same black eagle on silver. Behind him Prague Castle and St. Vitus Cathedral above the Vltava. Keep the scene inside the arched window.
face: A man of about twenty-eight with a BROAD Slavic face, widest at the high, flat cheekbones and narrowing to a short, firm chin — a short, straight nose, light grey eyes set wide under level, fair-brown brows, a well-shaped mouth; straight chestnut hair cut level just below the ears (not long), a neat moustache and a short, small forked chestnut beard, and a clear, candid gaze toward the viewer; not Christ-like.

subject: Half-length, kneeling in adoration, hands joined at the breast: a black cassock with the white-edged French clerical bands (rabat) at the throat, as in his portraits. Before him, on a white-clothed altar to one side, a gold sunburst monstrance with the Host exposed between tall candles. Background: the chapel of his first house of perpetual adoration in Paris, simple white walls and a round window, with the grey rooftops of Paris outside.
face: A slight man of about fifty-five, clean-shaven, with a long, narrow face tapering to a pointed chin — a very high, domed forehead with the hair receding at the temples, a long, straight nose with a fine ridge, deep-set, intense grey-blue eyes under thin, straight brows, hollow cheeks under distinct cheekbones, a thin, compressed mouth; brown hair greying and combed back, falling behind the ears to the collar, and a rapt gaze fixed on the Host.

subject: Half-length, bareheaded, in the all-white habit of the Premonstratensian canons: a white cassock, a white linen rochet and a short white shoulder cape, the white pallium with small black crosses of an archbishop. He holds up a gold sunburst monstrance in his right hand and a tall archiepiscopal cross with two crossbars in his left, and a small olive branch rests against the cross. Background: the wooded valley of Prémontré in the forest of Coucy, northern France, with the first small abbey church of pale stone among the trees and a stream in the meadow below.
face: A man of about forty-five, clean-shaven, with a long, smooth, egg-shaped face narrowing evenly to a rounded chin — a long, fine, straight nose, dark almond-shaped eyes under thin, high-arched brows, smooth cheeks with little modelling, a small, firm mouth with a full lower lip; short dark-brown hair cut round the head with a broad clerical tonsure on the crown, and a calm, noble, slightly reserved look.

subject: Half-length, a very tall, big-framed priest in the black cassock and mantle of the Camillians, with the large red cloth cross sewn on the breast. He bends slightly toward a sick old man propped on white pillows in a hospital bed at the lower corner, one arm around his shoulders and the other hand holding a small crucifix for him to see; the patient is decently covered with a white sheet. Background: the long vaulted ward of the hospital of Santo Spirito in Sassia, Rome, with rows of curtained beds and high arched windows, the dome of St Peter's seen through one window.
face: A man of about fifty-five with a long, rectangular face and a heavy, square jaw — a large, long nose, broad at the bridge, deep-set, slightly hooded grey-brown eyes under thick, straight dark brows, lines running from the nose to the corners of a wide, firm mouth, lean cheeks; close-cropped dark hair greying and receding from a high forehead, a short, clipped dark beard and moustache flecked with grey, and a compassionate, weathered look down at the sick man.

subject: Half-length, a Syrian monk-deacon: a plain black monastic habit with the black hood drawn up over the head, and a narrow white deacon's stole (orarion) over the left shoulder. He holds a reed pen in his right hand over an open codex resting on a small wooden lectern, the pages covered only with faint lines, no legible writing; beside him a small wooden lyre recalls his title, the Harp of the Spirit. Background: Edessa (Urfa) under a warm evening sky, the citadel on its rocky hill with two tall columns, and the fish pools of Abraham among cypresses below.
face: A small, slight Syrian man of about sixty with an olive-brown complexion and a short, compact face — a broad, low forehead with fine lines, a short, blunt nose with a small hook, large, dark, luminous, deep-set eyes under thin arching brows, flat, lean cheeks, a small, soft chin and a wide, thin-lipped mouth; only a few wisps of grey hair at the temples under the hood, a sparse grey moustache and a thin wisp of beard at the chin (beardless by nature), and a rapt, singing look lifted toward the light.

subject: Half-length widowed queen as on her own tomb effigy in Coimbra: the grey-brown habit of a Franciscan tertiary with a knotted cord, a close white wimple and a black veil, and a slender gold crown set on the veil. In the gathered fold of her habit she holds a few red and white roses; her other hand holds a pilgrim's staff with a small scallop shell (from her pilgrimage to Compostela). No children. Background: Coimbra on the river Mondego, the Gothic monastery church of Santa Clara on the near bank and the white city climbing the hill opposite.
face: A woman of about fifty-five with a fair Iberian complexion and a long, rectangular face with a high forehead and a long, straight jaw — a slender, slightly aquiline nose, wide-set, heavy-lidded grey-green eyes under fine, arched brown brows, high, flat cheekbones with a soft flush, a small, full-lipped mouth with a faint, gentle smile; the hair hidden by the wimple, and a serene, kindly gaze toward the roses.

subject: Half-length Capuchin friar in the rough brown habit with the long pointed hood lying on the shoulders and a white knotted cord. He holds a crucifix raised high in his right hand, as when he rode before the imperial army in 1601, and a closed book (his sermons and Hebrew scholarship) against his side with the left. Background: the open Hungarian plain near Székesfehérvár under a wide sky, the small walled town with its church towers in the distance and far-off white tents and banners of the camp; no fighting.
face: A man of about forty-two with a broad-browed, strong face — a wide, high forehead, prominent, rounded cheekbones, a straight nose with a thick, rounded tip, large, dark, eager eyes under thick black brows, a wide mouth; short dark hair around a Capuchin tonsure, a very long, thick, dark-brown beard falling to the chest, and a fervent, commanding gaze lifted toward the crucifix.

subject: Half-length fifth-century bishop, bareheaded, in a full, bell-shaped deep gold chasuble over a white alb and the white pallium with small dark crosses, as in the Ravenna mosaics. He holds an open book of his sermons in the left hand and raises the right, open, in the gesture of a preacher. Background: Ravenna under a soft sky, the round brick bell tower and long basilica of Sant'Apollinare in Classe among umbrella pines, with the flat marsh toward the sea.
face: A man of about sixty with a broad, rounded, full face — a wide, smooth forehead with a receding hairline, a short, straight nose with a rounded tip, kind dark eyes set wide apart and creased at the corners, full, rounded cheeks, a broad, full-lipped mouth slightly open as if speaking, a soft, round chin; thin, short grey hair and a short, round-trimmed grey beard, and a warm, eloquent look.

subject: Half-length Greek patriarch in the Byzantine manner: a close-fitting white cap covering the head, marked with black crosses (his mark in Byzantine art), a white phelonion patterned with black crosses, a white omophorion with large black crosses over the shoulders. His right hand is raised in blessing; his left holds a small icon of the Mother of God with the Child (Theotokos) against his breast. Background: the harbour of Alexandria under a clear sky, the tall Pharos lighthouse on its island, white city walls and palms along the shore.
face: An Alexandrian Greek of about sixty with a warm olive complexion and a long, oblong face with a strong frame — a straight, high-bridged nose with a narrow ridge, intense dark eyes under strong, dark, slightly knitted brows angled down toward the nose, high cheekbones, a firm, set mouth; the hair hidden by the cap except a little greying brown at the temples, and a long, full brown beard streaked with grey, tapering to a single point on the chest; a fierce, resolute, watchful look.

subject: A hermit of the Minims in a coarse, dark brown-black habit with the HOOD UP over the head and a short rounded capuce over the shoulders, a knotted cord at the waist, half-length, leaning on a rough knotted wooden staff with his right hand. In his left hand he holds up a golden sun disc with straight rays (the CHARITAS emblem, shown as a plain radiant disc with NO letters or lettering). Behind him the rocky Calabrian coast at Paola above the Strait of Messina, a small stone hermitage among chestnut trees, and across the blue water the hills of Sicily with Etna faint in the distance. Keep the scene inside the arched window.
face: A very old but robust hermit of about seventy-five with a BROAD, SQUARE, weathered face seen in the shadow of the hood — a low, wide forehead, a short, broad, slightly flattened nose, small, kindly, deep-set brown eyes under heavy, bushy dark-grey brows, full, ruddy, rounded cheeks, a wide, full-lipped mouth; no hair visible under the hood; a full, BROAD, squared-off grey beard of medium length, streaked with dark, covering the chin like a spade (NOT long, thin or wispy), and a warm, steady, fatherly gaze out at the viewer. Nothing gaunt or hollow-cheeked.

subject: Two half-length figures side by side, as on the Philip and James card. Left and slightly larger, Pope Sixtus II, bareheaded, in a gold brocade cope lined with red over a white alb, holding a martyr's palm, seated in the stone bishop's chair of the catacomb as when he was seized while teaching. Right, a little behind, his deacon Agapitus in a red dalmatic, holding a closed gospel book with a jewelled cover. Background: a catacomb chamber on the Appian Way, a low vaulted room of warm tufa with plain marble slabs set in the walls (no lettering) and small clay oil lamps giving a golden light, a shaft of daylight from a light-well above. Keep both figures inside the arched window.
face: Sixtus: a man of about sixty-five with a broad, bony, rugged face — a high, bald dome with a fringe of short grey curls, a large, strongly hooked nose, deep-set eyes under bushy grey brows, prominent cheekbones, a wide mouth; a short, thick, tousled curly grey beard, the head lifted and the gaze raised upward. Agapitus: a man of about thirty with a wide, flat-planed, rectangular face and a broad, square chin with a small cleft — a short, straight nose, wide-set level dark eyes under heavy straight black brows, a full mouth; close-cropped straight black hair, clean-shaven with a dark shadow on the jaw, looking toward the pope.

subject: Two half-length figures side by side, as on the Philip and James card. Left, Bishop John Fisher of Rochester in a black skullcap-like bishop's cap with side flaps, a white linen rochet over a purple cassock and a black chimere, holding a plain wooden crucifix against his breast and a martyr's palm; a cardinal's red hat lies at the lower edge beside him. Right, Sir Thomas More as Holbein painted him: a soft black cap, a black gown with a broad brown fur collar over deep red velvet sleeves, the gold collar of SS links with the Tudor rose pendant across his shoulders, a small closed prayer book in his hands. Background: the Thames under a pale grey-blue sky with the White Tower of the Tower of London and its walls on the far bank. Keep both figures inside the arched window.
face: Fisher: a tall, lean man of about sixty-five, clean-shaven, with a long, gaunt, bony face — a high, broad forehead, prominent cheekbones above hollowed cheeks, a long, straight, prominent nose, large, wide-open pale grey eyes under high, thin brows, lines running down from the nose past the mouth, a long, firm chin and a thin, straight, closed mouth; grey hair hidden under the cap, and a steady, searching gaze. More: a man of about fifty-five, clean-shaven with the faintest shadow of stubble, with a straight-sided, rather square face — a broad forehead, a long, straight nose with a slightly rounded tip, grey-blue eyes under straight dark brows with a small vertical crease between them, firm, slightly sunken cheeks, a square chin and a straight, composed mouth with a hint of wry humour; straight dark auburn-brown hair falling to the ears under the black cap, the face in three-quarter view looking off to the side. Fisher is older, paler and much thinner; More is fuller in the face, darker-haired and fair-skinned with a light flush.

subject: A thirteenth-century nun of Helfta, half-length, in the black Benedictine habit with the wide, deep sleeves of the choir cowl, a white wimple and a black veil lined with white. On her breast a softly glowing golden heart with small rays, and within it a tiny Christ Child. In one hand she holds a quill, in the other a small open book resting against her. No crozier. Behind her the cloister and church of the abbey of Helfta near Eisleben, pale stone Romanesque arcades and a garden with a well, and the low rolling hills of Saxony in soft autumn light. Keep the scene inside the arched window.
face: A woman of about forty with a pale, fine-featured, narrow face — a smooth forehead, a slender, slightly aquiline nose, large, luminous grey eyes under fine, arched light-brown brows, delicately defined cheekbones, a small, gently curved mouth and a narrow, rounded chin; hair hidden under the wimple and veil; eyes lifted a little upward in quiet, rapt attention.

subject: A Passionist priest of the eighteenth century, half-length, in the black Passionist habit of coarse wool with a black mantle, a leather belt and a large rosary; on the left breast of both habit and mantle the white Passionist badge in its plain form: a white heart with a small white cross standing on it, with no lettering, words or letters on it at all. He holds a plain dark wooden crucifix to his breast with both hands, the head bowed toward it. Behind him the wooded promontory of Monte Argentario on the Tuscan coast, the small stone retreat of the Presentation among holm oaks, and the calm blue Tyrrhenian sea with the lagoon of Orbetello. Keep the scene inside the arched window.
face: A tall, slender, clean-shaven man of about seventy with a long oval face — a high, wide, elevated forehead, a long nose with a gently rounded, slightly drooping tip, clear, calm grey eyes with heavy lids lowered to the crucifix, softly hollowed cheeks, a gentle, closed mouth and a small rounded chin; thin, short grey hair brushed back and to the sides; a placid, modest and grave look with a trace of sorrow.

subject: A Visitation nun, half-length, in the black habit with a black veil over a white linen band, a wide, square white pleated guimpe covering the neck and chest, and a silver cross on her breast; she holds a small book of the Rule against her chest with both hands, a wooden rosary hanging from her belt. No heart, no flames, no monogram. Behind her the Visitation monastery at Annecy, a plain cloister arcade and garden with the green Semnoz mountain beyond; no lake. Keep the scene inside the arched window; no lettering besides the initial.
face: A MATRONLY woman of about sixty, a widow and foundress, with a BROAD, SQUARE face, full in the jaw — a long, straight, strong nose, wide-set clear grey-blue eyes with slightly heavy lids under straight, level brows, broad, flat cheekbones, a wide mouth with thin, closed lips and a faint, knowing smile, and a firm, squared chin; fair skin with visible fine lines at the eyes and mouth, hair hidden by the veil; a steady, direct, authoritative and kindly gaze straight at the viewer (NOT upturned, not girlish or delicate).

subject: An Observant Franciscan friar of the fifteenth century, half-length, in a patched grey-brown Franciscan habit with a hood and a white knotted cord. In his right hand he holds upright a tall wooden staff topped with a small cross, carrying a white banner with a plain red cross; in his left a small crucifix raised toward the viewer as if preaching. Behind him, calm and distant, the fortress of Belgrade on its hill where the Sava meets the Danube, stone walls and towers under a clear morning sky, the wide river with a single boat. No soldiers, no battle, no fallen figures. Keep the banner and scene inside the arched window.
face: A small, lean man of about seventy, clean-shaven, with a narrow, bony, triangular face — a broad, domed, bald head with only a small tuft of white hair over the brow and a thin white fringe, prominent cheekbones over sunken cheeks, a long, thin, slightly hooked nose, small, deep-set, lively dark eyes under sparse grey brows, thin lips and a small pointed chin; weathered, ascetic but cheerful and alert, looking out with fervour.

subject: A Carthusian monk, half-length, in the full white Carthusian habit: a white wool cowl with a broad band joining front and back panels at the sides and a large white hood lying on the shoulders, no scapular colour, no cord. His arms are crossed on his breast over a small plain wooden crucifix, head bowed in recollection. Behind him the high, narrow valley of the Grande Chartreuse near Grenoble: steep limestone cliffs and dark fir forest, a few small stone hermit cells with steep roofs in the snow, and above the peaks, in a pale evening sky, a small circle of seven faint golden stars (the bishop's dream). Keep the mountains and stars inside the arched window.
face: A clean-shaven man of about fifty with a long, rectangular face — a high, flat forehead, strong straight brows set low over deep-set grey eyes, a thin, straight, rather long nose, flat, lean cheeks without prominent cheekbones, a firmly squared chin and thin, closed lips; the head shaven with only the narrow Carthusian ring of short dark-brown hair just beginning to grey; eyes lowered, grave and inward, with the faintest peace at the mouth.

subject: A Dominican friar-bishop of the thirteenth century, half-length, in the white Dominican habit and scapular with the black cappa and hood over it, a white mitre embroidered with gold, a pectoral cross; seated at a writing desk with a large open manuscript book and a quill in his right hand, a small armillary sphere and a few plant sprigs and a crystal on the desk. Behind him, through an arched opening, the river Rhine at Cologne with medieval town walls, church spires and the tall new Gothic choir of the cathedral rising in scaffolding. Keep the scene inside the arched window.
face: An old man of about seventy-five, clean-shaven, with a large, heavy, broad face — a wide, square, jowled jaw, a big, slightly fleshy nose, small, keen, heavy-lidded grey eyes under low, straight white brows, a wide, thin, firmly set mouth and deep lines from nose to mouth; a white Dominican tonsure ring of short hair under the mitre; a shrewd, patient, scholarly gaze lifted slightly from the page.

subject: A widowed duchess of the thirteenth century, half-length, in a plain grey-brown woollen gown and a long grey mantle, a white wimple under the chin and a white veil, with a thin, simple gold ducal circlet over the veil. In her right hand she holds a small ivory statuette of the Virgin and Child against her breast; from her left hand hang a pair of plain leather shoes by their straps, and a string of wooden prayer beads is wound on that wrist (as in the Hedwig Codex of 1353). Behind her the Cistercian abbey of Trzebnica in Silesia, a Romanesque church of red brick and pale stone with a twin-towered front, among flat autumn fields and birch trees. Keep the scene inside the arched window.
face: A tall woman of about sixty with a long, oval face — prominent, high cheekbones above softly hollowed cheeks, a long, straight nose with a narrow bridge, large brown eyes with heavy lids under thin, high-arched pale brows, a small, firm mouth and a narrow chin; fine lines at the eyes; hair entirely hidden under the wimple and veil; her gaze lowered to the statuette with a quiet, humble tenderness.

subject: An early bishop of the third century, half-length, in a simple deep-red chasuble of antique bell shape over a white alb, a low white mitre with red bands, a plain gold crozier resting in the crook of his left arm; in his left hand a closed Gospel book, in his right a green martyr's palm held upright. His head is firmly on his shoulders and he holds nothing else — never his own head. Behind him the green hill of Montmartre above the river Seine with a small Gallo-Roman town of pale stone and red tiles at its foot, vineyards on the slope and a small stone chapel at the summit, under a calm autumn sky. Keep the scene inside the arched window.
face: A man of about sixty with a broad, short, square face — a wide, low forehead, wide cheekbones and a strong, square jaw; a short, straight nose with a broad bridge; round dark-brown eyes set well apart under heavy, arched dark brows; a full, firm mouth; thick, tightly curled dark hair turning pepper-and-salt showing under the mitre over the ears, and a full, rounded, closely curled beard of the same colour; a steady, kindly gaze straight ahead and slightly down.

subject: An eleventh-century queen, half-length, in a long gown of deep blue with a gold-embroidered border, a crimson mantle fastened with a round brooch, a white linen veil and a simple gold crown with fleurons. She holds in both hands, open against her breast, a small illuminated Gospel book in a jewelled gold-and-silver binding. Behind her the rock of Edinburgh Castle with the small, plain Romanesque stone chapel on its summit, and beyond, the grey-blue Firth of Forth with a small boat at the Queen's Ferry, under a soft northern sky. Keep the scene inside the arched window.
face: A woman of about forty-five with a gentle, broad-browed, softly square face — wide-set clear blue eyes under light, straight brows, a short, straight nose, fair, rosy full cheeks, a wide, gentle mouth and a rounded, firm chin; long golden-blonde hair plaited and partly visible under the veil; a serene, kindly gaze toward the book.

subject: A Spanish missionary archbishop of the 1850s, half-length, in a violet cassock with many small buttons, a violet mozzetta, a white rochet with plain linen sleeves, a violet zucchetto and a gold pectoral cross on a chain. He holds a small open book of his own devotional writings against his chest in one hand and a rosary in the other. Behind him the bay of Santiago de Cuba with its cathedral's white towers, palm trees, tiled roofs and green Sierra Maestra hills under a bright tropical sky. Keep the scene inside the arched window.
face: A stocky, clean-shaven Spaniard of about forty-five with a large, round, fleshy face and a warm olive-dark complexion — a short, broad nose, full cheeks, dark, rather small, penetrating eyes under thick, straight, black brows, a full lower lip and a rounded, heavy chin; short black hair receding at the temples under the zucchetto; a serious, energetic, kindly gaze to one side.

subject: Two Jesuit missionaries of the 1640s side by side, half-length, both in plain black Jesuit soutanes and black cloaks. Brébeuf (left, the taller and broader) holds a wooden crucifix against his chest with a large hand; Jogues (right, smaller) has his hands folded in prayer, fingers hidden in his sleeves, a small breviary tucked under his arm. Behind them the mission of Sainte-Marie among the Hurons: a wooden palisade and a bark-covered Wendat longhouse, a birchbark canoe drawn up on the shore of a calm northern lake (Georgian Bay), maples and pines in red and gold autumn colour. No wounds, no fire, no violence. Keep the two figures and the scene inside the arched window.
face: Two clearly different men. Brébeuf (left): a tall, powerfully built man of about fifty-five with a large, long, strong-boned face — a high, bald dome of a forehead with a short fringe of grey hair at the sides, a big, straight, prominent nose, deep-set steady grey eyes under heavy brows, broad cheekbones and a strong jaw under a clipped salt-and-pepper beard and moustache, cut to a blunt point; a grave, manly, fatherly look. Jogues (right): a slighter man of about thirty-nine with a narrower, finer, oval face — dark-brown hair receding high from the forehead, gently arched brows, soft brown eyes lowered, a thin straight nose, a small mouth, and a short dark-brown pointed beard with a light moustache; a gentle, humble, prayerful look.

subject: A Jesuit priest of the sixteenth century, half-length, in a plain black Jesuit cassock with a narrow white collar band showing at the neck and a black mantle, bare-headed. He holds against his breast with his left hand a small, thick, closed leather-bound book (his catechism), his right hand open in a gesture of teaching; a simple wooden rosary hangs from his fingers. Behind him the Swiss town of Fribourg on its rock above the green loop of the river Saane: steep tiled roofs, the tall Gothic bell tower of the church of St Nicholas, a covered wooden bridge, and wooded hills under a soft grey-blue winter sky. Keep the town inside the arched window.
face: A man of about sixty-five with an oblong face that broadens at the jaw — a broad, smooth forehead, a long, straight nose with a fleshy, rounded tip, wide-set, hooded pale-brown eyes under thin, level brows, full, softened lower cheeks, a wide, firm mouth; thick grey hair cut short and combed forward over the brow; a short, close-cropped grey beard and moustache covering the jaw; a mild, attentive gaze slightly to the side.

subject: A pope of the seventh century in exile, half-length, in a simple dark-red chasuble of antique bell shape over a white tunic and a white wool pallium with small dark crosses; NO tiara, NO mitre, bare-headed; a plain dark travelling cloak over his shoulders. He holds a closed book against his breast with his left hand and a green martyr's palm in his right. Behind him the stony shore of Chersonesus in the Crimea: ruined Greek walls and columns of pale limestone on a low headland, dry grass, and the dark-blue Black Sea under a wide, windswept spring sky. Keep the scene inside the arched window.
face: A man of about sixty, worn thin by hardship, with a long, rectangular face and a tall forehead — a strong, straight Roman nose, large, dark, sorrowful eyes under straight, thick black brows, hollow cheeks beneath pronounced cheekbones, a firm mouth; dark-brown hair streaked with grey, cut short; a full, dark-brown beard of medium length streaked with grey and cut square at the bottom, with a full moustache; a patient, steadfast gaze slightly downward.

subject: An early pope of the first century, half-length, in a simple deep-red chasuble of antique bell shape over a white tunic, with a plain narrow white wool pallium marked with small dark crosses; NO tiara, NO mitre, bare-headed. With his left hand he rests a dark iron ship's anchor upright against his shoulder, its ring near his cheek; in his right hand a small green martyr's palm. Behind him the Roman harbour of Ostia at the mouth of the Tiber: a stone lighthouse on the mole, a few moored merchant ships with furled square sails, warehouses of brick, and a calm blue-green sea under a clear morning sky. Keep the harbour and ships inside the arched window.
face: A man of about sixty with a diamond-shaped face — a narrow forehead and a narrow, firm chin, broadest at high, prominent cheekbones; a strong, high-bridged aquiline Roman nose; deep-set, dark, thoughtful eyes under straight black brows flecked with grey; a thin, firm mouth; close-cropped black hair receding at the temples and greying above the ears; a short, close-trimmed black beard following the line of the jaw, grizzled at the chin; a calm, attentive gaze slightly to one side.

subject: A Roman boy of about fourteen, half-length, in a knee-length white wool tunic with a narrow red stripe at the edge and a short deep-green cloak fastened at the right shoulder with a small round bronze brooch. In his right hand he holds a green martyr's palm upright; his left hand holds a small closed book to his breast. Behind him the Janiculum hill above Rome along the Via Aurelia: tall umbrella pines and cypresses, a low Roman tomb by the road, and beyond, the Tiber and the roofs and domes of the ancient city in the soft light of a spring morning. Keep the scene inside the arched window.
face: A boy of fourteen, visibly a boy and not a young man, with a round face still holding childhood fullness — a smooth, rounded forehead, round, soft cheeks, a short, straight nose with a small rounded tip, large, round dark-brown eyes under straight, thick dark brows, a small dimpled chin and a small mouth with the faint hint of a smile; a light olive, sun-warmed Mediterranean complexion; thick, dark-brown hair in short, tight curls close to the head; no beard; a brave, candid gaze lifted a little upward.

subject: A Camaldolese hermit and cardinal of the eleventh century, half-length, in the full white Camaldolese habit and hood with a scarlet cardinal's cape (mozzetta) over his shoulders and a simple gold pectoral cross. In his left hand he holds a closed book; from his right hand hangs a short plain white knotted cord. Behind him the hermitage of Fonte Avellana under Monte Catria in the Apennines: grey stone monastery buildings and a small Romanesque church on a wooded slope, dark beech and fir forest, a limestone peak with snow on it and a clear, cold sky. Keep the mountain and monastery inside the arched window.
face: A lean, ascetic man of about sixty-four with a long face and a craggy, prominent brow ridge — a high, furrowed forehead, deep-set, burning dark eyes looking upward, a long, strong nose with a slight hook, sharp cheekbones over sunken cheeks, thin, tight lips; short, thick, wiry grey hair; a long, narrow, grey beard falling to the breast in wavy, tapering strands, with a full grey moustache; an intense, searching upward gaze.

subject: An early pope of the fourth century, half-length, in a simple, full chasuble of warm brick-red over a white tunic, a plain white wool pallium falling straight down the front; NO tiara, NO mitre, bare-headed. He holds a large closed Gospel book bound in gold against his breast with both hands, as in the old Roman fresco. Behind him Mount Soracte north of Rome, a long lone limestone ridge rising from green, rolling Tiber-valley countryside, with a small stone hermitage near its summit, olive groves at its foot and a pale, clear winter sky. Keep the mountain inside the arched window.
face: A man of about sixty-five with a long, narrow face tapering to a small, rounded chin — a smooth, high forehead, very large, wide-open almond-shaped dark eyes under high, finely arched brows, a long, thin, perfectly straight nose, smooth cheeks without prominent cheekbones, a small, closed mouth; white hair cut in a neat round clerical ring (the crown shaven); a short, neat, pointed white beard and a thin white moustache; a calm, wide-eyed, gentle gaze straight ahead.

subject: An archbishop of the twelfth century, half-length, standing calmly, in a deep-red chasuble of full medieval cut over a white alb, a white wool pallium with small dark crosses over his shoulders, and a white mitre with gold bands; in his left hand a gilt crozier, in his right a closed Gospel book held to his breast. No sword, no wound, no violence. Behind him the Romanesque cathedral of Canterbury as it stood in 1170: pale Caen-stone walls, round arches and a massive square central tower, with the roofs of the city and green Kentish fields beyond under a soft winter sky. Keep the cathedral inside the arched window.
face: A tall, spare man of about fifty with a pale complexion and a long, narrow, well-formed face — a high forehead, a long, fine nose with a gently arched bridge, bright, lively dark eyes under dark, straight brows, lean cheeks with a faint colour high on the cheekbones, a firm, narrow chin and a finely shaped, closed mouth; clean-shaven; dark-brown hair, just touched with grey at the temples, cut short around the tonsure beneath the mitre; a steady, resolute, serene gaze straight ahead.

subject: A Syrian monk-priest of the eighth century, half-length, turned three-quarters, in a dark plum-purple monastic mantle over an ochre-gold tunic, his head wrapped in the white Arab head-cloth crossed with thin black stripes that Byzantine painters give him, falling to the shoulders. In his left hand a long, unrolled blank parchment scroll (no writing on it); in his right a reed pen lifted from a small ink-horn. Beside him on a ledge a small icon of the Mother of God with the Child. Behind him the Great Lavra of Mar Saba clinging to the cliffs of the Kidron gorge in the Judaean desert: honey-coloured stone walls, towers and cells stepped down the rock face, a pale dome, bare ochre hills and a hot, clear sky. Keep the monastery inside the arched window.
face: A Levantine man of about sixty-five with a warm olive complexion and a long, narrow face — a high, lined forehead, a long, thin nose with a high bridge curving slightly at the tip, heavy-lidded, almond-shaped dark-brown eyes under dark, gently sloping brows, lean cheeks under fine cheekbones, a narrow chin hidden in the beard and a small mouth; a long, wavy, iron-grey beard falling in soft strands to the breast and a grey moustache; a grave, gentle, contemplative gaze lowered to the scroll.

subject: An early pope of the third century, half-length, in a simple deep-green bell-shaped chasuble over a plain white tunic and a white wool pallium with small dark crosses; NO tiara, NO mitre, bare-headed. His right hand is raised in blessing; in his left a green martyr's palm and a small closed book. Behind him Trastevere on the right bank of the Tiber in the third century: a modest house-church of brick with a tiled roof among humble workshops and houses, a stone well-head in the small square before it, the river and the Aventine hill beyond, under a warm autumn sky. Keep the scene inside the arched window.
face: A stocky, broad-shouldered man of about fifty-five with a wide, rectangular face and a heavy, fleshy jaw on a thick neck — a low, broad forehead, a broad nose with a wide, flat bridge, small, shrewd, kindly hazel eyes set deep under a heavy brow with thick, straight black-and-grey brows, full cheeks, a wide, generous mouth; thick, straight, coarse hair of black mixed with grey, cropped short and combed forward in a blunt Roman fringe low on the brow (NOT bald, no curls); a short, dense, square-trimmed black-and-grey beard close to the face; a frank, warm, direct gaze.

subject: A bishop of the fourth century, half-length, in a white chasuble of antique bell shape over a white alb with a gold-embroidered border, a low white mitre with gold bands, a plain gold crozier in his left hand, and in his right a large closed book held upright against his breast (his treatise on the Trinity). Behind him Poitiers: the small fourth-century baptistery of Saint-Jean of pale stone with a triangular gable and a low tiled roof, the green valley of the river Clain and the old town on its hill beyond, under a clear, cold January sky. Keep the scene inside the arched window.
face: A robust man of about fifty-five with a broad, trapezoid face, wider at the temples than at the jaw — a high, broad forehead with white hair receding from it, a strong, straight nose with a broad bridge, wide-set, clear grey eyes under heavy, arched white brows, ruddy, full cheekbones, a firm mouth half-hidden by a white moustache; a long, broad, flowing white beard spread over the chest in soft waves; an earnest, penetrating gaze straight ahead.

subject: An eleventh-century queen, half-length, in a long gown of deep blue with a gold-embroidered border, a crimson mantle fastened with a round brooch, a white linen wimple covering the neck and a white veil covering all her hair and a simple gold crown with fleurons. She holds in both hands, open against her breast, a small illuminated Gospel book in a jewelled gold-and-silver binding. Behind her the rock of Edinburgh Castle with the small, plain Romanesque stone chapel on its summit, and beyond, the grey-blue Firth of Forth with a small boat at the Queen's Ferry, under a soft northern sky. Keep the scene inside the arched window.
face: A MATRONLY woman of about forty-five, mother of eight, with a LONG, OVAL face — a high forehead, a long, straight, rather strong nose, almond-shaped hazel eyes under dark, arched brows, long, smooth cheeks with a faint colour, a small, firm, closed mouth and a long, rounded chin; ALL hair covered by the wimple and veil (no blonde hair, no plaits); a grave, thoughtful gaze lowered to the book. Mature and dignified, not girlish.

subject: A thirteenth-century nun of Helfta, half-length, in the black Benedictine habit with the wide, deep sleeves of the choir cowl, a white wimple and a black veil lined with white. On her breast a softly glowing golden heart with small rays, and within it a tiny Christ Child. In one hand she holds a quill, in the other a small open book resting against her. No crozier. Behind her the cloister and church of the abbey of Helfta near Eisleben, pale stone Romanesque arcades and a garden with a well, and the low rolling hills of Saxony in soft autumn light. Keep the scene inside the arched window. The illuminated initial is the letter G — drawn clearly as a G with its inward horizontal bar, not a C.
face: A woman of about forty with a STRONG, HEART-SHAPED face — a high, broad, rounded forehead, straight, strongly marked dark brows nearly level, deep-set dark brown eyes, a long, straight, fine nose, high cheekbones narrowing to a small, pointed chin, a wide, thin-lipped mouth set in a composed line; warm olive-toned skin; hair hidden under the wimple and veil; a steady, intelligent, scholarly gaze looking level toward the viewer (NOT upturned, not girlish, not doll-like).

subject: A pope of the seventh century in exile, half-length, in a simple dark-red chasuble of antique bell shape over a white tunic and a white wool pallium with small dark crosses; NO tiara, NO mitre, bare-headed; a plain dark travelling cloak over his shoulders. He holds a closed book against his breast with his left hand and a green martyr's palm in his right. Behind him the stony shore of Chersonesus in the Crimea: ruined Greek walls and columns of pale limestone on a low headland, dry grass, and the dark-blue Black Sea under a wide, windswept spring sky. Keep the scene inside the arched window.
face: A man of about sixty-five, EMACIATED by prison and exile, with a LONG, NARROW, rectangular face and a tall forehead — a strong, straight Roman nose, large, dark, sorrowful eyes set deep in shadowed sockets under straight, thin grey brows, deeply HOLLOW cheeks beneath sharp, prominent cheekbones, a long, firm mouth; thin, straight, iron-GREY hair cut short and receding at the temples (no curls); a thin, iron-grey beard, close-trimmed and squared at the chin, showing the hollows of the cheeks (NOT full or bushy, not dark brown); a patient, steadfast gaze slightly downward.

subject: Two half-length figures side by side, as on the Philip and James card. Left and slightly larger, Pope Sixtus II, bareheaded, in a gold brocade cope lined with red over a white alb, holding a martyr's palm, seated in the stone bishop's chair of the catacomb as when he was seized while teaching. Right, a little behind, his deacon Agapitus in a red dalmatic, holding a closed gospel book with a jewelled cover. Background: a catacomb chamber on the Appian Way, a low vaulted room of warm tufa with plain marble slabs set in the walls (no lettering) and small clay oil lamps giving a golden light, a shaft of daylight from a light-well above. Keep both figures inside the arched window.
face: Sixtus: a man of about sixty-five with a LONG, LEAN, NARROW face — a high, completely bald dome with only thin wisps of white at the temples, a long, strongly hooked nose, heavy-lidded pale blue eyes under thin white brows, flat cheeks, a long upper lip and a thin mouth; CLEAN-SHAVEN but for close white stubble on the jaw (no beard, no curls), the head slightly bowed and the gaze lowered gently toward the viewer as he teaches. Agapitus: a man of about thirty with a wide, flat-planed, rectangular face and a broad, square chin with a small cleft — a short, straight nose, wide-set level dark eyes under heavy straight black brows, a full mouth; close-cropped straight black hair, clean-shaven with a dark shadow on the jaw, looking toward the pope.

subject: A Jesuit priest of the sixteenth century, half-length, in a plain black Jesuit cassock with a narrow white collar band showing at the neck and a black mantle, bare-headed. He holds against his breast with his left hand a small, thick, closed leather-bound book (his catechism), his right hand open in a gesture of teaching; a simple wooden rosary hangs from his fingers. Behind him the Swiss town of Fribourg on its rock above the green loop of the river Saane: steep tiled roofs, the tall Gothic bell tower of the church of St Nicholas, a covered wooden bridge, and wooded hills under a soft grey-blue winter sky. Keep the town inside the arched window.
face: A man of about sixty-five with an oblong face that broadens at the jaw — a broad, smooth forehead, a long, straight nose with a fleshy, rounded tip, wide-set, hooded pale-brown eyes under thin, level brows, full, softened lower cheeks, a wide, firm mouth; thick grey hair cut short and combed forward over the brow; a short, close-cropped grey beard and moustache covering the jaw; a mild, attentive gaze slightly to the side.

subject: The chalice: a tall gilded gothic chalice with a hexagonal knop set with small red and blue enamel bosses, the gilt paten resting on its rim and a stiff white pall on top, standing on a folded white linen corporal. Soft light glinting on the gold.

The First Sunday of Advent: on the step of a stone church altar, an evergreen Advent wreath with four tall candles — three violet and one rose — only the first violet candle lit, its small flame steady; violet altar frontal behind; through a round window above, a deep blue pre-dawn sky over a snowy village with a single bright morning star. Quiet, expectant, nocturnal light.

The Consecration at Mass: at a white-and-gold high altar with six tall lit candles and a crucifix, a priest in a gold chasuble seen from behind raises the white Host high above his head with both hands; an altar server in cassock and white surplice kneels on the step at the right lifting the hem of the chasuble, a small lit candle beside him; soft golden rays fall from above onto the Host. Figures small in the scene, the altar the centre.

A bishop of the tenth century, half-length, in a deep-red chasuble of antique bell shape over a white alb, bare-headed, NO mitre; a plain crozier in his left hand and a closed Gospel book against his chest with his right, a green martyr's palm resting in the crook of that arm. Behind him Prague of the tenth century: the wooded castle hill above the river Vltava with a small round Romanesque stone church and timber palisades, a ferry boat on the river, in clear morning light. Keep the castle hill and river inside the arched window.
face: A tall, lean Czech of about forty with an ANGULAR, high-cheekboned face narrowing to a firm, POINTED chin — a broad, straight forehead, strong, jutting cheekbones over slightly hollow cheeks, a straight nose with a broad base, deep-set, earnest blue-grey eyes under straight fair brows, a thin, firm mouth; straight ash-blond hair cut short around a tonsure; a short fair beard lying close along the jaw and ending in a small point at the chin; a fervent gaze toward the distance.

subject: A Capuchin friar of the early seventeenth century, half-length, in the rough brown Capuchin habit with the long pointed hood lying on his shoulders and a white knotted cord, a small wooden crucifix hanging at his belt; he holds a closed book of the Gospels against his chest with his right hand and a green martyr's palm in his left. NO weapons, no wounds. Behind him the village of Seewis in the Prättigau, Switzerland: a white church with a slender spire among dark wooden chalets on a steep green alpine meadow, dark pines and snowy peaks under a clear spring sky. Keep the village and mountains inside the arched window.
face: A lean German Capuchin of about forty-four, once a lawyer, with a FINE-BONED, NARROW face tapering to a neat chin — a high, narrow forehead, a fine, straight, narrow nose, clear, gentle hazel eyes under fine, straight brows, faint hollows under delicate cheekbones, a small, thin, kindly mouth; dark-brown hair cropped very short around the Capuchin tonsure; a full, neatly combed dark-brown beard reaching the upper chest and narrowing to a rounded point; a serene, resolute gaze toward the viewer.

subject: A Dominican friar of the thirteenth century, half-length, in the white habit and white scapular; his black cappa is not on his shoulders but rigged as a sail: one edge tied to the tall wooden walking staff he holds upright in his right hand, the black cloth billowing behind him in the wind. In his left hand, held against his chest, a small closed book and an iron key, sign of the confessor. He stands calmly upright on the water as on a floor. Behind him the open blue Mediterranean with small white-capped waves, the low hills of Mallorca a faint line on one side and, ahead on the other, the walled harbour of Barcelona with its Romanesque towers, under a bright sky with a few clouds. Keep the sea, the sail and the staff inside the arched window.
face: A very old but wiry Catalan of about eighty with a sun-browned complexion and a small, compact, SHIELD-SHAPED face — a broad, bony forehead, high cheekbones angling down to a narrow, squared-off chin; a short, straight nose with a firm, rounded tip; small, bright black eyes set in fine laughter lines under bushy white brows; a long upper lip and a thin, wide mouth with a faint smile; a white Dominican crown of short hair around the shaven head; a close-cropped white beard only a finger deep, following the line of the jaw; the gaze lifted with serene confidence toward the sky ahead.

subject: An Armenian monk-priest of the tenth century, half-length, in a black monastic robe with the black pointed Armenian monastic hood raised over his head and falling to the shoulders, a small silver cross on his chest. He holds against his chest an open book of prayers bound in red leather, its pages covered only with faint illegible lines, and a reed pen in his other hand. Behind him the monastery of Narek on the southern shore of Lake Van: a small church of pinkish stone with a conical Armenian dome, a carved stone cross-stone (khachkar) beside it, and the deep-blue lake with mountains beyond. Keep the monastery and the lake inside the arched window.
face: An Armenian monk of about fifty with a warm olive complexion and a BROAD, flat-planed OVAL face, as wide at the cheekbones as at the forehead, with a full, rounded jaw — a long, straight nose with a high, strong bridge, very large, wide-open dark almond eyes set level under thick, strongly arched black brows (the wide-eyed gaze of Armenian miniatures), smooth, full cheeks, a small, full mouth; short, thick black hair showing under the hood at the forehead; a short, dense black beard and moustache closely encircling the jaw, with a few grey threads; an intense, contemplative gaze lifted a little upward.

subject: A Polish-Lithuanian prince of the fifteenth century, half-length, in a long red robe lined and collared with white ermine, a gold chain on his chest, and on his head the red cap of the Grand Duke of Lithuania with a gold crown-band; in one hand a rosary of dark beads, in the other a tall stem of white lilies. Behind him Vilnius: the Gothic cathedral near the river Neris and the red-brick tower of the Upper Castle on its wooded hill, under a clear, cold late-winter sky with patches of snow. Keep the city inside the arched window.
face: A pale, slender young prince of about twenty-four (a young man, not a boy), clean-shaven, with a LONG, NARROW face — a high, smooth forehead, a long, straight, slender nose with a slightly drooping tip, heavy-lidded grey-green eyes under fine, high-arched light-brown brows, long, smooth cheeks with faint colour, a small, gently curved closed mouth and a narrow, rounded chin; straight chestnut-brown hair parted in the middle and falling to the shoulders; a gentle, recollected gaze to one side.

subject: A missionary archbishop of the ninth century, half-length, in the black Benedictine cowl with a plain narrow white wool pallium marked with small dark crosses over his shoulders; NO mitre, bare-headed. A plain wooden crozier with a simple curled head rests in his left hand; on his right forearm he carries a small model of a wooden church with a steep shingled roof. Behind him Birka on Lake Mälaren in Sweden: a Viking trading town of timber houses with turf roofs on a green island shore, two dragon-prowed longships drawn up on the beach, birch woods and grey-blue water under a pale northern sky. Keep the town and the ships inside the arched window.
face: A spare, weathered Frank of about sixty, clean-shaven, with a BROAD, SQUARE-BROWED face narrowing only a little to a wide, strongly CLEFT chin — a straight, flat brow line, small, deep-set, very pale grey-blue eyes crinkled against the northern wind, a short, straight nose with a broad bridge, lean cheeks with long vertical creases, a wide, straight, thin-lipped mouth; short, straight flaxen hair gone silver, cut in a straight Carolingian fringe around the shaven monastic crown; wind-reddened cheeks; a calm, far-seeing gaze a little to one side.

subject: A Spanish archbishop of the late sixteenth century on a pastoral visit, half-length, in a white lace-edged rochet under a red mozzetta, a gold pectoral cross, a plain travelling crozier in his left hand; his right hand rests in blessing on the head of a small Andean child held by the mother, a Quechua woman with brown skin and long black braids in a dark woven shawl, both shown at his side and a little lower. Behind them an Andean highland village: a whitewashed adobe church with a bell-gable, green terraced slopes, a llama, and snow-capped peaks under a deep-blue sky. Keep the mother, child and mountains inside the arched window.
face: A spare, tireless Castilian of about sixty-two, clean-shaven, with a LONG face BROAD AT THE JAW — a high, bald, domed crown with a short fringe of grey hair above the ears, a long, large, straight nose, pale grey-blue eyes under heavy lids and high-arched grey brows, lean cheeks with deep lines from nose to mouth, a small, tight-lipped, resolute mouth and a broad, firm chin; skin weathered and browned by years on the roads of the Andes; a grave, kindly gaze down toward the child.

subject: The seven founders of the Servants of Mary, Florentine gentlemen of the thirteenth century, grouped half-length: THREE in the front row side by side and FOUR close behind them, their heads a little higher, seven clearly separate faces. All wear the black Servite habit — black tunic, black scapular, black hood lying on the shoulders, a black leather belt — hands folded or holding plain rosaries. The central friar in front holds a small closed book of the Rule against his chest; the friar at his right holds up a small framed painting of the sorrowing Virgin Mary in a dark-blue mantle (a picture only, no text). Behind them Monte Senario north of Florence: a small stone hermitage and chapel among tall dark firs on a hilltop, and far below the Arno valley with the walls and towers of medieval Florence in blue haze. Keep all seven figures inside the arched window.
face: Seven clearly different Florentine men, none a stock face. FRONT ROW, left to right: (1) Alexis Falconieri, about forty-five, the humble lay brother: clean-shaven, a LONG, NARROW face with hollow cheeks, a long, thin nose with a slight hook, heavy-lidded eyes lowered in humility and a small pointed chin; short, straight, greying brown hair, no tonsure. (2) Bonfilius Monaldi, the prior, in the centre, about fifty-five: a BROAD, SQUARE face with a heavy jaw, a short, broad nose, steady grey eyes under thick, straight grey brows, a grey monastic crown of hair and a short, full, rounded grey beard. (3) Bonajuncta, about thirty-five: a ROUND, full face with plump cheeks, a small snub nose, large, bright black eyes under round-arched brows, a dimpled chin under a short, trim black beard, thick black hair in a tonsure ring. BACK ROW, left to right: (4) Amadeus, about fifty: a tall, domed, completely bald head, a LONG, RECTANGULAR clean-shaven face, a big straight nose, deep-set dark eyes. (5) Manettus, about forty-five: a HEART-SHAPED face, wide at the cheekbones and narrowing to a small chin, a fine straight nose, hazel eyes, auburn hair in a tonsure ring and a short, neat auburn beard. (6) Hugh, about thirty-five: a lean, ANGULAR face with sharp cheekbones and a square chin, a Roman nose, dark eyes under heavy black brows, clean-shaven, short curly black hair. (7) Sostene, about thirty-five: a fair OVAL face with a high forehead, a slender nose, light-blue eyes, straight fair-brown hair in a tonsure ring, a thin fair moustache and a small tuft of beard at the chin. All gazes calm and devotional, several turned toward the image of Our Lady.

subject: A bishop of seventh-century Visigothic Spain, half-length, seated at a writing desk, in a white chasuble of antique bell shape with a narrow gold border and a narrow white wool pallium marked with small dark crosses, bare-headed, NO mitre; he writes with a quill in a large open codex whose pages show only faint illegible lines, other bound codices stacked beside him. Behind him, through a Visigothic horseshoe arch: Seville, with Roman city walls, palm and orange trees and the broad Guadalquivir with a small boat, in warm evening light. Keep the city inside the arched window.
face: A venerable Hispano-Roman of about seventy with a LARGE, HEAVY, LONG face — a broad, high forehead, a large, strong nose with a gentle hook and a fleshy tip, heavy-lidded dark eyes lowered to the page under thick grey brows, full cheeks, and a broad chin under a full, thick grey beard of medium length, trimmed round and still dark at the moustache; thick grey hair cut short around a tonsure; a calm, absorbed, scholarly look.

subject: A Venetian nobleman turned servant of the poor, early sixteenth century, half-length, in a plain, worn black gown buttoned to the neck with a small white collar-band, no cloak and no mark of rank. His right arm is around the shoulders of an orphan boy of about ten (a round face, short brown hair, a simple grey smock) who leans against his side; in his left hand hangs loosely a short length of broken iron chain, the fetters from which he escaped as a prisoner of war, by Our Lady's help. Behind them Somasca near Lecco: a stone hamlet and a small church on a steep wooded hillside, a rocky crag above and the lake of the Adda below in soft evening light. Keep the boy and the landscape inside the arched window.
face: A Venetian man of about fifty, worn thin by famine and plague, with a LONG OVAL face — a high, domed forehead going bald, dark-brown hair thinning over the crown and falling a little unkempt at the sides behind the ears; a long, straight, rather prominent nose; large, dark, luminous eyes lifted upward under dark brows that slope down at the outer ends, giving a look of compassion; lean cheeks; a full, soft, dark-brown beard of medium length, rounded at the chin and threaded with grey, and a full moustache; the lips a little parted as in prayer.

subject: A missionary archbishop of the ninth century, half-length, in the black Benedictine cowl with a plain narrow white wool pallium marked with small dark crosses over his shoulders; NO mitre, bare-headed. A plain wooden crozier with a simple curled head rests in his left hand; on his right forearm he carries a small model of a wooden church with a steep shingled roof. Behind him Birka on Lake Mälaren in Sweden: a Viking trading town of timber houses with turf roofs on a green island shore, two dragon-prowed longships drawn up on the beach, birch woods and grey-blue water under a pale northern sky. Keep the town and the ships inside the arched window.
face: A spare, weathered Frank of about sixty, clean-shaven, with a BROAD, SQUARE-BROWED face narrowing only a little to a wide, strongly CLEFT chin — a straight, flat brow line, small, deep-set, very pale grey-blue eyes crinkled against the northern wind, a short, straight nose with a broad bridge, lean cheeks with long vertical creases, a wide, straight, thin-lipped mouth; short, straight flaxen hair gone silver, cut in a straight Carolingian fringe around the shaven monastic crown; wind-reddened cheeks; a calm, far-seeing gaze a little to one side.

subject: A young French Marist missionary priest of 1841, half-length, in a plain black soutane with a black clerical cravat and a black cloak over his shoulders; he holds a small brass missionary crucifix against his chest with both hands, a green palm branch resting in the crook of his arm. Behind him the island of Futuna in the South Pacific: steep green volcanic hills, tall coconut palms, a thatched Polynesian fale with a low roof, and a turquoise lagoon edged by white surf on the reef under a bright tropical sky. Peaceful and sunny: no weapons, no attackers, no violence. Keep the palms and the lagoon inside the arched window.
face: A gentle Frenchman of about thirty-seven, clean-shaven, with a SOFT, SQUARE-JAWED face and full cheeks — a broad, smooth forehead, a straight, rather strong nose with a rounded tip, large, heavy-lidded dark-brown eyes under softly arched dark brows, a full, kindly mouth and a small dimple in the rounded chin; thick dark-brown hair parted on one side, a soft wave falling across the forehead and the hair covering the tops of the ears; a mild, patient gaze toward the viewer.

subject: A Spanish secular priest of the 1560s, half-length, in a plain black cassock and a long black manteo (priest's cloak) with a narrow white collar at the neck, as in the portrait attributed to El Greco; his right hand laid flat on his breast, his left holding a small, closed, well-worn book against his side. Behind him Montilla in the Andalusian countryside: a whitewashed hill town with tiled roofs and a church tower, a ruined castle on the height, and rolling vineyards and olive groves under a warm evening sky. Keep the town inside the arched window.
face: A spare Castilian priest of about seventy with a LONG, gaunt face, narrow at the jaw — a broad forehead with short, cropped grey hair brushed forward in a thin fringe and receding at the temples, high cheekbones over hollow cheeks, a long, straight nose slightly full at the tip, large, dark, heavy-lidded eyes turned a little down at the outer corners, gentle and grave, under arched grey brows raised toward the middle, a small, thin-lipped mouth; a short, close-clipped grey beard and moustache that only follow the line of the jaw; a gaze of quiet compassion toward the viewer.

subject: A late-Roman bishop of about 420, half-length, with NO mitre: a white tunic, an ample, bell-shaped deep-purple paenula (early chasuble) and a white stole; in his right hand a small bronze hand-bell, over his left wrist a length of broken iron chain, sign of the legend that he gave himself as a slave to ransom a widow's son. Behind him Cimitile by Nola in Campania: the basilica of St Felix with colonnaded porticoes and a fountain in the courtyard, cypresses and orchards, and the cone of Vesuvius in blue haze. Keep the basilica and the mountain inside the arched window.
face: A Gallo-Roman aristocrat and poet of about seventy, clean-shaven in the late-Roman manner, with a FINE-BONED, HEART-SHAPED face — a wide forehead and temples tapering to a small, delicate, rounded chin; a well-shaped, high-bridged patrician nose; large, mild, light hazel eyes with fine crow's-feet under thin, gracefully arched silver brows; a gentle, full-lipped mouth set in a slight, warm smile; short, thick white hair combed forward in a straight Roman fringe; a courteous, tender gaze.

subject: An eleventh-century pope, half-length, as in the Exultet roll made in his lifetime: a tall, CONICAL white tiara ringed at the base with a gold band, a red chasuble over a white alb, a white pallium with dark crosses falling down the front; his right hand raised in blessing, his left holding a closed book of the Gospels. Behind him Canossa in winter: the castle on its steep white rock in the snowy Apennine foothills, bare trees, a pale winter sky. No other figures. Keep the castle and the rock inside the arched window.
face: A small, spare Tuscan of about sixty-five with an olive, sun-darkened complexion and a SHORT, COMPACT face — broad across the brow and cheekbones and short from brow to chin, ending in a firm, slightly jutting small chin; a short, strongly arched, beak-like nose; small, black, intensely bright and piercing eyes under straight, dark, bristling brows drawn a little together; a thin, tight-set, determined mouth; a very short, close-trimmed iron-grey beard and moustache; a little iron-grey hair showing under the tiara; a keen, unflinching gaze.

subject: Two Roman soldiers turned martyrs, side by side, half-length, bareheaded, in the red wool military tunic and a dark-red soldier's cloak pinned at the shoulder, leather belts. They have laid their arms down: Nereus (left) lowers a round shield, turned away, its rim at the bottom edge of the window; Achilleus (right) has let his sword-belt hang loose and holds the sheathed sword downward, point to the ground, in a gesture of giving it up. Each holds a green palm branch in the other hand. Behind them the Via Ardeatina outside Rome: umbrella pines and dark cypresses, the green Campagna, a low brick doorway leading down into the catacomb of Domitilla, and far off the walls of Rome. No wounds, no blood. Keep both figures inside the arched window.
face: Two clearly different men. Nereus (left, the elder): a man of about forty-five with a BLOCKY, FLAT-TOPPED head and a strong, wide face — a heavy, straight brow ridge, deep-set steady dark eyes, a thick, strong nose with a slight bend at the bridge, broad cheekbones and a wide, square jaw with a wide, firm mouth; short, soldier-cropped black hair greying at the temples and a close, dark stubble beard; a sober, resolute look. Achilleus (right, the younger): a slender man of about twenty-eight, clean-shaven, with a LONG face and HIGH, ROUNDED cheekbones over a squared-off chin — a thin, straight nose, large bright light-brown eyes under fine, arched brows, a small, well-cut mouth; short, light-brown hair in tight curls; his gaze lifted a little, hopeful.

subject: The first Christians of Rome under Nero, AD 64, as a modest group: THREE figures in front side by side, half-length, and behind them, smaller and softer, a few more faithful men and women. In front, left to right: a grey-haired freedman in a plain undyed wool tunic and brown cloak; a young matron in a long blue-grey stola with a white palla drawn over her hair; a youth in a short belted tunic of a household servant. Each holds a green palm branch; the matron also holds a small clay oil lamp, the elder a small plain wooden cross. Behind them the Vatican plain across the Tiber: Nero's gardens with umbrella pines, the long arena of the Circus with its tall Egyptian obelisk, and beyond the river the hills of Rome, a thin haze of smoke over the city after the Great Fire, under a calm dusk sky. No wounds, no flames, no crosses of execution, no beasts, no gore. Keep all figures inside the arched window.
face: Three clearly different people. The freedman (left): a Syrian-born man of about fifty-five with an olive complexion and a LONG, BONY face — a high, lined forehead, a long nose with a gentle hook, heavy-lidded dark eyes, a wide, thin mouth; short grey hair and a short, neat grey beard; a quiet, steadfast look. The matron (centre): a Roman woman of about thirty with a WIDE-CHEEKED, softly SQUARE face — a straight nose, large, dark, calm eyes under strong dark brows, full lips, dark-brown hair parted in the middle under the palla; a serene, brave look lifted a little. The youth (right): a Greek boy of about sixteen, clean-shaven, with a ROUND face and rounded cheeks — a short, straight nose, bright black eyes under round brows, black hair in short tight curls; a trusting look toward the others.

subject: A Roman monk and missionary bishop of 597, half-length, in the black Benedictine habit and cowl, over it a narrow white pallium with dark crosses; in his right hand the tall silver processional cross he carried as his banner, in his left, held against his chest, a small painted wooden panel of Christ the Saviour (an image only, no lettering). Behind him the Isle of Thanet in Kent: a wide sandy shore, white chalk cliffs, the grey-green Channel with a small Roman sailing ship at anchor, and green downs under a soft, cloudy English sky. Keep the cross and the ship inside the arched window.
face: A tall Roman monk of about fifty-five with a SLENDER, finely boned LONG face and gently hollowed cheeks — a smooth, high forehead, a narrow, high-bridged nose, large, grave dark-brown eyes with dark lashes under long, level dark brows, a small, firm mouth; dark hair streaked with grey in a monastic crown around the tonsure; a SHORT, SQUARE-CUT dark beard streaked with grey, trimmed straight across at the bottom; a calm, resolute gaze toward the horizon.

subject: Two Roman clerics of the Diocletian persecution side by side, half-length. Marcellinus (left), the priest: a white tunic and an ample dark-gold paenula (early chasuble), holding a plain silver chalice before his chest. Peter (right), the exorcist: a simple white tunic and a grey-brown cloak, holding a small closed book (the book of exorcisms) against his chest. Each holds a green palm branch. Behind them the Via Labicana outside Rome at the third milestone: two tall laurel trees side by side, a thicket of dark woodland, the green Campagna and a line of aqueduct arches under a clear sky. No wounds, no grave, no executioner. Keep both figures inside the arched window.
face: Two clearly different men. Marcellinus (left, the priest): about fifty-five, a WIDE, LOW-BROWED face with broad, flat cheekbones and a rounded chin — a short, straight nose, small, warm, deep-set brown eyes with laughter lines, thick grey-flecked brows, a kindly mouth; grey-brown hair in a tonsure crown and a short, curly pepper-and-salt beard; a fatherly, calm look. Peter (right, the exorcist): about thirty, a NARROW, fine-boned face tapering to a pointed chin — a thin nose with a slight hook, large, dark, intense eyes under strong, straight black brows, a firm, closed mouth; short-cropped black hair and a short, sparse black beard along the jaw (short hair, not a Christ-like figure); an earnest, watchful gaze.

subject: A pope of the early sixth century, half-length, in the dress of his time and NO tiara: a long white tunic, over it an ample, bell-shaped dark-red paenula (early chasuble) and a narrow white woollen pallium marked with small dark crosses; he holds a jewelled book of the Gospels closed against his chest with both hands. Beside him on one side a small stone window with iron bars, sign of the prison where he died. Behind him Ravenna: red-brick basilicas with long arcaded walls, the round, domed stone Mausoleum of Theodoric among cypresses, the flat marshy plain under a pale sky. No chains on him, no suffering shown. Keep the window and the city inside the arched window.
face: A Tuscan of about sixty-five, worn thin by the long journey and the prison, with a ROUNDED-TRIANGULAR face — a broad, low forehead and wide, flat temples tapering past softly drawn cheeks to a short, narrow chin; a straight nose with a wide, flat bridge; round, gentle, pale-brown eyes that droop a little at the outer corners, under thin grey brows raised in patient sorrow; a small, soft mouth; grey hair cut in a round Roman tonsure fringe and a short, neat grey beard trimmed to a small point; a meek, steady gaze.

subject: An aged hermit-abbot of the early eleventh century, half-length, in the ample WHITE Camaldolese habit with its white hood lying on the shoulders, leaning on a plain wooden staff held in his right hand, his left hand open at his breast. Behind him Camaldoli in the Casentino: small stone hermit cells with little gardens among tall, dark silver firs on a mountainside, and above the trees, faint in the sky, the ladder of his vision rising to heaven with small white-robed monks climbing it. Keep the ladder and the cells inside the arched window.
face: A very old but vigorous hermit of about seventy-five with a LONG face under a massive, high BALD dome — a broad, strongly furrowed forehead, grey-white brows KNIT DOWNWARD over deep-set, penetrating grey eyes with a searching, severe intensity, a long, strong, slightly hooked nose, sunken cheeks under the beard, a firm mouth half-hidden; a thin fringe of white hair low at the back of the head; a long, wavy, white beard falling in separate strands to mid-chest; the gaze fixed and searching, not gentle.

subject: Two men of the Roman Church, exiled together in 235 to the mines of Sardinia and reconciled there, half-length, SIDE BY SIDE. Left: Pontian, the pope, in a plain long white tunic and a coarse undyed brown cloak of the exile over it, and over that a narrow white pallium with small dark crosses as his only mark of office; he holds a small plain wooden cross. Right: Hippolytus, the priest and learned writer, in a white tunic and a grey-blue Greek philosopher's pallium (cloak) wrapped over one shoulder, holding a rolled scroll; his other hand rests gently on Pontian's shoulder in sign of reconciliation. Behind them the rugged, dry hills of south-west Sardinia with dark mine openings cut into the rock, ochre spoil heaps, scrub and a few wild olives, and beyond them the blue Mediterranean under a hazy sky. No chains, no tools of torment, no guards, no gore. Keep both figures inside the arched window.
face: Two clearly different men. Pontian (left, the pope): a Roman of about fifty with a ROUND, compact face and smooth, full cheeks — a low, rounded forehead, a short, broad, slightly upturned nose, round, warm brown eyes under soft, rounded brows, a small, gentle mouth, a round chin; close-cropped dark-brown hair greying at the temples and a short, neat, rounded dark beard; a humble, patient look. Hippolytus (right, the priest and scholar, older): a man of about sixty-five with a LONG, LEAN, HOLLOW-CHEEKED face and a high, bald crown — a tall, furrowed forehead, a long, thin, arched nose, narrow, heavy-lidded grey eyes under bushy, slanting grey brows, a thin-lipped mouth; long grey hair falling from the sides of the bald head to the nape; a long, flowing grey beard parted slightly at the chin, like an ancient philosopher; a thoughtful, searching gaze turned toward Pontian.

subject: A priest of Lucca around 1600, once a pharmacist, half-length, in a plain black cassock and a black mantle with a small white collar, his eyes raised to a small vision of Our Lady with the Child in a soft golden cloud in the upper corner (he founded the Clerks Regular of the Mother of God); he holds an open book of the Gospels against his chest, and on a ledge beside him stand a small bronze apothecary's mortar and pestle and a white-and-blue majolica jar, signs of his first trade. Behind him Lucca: its broad tree-lined walls, red roofs, the Guinigi tower with holm oaks growing on its top and the white marble front of San Michele in Foro, with the green Tuscan hills beyond under a clear sky. Keep the vision and the town inside the arched window.
face: A Tuscan of about sixty-five with a warm, ruddy complexion and a BROAD, full, RECTANGULAR face — a high, broad, bald forehead with short grey hair left at the sides and a small tuft above, wide, rounded cheekbones, a short, broad, straight nose with a wide tip, round dark-brown eyes turned upward under thick, straight grey brows, a wide mouth with full lips; a short, thick grey moustache and a short, full grey beard trimmed ROUND along the broad jaw; an upturned, trusting, devout gaze.

subject: A seventeenth-century Norman priest, half-length, as in his old portrait: a black cassock and a black cloak, a wide, flat white collar (rabat) lying over the cassock, a black skullcap on the back of the head; in his right hand he holds up a red heart crowned with small flames and a small cross (the Heart of Jesus and Mary he preached), and in his left a small wooden crucifix. Behind him Caen in Normandy: the pale stone Abbaye aux Hommes with its two tall spires, slate roofs and a green Norman orchard under a soft grey-blue sky. No lettering on the heart. Keep the heart and the town inside the arched window.
face: A Norman priest of about sixty-five with a fair, lightly ruddy complexion and a LONG, POINTED-OVAL face under a LARGE, SMOOTH BALD DOME — a high, rounded forehead, a narrow fringe of short grey hair above the ears, a long, straight nose with a gently rounded tip, heavy-lidded, half-lowered pale-grey eyes under thin, raised, arched grey brows, marked folds from the nose to the corners of the mouth, a thin mouth with a faint, knowing, kindly smile; a small grey moustache and a short, narrow grey GOATEE on the chin, the cheeks shaven; a shrewd, warm, faintly amused look toward the viewer.

subject: An old Aragonese priest in Rome, half-length, in the black habit and short black cape of the Piarists (Clerks Regular of the Pious Schools) with a narrow white collar and a black four-cornered biretta; his right hand is laid open on his breast as in the Prado portrait, his left rests on the shoulder of a small boy in a plain brown smock who holds a slate and a primer; a second small boy beside them holds a book. Behind them Rome near Piazza Navona: the ochre front of the little church of San Pantaleo with its school, Roman palaces and a dome against a warm late-afternoon sky. No readable writing on slate or book. Keep the children inside the arched window.
face: A spare Aragonese of about eighty-five, old but alert, with a pale complexion and a LONG face, broad at the temples and narrowing to the jaw — a high, bald forehead under the biretta, prominent cheekbones over softly hollowed cheeks, a long, strong, slightly hooked nose, large, bright, gentle grey-brown eyes under thin, high-arched white brows raised in the middle, deep smile lines at the eyes, a thin mouth parted in a faint, kind smile; a SHORT, neatly trimmed white beard and moustache close to the jaw; a warm, fatherly look. Not the stock white-bearded elder: the beard is short and trimmed, the face long and bright-eyed.

subject: Three Chinese martyrs of the Qing dynasty, half-length, SIDE BY SIDE, each holding a green palm branch, in authentic Qing-era Chinese dress (no Western clothes). Centre: Augustine Zhao Rong, the first Chinese diocesan priest (d. 1815), in a long dark-blue Chinese scholar's robe (changshan) with a high round collar and wide sleeves, a small black round cap, holding a small wooden cross and a string of rosary beads. Left: Lucy Yi Zhenmei, lay catechist of Guizhou (d. 1862), in a long, high-collared indigo cotton jacket fastened at the side with cloth knots over a dark skirt, her hair drawn back into a neat low bun, holding a small book of catechism against her breast. Right: Chi Zhuzi, a catechumen of eighteen (d. 1900), in a plain faded-blue cotton jacket with cloth-knot buttons, his forehead shaved and his long black hair in a single braided queue over his shoulder, his free hand laid on his breast.
