Behind them the green terraced hills and misty limestone peaks of south-west China (Guizhou and Sichuan), a small village with grey-tiled upturned roofs and a modest whitewashed chapel with a plain cross. No wounds, no chains, no executioners, no gore. Keep all three figures inside the arched window.
face: Three clearly different Chinese people, authentically East Asian (Han Chinese), none Westernised. Augustine Zhao Rong (centre): a former soldier of about sixty-nine with a weathered, warm-brown complexion and a BROAD, SQUARE face with a strong, wide jaw — a broad, flat forehead (the front of the head shaved in the Qing manner, grey hair drawn back into a queue), wide, flat cheekbones, a broad, low-bridged nose, narrow, deep-lidded dark eyes with calm crow's-feet, thin straight grey brows, a wide, firm mouth; a thin, drooping grey moustache and a short, sparse grey chin beard; a steady, grave, fatherly gaze. Lucy Yi Zhenmei (left): a woman of about forty-five with a pale golden complexion and a SMOOTH OVAL face with a gently rounded chin — a high, smooth forehead, fine, arched black brows, calm, almond-shaped dark eyes with single eyelids, a small, straight nose, a small, composed mouth; black hair parted in the middle and smoothed back into a low bun; a serene, gentle look lowered a little. Chi Zhuzi (right): a lean youth of eighteen, clean-shaven, with a golden-tan complexion and a NARROW, angular face — high cheekbones, a narrow, pointed chin, a slim, straight nose with a low bridge, bright, narrow dark eyes with single eyelids under straight black brows, a firm young mouth; shaved forehead and a long black queue; an eager, fearless look lifted upward.

subject: A young Lombard priest of 1539, half-length, in the plain black cassock of the Barnabites with its high, close collar and a narrow white edge of collar showing, turned a little to the right in three-quarter view; he holds a wooden crucifix upright in his right hand and a small white lily lies against his left arm; beside him, on a small draped altar, a gold monstrance with the Host in a soft glow, for the Forty Hours' adoration he spread. Behind him Cremona, his birthplace and the town where he died: the brick cathedral with its marble front and the very tall brick bell tower of the Torrazzo over red roofs, and the flat green Po plain under a clear evening sky. Keep the altar and the town inside the arched window.
face: A pale, slender Lombard of about thirty-six with a LONG OVAL face in three-quarter view — a high forehead with the dark hair already receding at the temples, a long, straight, prominent nose with a slightly lowered tip, deep-set dark-brown eyes under straight dark brows drawn a little together, flat cheeks over a strong cheekbone, a firm, closed mouth; short dark-brown hair lying close to the head and behind the ear; a full dark-brown moustache and a dense dark-brown beard trimmed close on the cheeks and ending in a short, squared POINT below the chin; an intent, far-seeing gaze lifted to the right. Not a young long-haired Christ type: the hair is short and receding.

subject: The first bishop of Ravenna, half-length, as in the sixth-century apse mosaic of Sant'Apollinare in Classe: a long white tunic with dark stripes at the cuffs, over it a gold-green paenula (early chasuble) woven with small gold leaves, and a narrow white pallium with a small black cross; both hands raised open at shoulder height in the ancient orans gesture of prayer. Beside him two white lambs among white lilies and small green shrubs, as in the mosaic. Behind him Classe near Ravenna: the brick basilica of Sant'Apollinare in Classe with its tall round bell tower, the umbrella pines of the Pineta, the flat green plain toward the Adriatic, under a pale gold sky. No wounds, no martyrdom shown. Keep the lambs and the basilica inside the arched window.
face: A Syrian-born bishop of about sixty with a warm olive complexion and a SHORT, WIDE-CHEEKED face under a FLAT, SQUARE forehead — broad, rounded cheekbones set high, a long, straight, narrow nose running down from a low bridge, large, round, wide-open dark eyes under level dark-grey brows, a small, closed mouth; thick, short white hair combed forward in a straight, even fringe low on the forehead, as in the mosaic; a short white beard and moustache narrowing to a neat POINT at the chin; a calm, wide-eyed, frontal gaze.

subject: The Ottonian emperor Henry II (d. 1024), half-length, in the dress of the Regensburg Sacramentary: a long golden-yellow tunic edged with jewelled bands, a deep-blue imperial mantle clasped on the right shoulder, and a gold, jewel-set eight-plated crown with a small arch and cross; in his left arm a small model of Bamberg Cathedral with its towers (the church he founded), in his right hand a slender gold sceptre topped with a lily. Behind him Bamberg on its hills above the river Regnitz: the four-towered cathedral on the cathedral hill, the Michaelsberg abbey on the next hill, green Franconian slopes and a summer sky. No sword drawn, no battle. Keep the model and the town inside the arched window.
face: A German prince of about forty-five with a fair, ruddy complexion and a SHORT, BROAD, HEART-SHAPED face — a wide, rounded forehead and full, wide cheeks tapering to a small, rounded chin under the beard; a short, straight nose with a rounded tip; wide-set, light hazel eyes under gently arched light-brown brows; a small, full mouth; chestnut-brown hair cut level at the ears in the Ottonian manner beneath the crown; a short, rounded chestnut beard and moustache trimmed close to the jaw; a mild, earnest, devout look. Not the stock thirties man with curls: straight, level-cut hair and a heart-shaped face.

subject: An Irish monk-missionary of about 615, half-length, in a coarse undyed cream-white woollen cowl with a deep hood lying on the shoulders, a leather cord at the waist; a tooled leather book satchel hangs from a strap across his chest and he holds a book of the Gospels in his left hand, a tall ash-wood staff in his right. Beside him a brown bear sits quietly, tamed, as in his legend. Behind him Bobbio in the Apennines: the valley of the Trebbia with its long humpbacked stone bridge, the stone abbey church and wooded hills under a cool sky. No wolves attacking, no violence. Keep the bear inside the arched window.
face: A weathered Irishman of about seventy, lean and strong, with a fair, windburnt, freckled complexion and a LONG, BIG-BONED face with a strong, JUTTING CHIN — the front of the head shaved from ear to ear in the Irish tonsure, leaving a high, bare, sun-browned forehead, and long red hair gone mostly grey falling from behind the ears to the shoulders; deep-set, pale-blue eyes under bristling reddish-grey brows, crinkled at the corners as against the sea wind; a long, straight, bony nose; wide, flat cheeks; a wide, firm mouth; a short, grizzled red-grey beard close to the jaw; a fearless, far-looking, zealous gaze.

subject: A fourth-century bishop, half-length, in the dress of his time: a long white tunic, an ample dark-crimson paenula (early chasuble) and a narrow white pallium with small dark crosses; no mitre. He holds against his chest a thick open codex of the Gospels in Latin with purple-stained pages and silver lettering-like lines too small to read (the Codex Vercellensis, traditionally written by him), and a plain wooden pastoral staff with a curved top. Behind him Vercelli on the flat Piedmont plain, its early brick basilica and bell tower among poplars, and far off the white snowy wall of the Alps with Monte Rosa under a clear sky. No chains, no persecutors. No readable text. Keep the book and the town inside the arched window.
face: A Sardinian of about sixty-five with a dark, sun-browned Mediterranean complexion and an OBLONG face under a HEAVY, PROMINENT BROW RIDGE — a straight, low forehead with two deep horizontal lines, deep-set, intense black eyes under thick, straight, dark-grey brows, a strong nose with a broad bridge and a rounded tip, lean cheeks with deep lines from nose to mouth, a wide, firm mouth; short, dense, tightly CURLED grey-black hair; a thick, short, dense iron-grey beard cut SQUARE at the jaw line; a resolute, unflinching gaze straight ahead.

subject: A procession of relics in the Romanesque nave of the Basilica of St. Servatius in Maastricht, as in its Heiligdomsvaart: at the centre, carried shoulder-high on poles under a gold-fringed canopy by four bearers in white surplices over dark cassocks, the great gilded house-shaped reliquary chest of St. Servatius (the Noodkist), with little gilded figures of apostles under arches, enamel bands and rock crystals shining; before it a server swings a smoking censer and two servers carry tall lit candles; behind, a priest in a gold cope walks with joined hands. Round Romanesque arches, pale stone columns and candlelight fill the background. Figures small to half-length and serene, the shrine the focus. No lettering. Keep the procession inside the arched window.
face: The bearers and servers are secondary and differ: the front bearer, about thirty, with a long face and short dark hair in profile; the bearer beside him, about fifty, with a broad ruddy face and grey temples; a fair, round-faced boy server of about twelve with the censer; the priest in the gold cope, about sixty-five, clean-shaven with a lean, narrow face and white hair, eyes lowered.

subject: The miraculous image of Nossa Senhora da Conceição Aparecida exactly as venerated in her basilica: a SMALL terracotta statue of the Immaculate Conception with a dark cinnamon-brown face and dark joined hands, clearly a statue and not a living woman, wrapped in her stiff, triangular royal-blue mantle embroidered with gold and edged in gold, which falls from the shoulders to the base, and wearing a jewelled imperial gold crown; no flags, no ribbons with writing. The little image stands radiant in a soft golden glow just above a wooden dugout canoe on the broad, calm Paraíba do Sul river at dawn, the dripping fishing net draped below her and heavy with silver fish. In the canoe, small and half-length, the three fishermen of 1717 kneel and look up at her in awe. Behind them green river banks of Atlantic forest, palms and the blue ridge of the Serra da Mantiqueira under a pink sunrise. Keep the canoe, the net and the river inside the arched window.
face: The image: the statue's own small, dark cinnamon-brown terracotta face — a round, gentle girl's face with lowered eyes and the hint of a smile, framed by the crown and mantle, hands joined at the breast. The fishermen, colonial caboclos of the Paraíba valley with warm brown skin, in coarse white cotton shirts and rolled trousers: Domingos Garcia (left), about fifty, a broad, SQUARE face with heavy cheekbones, a flat wide nose, deep-set eyes and grey stubble, under a frayed straw hat held to his chest; João Alves (centre), about twenty-five, a lean, LONG face with a narrow jaw, straight black hair and a thin black moustache, holding the net; Filipe Pedroso (right), about forty, a full ROUND face with a short black beard and bright dark eyes, hands raised in wonder.

subject: St. John the Baptist in the dungeon of Machaerus on the night before his death, half-length, seated on a stone ledge in his camel-hair garment and a faded red mantle, his wrists loosely chained; he holds his slender reed cross against his shoulder and lifts his face in prayer toward a shaft of moonlight falling through a small barred window high in the rock wall. Through the bars, the moonlit Dead Sea and the hills of Judaea far below the fortress. In the dark doorway at the right, only the long shadow of a guard and the faint gleam of a sword hilt: his death is implied, never shown. No blood, no charger, no head. Keep the cell inside the arched window.
face: John as on the john_baptist card, made ascetic by prison: a lean man of about thirty with a LONG face — high cheekbones over hollowed cheeks, a straight nose, large dark-brown eyes under straight dark brows, a firm mouth; thick, unkempt curly dark-brown hair to the shoulders and a rough, short dark-brown beard; the gaze lifted to the light, steadfast and at peace. Not a Christ type: wild hair, weathered skin, wilderness gauntness.

subject: An aged Roman bishop of the 380s, half-length, turned a little to the left in three-quarter view, in the dress of his own century and NOT a later papal tiara: a long white tunic, a deep red bell-shaped paenula (chasuble) falling in soft folds, and over it a narrow white woollen pallium marked with small dark crosses hanging down the front; on his head a low, rounded white cap. He holds a thick bound codex of the Scriptures against his breast in his left hand and raises his right hand in a gentle blessing. Behind him the catacomb of San Callisto on the Via Appia, which he adorned for the martyrs: a tufa gallery lit by small clay oil lamps, rows of closed wall-tombs, and the arched opening of the crypt of the popes with two slender marble columns; any marble slab is plain, with no carving. Through an opening at the right, a glimpse of the Appian Way with umbrella pines and cypresses in evening light. Keep the gallery inside the arched window.
face: A Roman of Spanish stock, about seventy-five, with a broad-browed, RECTANGULAR face — a wide, flat forehead, a long straight nose with a broad bridge, large, wide-set dark eyes under level, heavy grey brows, flat broad cheekbones, a strong, square jaw and a firm, straight mouth; short grey hair showing under the cap at the temples; a short, ROUNDED grey-and-white beard trimmed close to the jaw, with a grey moustache; a calm, watchful gaze looking out a little to the side. Not a flowing white-bearded patriarch: the beard is short and round.

subject: The Child Jesus in glory, adored in heaven and on earth, after the manner of Gaulli's Triumph of the Name of Jesus but without its letters: the Child, about three years old, stands on a bank of clouds in the upper centre within a great golden sunburst of rays that holds NO letters or monogram, wearing a simple white tunic, his right hand raised in blessing and his left holding a small gold globe with a cross. Below him, on either side, two kneeling angels in rose and green robes bow with hands crossed on their breasts; lower still, small and serene, the faithful of every age kneel on a green hillside above Bethlehem, looking up. Keep the clouds, angels and people inside the arched window; no text anywhere.
face: The Christ Child as in recurring-figures.md: a plump, ROUND child's face with full rosy cheeks, a high rounded forehead, a small button nose, large clear brown eyes, a small rosy mouth, soft short golden-brown curls, a plain gold halo, now a child of about three with a steady, gentle gaze looking out at the viewer. The angels: youthful, one with a heart-shaped face and short golden curls, the other with a narrower face and dark-brown wavy hair.

subject: The naming of Jesus on the eighth day (Luke 2:21), with nothing of the rite itself shown: in the lamplit room of a simple stone house in Bethlehem, Our Lady sits holding the Infant wrapped in white linen on her lap; an elderly village elder in a white robe with a blue-striped prayer shawl over his head stands beside her and raises his right hand over the Child as he names him; St. Joseph stands behind Mary, bowing his head, a hand on his breast. On a low wooden table a small silver bowl, a folded white cloth and a lit clay lamp; no knife, no instrument. Through an open window, the terraced hills of Bethlehem at dusk with the first star. Half-length figures close together; keep them inside the arched window.
face: Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md: a young woman of about eighteen with a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, lids lowered in a recollected gaze, softly rounded cheeks, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre under a white inner veil and a blue mantle drawn over the head. The Christ Child as in recurring-figures.md: a plump, ROUND baby face with full rosy cheeks, a high rounded forehead, a small button nose, large clear brown eyes, a small rosy mouth, soft short golden-brown curls, a plain gold halo, a newborn eight days old, eyes open and calm. St. Joseph as in recurring-figures.md: a man of about forty with a LONG OVAL face — a straight nose, gentle dark-brown eyes under level brows, a quiet mouth; full dark-brown curly hair to the nape and a short full dark-brown beard; green tunic and ochre-brown mantle. The elder: about sixty-five, a broad, ROUND face with full cheeks and a short, rounded grey beard, a short wide nose, kind crinkled dark eyes under bushy grey brows — clearly not Simeon's long face.

subject: The Presentation in the Temple (Luke 2:22-38), figures half-length and close: at the centre the aged Simeon holds the Infant Jesus in his arms, his hands veiled in a fold of his white mantle, and lifts his eyes to heaven as he sings his canticle; at the left Our Lady, her hands still open toward her Son, and St. Joseph behind her holding a small wicker basket with two white turtledoves; at the right the prophetess Anna, very old, in a dark-blue veil, raising one hand toward the Child and holding a closed scroll. Behind them the Temple of Jerusalem: Herodian colonnades of pale stone, bronze doors, a golden seven-branched lampstand and the rising smoke of incense in warm light. No lettering. Keep all five figures inside the arched window.
face: Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md: a young woman of about eighteen with a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, lids lowered in a recollected gaze, softly rounded cheeks, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre under a white inner veil and a blue mantle drawn over the head. The Christ Child as in recurring-figures.md: a plump, ROUND baby face with full rosy cheeks, a high rounded forehead, a small button nose, large clear brown eyes, a small rosy mouth, soft short golden-brown curls, a plain gold halo, about forty days old, eyes open, one small hand reaching up to Simeon's beard. St. Joseph as in recurring-figures.md: a man of about forty with a LONG OVAL face — a straight nose, gentle dark-brown eyes under level brows, a quiet mouth; full dark-brown curly hair to the nape and a short full dark-brown beard; green tunic and ochre-brown mantle. Simeon: a very old man of about eighty-five with a LONG, NARROW face — a high, lined forehead, a slightly hooked nose, deep-set eyes wet with joy under white brows, hollow cheeks over high cheekbones; a long, soft white beard that divides into two locks, and white hair falling to the shoulders, uncovered. Anna: a woman of about eighty-four with a small, HEART-SHAPED face tapering to a pointed chin — a fine thin nose, bright dark eyes deep in soft wrinkles, a small smiling mouth; grey hair hidden under her dark veil.

subject: An old Polish priest and master of the Kraków Academy in the 1460s, half-length, turned a little to the right in three-quarter view, bareheaded, in a black academic doctor's gown with wide sleeves and a deep red lining, a white collar at the neck; his black biretta rests on a closed book in the crook of his left arm. With his right hand he lays his own dark wool cloak over the shoulders of a thin, barefoot young student standing small at the lower right, as the story of his charity tells. Behind them the arcaded Gothic courtyard of the Collegium Maius in Kraków — red brick, pale stone arcades, a steep tiled roof — under a light fall of snow on a winter evening, a warm light in the windows. Keep the student and the courtyard inside the arched window.
face: John: an old Pole of about seventy-five with a LONG, NARROW, sculpted face — a very high bald forehead and crown ringed by a short wreath of grey-white hair, prominent high cheekbones, a straight nose, heavy-lidded, half-closed gentle grey eyes, a ruddy complexion, full prominent lips, and a short, close grey beard following the line of the jaw; a kindly, downcast look toward the student. The student: a pale, thin Polish lad of about seventeen with a narrow face, straw-fair hair cut straight across the brow, and wide grateful blue eyes.

subject: Saul of Tarsus struck down on the road to Damascus, half-length and close: thrown to the ground on one knee and one hand, his head lifted, his right arm raised to shield his dazzled eyes from a great shaft of white-gold light that pours down from an opening in the clouds at the upper left; he wears a deep red tunic, a blue travelling cloak slipping from his shoulders and a sword at his belt, the persecutor's sword that becomes his emblem. Behind him his startled chestnut horse rears, and two small companions in plain tunics shrink back, seeing the light but no one. Beyond, the stony road runs toward the walled city of Damascus among green orchards, with snow-capped Mount Hermon on the horizon. Keep the horse and the companions inside the arched window.
face: Paul as on the paul card, a little younger (about forty-five): a noble, kindly LONG face — a high domed forehead, bald on top with a receding hairline and dark wavy hair at the sides, a straight fine nose, calm luminous dark eyes now wide with awe, a long dark pointed beard reaching well below the chin. The companions: small, one a young man with a round face and short black hair, the other older with a grey short beard, both faces half-turned away.

subject: St. Peter enthroned as teacher, seated frontally and half-length on an ancient wooden chair with a high back decorated with carved ivory panels, in his blue tunic and golden-ochre mantle as on the peter card; his right hand raised with two fingers extended in teaching, his left hand holding the two great keys, one gold and one silver, and an open codex resting on his knee. Behind and above him the apse of St. Peter's Basilica: the golden glory of rays and clouds around the round amber window of the Holy Spirit with the white dove, warm light falling on the chair; no lettering anywhere. Keep the chair and the glory inside the arched window.
face: Peter as on the peter card: an elderly man around sixty-five with a broad, weathered fisherman's face, a strong wide nose, deep-set earnest eyes and a lined forehead; curly grey-white hair balding from the back of the head with a curly tuft left at the forehead; a short, square, curly grey-white beard; a steady, teaching gaze straight out at the viewer.

subject: Our Lady half-length and close, holding the newborn Child in white swaddling bands upright against her shoulder, his cheek pressed to hers and one small hand at her neck, her hand cradling his back: the tender embrace of the Virgin of Tenderness (Eleousa), painted in the card's own style. Her eyes are lowered, pondering. She wears her blue mantle over the white veil and a rose-red gown. Behind them the rock-hewn stable of Bethlehem, a manger with straw and the dim head of an ox in the shadow at the left, and through the rough stone opening at the right the terraced hills of Bethlehem and a few sleeping sheep under the first pale gold light of a winter dawn, a single bright star fading in the sky. Keep the stable opening inside the arched window.
face: Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md: a young woman of about eighteen with a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, softly rounded cheeks, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre under a white inner veil and a blue mantle drawn over the head; her lids lowered, her cheek against the Child's. The Christ Child as in recurring-figures.md: a plump, ROUND baby face with full rosy cheeks, a high rounded forehead, a small button nose, large clear brown eyes, a small rosy mouth, soft short golden-brown curls, a plain gold halo; eight days old, eyes open and resting on his mother.

subject: Christ standing in the shallow Jordan, seen from the waist up, bare-shouldered and modest, the water about his waist, head gently bowed and hands joined at his breast. St. John the Baptist stands on the rocky bank at the right in his camel-hair tunic and red mantle, pouring water over Christ's head from a scallop shell, a slender reed cross in the crook of his other arm. At the left two small kneeling angels on the bank hold Christ's rose-red tunic and blue mantle ready. Above, the heavens open in a burst of gold between clouds and the white dove of the Holy Spirit descends in a shaft of light. Around them green reeds and tamarisks along the river, the bare hills of the Judaean wilderness beyond in soft morning light. Keep the dove, the angels and the bank inside the arched window.
face: Christ as in recurring-figures.md: a man of about thirty-three with a LONG OVAL face narrowing gently to the chin — a high, smooth forehead, a long straight nose with a fine bridge, calm almond-shaped dark-brown eyes under level brown brows, high, softly modelled cheekbones, a quiet closed mouth; chestnut-brown hair parted in the centre and falling in soft waves past the shoulders; a short, full chestnut beard and moustache, lightly parted at the chin; eyes lowered in humility. John as on the john_baptist card: a man of about thirty with a LONG face — high cheekbones, a straight nose, large dark-brown eyes under straight dark brows, a firm mouth; thick, unkempt curly dark-brown hair to the shoulders and a rough, short dark-brown beard, sunburnt wilderness skin; a reverent look. The two must stay clearly different: Christ's hair smooth, chestnut and centre-parted, John's dark, wild and curly. The angels: fair, childlike, one round-faced with golden curls, one with an oval face and light-brown hair.

subject: The Upper Room in Jerusalem on the morning of Pentecost: Our Lady seated at the centre, half-length, hands joined, eyes raised, with the Apostles gathered close around her, their mantles stirred by a rushing wind; above each head, Mary's included, a small, clear tongue of golden flame. Over her, the white dove of the Holy Spirit spreads its wings in a burst of golden light that fills the room. St. Peter at her right in his blue tunic and golden-ochre mantle, hands open; St. John at her left in his green tunic and red-orange mantle, hand on his heart; the other Apostles behind them in varied colours, some raising their hands, one bowing. A plain stone room with a round arch and a small window showing the flat roofs of Jerusalem in morning light. Keep the dove and all figures inside the arched window.
face: Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md: the same face matured, a woman of about fifty with a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, softly rounded cheeks, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre under a white inner veil and a blue mantle drawn over the head; eyes raised, radiant. Peter as on the peter card: about sixty-five, a broad, weathered fisherman's face, a strong wide nose, deep-set earnest eyes, a lined forehead; curly grey-white hair balding from the back with a curly tuft at the forehead; a short, square, curly grey-white beard. John as on the john_evangelist card: a beardless young man of about twenty-two with a smooth OVAL face, large upturned brown eyes, a straight nose, a small full mouth; wavy golden-brown hair to the jaw. The others behind, each different: a dark-bearded man of forty with a long face (James); a grey-bearded older man with a broad face and short hair (Andrew); a young man with short black hair and a narrow, beardless face (Thomas); a bald man of fifty with a round face and a short brown beard (Bartholomew).

subject: The Archbasilica of the Most Holy Saviour and St. John Lateran in Rome, its east façade by Alessandro Galilei seen from the piazza in warm late-afternoon light: a single giant order of paired Corinthian pilasters and half-columns in pale golden travertine, five tall arched openings of the portico below and the benediction loggia above, the central bay projecting under a triangular pediment, and along the balustrade the fifteen colossal white statues, the Saviour at the centre holding his cross, St. John the Baptist and St. John the Evangelist on either side, and the Doctors of the Church in their robes, mitres and hats beyond. The pediment and frieze are plain, with no inscription. The great bronze central doors stand open onto the candlelit gold of the nave. Small figures on the wide steps: a priest in a white surplice and violet stole greeting a family of pilgrims, two nuns, a boy with a candle. Clear sky with a few gold-edged clouds and swallows. Keep the whole façade inside the arched window.
face: The figures are small and secondary: the priest, about sixty, a lean, NARROW face, clean-shaven, silver hair, turned in three-quarter view; the pilgrim father, about thirty-five, a broad, ruddy face with a short brown beard; his wife with a round face under a light scarf; the boy, about ten, dark-haired, looking up at the statues. The statues are white stone, not living people.

subject: The risen Christ standing before the open rock-hewn tomb at sunrise, seen to the knees, radiant in a white robe and white mantle, a soft golden light around him; his right hand raised in blessing, his left holding the white banner of victory with a red cross on a slender gold cross-staff (no lettering); the wounds only small, clean marks on his hands. Behind him the round millstone rolled aside from the dark doorway of the tomb, and a young angel in white seated on the stone. At the lower right, small, two Roman soldiers asleep against the rock with their shields, faces turned away. A garden of white lilies and olive trees, and on the horizon the walls and towers of Jerusalem under a rose-gold dawn sky. Keep the tomb and the soldiers inside the arched window.
face: Christ as in recurring-figures.md: a man of about thirty-three with a LONG OVAL face narrowing gently to the chin — a high, smooth forehead, a long straight nose with a fine bridge, calm almond-shaped dark-brown eyes under level brown brows, high, softly modelled cheekbones, a quiet closed mouth; chestnut-brown hair parted in the centre and falling in soft waves past the shoulders; a short, full chestnut beard and moustache, lightly parted at the chin; in glory, a plain gold halo ringed with rays, a serene, victorious look straight out at the viewer. The angel: youthful, an OVAL face with a straight nose, fair skin and loose light-golden hair, looking toward Christ. The soldiers' faces are hidden.

subject: In the upper half, Christ rising on a bright cloud above the summit of the Mount of Olives, in a white robe and white-gold mantle, both hands raised in blessing, the wounds only small, clean marks on his palms, in a glory of gold light. In the lower half, gathered on the hilltop and looking up in wonder, half-length: Our Lady in the centre with hands joined, St. Peter at the left in his blue tunic and golden-ochre mantle, St. John at the right in his green tunic and red-orange mantle, and a few other Apostles behind them; two angels in white stand at the sides, one pointing upward. Olive trees around them, and far below the walls of Jerusalem and the Temple mount in clear afternoon light. Keep the cloud and all figures inside the arched window.
face: Christ as in recurring-figures.md: a man of about thirty-three with a LONG OVAL face narrowing gently to the chin — a high, smooth forehead, a long straight nose with a fine bridge, calm almond-shaped dark-brown eyes under level brown brows, high, softly modelled cheekbones, a quiet closed mouth; chestnut-brown hair parted in the centre and falling in soft waves past the shoulders; a short, full chestnut beard and moustache, lightly parted at the chin; in glory, a plain gold halo ringed with rays, a serene, loving look down on his disciples. Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md: the same face matured, a woman of about fifty with a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, softly rounded cheeks, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre under a white inner veil and a blue mantle drawn over the head. Peter as on the peter card: about sixty-five, a broad, weathered fisherman's face, a strong wide nose, deep-set earnest eyes, a lined forehead; curly grey-white hair balding from the back with a curly tuft at the forehead; a short, square, curly grey-white beard. John as on the john_evangelist card: a beardless young man of about twenty-two with a smooth OVAL face, large upturned brown eyes, a straight nose, a small full mouth; wavy golden-brown hair to the jaw. The other Apostles behind, small and different: a dark-bearded man of forty with a long face (James), a grey-bearded older man with a broad face (Andrew), a young man with short black hair and a narrow, beardless face (Thomas). The angels: youthful, fair, oval-faced.

subject: The great multitude of Revelation 7:9 before the throne and the Lamb, composed for the arched window as a golden heaven. At the top centre, in a round glory of gold light, the white Lamb of God standing on a small green mount from which four streams flow, with a plain gold halo and a small white banner bearing a red cross (no lettering). Around and below him, on tiers of soft white cloud that curve like an amphitheatre, the saints half-length and small, all in white robes or in their own dress, many holding green palm branches: nearest the Lamb, Our Lady in her blue mantle with hands joined; St. Peter with his keys and St. Paul with his sword; martyrs with palms; virgins with white lilies; a bishop in a white mitre; a king with a simple gold crown laid at his breast; a brown-habited friar; a mother and a young shepherd boy; men and women of Africa, Asia and the Americas in their own dress. Everyone's face turns toward the Lamb, joyful and at peace. At the very bottom, a thin band of green earth with a small village church under a clear morning sky. Keep every cloud and figure inside the arched window.
face: Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md: a young woman of about eighteen with a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, softly rounded cheeks, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre under a white inner veil and a blue mantle drawn over the head; she is nearest the Lamb, looking up. Peter as on the peter card: about sixty-five, a broad, weathered fisherman's face, a strong wide nose, deep-set earnest eyes, a lined forehead; curly grey-white hair balding from the back with a curly tuft at the forehead; a short, square, curly grey-white beard; Paul as on the paul card: about sixty, a noble LONG face — a high domed forehead, bald on top with dark wavy hair greying at the sides, a straight fine nose, calm luminous dark eyes, a long dark pointed beard streaked with grey reaching well below the chin; both small, on the tier below Our Lady. The rest of the multitude is small and deliberately varied: a young Roman virgin with a round face and dark braided hair; a tall, lean East African martyr with a long face and close-cropped hair; a round-faced Japanese youth with straight black hair; an old bishop with a square face and white beard; a Brazilian mother with warm brown skin and a broad smile; a freckled boy with straw-coloured hair.

subject: A quiet country churchyard at dusk on the evening of All Souls, peaceful and hopeful, with no skulls, no bones and no dark or frightening imagery. In the lower half, a widow in a dark shawl kneels half-length at a grave marked by a plain wooden cross (no inscription), a rosary in her joined hands, her young son beside her setting down a lit candle; around them other graves with plain stone crosses, glowing votive candles in small glass lanterns, pots of white and golden chrysanthemums, two dark cypresses and the lit doorway of a small whitewashed chapel with a bell-cote. In the upper half, the deep blue-violet evening sky opens into a soft rose-gold glow: a tall angel in white and pale gold robes, wings spread, bends down to take by the hand a soul in a plain white robe, a grey-haired man with joined hands, and lifts him gently upward toward the light, while a few other souls in white, small, wait calmly with hands joined, looking up with hope amid low, gentle rose-gold light like the last of the sunset. Keep the churchyard and the sky inside the arched window.
face: The angel: youthful and serene, a HEART-SHAPED face with a broad smooth brow tapering to a small pointed chin, wide-set grey-blue eyes, a fine straight nose, fair skin and short golden hair curling at the ears; a gentle, consoling smile. The soul being raised: a man of about seventy with a SQUARE face, a broad nose, deep smile-lines and short grey hair, clean-shaven, his face lit with relief. The widow: about forty, a LONG, narrow face with a high-bridged nose, dark brows and dark eyes lowered in prayer, dark hair under her shawl. The boy: about eight, a ROUND freckled face and tousled brown hair.

subject: Sts. Peter and Paul half-length side by side, each holding on his arm a small model of the basilica built over his tomb, as founders do in old altarpieces. Peter (left), turned a little right, in his blue tunic and golden-ochre mantle, his keys hanging from his right hand, holds on his left forearm a model of St. Peter's with Michelangelo's great ribbed dome and Maderno's façade. Paul (right), turned a little left, in a green tunic and a deep red mantle, a long sword resting point-down against his shoulder, holds a model of St. Paul Outside the Walls: its long basilica roof, the gabled façade glinting with gold mosaic, the square campanile and the colonnaded courtyard with palm trees. Behind them, Rome at sunset along the Tiber: the dome of St. Peter's far off at the left, umbrella pines, bridges and ochre roofs, the Aventine hill at the right. No lettering on the models. Keep both models inside the arched window.
face: Peter as on the peter card: about sixty-five, a broad, weathered fisherman's face, a strong wide nose, deep-set earnest eyes, a lined forehead; curly grey-white hair balding from the back with a curly tuft at the forehead; a short, square, curly grey-white beard; a steady, fatherly gaze toward the viewer. Paul as on the paul card: about sixty, a noble LONG face — a high domed forehead, bald on top with dark wavy hair greying at the sides, a straight fine nose, calm luminous dark eyes, a long dark pointed beard streaked with grey reaching well below the chin; eyes lifted, thoughtful. The two faces must stay clearly different: Peter broad, square-bearded and grey-white; Paul long, bald-domed and dark-bearded.

subject: The house and workshop of Nazareth in the warm light of late afternoon, three figures half-length side by side. St. Joseph (left) at his carpenter's bench, a plane in his hand, pausing to look down with love; the boy Jesus (centre), about seven, in a simple rose-red tunic, carrying a small plank of fresh wood toward him, curled shavings at his feet; Our Lady (right), seated, spinning white wool with a distaff and looking up at them both with a quiet smile. On the wall hang saws and a mallet; a clay water jar and a loaf on a low shelf; a white dove on the window sill. Through the open doorway, the flat-roofed white houses of Nazareth climbing a green hillside with olive trees and a few cypresses under a clear sky. Keep the workshop and the doorway inside the arched window.
face: St. Joseph as in recurring-figures.md: a man of about forty with a LONG OVAL face — a straight nose, gentle dark-brown eyes under level brows, a quiet mouth; full dark-brown curly hair to the nape and a short full dark-brown beard; a green tunic and an ochre-brown mantle. The boy Jesus: the Christ Child's face as in recurring-figures.md, lengthened to about seven — a softly rounded face with full cheeks, a high rounded forehead, a small straight nose, large clear brown eyes, a small rosy mouth, golden-brown curls to the ears, a plain gold halo; an eager, trusting look up at Joseph. Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md: a young woman of about twenty-five with a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, softly rounded cheeks, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre under a white inner veil and a blue mantle drawn over the head.

subject: Christ half-length, facing the viewer, in a rose-red tunic and a blue mantle, his left hand gently drawing the mantle aside and his right hand pointing to his Heart, shown on his breast above the tunic: a radiant heart surrounded by a small crown of thorns, a little flame and a small cross rising from its top, golden rays streaming from it; a small, clean mark on it, no blood. The wounds on his hands show only as small, clean marks. His gaze meets the viewer with tender invitation. Behind him, through a soft golden light, the quiet chapel of the Visitation convent at Paray-le-Monial in Burgundy, its round-arched stone nave and the grille of the nuns' choir, candles on the altar. No lettering anywhere.
face: Christ as in recurring-figures.md: a man of about thirty-three with a LONG OVAL face narrowing gently to the chin — a high, smooth forehead, a long straight nose with a fine bridge, calm almond-shaped dark-brown eyes under level brown brows, high, softly modelled cheekbones, a quiet closed mouth; chestnut-brown hair parted in the centre and falling in soft waves past the shoulders; a short, full chestnut beard and moustache, lightly parted at the chin; a plain gold halo; he looks straight out at the viewer with a gentle, inviting gaze.

subject: The Corpus Christi procession passing through the narrow street of a small hill town at mid-morning, composed for the arched window. In the centre, a priest seen in profile, in a white-and-gold cope with a white humeral veil over his shoulders, holds up a golden sunburst monstrance with the white Host at its heart, plain and unmarked; above him four men carry a white-and-gold canopy on poles. Before him two small altar servers in red cassocks and white surplices swing a censer and carry tall candles, and a little girl in white scatters rose petals. The cobbled street is laid with a carpet of flower petals in simple geometric patterns (no lettering); townsfolk kneel at both sides, a mother with a child, an old man with his hat in his hands. Behind, whitewashed houses with hanging tapestries at the windows and a bell tower against a clear blue sky. The monstrance, bright with light, is the focus. Figures small and serene; no lettering anywhere, no symbols or letters on the Host, the canopy or the tapestries.
face: The figures are small and secondary: the priest, about fifty, a lean, LONG face with a high forehead and a straight nose, clean-shaven, short grey hair, seen in profile with eyes on the Host; the servers, two boys of about ten, one round-faced and dark, one freckled and fair; the flower girl, about seven, dark braids; the kneeling mother with a broad, warm face under a light scarf; the old man with a narrow, bony face and white stubble.

subject: The Most Holy Trinity enthroned in heaven, composed for the arched window. God the Father (left) and God the Son (right) seated side by side on a long bank of golden cloud, both half-length, turned slightly toward each other: the Father in a white robe and a golden-yellow mantle, his right hand raised in blessing, his left resting on a clear crystal globe of the world topped by a small gold cross; the Son in his rose-red tunic and blue mantle, bare-footed, the wounds only as small clean marks on his hands, holding a plain upright wooden cross in the crook of his left arm and raising his right hand in blessing. Between their heads and a little above them, the white dove of the Holy Spirit with outspread wings in a radiant burst of golden light, rays falling on both. Around them, small child-angels' heads among the clouds and a deep blue sky scattered with gold stars at the top of the arch. No lettering anywhere; keep the dove, the cloud and both figures inside the arched window.
face: God the Father as in recurring-figures.md: the Ancient of Days, a venerable man of about seventy with a BROAD, SQUARE-BROWED face — a wide, smooth forehead, a strong straight nose, deep-set, kindly grey-blue eyes under full white brows, broad cheekbones, a calm mouth half hidden by the moustache; snow-white hair falling in soft waves to the shoulders and a long, full, flowing white beard; a triangular gold halo; he sits at the left. Christ as in recurring-figures.md: a man of about thirty-three with a LONG OVAL face narrowing gently to the chin — a high, smooth forehead, a long straight nose with a fine bridge, calm almond-shaped dark-brown eyes under level brown brows, high, softly modelled cheekbones, a quiet closed mouth; chestnut-brown hair parted in the centre and falling in soft waves past the shoulders; a short, full chestnut beard and moustache, lightly parted at the chin; a plain gold halo ringed with rays; he sits at the right. The two must read as clearly different: the Father old, white-haired and white-bearded with a broad square brow; the Son young, chestnut-haired, with a long oval face.

subject: The grotto of Massabielle at Lourdes, 1858, composed for the arched window. High in the rock, in the small oval niche above the grotto's dark mouth, Our Lady stands small and luminous in a soft golden light: a plain white dress falling to her feet, a long white veil over head and shoulders, a sky-blue sash at the waist with its two ends hanging down in front, a golden-yellow rose on each bare foot, her hands joined at the breast, a rosary of white beads on a gold chain hanging from her arm; her eyes lowered kindly toward the girl. A wild rose bush (eglantine) grows from the rock beneath the niche, and ivy trails down the grey stone. In the foreground, half-length at the lower left, Bernadette kneels in three-quarter view, looking up, hands joined around her rosary: a white capulet (the Bigourdan hood) over her head and shoulders, a dark wool dress, a small brown shawl. At the right, the clear waters of the river Gave, poplars and a winter sky. No lettering anywhere.
face: Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md: a young woman of about eighteen with a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, softly rounded cheeks, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre, under the long white veil of the apparition, about sixteen as Bernadette saw her, smiling faintly. Bernadette, clearly different and earthier: a girl of fourteen, small and slight, with a SOFT OVAL face a little broad across the cheekbones — a smooth, rather high forehead, strong, straight, dark brows nearly level, large dark-brown eyes set wide apart, a straight nose with a slightly broad, rounded tip, full lips in a small closed mouth, a softly rounded chin; olive, sun-browned skin; very dark brown hair, centre-parted and drawn back under the capulet; her gaze lifted, rapt and simple.

subject: Our Lady, Star of the Sea: at dusk over a rough, dark-green sea, Our Lady appears half-length above the waves on a soft bank of cloud, in a white gown and a deep blue mantle drawn over a white veil, her hands open and lowered in protection; directly above her head a single bright eight-pointed gold star shines, its light spreading across the clouds and the water. Below at the right, small, a wooden sailing ship with patched sails rides the swell, its sailors turned toward her, one raising his arms; at the far left, on a rocky headland, a small white chapel and a lighthouse. The storm clouds break to a clear violet sky around the star. No lettering, no monogram anywhere.
face: Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md: a young woman of about eighteen with a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, softly rounded cheeks, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre, under a white inner veil and blue mantle drawn over the head; she looks down toward the ship with a calm, protective gaze.

subject: Mater Dolorosa, half-length, facing the viewer in slight three-quarter view, composed for the arched window. Our Lady in a deep violet-blue mantle over a black gown, a white veil framing her face, her hands clasped at her breast; on her breast, over the mantle, a glowing golden heart from which seven slender silver swords fan outward, three on one side and four on the other, their hilts gold; no blood, no wound shown, only the heart shining. A single clear tear on her cheek. Behind her, at dusk, the hill of Calvary with the empty cross, a white linen cloth hanging over its arms, dark against a sky of deep rose and violet; the walls of Jerusalem faint in the distance. No lettering anywhere.
face: Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md, matured to about forty-eight (the same woman, not a different face): a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, softly rounded cheeks now a little thinner, faint lines at the eyes, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre, under a white veil and violet-blue mantle; her eyes raised a little toward heaven in quiet grief, sorrowful but serene.

subject: Christ the King enthroned in glory, half-length, facing the viewer, composed for the arched window. He wears a white robe embroidered at the neck and hem with gold and a crimson royal mantle lined with gold, clasped at the breast; on his head a simple gold crown set with a few red stones, a plain gold halo ringed with rays behind it. In his right hand, raised, a slender gold sceptre; in his left, held against his knee, a golden orb of the world topped by a cross. The wounds on his hands show only as small, clean marks. He sits on a gold throne on clouds; below the clouds, far off and small, the round blue earth with its seas and lands in soft light, and on either side of the throne a kneeling angel in white with folded wings, adoring. A deep blue sky with gold stars at the top of the arch. No lettering anywhere.
face: Christ as in recurring-figures.md: a man of about thirty-three with a LONG OVAL face narrowing gently to the chin — a high, smooth forehead, a long straight nose with a fine bridge, calm almond-shaped dark-brown eyes under level brown brows, high, softly modelled cheekbones, a quiet closed mouth; chestnut-brown hair parted in the centre and falling in soft waves past the shoulders; a short, full chestnut beard and moustache, lightly parted at the chin; he looks out at the viewer with calm, serene majesty.

subject: The vision of the scapular, composed for the arched window. At the upper left Our Lady appears on a bank of golden cloud, half-length, in the Carmelite colours: a brown gown, a white mantle drawn over her head above a white veil, a small gold crown; she holds the Christ Child on her left arm and with her right hand holds out a brown scapular, two small plain rectangles of brown wool joined by cords (no lettering, no emblem). The Child, in a white shift, leans toward the friar and blesses him. At the lower right, half-length, St. Simon Stock kneels in three-quarter view, arms opened in wonder to receive it: the brown Carmelite habit with its brown scapular and a white mantle over the shoulders, a hood fallen back. Behind him, the grey stone cloister and chapel of an English medieval friary beside a quiet river at Aylesford in Kent, green meadows and oaks under a summer sky. No lettering anywhere.
face: Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md: a young woman of about eighteen with a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, softly rounded cheeks, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre, under a white veil and white mantle, a small gold crown; she looks down at the friar with tender gravity. the Christ Child as in recurring-figures.md, about two: a plump, ROUND baby face with full rosy cheeks, a high rounded forehead, a small button nose, large clear brown eyes, a small rosy mouth, soft short golden-brown curls; a plain gold halo. St. Simon Stock, clearly different: an Englishman of about seventy, clean-shaven, with a gaunt TRIANGULAR face — broad temples narrowing to a small pointed chin, hollow cheeks, a long, thin, slightly aquiline nose, deep-set pale blue eyes lifted in wonder under sparse white brows, a thin-lipped mouth slightly open; white hair in a narrow ring around a wide tonsure.

subject: The Coronation of Our Lady in heaven, composed for the arched window. Christ (right), seated on a throne of golden cloud, half-length, in a white robe and a blue mantle, lifts a gold crown set with small stars and holds it over the head of Our Lady (left), who kneels beside him on the cloud with her head bowed and her hands crossed on her breast, in a white gown woven with gold and a blue mantle over a white veil. Above them the white dove of the Holy Spirit with outspread wings in a burst of golden light. Around them small angels in white and rose play lutes and a portative organ among the clouds; the whole heaven glows gold, with a deep blue band of stars at the top of the arch. No lettering anywhere.
face: Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md, matured to about forty-eight (the same woman, not a different face): a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, softly rounded cheeks now a little thinner, faint lines at the eyes, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre, under a white veil and blue mantle; she kneels humbly with eyes lowered. Christ as in recurring-figures.md: a man of about thirty-three with a LONG OVAL face narrowing gently to the chin — a high, smooth forehead, a long straight nose with a fine bridge, calm almond-shaped dark-brown eyes under level brown brows, high, softly modelled cheekbones, a quiet closed mouth; chestnut-brown hair parted in the centre and falling in soft waves past the shoulders; a short, full chestnut beard and moustache, lightly parted at the chin; a plain gold halo ringed with rays; he looks at his Mother with tender love.

subject: The miracle of the snow on the Esquiline hill in Rome, a summer night of August turning to dawn, after Masolino's panel. Above, in a round golden glory on a bank of cloud, Our Lady half-length in her blue mantle lets snow fall from her open hands; soft white flakes drift down through a warm summer sky. Below, on the green hilltop among umbrella pines, cypresses and the ruined brick walls of ancient Rome, a patch of fresh white snow lies on the summer grass in the shape of a church's ground plan. In the left foreground, half-length, Pope Liberius in a deep crimson cope with a gold border over a white alb and a white papal tiara bends to trace the outline in the snow with a long-handled hoe; at the right, the Roman patrician John and his wife kneel in wonder in rich dark-blue and rose robes. No lettering anywhere; keep the glory, the snow and all figures inside the arched window.
face: Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md: a young woman of about eighteen with a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, softly rounded cheeks, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre, under a white inner veil and blue mantle drawn over the head; small, above, looking down with a gentle smile. Pope Liberius: about sixty-five, clean-shaven, with a BROAD, SQUARE face and a heavy, strong jaw — a low, wide brow, a short, blunt nose, small, wide-set grey eyes under straight grey brows, full cheeks, a firm, wide mouth; short white hair beneath the tiara; eyes down on the snow, absorbed. The patrician John: about fifty, a LONG, NARROW face with a high forehead, a long nose, dark eyes, a short, neat black beard; his wife: about forty-five, a ROUND face with plump cheeks and a small mouth under a white veil, hands joined.

subject: The Immaculate Heart of Mary, half-length, facing the viewer in slight three-quarter view, composed for the arched window. Our Lady in a white gown and her blue mantle over a white veil, her left hand laid on her breast and her right hand gently indicating her heart, which shines on her breast over the gown: a glowing golden-red heart wreathed with a ring of small white roses, a small clear flame rising from its top, soft golden rays around it; no sword, no thorns, no wound. Behind her an enclosed garden in the gold of late afternoon: a low stone wall, white lilies and white roses, a small stone fountain, a slender cypress, and over the wall the soft hills of Galilee under a pale sky. Calm and radiant. No lettering anywhere; keep the figure and garden inside the arched window.
face: Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md: a young woman of about eighteen with a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, softly rounded cheeks, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre under a white inner veil and a blue mantle drawn over the head; her gaze lowered and inward, recollected, with the faintest smile.

subject: The image of Our Lady of Guadalupe as it appears on St. Juan Diego's tilma, painted faithfully and filling the arched window: Our Lady standing, full-length, small within the arch, her head inclined gently to her right, her eyes lowered, her hands joined in prayer before her breast; a rose-pink tunic patterned with small gold flowers and leaves, gathered with a narrow dark sash tied high above the waist, a small gold brooch with a tiny cross at the neck; over all a blue-green mantle edged with gold and scattered with small gold stars, drawn over her head. She stands on a dark crescent moon held up by a small angel with wings of green, white and red feathers, his arms spread holding her mantle and tunic. Behind her the full golden sunburst of straight and wavy rays in an almond-shaped glory, edged by soft white-and-blue clouds. The ground of the window around the glory is the warm, faintly woven natural cream of the maguey-fibre cloth, with a few Castilian roses at the lower corners. Juan Diego does not appear (he has his own card holding the tilma). No lettering anywhere; keep the whole image inside the arched window.
face: The image's own face, not the set's Our Lady: a young Mexican woman of about sixteen with warm olive-brown skin and a small, softly OVAL, slightly elongated face — a straight, gentle nose, lowered dark eyes under fine dark brows, a small closed mouth with a faint serene smile, a smooth rounded chin; straight dark-brown hair parted in the centre and falling beneath the mantle; her head tilted to her right. The angel below: a small child's face with a round chin and short dark curls, looking out.

subject: The gift of the Rosary to St. Dominic, composed for the arched window. Our Lady sits enthroned on a bank of golden cloud at the upper right, half-length, in a rose-red gown and her blue mantle over a white veil, a small gold crown on her head; on her left knee the Christ Child in a white shift, and with her right hand she holds out a rosary of dark wooden beads with a small gold cross, letting it fall toward St. Dominic. The Child also holds out a second rosary toward him. St. Dominic kneels at the lower left, half-length, in the white habit and black cappa of his Order, his face lifted to her, both hands reaching up to receive the beads; a white lily lies on the ground beside him. Behind, the hill country of Languedoc near Prouille: green slopes, a small stone chapel with a bell-cote, cypresses, and a clear blue sky with a few small child-angels' heads in the cloud around Our Lady. No lettering anywhere; keep the cloud and both figures inside the arched window.
face: Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md: a young woman of about eighteen with a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, softly rounded cheeks, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre under a white inner veil and a blue mantle drawn over the head; she looks down at St. Dominic with a gentle smile. The Christ Child as in recurring-figures.md, about two years old: a plump, ROUND child's face with full rosy cheeks, a high rounded forehead, a small button nose, large clear brown eyes, a small rosy mouth, soft short golden-brown curls; fair, glowing skin; a plain gold halo. St. Dominic as on the dominic card: a man of about thirty-five with a gentle, OVAL face — a straight, fine nose, soft brown eyes under level brows, a calm closed mouth; short brown hair in a monastic tonsure (a ring of short curls around a shaven crown), a short trimmed brown beard; a white habit and scapular under a black cappa and hood; the same face as that card, raised in wonder. The three must read as clearly different: the Mother young and fair under her blue mantle, the Child round and golden-curled, Dominic a tonsured, bearded friar in black and white.

subject: Our Lady of Mercy in the Mercedarian image, composed for the arched window. Our Lady stands at the centre, half-length and a little above the other figures, in the white habit of the Order of Mercy: a white tunic, a white scapular and a wide white mantle, a white veil, a small gold crown; on the breast of her scapular the small shield of the Order (a white cross on a red field above upright red and gold bars, no letters). In her right hand a slender gold sceptre; with her left arm she spreads her open white mantle wide over the captives who kneel beneath it, and from that hand hangs a small white scapular offered to them. Under the mantle, small and half-length, three captives in plain, worn clothes turn their faces up to her, their hands joined; a broken iron chain and an opened shackle lie before them on the ground. Behind, the harbour of Barcelona in soft morning light: a stone quay, a tall-masted galley at anchor, the sea and a clear sky. Serene and devotional: no wounds, no suffering shown, only relief. No lettering anywhere; keep the mantle and every figure inside the arched window.
face: Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md, a young woman of about eighteen with a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, softly rounded cheeks, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre under a white inner veil and a blue mantle drawn over the head — here the veil and mantle are white, not blue, and she looks down with tenderness at the captives. The captives are small and clearly different: a North African-born Christian sailor of about forty with a LEAN, LONG face, a hooked nose, dark sun-browned skin and a short black beard; a young mother of about twenty-five with a ROUND, soft face and a dark headscarf, holding a small child; an old man of about seventy with a NARROW, bony face, a bald crown and white stubble.

subject: The Last Supper at the moment of the Institution, composed for the arched window. Christ sits at the centre behind a long table with a white cloth, half-length and facing us, his eyes raised to heaven, holding up in both hands a round, plain unleavened loaf over a simple gold cup of wine; a soft golden light falls on the bread. At his right, St. John, the youngest, leans close against him with his hands joined; at his left, St. Peter bends forward with his hand on his breast. Along the table, smaller and half-length, other Apostles in varied tunics and mantles turn toward him in wonder. On the table a few more loaves, a clay pitcher, a dish with bitter herbs. The upper room of plain stone with a round arch, an oil lamp hanging from a chain, and through a small window the flat roofs of Jerusalem under a deep blue evening sky. Reverent and still. No lettering anywhere, no symbols on the bread; keep all figures inside the arched window.
face: Christ as in recurring-figures.md: a man of about thirty-three with a LONG OVAL face narrowing gently to the chin — a high, smooth forehead, a long straight nose with a fine bridge, calm almond-shaped dark-brown eyes under level brown brows, high, softly modelled cheekbones, a quiet closed mouth; chestnut-brown hair parted in the centre and falling in soft waves past the shoulders; a short, full chestnut beard and moustache, lightly parted at the chin; a plain gold halo; a rose-red tunic and a blue mantle; his eyes lifted in thanksgiving. St. John as in recurring-figures.md: a beardless young man of about twenty-two with a smooth OVAL face, large upturned brown eyes, a straight nose, a small full mouth; wavy golden-brown hair to the jaw; a green tunic and a red-orange mantle. St. Peter as in recurring-figures.md: about sixty-five, a broad, weathered fisherman's face, a strong wide nose, deep-set earnest eyes, a lined forehead; curly grey-white hair balding from the back with a curly tuft at the forehead; a short, square, curly grey-white beard; a blue tunic and golden-ochre mantle. The other Apostles behind, each different: St. Andrew as on the andrew card, an old man with curly grey-white hair and a long grey-white beard forked in two points; St. James the Greater as on the james_greater card, a young man of about twenty-eight with chestnut hair to the jaw and a sparse short beard; St. Thomas as on the thomas_apostle card, a beardless young man of about twenty-five with short dark hair; St. Bartholomew as on the bartholomew card, a man of about forty-five with black curly hair and a long black beard beginning to grey.

subject: Our Lady entrusted to St. John, the moment after Calvary, composed for the arched window. In the foreground, half-length side by side, Our Lady (left) in a deep blue mantle over a white veil and a rose-red gown, her hands crossed on her breast, her face grave and peaceful; St. John (right) turned toward her, one arm around her shoulders to lead her home and his other hand on his heart, taking her as his mother. Behind them, small and far off on the hill of Golgotha under a dusk sky of violet and gold, the plain silhouette of three wooden crosses, the central one taller; the walls and towers of Jerusalem at the right in the fading light. No body, no wounds, no blood shown: only the distant crosses. Quiet and tender. No lettering anywhere; keep both figures and the hill inside the arched window.
face: Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md, the same face matured (the same woman, not a different face), a woman of about forty-eight with a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, softly rounded cheeks, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre under a white inner veil and a blue mantle drawn over the head; eyes lowered in sorrow and trust. St. John as in recurring-figures.md: a beardless young man of about twenty-two with a smooth OVAL face, large upturned brown eyes, a straight nose, a small full mouth; wavy golden-brown hair to the jaw; a green tunic and a red-orange mantle; he looks at her with devotion. The two must read as clearly different: she mature, veiled, in blue; he beardless and golden-haired, in green and red-orange.

subject: The boy Jesus found in the Temple of Jerusalem, composed for the arched window. At the centre, seated a little raised on a stone bench in a colonnade of the Temple, the boy Jesus, twelve, in a rose-red tunic, one hand raised as he speaks; around him, half-length, three teachers of the Law in striped prayer shawls and turbans, one holding an open scroll (blank, no writing), listening astonished. At the left, just arriving through the colonnade, Our Lady and St. Joseph, half-length: Mary with her hands stretched toward her son in relief, Joseph behind her with his staff. Tall golden-brown stone columns, a bronze lamp, and beyond them the sunlit courts and walls of the Temple under a clear sky. No lettering anywhere, no letters on the scroll; keep all figures inside the arched window.
face: The Christ Child as in recurring-figures.md, now twelve: the same face lengthened — a softly ROUND, youthful face with rosy cheeks, a high rounded forehead, a small straight nose, large clear brown eyes, a small rosy mouth, golden-brown curls grown to the neck; a plain gold halo; his gaze calm and assured. Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md: a young woman of about thirty with a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, softly rounded cheeks, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre under a white inner veil and a blue mantle drawn over the head; eyes wide with relief. St. Joseph as in recurring-figures.md: a man of about forty with a LONG OVAL face — a straight nose, gentle dark-brown eyes under level brows, a quiet mouth; full dark-brown curly hair to the nape and a short full dark-brown beard; a green tunic and an ochre-brown mantle, holding a staff. The three teachers differ clearly: an old man of about seventy-five with a LONG, NARROW face, a high bald forehead, a thin aquiline nose and a long white beard; a heavy man of about fifty-five with a BROAD, SQUARE face, a flat wide nose, bushy black brows and a short grizzled black beard; a younger scribe of about thirty-five with a TRIANGULAR face, sharp cheekbones, a narrow chin and a thin brown beard.

subject: Christ proclaiming the Kingdom on the shore of the Sea of Galilee, composed for the arched window. Christ stands at the centre on a low grassy rise, half-length, in his rose-red tunic and blue mantle, his right hand raised as he speaks and his left open toward the listeners. Before him, smaller, a gathered crowd seated and standing on the slope: at the left Peter and Andrew in fishermen's tunics with a wet net over Andrew's arm, turned toward him; a mother with a small child in her lap; an old shepherd leaning on his staff; a young boy kneeling at the front. Behind, the calm blue lake with two small fishing boats drawn up on the pebbly shore, the brown hills of the far side and a bright morning sky. No lettering anywhere; keep Christ and the crowd inside the arched window.
face: Christ as in recurring-figures.md: a man of about thirty-three with a LONG OVAL face narrowing gently to the chin — a high, smooth forehead, a long straight nose with a fine bridge, calm almond-shaped dark-brown eyes under level brown brows, high, softly modelled cheekbones, a quiet closed mouth; chestnut-brown hair parted in the centre and falling in soft waves past the shoulders; a short, full chestnut beard and moustache, lightly parted at the chin; a plain gold halo; a rose-red tunic and a blue mantle; his gaze earnest and warm, looking at the crowd. St. Peter as in recurring-figures.md: about sixty-five, a broad, weathered fisherman's face, a strong wide nose, deep-set earnest eyes, a lined forehead; curly grey-white hair balding from the back with a curly tuft at the forehead; a short, square, curly grey-white beard; a blue tunic and golden-ochre mantle. St. Andrew as on the andrew card: an old man of about seventy with a kindly, weathered, LONG face — a long nose, deep-set eyes; abundant unruly curly grey-white hair and a long grey-white beard divided at the end into two points; a green tunic and a red mantle. The others are small and different: the mother, about twenty-five, a ROUND, soft face under a brown headscarf; the shepherd, about seventy, a NARROW, bony face with a hooked nose and a thin white beard; the boy, about eight, a heart-shaped face with black curls.

subject: The Holy House of Nazareth carried through the night sky by angels, composed for the arched window. At the centre, a small, plain house of rough reddish-brown and grey stone with a low pitched roof and one small window, borne on a bank of cloud by four angels in white and pale-rose robes with broad white-and-gold wings, two beneath and one at each end, their hands under its walls. Seated on the roof, half-length, Our Lady in her rose-red gown and blue mantle over a white veil, holding the Christ Child on her lap; the Child raises his right hand in blessing toward the land below. Beneath them, small, the dark blue Adriatic Sea under a starry night sky with a first pale glow of dawn at the horizon, and on a green hill by the shore a wood of laurel trees where the house will come to rest. No lettering anywhere; keep the house, the angels and the cloud inside the arched window.
face: Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md: a young woman of about eighteen with a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, softly rounded cheeks, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre under a white inner veil and a blue mantle drawn over the head; she looks down at the land with quiet calm. The Christ Child as in recurring-figures.md, about two years old: a plump, ROUND child's face with full rosy cheeks, a high rounded forehead, a small button nose, large clear brown eyes, a small rosy mouth, soft short golden-brown curls; fair, glowing skin; a plain gold halo. The angels are small and secondary, youthful and serene, each different: one with a HEART-SHAPED face and golden curls, one with a LONGER face and straight dark-brown hair, one with a ROUND face and auburn curls, one in profile.

subject: The Wedding at Cana, composed for the arched window. At the left, half-length, Our Lady in her rose-red gown and blue mantle bends toward a young servant and gestures toward her Son; at the centre Christ, half-length, in his rose-red tunic and blue mantle, raises his right hand in blessing over six large stone water jars standing in a row in the foreground, from one of which a second servant pours a stream of deep red wine into a clay pitcher. At the right, behind a long table with a white cloth, bread, figs and clay cups, the steward in a yellow robe tastes from a cup in surprise, and beside him the young bride in white with a garland of flowers and the groom in a blue robe. A courtyard of a whitewashed Galilean house with a vine-covered pergola and hanging lamps, hills in evening light beyond. Festive and serene. No lettering anywhere; keep all figures and the jars inside the arched window.
face: Christ as in recurring-figures.md: a man of about thirty-three with a LONG OVAL face narrowing gently to the chin — a high, smooth forehead, a long straight nose with a fine bridge, calm almond-shaped dark-brown eyes under level brown brows, high, softly modelled cheekbones, a quiet closed mouth; chestnut-brown hair parted in the centre and falling in soft waves past the shoulders; a short, full chestnut beard and moustache, lightly parted at the chin; a plain gold halo; a rose-red tunic and a blue mantle. Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md, a woman of about forty-six, with a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, softly rounded cheeks, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre under a white inner veil and a blue mantle drawn over the head. The others are secondary and clearly different: the servant she speaks to, a lad of about fifteen with a narrow, eager face and short black curls; the pouring servant, a stocky man of about forty with a ROUND, ruddy face and a thick black beard; the steward, about sixty, with a LONG, fleshy face, a bulbous nose, raised grey brows and a short white beard; the bride, about sixteen, a HEART-SHAPED face with dark eyes and dark hair under a white veil; the groom, about twenty, a SQUARE-JAWED face with a first dark beard.

subject: St. John unharmed in the cauldron of oil outside the Latin Gate of Rome, composed for the arched window. St. John is seen half-length rising from a great round bronze cauldron set on a low brick hearth, dressed in a plain white tunic, his hands joined in prayer and his face lifted serenely to heaven; a soft golden light from above falls on him, and the oil is calm and golden as a bath; only a few small flames lick the hearth beneath, and no steam, no burn, no pain is shown. At the left, small, two Roman executioners with a bellows and a long iron poker stop and stare in astonishment; behind them a helmeted soldier. Behind, the Porta Latina in the brick Aurelian Wall: a single stone arch between two round towers, crenellated walls, a few cypresses and a clear evening sky. Peaceful and miraculous. No lettering anywhere; keep every figure inside the arched window.
face: St. John as in recurring-figures.md: a beardless young man of about twenty-two with a smooth OVAL face, large upturned brown eyes, a straight nose, a small full mouth; wavy golden-brown hair to the jaw; here in a plain white tunic, his green and red-orange mantle laid over the cauldron's rim; the ever-young, beardless John of the Western tradition, not aged to his historical ninety; eyes raised, peaceful and joyful. The executioners are small and clearly different: one burly with a SQUARE face and a black stubble beard, one young and thin with cropped fair hair; both astonished.

subject: Christ alone at the pillar after the scourging, composed for the arched window, as in the devotional image of Christ at the Column. Christ stands half-length at the centre beside a short, round column of pale veined marble, his crossed wrists bound to it with a loose cord, his head bowed a little and his eyes turned toward us with patience and love. He wears a white loincloth and his rose-red tunic has slipped from his shoulders to the ground; his body is whole and serene, with only a few thin, clean red lines on the arms and shoulders, no blood running, no torn flesh. A bundle of rods lies on the floor at the foot of the column. Behind, the paved courtyard of Pilate's praetorium: a Roman arcade of warm stone, a doorway into shadow, and far off one Roman soldier in a red cloak walking away; late-morning light falls in from the left.
