Quiet, compassionate, never cruel. No lettering anywhere; keep every figure inside the arched window.
face: Christ as in recurring-figures.md: a man of about thirty-three with a LONG OVAL face narrowing gently to the chin — a high, smooth forehead, a long straight nose with a fine bridge, calm almond-shaped dark-brown eyes under level brown brows, high, softly modelled cheekbones, a quiet closed mouth; chestnut-brown hair parted in the centre and falling in soft waves past the shoulders; a short, full chestnut beard and moustache, lightly parted at the chin; a plain gold halo; his hair falls forward past the shoulders, his face pale and gentle, eyes turned to us; bare-shouldered in a white loincloth, shown modestly at half-length. The distant soldier is tiny, seen from behind, face not visible.

subject: Christ carrying the Cross meets his Mother on the way to Calvary, composed for the arched window. Christ, half-length at the right, bears a heavy plain wooden cross on his right shoulder, bending under it, in his rose-red tunic (no mantle), the thin crown of thorns on his head; he turns his face toward his Mother. Our Lady, half-length at the left, in her blue mantle over a white veil and rose-red gown, reaches out both hands toward him, her face full of sorrow and love. Behind her, a little smaller, St. John supports her. Behind them a narrow stone street of Jerusalem climbing to a city gate, with the green hill of Golgotha beyond under a clouded sky; a Roman soldier's spear-point small at the edge. No blood, no fall shown; tender and grave. No lettering anywhere; keep every figure inside the arched window.
face: Christ as in recurring-figures.md: a man of about thirty-three with a LONG OVAL face narrowing gently to the chin — a high, smooth forehead, a long straight nose with a fine bridge, calm almond-shaped dark-brown eyes under level brown brows, high, softly modelled cheekbones, a quiet closed mouth; chestnut-brown hair parted in the centre and falling in soft waves past the shoulders; a short, full chestnut beard and moustache, lightly parted at the chin; a plain gold halo; the crown of thorns thin, no blood; his gaze on his Mother, full of compassion. Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md, the same face matured (the same woman, not a different face), a woman of about forty-eight with a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, softly rounded cheeks, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre under a white inner veil and a blue mantle drawn over the head (a rose-red gown beneath); eyes on her Son in sorrow. St. John as in recurring-figures.md: a beardless young man of about twenty-two with a smooth OVAL face, large upturned brown eyes, a straight nose, a small full mouth; wavy golden-brown hair to the jaw; a green tunic and a red-orange mantle; he stands behind her, his hand at her shoulder. The three must read as clearly different: Christ bearded in rose-red under the Cross, Mary mature and veiled in blue, John beardless and golden-haired in green and red-orange.

subject: Christ crowned with thorns and mocked as king, composed for the arched window. Christ sits half-length at the centre on a low stone bench, a faded scarlet soldier's cloak thrown over his shoulders over a white loincloth, a slender woven crown of green-brown thorns on his head, a plain reed held like a sceptre in his bound hands. His face is calm and majestic, the eyes lowered in meekness, the true King in mock regalia; at most two or three tiny clean drops at the brow, no streaming blood. Behind him, in the shadow of a pillared guardroom of the praetorium, two Roman soldiers stand small and half-turned away, one with a helmet and spear. A warm, low light from a high window falls on Christ alone. Dignified, never grotesque. No lettering anywhere; keep every figure inside the arched window.
face: Christ as in recurring-figures.md: a man of about thirty-three with a LONG OVAL face narrowing gently to the chin — a high, smooth forehead, a long straight nose with a fine bridge, calm almond-shaped dark-brown eyes under level brown brows, high, softly modelled cheekbones, a quiet closed mouth; chestnut-brown hair parted in the centre and falling in soft waves past the shoulders; a short, full chestnut beard and moustache, lightly parted at the chin; a plain gold halo behind the thin crown of thorns; eyes lowered, serene. The soldiers are small and secondary, in shadow, faces turned away: one broad-shouldered with a bronze helmet, one lean and bare-headed with cropped dark hair.

subject: Christ praying in Gethsemane, composed for the arched window. Christ kneels half-length at the right beside a large grey rock, in his rose-red tunic and blue mantle, his hands joined on the rock and his face lifted toward the upper left, where a young angel appears in a shaft of soft golden light out of the night sky, holding out a plain gold chalice to him. His face is grave and peaceful; no sweat of blood, only a pale light on his brow. Far below at the lower left, small in the shadow of the olive trees, three Apostles lie asleep wrapped in their mantles: Peter, James and John. Twisted old olive trees, a low stone wall, and beyond the Kidron valley the walls and towers of Jerusalem under a deep blue night sky with a full moon and a few stars. Nocturnal, still, devotional. No lettering anywhere; keep every figure inside the arched window.
face: Christ as in recurring-figures.md: a man of about thirty-three with a LONG OVAL face narrowing gently to the chin — a high, smooth forehead, a long straight nose with a fine bridge, calm almond-shaped dark-brown eyes under level brown brows, high, softly modelled cheekbones, a quiet closed mouth; chestnut-brown hair parted in the centre and falling in soft waves past the shoulders; a short, full chestnut beard and moustache, lightly parted at the chin; a plain gold halo; a rose-red tunic and a blue mantle; eyes lifted to the angel in sorrow and surrender. The angel is clearly different from him and from St. Michael: a youthful angel with a SOFT, ROUND face, a small straight nose, wide-set dark-brown eyes, full cheeks, a gentle mouth; short dark-auburn curls; a pale rose-gold robe and white wings edged in gold, no armour. The sleeping Apostles are small, faces half hidden: Peter as in recurring-figures.md, about sixty-five, a broad, weathered fisherman's face, a strong wide nose, deep-set earnest eyes, a lined forehead; curly grey-white hair balding from the back with a curly tuft at the forehead; a short, square, curly grey-white beard; a blue tunic and golden-ochre mantle; James as on the james_greater card, chestnut hair to the jaw and a short sparse beard; John as in recurring-figures.md, beardless with wavy golden-brown hair, in green and red-orange.

subject: The angel freeing St. Peter from Herod's prison (Acts 12:6-10), composed for the arched window. In a dark stone dungeon, St. Peter sits up half-length on a bed of straw at the right, waking, in his blue tunic, his golden-ochre mantle beside him; the iron chains are falling open from his wrists. At the left, a tall angel in a white robe, filled with light, bends toward him, one hand touching his shoulder and the other pointing to the open door; a bright white-gold light fills the cell from the angel. On either side two Roman soldiers sleep, slumped against the wall with their spears and helmets, faces hidden. Through the opened iron gate behind, a glimpse of a moonlit Jerusalem street. Wonder and quiet, no fear. No lettering anywhere; keep every figure inside the arched window.
face: St. Peter as in recurring-figures.md: about sixty-five, a broad, weathered fisherman's face, a strong wide nose, deep-set earnest eyes, a lined forehead; curly grey-white hair balding from the back with a curly tuft at the forehead; a short, square, curly grey-white beard; a blue tunic and golden-ochre mantle; half awake, astonished and trusting. The angel is clearly different from St. Michael and from the other angels of the set: a tall, youthful angel with a LONG, NARROW face, a fine slightly aquiline nose, deep-set clear grey eyes under straight dark-blond brows, a long smooth jaw, a calm closed mouth; straight ash-blond hair to the jaw; white robe and pale silver-white wings, no armour.

subject: St. Peter's first service with the faithful of Rome, composed for the arched window: daylight and a household, clearly not the golden basilica apse of the chair_peter card. St. Peter sits half-length at the left of centre on a plain, heavy wooden chair made of straight timbers, in his blue tunic and golden-ochre mantle, the two keys (one gold, one silver) resting on his knee; he leans forward with his right hand open and extended toward his listeners, teaching, a small scroll in his left. At the right, smaller and half-length, the first Roman faithful listen: the senator Pudens in a white toga with a narrow purple border, and his young daughter with a veil and a small clay oil lamp in her hands. Beside Peter a low stone basin of clear water, the reservoir where he baptised. Behind, the colonnaded garden court of a Roman villa on the Via Salaria: umbrella pines, cypresses, a red-tiled roof, and far off the walls and temples of Rome in soft winter light. No lettering anywhere; keep every figure inside the arched window.
face: St. Peter as in recurring-figures.md: about sixty-five, a broad, weathered fisherman's face, a strong wide nose, deep-set earnest eyes, a lined forehead; curly grey-white hair balding from the back with a curly tuft at the forehead; a short, square, curly grey-white beard; a blue tunic and golden-ochre mantle; here gentle and earnest as he teaches. The listeners are clearly different from him and from each other: Pudens, a Roman of about fifty with a SQUARE, clean-shaven face, a short straight nose, a broad firm jaw and short-cropped dark hair greying at the temples, attentive; his daughter, about sixteen, with a small HEART-SHAPED face, dark eyes and dark hair parted under a pale veil, lips parted in wonder.

subject: The finding of the True Cross at Golgotha and the miracle that told it apart, composed for the arched window: not the upraised Cross of the exaltation_cross card. At the left, half-length, the aged empress St. Helena stands with her hands raised in thanksgiving. In the centre, laid on the edge of a freshly dug pit in the pale rock, the third of three rough wooden crosses is being touched to a sick woman of Jerusalem who, on a simple litter, sits up healed, her arms lifted in joy; the two other crosses lie on the earth behind, with a plain small blank board (the title, no letters) and three iron nails on a white cloth. Behind the litter the bishop Macarius, small, holds the cross-beam steady; two workmen with mattocks rest at the edge of the excavation. Background: broken masonry of the pulled-down pagan temple, the rock of Calvary, and the walls of Jerusalem in clear morning light. Joyful and reverent. No lettering anywhere; keep every figure inside the arched window.
face: St. Helena as in recurring-figures.md: the empress at about seventy-eight, a LONG, dignified face narrowing to a FIRM, slightly prominent chin — a high forehead, a STRONG, STRAIGHT ROMAN NOSE running on from the line of the brow, large deep-set grey-brown eyes under thin, arched silver brows, lean cheeks with fine lines at the eyes and mouth; silver-white hair waved back from the brow and gathered in a low bun at the nape, as on her coins, under a white veil and a slender jewelled gold diadem; a white stola bordered in gold and a deep purple imperial mantle; she looks at the Cross with wonder and gratitude. The others are small and clearly different: the healed woman, about forty, with a ROUND, flushed face, dark hair loose on the pillow, a plain linen shift; the bishop Macarius, about sixty, a LEAN, NARROW face with a hooked nose and a short dark-grey pointed beard, bare-headed with a small tonsure, in a white tunic and a white pallium with dark crosses (no mitre, unlike the white-bearded mitred bishop of exaltation_cross); the workmen tanned, in short tunics, faces turned to the miracle.

subject: St. Michael appearing at the grotto of Monte Gargano to the bishop of Siponto, composed for the arched window. St. Michael stands half-length on a rocky ledge above the dark mouth of a limestone cave, in a burst of golden light, dressed exactly as on the michael_archangel card, his sword held upright in his right hand and his left hand pointing down to the grotto that he claims for his church; his shield with the red cross on his arm; no dragon, no demon. Below at the left, smaller and half-length, the bishop of Siponto kneels in a white alb and gold cope, his mitre laid on the rock beside him, his hands joined, looking up. At the cave mouth a small white bull lies quietly (the herd's bull of the legend). Background: the rugged white cliffs and holm-oak woods of Monte Gargano, and far below the blue Adriatic under a bright sky. No lettering anywhere; keep every figure inside the arched window.
face: St. Michael as on the michael_archangel card and in recurring-figures.md: a radiant youthful angel with a softly OVAL face, a smooth brow, a fine straight nose, large clear blue-grey eyes under lightly arched golden brows, rosy rounded cheeks, a small firm mouth, a gently rounded chin; thick golden curls to the jaw; a gold halo; great white wings; a silver breastplate trimmed in gold over a blue skirt, a billowing red-orange mantle; here grave and gentle, commanding, not fighting. The bishop is clearly different: about sixty, a BROAD, LOW-BROWED face with heavy cheekbones, a short blunt nose, small kind dark eyes, a wide mouth; a white tonsured fringe and a short rounded white-grey beard.

subject: Christ on the Cross with his Mother and St. John standing beneath, composed for the arched window: the Cross itself is the centre, close and large, not distant. Christ hangs on a plain dark wooden cross with a small blank wooden titulus (no letters), in a white loincloth, his arms outstretched, his head inclined and his eyes raised to heaven as he gives up his spirit; the thin crown of thorns; the nail wounds only as small, clean dark-red marks on hands and feet, the side not yet opened, no blood running. At the foot of the Cross, half-length and smaller, Our Lady stands at the left, her hands clasped at her breast, looking up at her Son; St. John stands at the right, his hands joined, looking up. Behind, the rocky hill of Golgotha, a darkened sky of deep blue and violet with a pale eclipsed sun, and the walls of Jerusalem low on the horizon. Solemn and devotional, the Stabat Mater. No lettering anywhere; keep every figure inside the arched window.
face: Christ as in recurring-figures.md: a man of about thirty-three with a LONG OVAL face narrowing gently to the chin — a high, smooth forehead, a long straight nose with a fine bridge, calm almond-shaped dark-brown eyes under level brown brows, high, softly modelled cheekbones, a quiet closed mouth; chestnut-brown hair parted in the centre and falling in soft waves past the shoulders; a short, full chestnut beard and moustache, lightly parted at the chin; a plain gold halo; the face lifted to heaven, peaceful in surrender. Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md, the same face matured (the same woman, not a different face), a woman of about forty-eight with a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, softly rounded cheeks, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre under a white inner veil and a blue mantle drawn over the head (a rose-red gown beneath); she stands upright, sorrowful and steadfast. St. John as in recurring-figures.md: a beardless young man of about twenty-two with a smooth OVAL face, large upturned brown eyes, a straight nose, a small full mouth; wavy golden-brown hair to the jaw; a green tunic and a red-orange mantle; he looks up at the Lord. Unlike mother_of_church (where Mary and John turn away together and the crosses are small and far off), here Christ on the Cross fills the upper centre and the two stand apart on either side of it, facing him.

subject: St. Claudius Apollinaris, Bishop of Hierapolis in Phrygia in the second century, half-length: an early bishop's dress — a white tunic, a golden-brown paenula (bell-shaped cloak) and a plain white woollen pallium with small dark crosses, no mitre; he holds before him a large rolled scroll, the apology he addressed to the emperor, and raises his right hand as if speaking. Behind him, the city of Hierapolis on its hill with a Roman colonnade and theatre, and below it the dazzling white travertine terraces and pale-blue pools of the hot springs, under a bright sky. Eloquent and calm; no lettering on the scroll.
face: A Greek of Asia Minor about sixty, with a light olive complexion and a BROAD, full OVAL face — a high forehead going bald at the crown, a large, gently hooked nose with a strong bridge, lively, wide-set brown eyes under thick, arched dark brows, full cheeks, a firm, wide mouth; black hair greying at the temples; a thick, black, SQUARE-CUT beard streaked with grey to below the chin; an earnest, persuasive gaze to one side.

subject: St. Macarius of Alexandria, the desert hermit, half-length: a coarse brown tunic and a dark-brown monastic hood drawn over the head, a rough rope belt; he carries on one shoulder a woven palm-leaf basket (the basket of sand of his penance) and holds in the other hand a small cluster of green grapes, which he is about to pass on untasted. Behind him, the Nitrian desert of Egypt: low pale-ochre dunes, a few scattered stone cells and a single palm, under a hot, pale-gold sky. Serene and warm, with the hint of a smile; no lettering.
face: An Egyptian of about seventy-five, sun-browned to a deep bronze, with a WIDE, LOW, ROUNDED-SQUARE face, broad through the jaw — a short, lined forehead half hidden by the hood, a short, broad nose with a rounded tip, narrow dark eyes deeply creased at the corners by a quiet smile, thick, low grey brows, broad cheeks lifted by the smile, a wide, kindly mouth; only a thin, short, sparse grey beard and moustache; the gaze warm and a little amused, toward us.

subject: St. Theodosius the Cenobiarch, the old abbot of the Judaean desert, half-length at the mouth of his cave: a dark-brown monastic habit with a rope belt and a brown mantle, a hood lying back on his shoulders; he holds out a round loaf of bread in both hands, as he gave to the poor, and a plain wooden staff leans beside him. Behind him, the rocky cave opening, and beyond it the bare golden hills of the Judaean desert near Bethlehem with the low stone walls and small domed church of his monastery, under a clear evening sky. Kindly and generous; no lettering.
face: A Cappadocian of about ninety, very old but gentle, with a weathered, lightly tanned complexion and a BROAD, FLAT-PLANED face, widest at high, full cheekbones that sit over soft, rounded cheeks — a broad, bald forehead and crown with a few wisps of white at the temples, a short, broad, straight nose, small, deep-set, kindly brown eyes creased at the corners, thin white brows, a gentle closed mouth; a long, full white beard divided into two points at the chest; eyes toward the bread and the poor he gives it to.

subject: St. Simeon Stylites at prayer on top of his pillar, half-length: he stands behind the low wooden railing of the small square platform that crowns a tall stone column with a carved capital, in a plain, patched brown tunic and a dark monk's hood and cowl, his arms raised and opened to heaven. Far below and small, the rocky hills of northern Syria near Aleppo, with a few pilgrims climbing the path toward the column and a small stone chapel, under a wide, clear morning sky. Lofty, still and luminous; keep the column and every figure inside the arched window; no lettering.
face: A Syrian ascetic of about sixty-five with a sun-darkened olive complexion and a SMALL, NARROW, sharply CHISELLED face — a narrow, creased forehead under the hood, very prominent, sharp cheekbones over deeply hollowed cheeks, a thin, fine aquiline nose, large, deep-set, luminous dark eyes lifted to heaven, thin lips; a short grey beard parted into two points at the chin; dark-grey hair hidden under the hood.

subject: St. Fulgentius, Bishop of Ruspe in North Africa, half-length, turned a little to the right: a plain black monk's habit with its hood lying on the shoulders, and over it a white woollen pallium marked with small black crosses; a simple gold pectoral cross; his right hand rests on an open book of his writings lying on a table draped in red, his left holds a plain wooden crozier against his shoulder. Behind him, the white-walled monastery on a small low island off the Tunisian coast, with a few date palms and a calm turquoise sea under a clear, warm evening sky. Devotional and peaceful; no mitre, no lettering on the book or anywhere.
face: A North African of about sixty-five with a warm olive-brown complexion and a SHORT, BROAD face, as wide at the flat cheekbones as it is long — a broad, rounded forehead running up into a BALD crown with a ring of close-cropped grey-black curls above the ears, a short, wide nose with a low, flat bridge and broad nostrils, large, round, dark-brown eyes set wide apart under thick, straight grey-black brows, full lips, a short, rounded chin; a full, short, grizzled grey beard trimmed close to the jaw; a mild, patient gaze toward us.

subject: St. Genevieve, a young consecrated virgin, half-length: a plain undyed woollen gown with a blue mantle, a white veil over her hair; in her right hand she holds up a lit wax candle whose small flame burns steadily, her left hand resting on a shepherd's crook; two white sheep at her side. Behind her, the Seine and, beyond the river, the walled Gallo-Roman island city of Paris with a few red roofs and a small early church, under a pale winter-morning sky. Gentle, steadfast, devotional; no crown, no lettering.
face: A young woman of about twenty with a fair, fresh complexion and a BROAD, SQUARE-JAWED face, wide at the cheekbones and firm at the jaw — a smooth, low forehead, a short, straight nose, wide-set clear grey-green eyes under straight, fair brows, a wide, calm, closed mouth, a firm, rounded chin; flaxen-blond hair in two thick braids falling from under the veil; her eyes lowered to the candle flame.

subject: St. Gregory of Langres, once a senator of Autun, now an aged bishop, half-length and standing with his hands joined in prayer: a white mitre with gold bands, a deep-green chasuble over a white alb, a gold pectoral cross, a crozier resting in the crook of his arm. Behind him, a Romanesque cloister of pale stone opening onto the old walled hill town of Langres in the soft light of a winter morning. Grave, humble and prayerful; no angels, no lettering.
face: A Gallo-Roman patrician of about eighty-five with a pale complexion and a LONG face with a broad, heavy LANTERN JAW — a high, lined forehead, a large, straight, high-bridged nose, small, heavy-lidded pale-grey eyes under sparse, straight white brows, deep lines running from the nose to the corners of a thin, wide, firm mouth; short white hair under the mitre, and a short white beard clipped close along the square jaw; his eyes lifted a little, in prayer.

subject: St. William, Cistercian monk and Archbishop of Bourges, half-length: the white Cistercian cowl with its wide sleeves under a white pallium with black crosses, a plain white mitre, a gold pectoral cross; he holds a crozier and, cradled against his chest, a small gold monstrance with the Host (his devotion to the Blessed Sacrament), his eyes lowered to it. Behind him, the tall Gothic choir of Bourges Cathedral rising in pale stone with its first flying buttresses and wooden scaffolding, whose choir was nearly finished at his death, under a soft grey-blue sky. Humble and recollected; no lettering.
face: A Frenchman of about sixty-five with a fair, lightly ruddy complexion and a WIDE, SHORT face with a FLAT profile — prominent, rounded cheekbones set high, a short, broad nose with a flattish bridge, heavy-lidded gentle blue-grey eyes, low, straight light-brown brows, a small, closed mouth, a broad, rounded chin; brown hair turning grey, cut short around the monastic tonsure under the mitre; a short, full brown-grey beard; downcast, meditative gaze.

subject: St. Lucian, priest and scholar of Antioch, half-length at a writing desk: a plain off-white tunic and a dark-red mantle, as in the Byzantine miniatures; he holds open on the desk a large codex of the Scriptures he corrected, a reed pen in his hand, and a martyr's palm leans against the desk beside a stack of rolled scrolls. Behind him, through an arched window, Antioch on the Orontes: pale colonnaded streets and the green slope of Mount Silpius under a clear afternoon sky. Studious and serene; no chains, no wounds, no lettering on the pages.
face: A Syrian of about sixty with a warm olive complexion and a BROAD-BROWED, SHORT face — a wide, high, domed forehead, a short, straight nose, dark, intent, slightly narrowed eyes under straight black-grey brows, flat, broad cheeks, a wide, firm mouth, a square chin; thick, short, iron-grey hair combed forward; a short, ROUNDED iron-grey beard; a scholar's steady gaze lifted from the page.

subject: Sts. Julian and Basilissa side by side, half-length, in the house they made a hospital in Egypt. Julian (left) in a plain long brown tunic with a light mantle, holding a martyr's palm and extending his other hand in welcome; Basilissa (right) in a soft blue gown and a long white veil over her head and shoulders, holding a small tray with a clay cup and little glass phials of medicine. Behind them, a whitewashed hall of their hospice with a row of low beds and a shelf of jars, and through an arch the palms and the Nile at Antinoë in golden afternoon light. Tender and dignified; no suffering shown, no lettering.
face: Two clearly different people, both Egyptians of the Roman age with warm olive-brown skin. Julian (left): a man of about forty-five with a KITE-SHAPED face, widest at high, angular cheekbones and narrowing both to a moderate forehead and to a small, firm chin — a straight nose with a narrow bridge, deep-set, kind hazel eyes, short, straight grey brows, a thin, gentle mouth; short, grey-streaked dark hair; a short grey-streaked beard trimmed to the line of the jaw. Basilissa (right): a woman of about thirty-five with a LONG, slender face and a long, graceful neck — a smooth, high forehead, a long, straight nose, large, dark, almond-shaped eyes set under long, dark, softly arched brows, gently hollowed cheeks, a small full mouth, a narrow, rounded chin; dark hair under the white veil; eyes lowered toward the tray.

subject: St. Claudius Apollinaris, Bishop of Hierapolis in Phrygia in the second century, half-length: an early bishop's dress — a white tunic, a golden-brown paenula (bell-shaped cloak) and a plain white woollen pallium with small dark crosses, no mitre; he holds before him a large rolled scroll, the apology he addressed to the emperor, and raises his right hand as if speaking. Behind him, the city of Hierapolis on its hill with a Roman colonnade and theatre, and below it the dazzling white travertine terraces and pale-blue pools of the hot springs, under a bright sky. Eloquent and calm; no lettering on the scroll.
face: A Greek of Asia Minor about sixty, with a light olive complexion and a BROAD, full OVAL face — a high forehead going bald at the crown, a large, gently hooked nose with a strong bridge, lively, wide-set brown eyes under thick, arched dark brows, full cheeks, a firm, wide mouth; black hair greying at the temples; a thick, black, SQUARE-CUT beard streaked with grey to below the chin; an earnest, persuasive gaze to one side.

subject: St. Bathildes, Queen of the Franks, half-length: a slender gold crown set over a white linen veil; a long gown of deep blue, and over it a plain linen tabard embroidered in coloured silk with rows of necklaces and a pendant jewelled cross at the breast, like her chemise kept at Chelles; with both hands she offers a small loaf and a folded length of cloth, as to the poor. Behind her, the timber-and-stone abbey of Chelles in the green valley of the Marne, with a small hospice and its garden, under a mild spring sky. Humble, motherly and serene; no lettering.
face: An Anglo-Saxon woman of about thirty-five with a fair, pale complexion and a ROUND, FULL face — a high, rounded forehead, a short, straight nose, ROUND, clear grey-blue eyes under light, softly curved honey-coloured brows, full, rounded cheeks with a faint flush, a small, bow-shaped mouth, a round chin with a small DIMPLE; honey-blond hair in a single long braid showing beneath the veil; her eyes lowered kindly toward the gifts.

subject: St. Canutus, King of Denmark, half-length: a gold crown with small cross-topped points, a coat of mail under a deep-red royal mantle lined with ermine and fastened at the shoulder with a gold brooch; he holds a lance upright in his right hand and on his left arm a round shield painted with a red cross, as in the twelfth-century picture of him at Bethlehem; a palm of martyrdom rests against the shield. Behind him, the small stone church of St. Alban at Odense with its round-arched windows, green Funen fields, and the grey-blue Danish sea beyond, under a pale northern sky. Kingly, steadfast and devout; no wounds, no weapons raised, no lettering.
face: A Dane of about forty-two, strongly built, with a fair, weather-reddened complexion and a DIAMOND-SHAPED face — a narrowish forehead under the crown, VERY WIDE, high cheekbones, tapering to a firm, rounded chin; a short, straight nose with a slightly upturned tip; narrow, wide-set pale-blue eyes under straight, sandy brows; a full, wide mouth; thick, straight red-gold hair to the jaw; a short, full red-gold beard and moustache; a calm, resolute gaze to one side.

subject: St. Paul the First Hermit, very old and thin, half-length at the mouth of his cave: a plain tunic of woven palm leaves reaching from the shoulders, his arms bare and lean; his hands raised and open in thanksgiving toward a black raven that flies down to him with a round loaf of bread in its beak. Behind him, the rough rock of the cave, a single date palm and a small clear spring, and beyond, the bare, rose-gold mountains of the Egyptian desert near the Red Sea under a clear dawn sky. Peaceful and full of wonder; no lions, no skull, no lettering.
face: An Egyptian of great age, about a hundred and ten, deeply sun-browned and very lean, with a LONG, TAPERING face — a high, BALD, rounded crown with long, thin, straight white hair falling from the sides to the shoulders, a LONG, THIN, gently hooked nose, LARGE, soft, dark eyes WIDE OPEN and lifted in wonder, thin white brows RAISED, cheeks hollow beneath the cheekbones; a very long, thin, straight, silky white beard falling UNDIVIDED to the waist; an expression of gentle, childlike joy.

subject: St. Honoratus, founder of the monastery of Lérins and Archbishop of Arles, half-length: a plain dark-grey monastic tunic and cowl, and over it an early bishop's white woollen pallium with small dark crosses; no mitre; he holds a simple wooden crozier in one hand and raises the other in blessing. Behind him, the small, low, rocky island of Lérins with umbrella pines, a few monks' cells and a small stone chapel by the shore, the calm, deep-blue Mediterranean, and on the horizon the red Estérel hills of the Provençal coast under a bright afternoon sky. Serene, kindly and welcoming; no snakes, no lettering.
face: A Gallo-Roman of about seventy-five with a light olive complexion and a face whose HIGH, BROAD, DOMED forehead is much larger than the SHORT, SMALL lower face — widely spaced, pale-blue eyes with gently drooping outer corners under thin, level white brows, a small, neat, straight nose, soft, full, rosy cheeks, a small mouth with a gentle smile, a small, rounded chin; the crown bald with a light fringe of white hair; a short, neat, rounded white beard close to the chin; a mild, fatherly gaze toward us.

subject: St. Jane of Valois as foundress of the Order of the Annunciation, half-length and a little turned: the grey habit with a scarlet scapular and a white mantle of her Order, a white wimple and black veil, and a slender gold crown resting on the veil for the queen she was; she holds a small crucifix in her joined hands, with a rosary looped over them. Behind her, the Gothic town of Bourges with the tall towers of its cathedral and the low new convent of the Annunciation, under a soft evening sky, as if the Angelus were ringing. Humble, gentle and at peace; no lettering.
face: A French princess of about forty with a pale, smooth complexion and a LONG face that is fuller in its LOWER half — a very HIGH, smooth forehead, a long, straight nose with a softly rounded tip, SMALL, HEAVY-LIDDED, rather close-set blue-grey eyes under faint, fine brows, a LONG upper lip, a small, closed, gently pursed mouth, soft, full lower cheeks and a rounded chin; hair hidden by the wimple; a quiet, patient, inward gaze lowered to the crucifix.

subject: St. Marcella, the Roman widow, very old, half-length: a plain, coarse dark-brown woollen dress and a long dark veil over a white head-cloth, no jewels; she holds open on her lap a large codex of the Scriptures and turns one page with her finger, a rolled letter beside it on the table. Behind her, the terrace of her house on the Aventine hill with a cypress and an oleander, looking across the Tiber to the roofs, columns and domes of Rome in warm late-afternoon light. Wise, peaceful and ardent; no soldiers, no lettering.
face: A Roman lady of great age, about eighty-five, with a pale olive complexion and a SHORT, HEART-SHAPED face grown thin — a broad, finely lined forehead, PROMINENT cheekbones with the cheeks fallen in below them, tapering to a small, POINTED chin; a small, finely HOOKED nose; small, bright, quick dark eyes, keen and humorous, under thin white brows; a thin, wide mouth; white hair under the veil; her gaze lifted from the page as if about to ask a question.

subject: St. Veronica of Milan, Augustinian lay sister, half-length: a black Augustinian habit with a leather belt, a white linen wimple framing the face and a black veil; a coarse linen alms-sack slung over one shoulder, and in her hands a round loaf of bread begged for her community; a small sprig of olive tucked into the belt. Behind her, a narrow street of old Milan with brick houses and arcades, and in the distance the flat green Lombard fields with rows of poplars where she once worked, under a pale, hazy morning sky. Cheerful, humble and hard-working; no lettering.
face: A Lombard countrywoman of about fifty with a sun-weathered, ruddy complexion and a SHORT, BROAD face under a LOW, WIDE brow — high, round APPLE cheekbones, a short, broad nose with a slightly upturned tip, small, bright, deep-set dark-brown eyes under thick, straight dark brows, a wide mouth with thin lips set in a patient half-smile, a small, firm, square chin; hair hidden by the wimple; her gaze lifted a little, cheerful and willing.
verdict: rejected: drawn with a saint's halo; a Blessed has rays

subject: St. Aelred, Cistercian Abbot of Rievaulx, half-length: the white Cistercian cowl with wide sleeves and its hood lying back on the shoulders, a plain wooden abbot's crozier resting in the crook of his left arm; in his right hand an open manuscript book (his Mirror of Charity) held against his chest, his fingers keeping the page. Behind him, the tall pale-stone church and cloister of Rievaulx Abbey in its narrow green Yorkshire valley, wooded hills on either side and the little river Rye, under a soft, clear late-afternoon sky. Warm, gentle and friendly; no mitre, no lettering on the book or anywhere.
face: An Englishman of about fifty-five, clean-shaven, with a fair, lightly flushed complexion and a LONG face that ends in a SOFT, ROUNDED chin — a smooth forehead, a short nose with a gently UPTURNED tip, very LARGE, soft, wide-set grey eyes under HIGH, ARCHED light-brown brows that give an open, tender look, faint hollows beneath the cheekbones, a WIDE, generous mouth in a slight, warm smile; a ring of short auburn hair turning grey around the monastic tonsure; the gaze kind and direct, toward us.

subject: St. Dorothy, young virgin martyr of Caesarea in Cappadocia, half-length: a rose-pink gown and a golden-yellow mantle, a wreath of red and white roses on her dark hair; she holds before her a small woven basket with three red roses and three golden apples, and a martyr's palm rests against her shoulder. Behind her, the old city of Caesarea in winter, low stone walls and roofs lightly touched with snow, and the great white snow-capped cone of Mount Argaeus rising beyond under a clear, pale-blue winter sky. Joyful and radiant; no instruments of torture, no lettering.
face: A Cappadocian Greek girl of about eighteen with a warm, light olive complexion and a small, ROUND face lit by a JOYFUL SMILE — a smooth, rounded forehead, a short, rounded nose, very large, sparkling dark eyes, softly arched black brows, full, round cheeks with DIMPLES, a small, smiling mouth showing the joy the book speaks of, a small, round chin; thick, curling black hair gathered up under the wreath; her eyes lifted, bright with gladness.

subject: St. Bridgid, Abbess of Kildare, half-length: the snow-white habit and white cloak the book says St. Mel gave her, with a white veil; a plain wooden abbess's crozier in the crook of one arm, and in her other hand a small clay lamp whose flame burns steadily; a St. Bridgid's cross woven of green rushes hangs from her belt. Behind her, a great oak tree and the small wooden church and round thatched huts of her monastery at Kildare on the open green plain, with a white cow grazing nearby, under a soft, bright Irish spring sky with drifting clouds. Warm, strong and motherly; no lettering.
face: An Irishwoman of about forty-five with a fair, freckled, fresh complexion and a WIDE, OBLONG face — broad, flat cheekbones and a LONG, firm, rounded jaw; a straight nose, a little long, with a rounded tip; large, wide-set, clear blue eyes under straight, copper-brown brows; a wide, calm mouth; a few strands of copper-red hair at the brow under the white veil; a steady, warm gaze toward us.

subject: St. John de Britto, Jesuit missionary of the Madurai mission, half-length, dressed as a Tamil sannyasi as he lived: a long, loose robe of saffron-yellow cotton with a saffron shawl over the shoulders and a small saffron cloth wound as a turban; he holds a wooden crucifix against his breast with both hands and a green martyr's palm leans on his shoulder. Behind him, the coast of the Marava country near Oriyur: tall palmyra palms, golden sand dunes, a small village of thatched houses, and the blue sea of the Palk Strait under a hot, bright sky. Gentle, ardent and humble; no wounds, no lettering.
face: A Portuguese nobleman of about forty-five, deeply sun-browned by India, with a LEAN, LONG face — HIGH, sharply cut cheekbones with DEEP HOLLOWS beneath them, a NARROW, very HIGH-BRIDGED nose, large, dark, deep-set, burning eyes under strong, ARCHED black brows, a wide forehead, a firm mouth; black hair under the saffron turban-cloth; a full black beard, cut round and not too long, framing the hollow cheeks; the gaze lifted a little, ardent.

subject: St. Valentine, priest of Rome, half-length: a third-century priest's dress, a long white tunic under a deep wine-red paenula (the round bell-shaped cloak of the time) with a plain white linen scarf about the neck; he holds a green martyr's palm and a small bound codex of the Gospels against his breast. Behind him, the Via Flaminia north of Rome where he was buried: the stone arches of the Milvian Bridge (the book's 'Ponte Mole') over the green Tiber, umbrella pines and cypresses, white roadside tombs, under a clear, cold February sky. Warm and courageous; no hearts, no mitre, no lettering.
face: A Roman of about fifty with a warm olive complexion and an OBLONG face — prominent, ROUNDED cheekbones that lift when he smiles, a broad, straight nose, dark-brown eyes that CRINKLE at the corners under softly arched dark brows, deep SMILE LINES, and a notably WIDE, generous mouth with full lips in an open, warm smile; short, dark, CURLY hair greying at the temples; a short, rounded dark beard with grey at the chin; his gaze warm and direct.

subject: St. Catherine of Ricci, Dominican nun and prioress of San Vincenzo at Prato, half-length, as in the portrait attributed to Naldini: an all-white Dominican habit with a white wimple and a white veil (no black mantle), a black leather belt; in her left hand an open book held low; her right hand open, palm up, in a gesture of offering for the Holy Souls. Beside her on a stone ledge a simple dark wooden crucifix stands. Behind her, Prato: the green-and-white banded marble front of its cathedral with the round corner pulpit, red-tiled roofs and a cloister wall, and the dark hill of Monteferrato beyond, under a soft, pearly morning sky. Calm and tender; no crown of thorns, no lily, no lettering.
face: A Florentine woman of about forty-five with a fair complexion and a natural HIGH COLOUR on the cheeks, and a BROAD, full, MOON-SHAPED face — WIDE, FLAT cheeks, a SHORT, broad nose with rounded, slightly FLARED nostrils, SMALL, WIDE-SET grey eyes under HEAVY upper lids, FAINT, thin brows set HIGH above them, a small, soft mouth with a full lower lip, just parted, and a soft, rounded chin; hair hidden by the white wimple and veil; a quiet, open gaze straight at us.

subject: St. John of Matha, founder of the Order of the Most Holy Trinity for the redemption of captives, half-length: the white habit and white scapular of his Order with its cross on the breast, the upright RED and the crossbar BLUE, a white hood lying back on the shoulders; in his left hand an open iron shackle hanging from a short broken chain, in his right a small leather purse of ransom money held out a little, as in the book's engraving. Behind him, a calm blue Mediterranean with a small ship whose only sail is a white monk's cloak tied to the mast, carrying a few tiny freed captives toward the low shore and tower of Ostia, under a clear, windy sky. Compassionate and steadfast; no lettering.
face: A Provençal Frenchman of about fifty, CLEAN-SHAVEN, with a fair, lightly sun-browned complexion and a medium-width OVAL face with a CONVEX PROFILE — a gently SLOPING forehead, a LARGE, CURVED, high-bridged nose that leads the face, a SHORT, softly rounded chin set a little back under the mouth, lean cheeks with shallow hollows; CLOSE-SET, bright dark-brown eyes under thin, ARCHED dark brows; a small, gentle mouth; dark-brown hair cropped short in a round crown with a small tonsure; the gaze turned toward us, kind and resolute.

subject: St. Severinus, Abbot of Agaunum, half-length: a monk's cowl of undyed grey-brown wool with a hood lying back; over his left forearm he holds his heavy dark-brown woollen cloak, half unfolded and offered forward, the cloak by which he healed King Clovis; in his right hand a plain wooden staff. Behind him, the narrow valley of the Rhône at Agaunum (Saint-Maurice in the Valais), a small early abbey church and cells at the foot of a great sheer grey cliff, with snowy Alpine peaks and dark pines under a cold, clear winter sky. Kindly and grave; no mitre, no lettering.
face: A Burgundian of about sixty with a fair, weathered, ruddy complexion and a LONG face whose middle is LONG — a LONG, STRAIGHT nose with a broad, rounded tip, a LONG upper lip, WIDE-SET, kindly grey eyes whose outer corners DROOP, with soft pouches beneath, thick UPSWEPT iron-grey brows, full cheeks, and rather LARGE EARS standing a little out from the head; a ring of iron-grey hair around the monastic tonsure; a LONG, SPADE-SHAPED beard of iron-grey streaked with brown, broad and squared at the end, reaching the breast; the gaze gentle and a little sad.

subject: St. Flavian, Patriarch of Constantinople, half-length, in fifth-century Byzantine vestments as the Menologion of Basil II and the icons show him: a pale phelonion over a darker tunic and a white omophorion with large dark crosses about the shoulders; no mitre. He holds to his breast a rolled scroll tied and sealed, his appeal to Pope Leo. Behind him, the Bosporus and the sea walls of Constantinople, the timber-roofed basilicas and red-tiled roofs of the city on its hills with dark cypresses, under a clear evening sky. Steadfast and meek; no wounds, no lettering.
face: A Greek of about fifty-eight with a light olive complexion and a face of HIGH, rounded cheekbones over SUNKEN temples — a SHORT, flat forehead with the grey hair growing LOW on it in short, tight curls, a LONG, thin, BEAKED nose, CLOSE-SET, deep-set grey eyes under straight grey brows, lean cheeks, a small, firm mouth, and a LONG, NARROW chin carried down by a long, narrow, POINTED grey beard; the gaze calm and unflinching, toward us.

subject: St. Onesimus, the Phrygian slave whom St. Paul converted and sent back to Philemon, half-length, as the bearer of the Apostle's letter: a plain, undyed knee-length woollen tunic with a leather belt, a dark-brown travelling cloak over one shoulder, a traveller's staff in one hand; with the other he holds a small rolled letter, tied and sealed with red wax, close to his breast. Behind him, the Lycus valley in Phrygia: the small hill-city of Colossae with its white houses, a road winding toward it through olive groves, and the great snow-capped ridge of Mount Cadmus above, under a fresh, clear sky. Grateful, eager and free; no chains, no lettering.
face: A Phrygian of about thirty, BEARDLESS, with a warm light-brown Anatolian complexion and a WIDE, FLAT-PLANED face — broad, HIGH cheekbones set wide, a BROAD, low-bridged nose, VERY WIDE-SET dark almond eyes under straight, thick black brows, a WIDE mouth with full lips in a small, grateful smile, a SQUARE chin with a small cleft; short, tight black curls close to the head; the gaze lifted, full of hope.

subject: St. Benedict of Anian, the reformer of the monasteries of the Frankish empire, half-length: the black Benedictine cowl with wide sleeves and its hood lying back; he holds open a large manuscript codex, his finger resting on the page (his collection of the monastic rules), and a second closed book is tucked under his arm; no crozier. Behind him, the brook Anian running between holm-oaks and grey Languedoc garrigue, his little stone hermitage beside it, and further off on the plain a great Carolingian abbey church with its monks' buildings, under a warm, clear southern sky. Earnest and humble; no lettering on the books or anywhere.
face: A Visigothic noble of about seventy, lean and fair-skinned, with a LONG face whose most striking part is a very HIGH, SQUARE forehead crossed by three deep, level lines — deep-set, MOIST, pale-blue eyes that glisten as if near tears, straight grey brows, a long, thin nose with a slight CROOK in its bridge, HOLLOW cheeks under firm cheekbones, and a lean, SQUARE jaw whose line shows through a SHORT, close-trimmed white beard; a thin ring of white hair around the tonsure; the gaze searching and tender, toward us.

subject: St. Apollonia, the aged virgin of Alexandria, half-length: a long deep-blue veil (palla) over grey-streaked hair, drawn around the shoulders over a plain earth-red woollen tunic; in her right hand, held up gently, a pair of small iron pincers gripping a single white tooth, her traditional sign; in her left a green martyr's palm resting against her shoulder. Behind her, outside the city gate, the pale walls and roofs of Roman Alexandria and its harbour, with the tall white Pharos lighthouse far off on its island, under a hazy, luminous sky. No fire, no wounds; serene and unafraid; no lettering.
face: An Alexandrian woman of about sixty-five with a warm olive complexion and a SHORT, WIDE face — a BROAD, LOW forehead, smooth, full cheeks and a SMALL, soft, rounded chin; very LARGE, dark, luminous eyes, CLOSE-SET, like those of a Fayum portrait, under THICK, strongly ARCHED black brows flecked with grey that nearly MEET above the nose; a LONG, slender nose with a narrow bridge and a gentle HOOK; a small, full mouth closed calmly; fine lines at the eyes; a few grey-streaked black waves showing under the veil; her gaze lifted a little, steadfast.

subject: Sts. Faustinus and Jovita, noble brothers of Brescia, half-length side by side. Faustinus (left), the elder, a priest: a white alb under a full, bell-shaped deep-red chasuble, holding a closed Gospel book and a green palm. Jovita (right), the younger, a deacon: a white alb under a red dalmatic with wide sleeves, holding a green palm upright, his other hand on his breast. Behind them, Roman Brescia: the tall Corinthian columns of the Capitoline temple and the forum, and above the town the green Cidneo hill, under a bright, clear sky. Brotherly, fearless and serene; no swords, no lettering.
face: Two clearly different brothers of a fair-olive Lombard family. Faustinus (left): about thirty-two, with a LONG, RECTANGULAR face and a strong, STRAIGHT jaw — a high forehead, a high, narrow nose bridge running into a straight nose, deep-set grey eyes under HEAVY, straight dark-blond brows, flat cheeks, a firm, level mouth; short wavy dark-blond hair and a short, neatly trimmed dark-blond beard; his gaze grave and steady toward us. Jovita (right): about twenty-five, BEARDLESS, with a SHORT, soft, ROUND face — a low, rounded forehead, a short, WIDE SNUB nose, ROUND, bright brown eyes under curved brows, full cheeks, a small, smiling mouth and a small, rounded chin; thick chestnut curls to the ears; his gaze lifted, eager.

subject: St. Severianus, Bishop of Scythopolis in Palestine, who upheld the Council of Chalcedon, half-length, in fifth-century Eastern vestments: a deep PURPLE-RED phelonion over a white tunic and a white omophorion with small dark crosses; no mitre. He holds a closed Gospel book against his breast with his left hand and a green martyr's palm in his right. Behind him, Scythopolis (Beth Shean): its long colonnaded Roman street, the curved stone theatre and the high green tell above the town, with the hills of Gilboa beyond under a hot, clear sky. Steadfast and grave; no soldiers, no wounds, no lettering.
face: A Palestinian Greek of about fifty-five with a warm, dark olive complexion and a ROUND, FULL face — soft, fleshy cheeks, a SHORT, rounded, fleshy nose, LARGE, heavy-lidded dark almond eyes under THICK, HORIZONTAL black brows, a small, full mouth; black, curly hair receding at the temples; a short, ROUND black beard with a single WHITE BLAZE in it at the chin; the gaze quiet and resolute, straight at us.

subject: St. Simeon, son of Cleophas, kinsman of the Lord and second Bishop of Jerusalem, half-length and bare-headed: a plain unbleached linen tunic under a deep-blue woollen mantle wrapped about the shoulders; in his right hand a tall, plain shepherd's staff, as in the book's engraving, and held to his breast in his left a small, plain wooden cross, the sign of his crucifixion. Behind him, the ruined walls and tumbled golden stones of Jerusalem after the siege, a few humble new houses rising among them, and the Mount of Olives with its grey olive groves beyond, under a clear, pale morning sky. Venerable and serene; no wounds, no mitre, no lettering.
face: A Jew of great age, well past a hundred, with a warm, weathered olive complexion and a LONG, NARROW, HATCHET-SHAPED face, keeled down the middle like a blade — a high, narrow forehead, a LONG, THIN, perfectly STRAIGHT nose, small, bright, very dark eyes set DEEP under a jutting brow, sunken temples and cheeks, two deep vertical furrows from nose to mouth, thin lips; long, thin, STRAIGHT white hair falling to the shoulders from a high bald crown; a SPARSE, wispy white beard, straight and thin, reaching only the collarbone, with a thin white moustache; the gaze clear and unafraid, toward us.

subject: St. Porphyry, Bishop of Gaza, once keeper of the relics of the True Cross at Jerusalem, half-length, in early-fifth-century Eastern vestments: a plain ivory phelonion and a white omophorion with dark-red crosses; no mitre. He holds before his breast a small gold reliquary cross with a sliver of dark wood set in it, and a closed book under his arm. Behind him, Gaza near the sea: a new basilica rising on the site of the pagan temple, its approach paved with reused marble slabs, low houses and palms, and the Mediterranean beyond under a bright, dry sky. Humble and zealous; no idols, no lettering.
face: A Greek of Thessalonica of about sixty-five, worn lean by desert penance, with a light olive complexion and a DIAMOND-SHAPED face — a NARROW forehead and a NARROW chin, broadest at WIDE, jutting cheekbones; a SHORT, straight nose with a LOW bridge; very LARGE, PROMINENT dark eyes under thin, arched brows; a wide, thin-lipped mouth; a BALD crown with dark-grey hair left long at the back and sides; a long, STRAIGHT, dark beard streaked with grey, narrowing to the breast; the gaze wide and earnest.

subject: St. Eucherius, Bishop of Orléans, exiled by Charles Martel and made almoner at the abbey of Sarchinium (Saint-Trond), half-length, as an eighth-century monk-bishop without a mitre: the black Benedictine habit of Jumièges under a plain, bell-shaped crimson chasuble; on his left arm a wicker basket of round loaves, and in his right hand one loaf held out to the poor, as in the book's engraving. Behind him, the flat, green Hesbaye country with the stone abbey church and cloister of Saint-Trond, a few poor folk waiting at its gate, and poplars under a soft grey-blue northern sky. Gentle and recollected; no lettering.
face: A Frank of Orléans of about fifty-five, CLEAN-SHAVEN, with a fair complexion and a face with a CONCAVE, DISHED PROFILE — a rounded, prominent forehead, a SHORT, softly SCOOPED nose, and a firm, FORWARD chin, so that the profile curves in like a crescent; deep-set, long-lashed grey-green eyes set close under STRAIGHT, low fair brows; smooth, flat cheeks; full, calm lips; a LONG, slender neck; light-brown hair greying, cut in a monk's crown round the tonsure; a pensive gaze, lowered a little toward the poor.

subject: St. Oswald, Bishop of Worcester and Archbishop of York, reformer of the English monasteries, half-length, as a tenth-century bishop without a mitre: a black Benedictine habit under a full, bell-shaped deep-blue chasuble and a white woollen pallium with black crosses; a plain crozier in his left hand; over his right forearm a white linen towel and in that hand a small bronze basin, for the washing of the poor men's feet in Lent, which he was doing when he died. Behind him, Worcester on the broad River Severn: a small stone Saxon church of St. Mary beside the old cathedral, water meadows and willows, under a soft, luminous English sky. Kindly and noble; no lettering.
face: An Englishman of Danish blood, about sixty-five, fair-skinned with a light ruddy colour, of a noble, well-proportioned build, with a LONG, HANDSOME face — a broad, high forehead, a LONG, NARROW, straight nose, HIGH, broad cheekbones, deep-set, clear blue eyes under straight, fair-grey brows, a firm, CLEAN-CUT jaw and a strong chin; a calm, finely drawn mouth; silver-fair hair cut level at the ears; a SHORT, neat, silver-fair beard close along the jaw; the gaze kindly and direct.

subject: St. Tarasius, Patriarch of Constantinople, who called the Second Council of Nicaea, half-length, as in the fourteenth-century fresco in the church of the Theotokos Peribleptos: a white polystavrion phelonion patterned with black crosses and a white omophorion with large black crosses; he holds a Gospel book with a jewelled gold cover against his breast in his left hand and raises his right in blessing; no mitre. Behind him, Constantinople across the water: the great dome of Hagia Sophia, the sea walls and red-tiled roofs, and ships on the Bosporus, under a golden evening sky. Mild and upright; no lettering.
face: A Byzantine noble of about seventy with a fair, lightly olive complexion and a full OVAL face — a HIGH, BALD, DOMED forehead with a single grey wisp at the top, heavy-lidded, almond-shaped dark eyes with soft pouches beneath, arched grey brows, a straight nose with a broad bridge, FULL, soft cheeks, a small, full-lipped mouth; grey-brown hair at the sides and back, falling to the nape; a LONG, WEDGE-SHAPED beard of grey-brown combed in waves and ending in a POINT at mid-chest; the gaze gentle and composed.

subject: St. Serenus, the Greek who lived by his own garden at Sirmium in Pannonia, half-length: a plain undyed woollen tunic with the sleeves pushed up, a coarse brown mantle knotted at the shoulder; he leans a long iron-shod wooden spade against his shoulder and holds in his other hand a green martyr's palm, with a little basket of fresh herbs and green vegetables on the low wall beside him. Behind him, his walled kitchen garden in neat rows of beans and cabbages with a fig tree and a well, and beyond the wall the broad River Sava and the roofs of Roman Sirmium, under a soft spring sky. Honest and serene; no woman, no wounds, no lettering.
face: A Greek of about forty-five, sun-darkened and weathered from the soil, with a LEAN, ANGULAR face and a CLASSICAL GREEK PROFILE — the long, straight nose running on from the forehead with almost no dip at the bridge, SHARP, HIGH cheekbones with hollows beneath, a LONG, strong jaw, deep-set green-brown eyes with fine crow's feet, level black brows, a WIDE, thin-lipped mouth; short-cropped black hair greying at the temples; a close-trimmed short black beard following the jaw; a steady, open gaze.

subject: St. Leander, Bishop of Seville, who brought the Visigoths from Arianism to the Catholic faith, half-length, as in Murillo's portrait in Seville Cathedral: a tall white mitre edged in gold, a white cope with gold orphreys over a white rochet, a gold crozier in his left hand; in his right a rolled parchment held up, his writing against the Arians (blank, no lettering). Behind him, a heavy crimson curtain drawn back on one side and, beyond, the Guadalquivir with the Roman walls and roofs of Hispalis on its bank, under a warm, hazy Andalusian sky. Grave and zealous; no lettering on the scroll or anywhere.
face: A Hispano-Roman of about sixty with a pale, sallow olive complexion and a LEAN, LONG face — a high, narrow forehead with the dark hair RECEDING, deep-set, heavy-lidded black eyes under STRONG, ARCHED black brows, a long, straight nose with a slight HUMP at the bridge, flat, lean cheeks, a thin, firm mouth, and a NARROW, POINTED chin; a SHORT, close-trimmed black beard and moustache flecked with grey; the gaze searching and serious, turned a little aside.

subject: St. Barbatus, Bishop of Benevento, half-length, as a seventh-century bishop without a mitre: a white alb under a full, bell-shaped deep-green chasuble; in his right hand, raised a little, a plain golden chalice (the golden viper of the Lombards melted down for the altar), in his left a plain wooden pastoral staff. Behind him, Benevento: the white marble Arch of Trajan and the city's walls and red roofs on their hill, and down by the river the stump and felled trunk of a great walnut tree, the tree the people had worshipped, under a bright, clearing sky. Fervent and warm-hearted; no serpent, no lettering.
face: A Samnite Italian of about sixty-five with a ruddy, sun-browned complexion and a BROAD face with a wide, FLAT-TOPPED, low forehead — a LARGE, FLESHY, BULBOUS nose, small, bright, laughing black eyes set in a web of creases, thick, bushy, straight black-and-grey brows, full, rosy cheeks, a wide, mobile mouth; grey hair cropped round the head; a GREAT, BUSHY, salt-and-pepper beard spreading WIDE over the chest; the gaze eager, as of a preacher about to speak.

subject: Sts. Romanus and Lupicinus, brothers and abbots of Condat in the Jura, half-length side by side. Romanus (left), the elder and gentler, in a plain undyed grey-brown woollen cowl with the hood lying back, holds a small closed book with a plain red cover against his breast, as his statue shows. Lupicinus (right), the stricter, in the tunic the book describes, made of the skins of beasts sewn together, with its cowl drawn up over his head, holds a wooden bowl with a crust of hard bread and a spoon. Behind them, the dark fir forest of Mount Jura at Condat, where two clear mountain rivers meet, a small clearing with wooden cells and a little chapel, and snow on the upper slopes under a cold, clear sky. Brotherly and peaceful; no lettering.
face: Two brothers who must read as different men. ROMANUS, about seventy, fair and rosy, CLEAN-SHAVEN, with a SOFT, rounded OVAL face — a smooth, rounded forehead, a LONG, broad, BLUNT nose with a rounded tip, ROUND, wide-open, kindly light-brown eyes under RAISED, curved white brows that give a look of gentle wonder, full, soft cheeks, a small, smiling mouth over a small, softly rounded chin; a ring of white hair round the tonsure. LUPICINUS, about fifty-five, weathered and gaunt, with a LONG, BONY face and a strong, slightly UNDERSHOT jaw that juts a little beyond the upper lip — a straight, stern, wide mouth, a long, straight nose, DEEP-SET, piercing dark eyes under HEAVY black brows knotted by a deep vertical furrow, sunken cheeks under hard cheekbones; a short, stiff black beard shot with grey; the hood hides his hair.

subject: St. Maud (Matilda of Ringelheim), Queen of Germany, wife of Henry the Fowler and mother of Otto the Great, half-length, as a widow queen: a plain dark-violet gown, a white widow's veil and wimple close about the face under a simple gold crown; she holds out in both hands a wooden bowl of broth and a round loaf, as in the book's engraving where she serves the sick at their beds. Behind her, Quedlinburg in Saxony: the abbey church she founded above the red roofs of the town, and a green, wooded Saxon countryside, under a soft, bright sky. Warm and motherly; no lettering.
face: A Saxon matron of about sixty-five with a fair, fresh, lightly ruddy complexion and a BROAD, SQUARE, strong-boned face — a wide, low forehead, a SHORT nose with a broad, flat bridge, a PROMINENT, SQUARE jaw softening into slight jowls, small, deep-set, twinkling grey eyes in a web of laughter lines, straight, fair-grey brows, a wide, thin-lipped mouth in a kindly half-smile; hair hidden under the wimple; the gaze warm and attentive, toward the sick.

subject: St. Colette of Corbie, reformer of the Poor Clares, half-length, as in the Master of Lourinhã's panel: a coarse ASH-GREY habit girded with a white knotted Franciscan cord, a white wimple and a black veil; she holds an open prayer book in both hands, her eyes lifted from it, and a slender ray of light falls on her from the upper corner, as in the book's engraving of her at prayer in her cell. Behind her, Corbie in Picardy: her small anchoress's cell built against the flank of the parish church, the great abbey church beyond, and the wide, marshy Somme valley with poplars, under a pale northern sky. Ardent and recollected; no demons, no lettering.
face: A Picard woman of about forty-five with a pale, fine complexion and a SMALL, NARROW face with sharply defined CHEEKBONES and a small, slightly JUTTING, POINTED chin — a smooth, low forehead under the wimple, a SHORT, fine, straight nose, VERY LARGE, dark-brown eyes that seem too big for the face, fine, straight dark brows, faint hollows under the cheekbones, a small, firm, closed mouth; hair hidden; the gaze intense and burning, lifted toward the light.

subject: St. David, monk and Bishop of Menevia, half-length, preaching at the synod of Brefi, as a sixth-century Welsh monk-bishop without a mitre: a rough, undyed cream woollen cowl over a plain white tunic, a leather belt; a plain wooden staff with a curved head in his left hand, his right hand raised as he preaches; a WHITE DOVE settled on his right shoulder. He stands on a green rise of ground, and below it, small, a crowd of Welsh folk listening; behind, the rolling green hills and stone walls of Ceredigion and a small stone church, under a clear, luminous sky with a break of sunlight. Fervent and ascetic; no leek, no lettering.
face: A Briton of about seventy, lean and weathered by the sea wind, with a fair, ruddy complexion and a BROAD, UPRIGHT RECTANGULAR face whose most striking feature is a HEAVY, OVERHANGING BROW RIDGE — small, bright, sea-grey eyes set DEEP in its shadow, thick, straight white brows, a SHORT, BROAD nose with a FLAT bridge, wide, high cheekbones over lean cheeks, a broad, straight, thin-lipped mouth open a little as he speaks, a firm, SQUARE chin; the front of the head shaved back to a line from ear to ear in the old insular monk's tonsure, the white hair behind it falling straight to the collar; a SHORT, close-cropped white beard following the square jaw; the gaze fiery and direct, out over the crowd.

subject: St. Euphrasia, the noble girl of Constantinople who became a nun in a monastery of Egypt, half-length: a plain, undyed brown woollen habit and a dark-brown veil over a white head-cloth; she carries in her arms against her breast a rough, heavy block of pale stone, the penance her abbess set her, as in the book's engraving, and hanging at her breast a small painted wooden image of Christ, the one she kissed when she gave herself to Him. Behind her, the Egyptian desert: the low mud-brick walls and domed cells of the monastery, a few palms and scattered blocks of stone, as in the engraving, under a hot, pale-gold sky. Humble and cheerful; no lettering.
face: A young Greek noblewoman of about twenty-two with a pale olive complexion and a LONG, SLENDER NECK and a NARROW, oblong face under a notably HIGH, ROUNDED forehead — a fine, straight nose with a HIGH, narrow bridge, large, heavy-lashed dark almond eyes set rather CLOSE together, straight, fine dark brows, a long, smooth cheek line, a small, full mouth with a slight, content smile, a small, rounded chin; hair hidden under the veil; the gaze simple and happy, lowered toward the stone.

subject: St. Cunegundes, Empress, wife of St. Henry, half-length, in Ottonian imperial dress: a long-sleeved deep-blue gown with a jewelled gold band at the neck, a crimson mantle clasped at the breast, a white veil falling to the shoulders under a gold imperial crown set with pearls and coloured stones; she holds a small model of a church in her right hand, as founder of Bamberg, as the portal of Bamberg Cathedral shows her, and with her left hand points gently toward it; at the lower edge beside her, a single plain iron ploughshare lying cool and harmless on the ground, the sign of her ordeal. Behind her, the Franconian town of Bamberg with the stone cathedral she and Henry founded rising above its roofs, and green fields, under a bright, clear sky. Pure and serene; no fire, no lettering.
face: A Luxembourg countess of about forty with a fair, clear complexion and a softly TRIANGULAR face — a BROAD, smooth, high forehead and wide-set cheekbones tapering in straight lines to a NARROW, POINTED chin; a SHORT, straight nose; LARGE, prominent, pale-blue eyes set FAR APART under very HIGH, thin, arched fair brows that give a look of calm candour; a small, full, bow-shaped mouth; fair hair in two long plaits falling beside the neck from under the veil; the gaze clear and untroubled, toward us.

subject: The Forty Martyrs of Sebaste, Roman soldiers of Armenia, on the frozen pond on a winter night, composed for the arched window: the four nearest half-length in the foreground, the rest a close company of small, haloed figures standing behind them on the ice, all stripped to plain white linen loincloths, arms crossed on their breasts or lifted in prayer; above them, in a break of golden light in the dark-blue sky, small angels descend with a row of golden crowns. At one side on the shore a small, warm-lit bathhouse, and in front of it a soldier guard in a red cloak and bronze helmet (Aglaius) unclasping his cloak to join them. Snow on the ground, a pale winter moon, the snowy hills of Armenia beyond. Steadfast and luminous; the bodies modest and unhurt, no wounds, no fire, no lettering.
face: Four principal figures, each a different man. (1) Centre front, THE YOUNGEST: about eighteen, BEARDLESS, with a warm, light-olive complexion and a SMALL, NARROW, heart-shaped face — a short, straight nose, very large, dark eyes lifted to the crowns, fine arched brows, a small mouth; short, straight black hair. (2) Left: an old soldier of about sixty, BALD, with a BROAD, SQUARE, heavy-jawed face, a short, BROKEN, flattened nose, small, deep-set grey eyes under bristling grey brows, and a ROUNDED white beard. (3) Right: a grey-haired man of about fifty with a LONG, NARROW face, a long, thin, hooked nose, hollow cheeks, deep-set dark eyes, and a POINTED grey beard. (4) Behind them, the guard Aglaius: about thirty-five, with a WIDE, flat-cheeked face, a strong straight nose, level black brows, a black moustache and short black stubble, looking up in wonder at the crowns. The small figures behind: varied ages, some bearded, some beardless.

subject: St. Eulogius, priest of Córdoba and head of its school, who wrote in prison his Exhortation to Martyrdom, half-length, as a ninth-century Mozarabic priest: a white linen alb and a dark-red chasuble of simple cut; in his left hand a bound book with a plain leather cover held against his breast, in his right a green martyr's palm. Behind him, Córdoba on the Guadalquivir: the long arches of the Roman bridge over the broad, slow river, the walls and white houses of the city with a few palms, under a clear, golden Andalusian sky. Gentle and firm; no sword, no lettering.
face: A Hispano-Roman of about forty-five with a warm, sun-browned olive complexion and a WIDE face with a LOW, BROAD forehead — the crown BALD with a fringe of short black hair, a STRONG, AQUILINE, sharply HOOKED nose, WIDE, FLAT cheekbones, small, bright, kindly dark eyes crinkled at the corners, thick, straight black brows, a wide, gentle mouth; a dense, SHORT black beard cut SQUARE at the chin, touched with grey; the gaze warm and encouraging, toward us.

subject: St. Albinus, abbot of Tintillant and Bishop of Angers, half-length, as a sixth-century Gallo-Roman bishop without a mitre: a white alb under a full, bell-shaped, deep-violet chasuble; a plain wooden pastoral staff in his left arm; with his right hand he gives a round loaf to a small, barefoot poor child who reaches up at the lower edge, as in the book's engraving, where he gives alms to the poor at a church door. Behind him, Roman Angers on the broad river Maine: its old stone walls and a small early church, boats on the river and green water meadows, under a soft, silvery western sky. Humble and gentle; no lettering.
face: A Breton Gallo-Roman of about eighty, CLEAN-SHAVEN, with a pale, soft, pink complexion and a PEAR-SHAPED face — NARROW temples and a narrowish, high, lined forehead widening down to FULL, soft, heavy JOWLS and a broad, soft double chin; a LONG, THICK, straight nose with a rounded tip; small, gentle, deep-set brown eyes with heavy pouches beneath, lowered in humility; sparse, faint white brows; a small mouth with a soft, full lower lip; a thin ring of white hair round a bald crown; the gaze modest and kind, down toward the child.

subject: Sts. Adrian and Eubulus, two Christians of Palestine who came to Caesarea to visit the confessors in prison, half-length side by side, in plain travellers' dress of the early fourth century: Adrian (left) in a rust-brown woollen tunic with a grey travelling cloak over one shoulder, a traveller's staff in his hand and a green martyr's palm; Eubulus (right) in an undyed linen tunic with a blue-grey cloak, holding a green palm and a small cloth bundle of bread for the prisoners. Behind them, the arched stone gate of Caesarea Maritima, where they confessed their faith, and beyond it Herod's great harbour with its moles and ships on a bright blue sea, under a clear Mediterranean sky. Candid and fearless; no soldiers, no beasts, no wounds, no lettering.
face: Two clearly different young men of Palestine with warm olive-brown skin. ADRIAN (left): about thirty, with a COMPACT, ROUND-TOPPED head and a BROAD, SHORT face — PROMINENT, round, high cheekbones, a SHORT, broad nose with a slightly flattened tip, narrow, dark almond eyes that turn up at the outer corners, thick, straight black brows, a wide, full mouth; short, tight black curls; a SHORT, ROUNDED black beard; his gaze bold, toward us. EUBULUS (right): about twenty-two, with a LONG, THIN, bony face — a high, narrow forehead, a LONG nose with a pronounced HUMP, large, soft, dark eyes under softly arched brows, lean cheeks, a small mouth, a LONG, narrow chin; straight black hair falling over the forehead; only a faint DOWN of first beard on the lip and chin; his gaze gentle, turned toward Adrian.

subject: St. Simplicius, Bishop of Rome in the years the Western Empire fell, half-length, as a fifth-century pope without a tiara: a white tunic under a full, bell-shaped IVORY-WHITE chasuble with a narrow gold border, and over it the white woollen pallium with small black crosses; in his left hand a closed Gospel book bound in plain red leather, his right hand raised in blessing. Behind him, fifth-century Rome at evening: the long roof and atrium of Old St. Peter's, where he was buried, the grey walls of the city and the Tiber, under a sky clearing after a storm. Steadfast and fatherly; no tiara, no lettering.
face: A Roman of Tivoli of about sixty-five, CLEAN-SHAVEN in the Roman manner, with a warm olive complexion and a BROAD, POWERFUL head — a WIDE, FLAT forehead, a BIG, fleshy Roman nose with a STRONG HUMP at the bridge, heavy-lidded, shrewd dark eyes under thick, LEVEL black-and-grey brows, broad, flat cheeks cut by two deep vertical creases, a WIDE, full-lipped mouth, and a BROAD, JUTTING chin; short grey hair combed forward in a straight Roman fringe; the gaze steady and comforting, toward us.

subject: St. Abraham Kidunaia, hermit and priest of Edessa, and his niece St. Mary, half-length side by side, as in the book's engraving where he stands at the door of his cell and she kneels at hers: Abraham (left) in a coarse dark-brown hair-cloth tunic and a black monk's mantle, his right hand raised to bless, his left on the rough doorpost of his walled-up stone cell with its small window; Mary (right), come home a penitent, in a plain grey-blue woollen gown and a dark-violet veil over her head, her hands folded at her breast, her head a little bowed. Behind them the bare, stony hills outside Edessa, a second small cell of rough stone beside the first, and far off the walls of the city, under a clear dawn sky. Tender and full of hope; modest, no lettering.
face: Two clearly different Syrians with warm olive-brown skin. ABRAHAM (left): about sixty-five, with a LONG, NARROW face and a PROMINENT, KNOBBY CHIN that juts forward below a lean jaw — a high, lined forehead, large, dark, heavy-lidded eyes under thin, curved grey brows, a long, thin, straight nose, a wide, thin-lipped mouth; bald crown with grey-black hair falling straight to the shoulders; a THIN grey-black beard trimmed SHORT along the jaw so that the knobbed chin shows; the gaze grave and gentle, on Mary. MARY (right): about twenty-seven, with a ROUND, SOFT face — a broad, smooth brow, wide-set, large, dark eyes wet with tears, straight dark brows, a short nose with a rounded tip, full cheeks, a small, full mouth, a small, round chin; dark hair hidden under the veil; the gaze lowered in contrition.

subject: St. Catharine of Sweden, daughter of St. Bridget and first abbess of Vadstena, half-length, in the Bridgettine habit: a grey woollen habit and mantle, a white wimple, a black veil, and over it the white linen band of the 'Crown of the Five Holy Wounds' with its five small red marks; she holds a closed book of the Rule against her breast with her left hand, and her right rests on the neck of a gentle red HIND standing close beside her, her attribute. Behind her, Vadstena: the long grey stone abbey church on the shore of the broad, blue Lake Vättern, birch trees and a green Swedish shore, under a clear, pale northern sky. Prudent and serene; no lettering.
face: A Swedish noblewoman of about forty-five with a fair, clear, lightly freckled complexion and a SHORT, BROAD, HEART-SHAPED face — a WIDE forehead and WIDE, rounded cheekbones narrowing to a small, neat chin; LARGE, round, clear grey-blue eyes set wide under softly rounded fair brows; a small, straight nose; a SHORT upper lip over a small, full, gently smiling mouth; hair hidden under the wimple; the gaze calm and kindly, toward us.

subject: St. Gontran, Merovingian King of Orleans and Burgundy, half-length, as a sixth-century Frankish king: a long-sleeved tunic of deep crimson with a gold-embroidered border, a dark-blue cloak fastened at the shoulder with a round gold brooch, a simple open gold circlet crown; he holds out a round loaf in his right hand to a thin sick man in a grey blanket who reaches up from the lower edge, as in the book's engraving where he goes among the sick; his left hand on his breast. Behind him, Chalon-sur-Saône, his capital: the broad Saône with a stone bridge, the small church of Saint-Marcel he founded, and Burgundian vineyards on low hills, under a soft, golden sky. Merciful and penitent; no weapons, no lettering.
face: A Frank of about sixty with a fair, ruddy complexion and a LARGE, FULL, ROUND face — a broad forehead, FULL, heavy cheeks sagging into soft JOWLS and a DOUBLE CHIN, a SHORT, THICK, straight nose, deep-set, pale-blue eyes under HEAVY, DROOPING lids, red-rimmed as from weeping, thick fair-grey brows, a small, full mouth; LONG, fair-grey hair, parted in the middle and falling PAST THE SHOULDERS, the mark of the Merovingian kings; a drooping fair-grey MOUSTACHE and a short, rounded beard; the gaze compassionate and sorrowful, down toward the sick man.

subject: St. Victorian, Proconsul of Carthage, with the two brothers who suffered in the same persecution, half-length side by side: Victorian (centre) as a late-Roman high official, a long-sleeved white tunic with dark-purple bands and a long cloak of deep crimson fastened at the right shoulder with a gold brooch; his right hand pressed to his breast, his left holding a green martyr's palm, as when he gave the king his answer; the two brothers (left and right, a little behind him) in plain belted tunics of undyed linen and brown wool, each holding a green palm, one with an arm about the other's shoulders. Behind them, Roman Carthage: white colonnades and the hill of Byrsa, the round harbour with ships, and the blue Gulf of Tunis, under a bright African sky. Steadfast and luminous; no rack, no wounds, no lettering.
face: Three clearly different men of Roman Africa with warm olive-to-bronze skin.
