VICTORIAN (centre): about fifty, CLEAN-SHAVEN, with a LONG, STRONG face and a LARGE, HIGH-BRIDGED, straight nose — deep NASOLABIAL folds from the nose to the corners of a firm, wide mouth, heavy-lidded, level dark eyes under thick straight black-grey brows, flat cheeks, a long, square chin; short grey hair combed forward in the late-Roman way; the gaze calm and unbending, toward us. THE ELDER BROTHER (left): about thirty, with a BROAD, ROUND face, full cheeks, a short, wide nose, round dark eyes, a short curly black beard; short tight black curls. THE YOUNGER BROTHER (right): about twenty, BEARDLESS, with a NARROW, TRIANGULAR face — a wide brow tapering to a small pointed chin, a fine straight nose, large, shining dark eyes; wavy black hair; looking up at his brother.

subject: St. Wulfran, Archbishop of Sens who resigned his see to preach to the Frisians as a poor missionary priest, half-length: a plain, undyed woollen travelling cloak over a white alb, a simple wooden cross-staff in his left hand; his right hand rests on the head of a small, fair-haired Frisian child in a rough tunic who clings to his cloak, one of the children he saved from drowning. Behind him, the flat coast of Friesland: green salt-marsh, a village of long thatched houses on a raised mound, a small new wooden church with a cross, and the grey North Sea under a wide, windy sky with a break of sunlight. Compassionate and bold; no gibbet, no idols, no lettering.
face: A Frank of about sixty with a fair, weathered complexion and a LONG face dominated by a LONG, BROAD, gently DROOPING nose with a big, soft, rounded tip — small, DEEP-SET, warm brown eyes under BUSHY brown-grey brows that ARCH UP toward the centre in an earnest, pleading look, a smooth forehead, lean cheeks, a small mouth, a short, slightly RECEDING chin under a SHORT, FULL, CURLY brown-grey beard; brown-grey hair round a small monk's tonsure; the gaze earnest and compassionate, down toward the child.

subject: St. Ludger, missionary of the Frisians and Saxons and first Bishop of Münster, half-length, as a Carolingian bishop: a white alb under a full, bell-shaped chasuble of deep BLUE with a narrow gold orphrey, bare-headed; in his left arm a small model of a stone church, in his right a closed book of the Gospels, as Wikipedia says he is shown; at the lower edge a grey goose, his later attribute, looks up at him. Behind him, the Ruhr valley at Werden, his abbey: a small Carolingian stone church and cloister by a wooded river, green Westphalian hills beyond, under a soft, bright sky. Recollected and firm; no lettering.
face: A Frisian of about sixty-five with a pale, fair complexion and a LONG, OBLONG head — a very HIGH, smooth forehead running up into a tonsured crown with a thin ring of short white hair, very SMALL, pale-blue eyes set CLOSE together under faint fair brows, a LONG, THIN, straight nose, LARGE, PROTRUDING EARS, a long, clean-shaven upper lip over a SMALL, PRIM, closed mouth, a small, rounded chin; CLEAN-SHAVEN; the gaze inward and steady, a little lowered.

subject: Sts. Jonas and Barachisius, brothers of Beth-Asa who went to encourage the Christians condemned under King Sapor II, half-length side by side, in fourth-century Persian dress: Jonas (left) in a knee-length belted tunic of deep blue with a woven border and a short cloak of rust red, a green martyr's palm in his hand; Barachisius (right) in a long, belted tunic of ochre wool and a dark cloak, a green palm in one hand, the other raised toward heaven. Behind them a Mesopotamian town of flat-roofed mud-brick houses, a few date palms, and a winter plain with a thin skin of ice on a pond under a pale sky, where the confessors were held. Steadfast and joyful; no torments, no fire, no lettering.
face: Two clearly different Persians with warm, light-brown skin. JONAS (left): about twenty-five, with a SQUARE-JAWED, BROAD young face — thick, straight black brows almost MEETING over the nose, large, dark almond eyes, a straight, strong nose, full lips, a firm, square chin; thick, wavy black hair to the nape; only a faint shadow of first beard; the gaze bright and eager, toward us. BARACHISIUS (right): about forty, with a LONG, GAUNT, hollow-cheeked face — a high, narrow forehead, a large AQUILINE nose, deep-set, dark eyes under heavy lids, prominent cheekbones, a narrow mouth; brown hair cut short; a long, straight, THIN brown beard falling in stiff, sparse strands; the gaze lifted, fervent.

subject: St. John Climacus, abbot of Mount Sinai and author of the Ladder, half-length, in the dress of a Sinai monk: a dark-brown habit and a black mantle, the monk's black hood down on his shoulders; he holds an open scroll in his left hand and with his right points up toward a slender golden LADDER that rises behind him into a luminous sky, small monks in black climbing its rungs toward the light, as in the Sinai icon of the Ladder. Behind him, the red-granite peaks of Sinai and the walled monastery in the valley below, under a clear, golden desert sky. Wise and luminous; no demons, no falling figures, no lettering.
face: A man of about seventy-five with a weathered, olive complexion and a LEAN, BONY, LONG RECTANGULAR face — a very high, lined forehead with two deep VERTICAL furrows between the brows, LARGE, luminous grey eyes under heavy lids, a long, straight nose ending in a BROAD tip, lean cheeks over strong cheekbones; bald crown with short curling grey hair at the sides; a LARGE, FULL, grey-white beard, broad and cut SQUARE across the bottom at mid-chest; the gaze deep and teaching, toward us.

subject: St. Zachary, Bishop of Rome, half-length, as an eighth-century pope without a tiara: a white tunic under a full, bell-shaped chasuble of deep MOSS-GREEN silk with a narrow gold border, and over it the white woollen pallium with small black crosses; his right hand rests in blessing on the shoulder of a young, dark-haired freed slave in a plain undyed tunic who looks up at him, one of those he bought back from the merchants, as in the book's engraving; at the lower edge a pair of opened iron fetters lies on the paving stones. Behind him, eighth-century Rome: the old Lateran palace he restored, with its arcaded loggia, and a small portico lit by oil lamps, the Aventine and the Tiber beyond, under a warm, golden evening sky. Meek and fatherly; no tiara, no lettering.
face: A Greek of Calabria of about seventy with a warm, sallow olive complexion and a SOFT, LONG face whose features all SLOPE GENTLY DOWNWARD — brows and outer corners of the eyes drooping in a mild, sorrowful slant, large, moist, dark-brown eyes with heavy upper lids, a LONG, SLENDER nose whose tip turns slightly DOWN, cheekbones set high with soft hollows beneath, a small, soft, closed mouth with downturned corners easing into a faint smile, a small, round chin; short, thin white hair combed forward; a SHORT, soft, ROUNDED white beard close to the jaw; the gaze tender, down toward the freed youth.

subject: St. John of Egypt, the hermit of Lycopolis who spoke with his visitors through a window, half-length, framed in the small rough-cut window of his cell in the cliff, as in the book's engraving: a coarse, undyed palm-fibre tunic and a dark goat-hair cloak; with his right hand he blesses a small clay flask of oil held up to him on the sill, for the sick; his left rests on the stone of the sill. Around the window the golden-ochre limestone of the cliff, and below and beyond, small, the green strip of the Nile valley at Lycopolis with palms and sycamores, the broad river, and the pale desert beyond, under a hot, clear sky. Joyful and holy; no demons, no lettering.
face: A Copt of about ninety with deep-brown, sun-dark skin and a small, ELFIN, TRIANGULAR face — a BROAD, BULGING, BALD forehead and wide temples tapering sharply to a SMALL, POINTED chin; LARGE, prominent ears; small, BRIGHT, black eyes deep in a web of laughter lines; a small, sharp, HOOKED nose; a WIDE, thin-lipped mouth in a broad, cheerful smile; a SHORT, thin, wispy white beard that leaves the pointed chin's shape clear; the gaze merry and piercing, toward us.

subject: St. John the Almoner, Patriarch of Alexandria, half-length, as a seventh-century Byzantine patriarch: a white sticharion under a full phelonion of deep PLUM-VIOLET silk and a white omophorion with large dark crosses over his shoulders; he sits on a plain stone bench before the church, as on the Wednesdays and Fridays when he heard the poor, and with his right hand drops coins into the cupped hands of a thin young mother holding a child at the lower edge, his 'lords', the poor; his left hand holds a small leather purse. Behind him, Alexandria: the harbour with a merchant ship under sail loaded with sacks of grain, and the tall, stepped Pharos lighthouse at the harbour mouth, white colonnades and palms, under a warm, bright Egyptian sky. Merciful and joyful; no lettering.
face: A Cypriot Greek of about sixty with a warm, ruddy olive complexion and a WIDE, SOFT face — broad at the temples, FULL, rounded, rosy cheeks, a SHORT, straight nose with a ROUND, FLESHY tip, small, bright, CLOSE-SET, twinkling brown eyes deep in laughter creases, bushy white brows lifted at their inner ends, a small, smiling mouth; a bald crown with short white hair curling above the ears; a LONG, flowing, WAVY white beard to mid-breast, rounded at the end, undivided; the gaze merry and tender, down toward the mother and child.

subject: St. Herman Joseph, canon of the Premonstratensian abbey of Steinfeld, half-length, in the all-white Premonstratensian habit: a white woollen tunic, a white scapular and a white shoulder-cape, bare-headed with his tonsure; kneeling on one knee at the left, he holds up a small red APPLE in both hands toward a Romanesque painted wooden statue of the Virgin and Child enthroned on a stone pedestal at the right, as the boy offered his apple to Our Lady's image in the church at Cologne. Around them, the round-arched Romanesque interior of St. Maria im Kapitol in Cologne, its pale stone piers and a curved apse lit by small arched windows, candles glowing at the pedestal, under warm, golden light. Childlike and trusting; the statue is a statue, not a living figure; no lettering.
face: A Rhinelander of about twenty-five, visibly a young man and not a boy, CLEAN-SHAVEN, with a fair, fresh complexion and a SHORT, ROUND face under a prominent, ROUNDED, BOSSED forehead — a WIDE, low, flat nose bridge and a SMALL, slightly UPTURNED nose, very LARGE, wide-set, clear brown eyes under soft, high-arched brows, round, full cheeks, a small, soft rosebud mouth, a small, round chin; thick, dark-brown CURLY hair round the tonsure; the gaze trusting and loving, lifted to the image. The statue's face: a Romanesque carved face, long, calm and stylised, painted, with a gilt crown.

subject: St. Hugh, Bishop of Grenoble, half-length, as an old twelfth-century bishop: a white alb and a full, bell-shaped chasuble of soft ROSE-VIOLET silk with a narrow gold orphrey, a low white mitre, a plain wooden crozier in the crook of his left arm; in both hands, held open before him, a small book of prayers, for his love of 'holy solitude, prayer, and pious reading'. Behind him, Grenoble: the city's walls and the cathedral of Notre-Dame by the broad, grey-green river Isère, with the steep, wooded foothills of the Alps close behind, under a soft, pearly morning sky. Humble, recollected, longing for solitude; no stars, no monks, no lettering.
face: A Dauphinois of about seventy, CLEAN-SHAVEN, with a fair, finely wrinkled complexion and a SMALL, delicate, APPLE-ROUND face — a high, rounded, bald dome with a thin fringe of fine white hair, very LARGE, round, clear blue-grey eyes under faint, HIGH-ARCHED white brows, a SMALL, short BUTTON nose, a noticeably LONG, smooth UPPER LIP over a small, soft mouth, softly rounded cheeks webbed with fine lines, a small, round chin; the gaze gentle and a little wistful, lifted from the page.

subject: St. Mary of Egypt, the penitent of the desert beyond the Jordan, half-length, in old age: wrapped entirely, from the shoulders down and over her head, in the worn, dark-brown woollen mantle the monk Zosimus gave her, held closed at the breast with her left hand; in her right hand, three small round loaves of bread, her attribute. Behind her, the desert east of the Jordan: bare, tawny hills, a few tamarisks, the green thread of the river with reeds, and far off on the other bank, small, the monastery of St. John the Baptist, under a pale, clear evening sky with the first star. Serene and at peace; fully and modestly covered, no lettering.
face: An Egyptian woman of great age, about seventy-five, burned a deep brown by the desert sun, lean and serene, with a LONG, NARROW face of strong, SCULPTED bone — a high, narrow forehead, very HIGH, PROMINENT cheekbones with deep HOLLOWS beneath, LARGE, dark, luminous, DEEP-SET eyes, straight dark-grey brows, a STRONG, LONG, STRAIGHT nose, a wide, closed, peaceful mouth, a LONG, firm chin; long white hair showing loose under the edge of the mantle; the gaze lowered, full of peace.

subject: St. Hegesippus, the Jewish Christian of Jerusalem who travelled through the churches to Rome and wrote the first history of the Church, half-length, as a second-century traveller: a long, undyed linen tunic and a heavy dark-blue woollen travelling cloak, a tall walking staff in his right hand; in his left arm a bundle of five rolled scrolls tied with a cord, his five books; as in the book's engraving he stands among ancient stones. Behind him, a Roman road lined with tombs and umbrella pines leading to the walls and hills of Rome, where he lived twenty years, and far off the pale hills of the East he came from, under a soft, golden afternoon sky. Wise and faithful; no lettering.
face: A Jew of Judaea of about seventy with a warm, olive-brown complexion and a TALL, HIGH-DOMED head with WIDE temples, the face narrowing to a long jaw — very LARGE, dark, slightly PROTRUDING eyes under HEAVY, arched black-and-grey brows that lift in the centre in a searching look, a LONG, FLESHY nose with a WIDE, ROUNDED tip and full nostrils, HIGH, rounded cheekbones, a full lower lip; thick grey-black hair in tight CURLS round a receding hairline; a long, full, CURLY grey-black beard, rounded at the end; the gaze keen and searching, as of one who has seen many churches.

subject: St. Bademus, rich noble of Bethlapeta who founded a monastery and ruled it as abbot, half-length, in the dress of a Persian monk of the fourth century: a coarse black woollen habit and a black hood down on his shoulders, a plain wooden cross on a cord at his breast; he holds a green martyr's palm in his right hand and an open book of the Psalms in his left, as in the book's engraving where he kneels at his reading-desk. Behind him, the plain of Khuzistan at Bethlapeta: a small monastery of mud brick with a courtyard and date palms, fields of green barley, and the blue foothills of the Zagros far off, under a clear, luminous sky. Joyful and patient; no sword, no chains, no wounds, no lettering.
face: A Persian of about fifty with a warm, light-brown complexion and a WIDE, HEAVY-JAWED face with SQUARE, fleshy cheeks — a strong, BROAD, STRAIGHT nose with FLARED nostrils, heavy-lidded, long almond eyes that TILT DOWN at the outer corners, thick, straight black brows set LOW, a full, wide, calm mouth; black hair cut short, streaked with grey; a THICK black beard shot with grey, cut ROUNDED at the chin; the gaze calm, joyful and inward.

subject: St. Benjamin, deacon of the Church in Persia, half-length, as a young fifth-century deacon: a long white linen tunic with narrow sleeves, a deacon's stole of deep crimson over his left shoulder, an open book of the Gospels held up in his left hand, his right hand raised, open, as one announcing Christ, as when he told the king he would miss no opportunity to preach. Behind him, a Persian town of flat-roofed mud-brick houses with a small, plain church among them, date palms and a broad, dusty river plain, under a clear, hot, pale-gold sky. Ardent and young; no reeds, no stake, no wounds, no lettering.
face: A Persian of about twenty-eight with a warm, light-brown complexion and a SOFT face with smooth, ROUND cheeks that fall away to a SHORT, gently RECEDING chin under a LONG, HIGH-BRIDGED, ARCHED nose — a smooth, rounded forehead, LARGE, dark, heavy-lidded almond eyes set WIDE apart, fine, HIGH-ARCHED black brows, a small, full, bow-shaped mouth; thick, glossy black hair in loose waves to the ears; only a first thin moustache and a sparse down of beard along the jaw; the gaze candid and ardent, toward us.

subject: St. Perpetuus, Bishop of Tours, half-length, as a fifth-century Gallo-Roman bishop: a white tunic with narrow dark-red bands under a full, bell-shaped chasuble of deep OCHRE-GOLD wool, a white pallium-like stole, bare-headed; in his left hand a sealed parchment roll, his will making the poor his heirs, and on a cord about his neck a small gold cross with relics, the cross he left to his sister; his right hand opens in welcome toward a poor old woman in a grey shawl at the lower edge. Behind him, Tours on the Loire: the new timber-roofed basilica he built over the tomb of St. Martin, of pale stone with a small bell-cote, the broad, shining river with sandbanks and poplars, under a soft, silvery sky. Generous and gentle; no lettering.
face: A Gallo-Roman of senatorial family, about sixty-five, with a pale, olive-tinged complexion and a LONG, OVAL face with HEAVY, HOODED eyelids that give the eyes a half-closed, gentle look — a broad, FLAT, low nose bridge widening to a broad nose, soft, sloping cheeks, a FULL, projecting LOWER LIP, a rounded, fleshy chin; thinning grey hair combed forward; a SHORT, close-trimmed grey beard following the jaw; the gaze mild and generous, down toward the poor woman.

subject: St. Celestine I, Bishop of Rome, half-length, as a fifth-century pope without a tiara: a white tunic under a full, bell-shaped chasuble of deep RED-BROWN silk with a narrow gold border, the white woollen pallium with small black crosses over it; in his left hand a folded letter with a hanging seal, one of those he sent to the Council of Ephesus and into Gaul; his right hand raised in blessing, sending out his missionaries. Behind him, fifth-century Rome on the Aventine: the new basilica of Santa Sabina with its plain brick walls and tall round-arched windows, cypresses, and the Tiber below, and on the horizon a small ship under sail toward the north, for Palladius and Germanus, under a clear, watchful morning sky. Vigilant and fatherly; no tiara, no lettering.
face: A Roman of about seventy with a warm olive complexion and a BROAD-JAWED, heavy-boned head whose centre is a MASSIVE, HOOKED Roman nose — a LOW, heavy BROW RIDGE with thick, STRAIGHT white brows in one level line, small, bright, deep-set dark eyes, flat cheeks cut by deep vertical creases, a thin, firm, straight mouth; short white hair combed forward; a SHORT, crisp, tightly CURLED white beard close to the jaw; the gaze vigilant, straight toward us.

subject: St. Richard, Bishop of Chichester, half-length, as a thirteenth-century English bishop: a white alb and a full chasuble of deep GREEN with a gold orphrey, a low white mitre with gold bands, a simple crozier in his left hand; with his right hand he gives a round loaf to a small, fair-haired peasant child in a patched brown tunic at the lower edge, for 'young and old loved St. Richard' and he gave all he had to feed the poor. Behind him, Chichester: the grey Norman cathedral with its round-arched nave and low central tower (no spire), the little city's roofs, green Sussex fields and the South Downs, under a fresh, bright English spring sky. Kindly and firm; no lettering.
face: An Englishman of about fifty-five, CLEAN-SHAVEN, with a fair, fresh, lightly freckled countryman's complexion reddened by the weather and a BROAD, SHORT, OPEN face — a wide, flat forehead, WIDE, rounded cheekbones, a SHORT, UPTURNED snub nose, WIDE-SET, bright light-blue eyes creased with smile lines under sandy brows, a WIDE, thin-lipped, smiling mouth, a SHORT, ROUNDED chin; sandy-red hair going grey, cut short around the tonsure; the gaze frank and warm, down toward the child.

subject: St. Perpetuus, Bishop of Tours, half-length, as a fifth-century Gallo-Roman bishop: a white tunic with narrow dark-red bands under a full, bell-shaped chasuble of deep OCHRE-GOLD wool, a white pallium-like stole, bare-headed; in his left hand a sealed parchment roll, his will making the poor his heirs, and on a cord about his neck a small gold cross with relics, the cross he left to his sister; his right hand opens in welcome toward a poor old woman in a grey shawl at the lower edge. Behind him, Tours on the Loire: the new timber-roofed basilica he built over the tomb of St. Martin, of pale stone with a small bell-cote, the broad, shining river with sandbanks and poplars, under a soft, silvery sky. Generous and gentle; no lettering.
face: A Gallo-Roman of senatorial family, about sixty-five, with a pale, olive-tinged complexion and a LONG, OVAL face with HEAVY, HOODED eyelids that give the eyes a half-closed, gentle look — a broad, FLAT, low nose bridge widening to a broad nose, soft, sloping cheeks, a FULL, projecting LOWER LIP, a rounded, fleshy chin; thinning grey hair combed forward; a SHORT, close-trimmed grey beard following the jaw; the gaze mild and generous, down toward the poor woman.

subject: St. Benezet, the shepherd boy of Avignon, half-length: a short, belted tunic of undyed brown wool, a rough sheepskin cape over his shoulders, a shepherd's crook in his left hand; on his right shoulder, steadied with his right hand, a great squared block of pale stone, the first stone of his bridge, carried without strain. Behind him, the broad, fast, blue-green Rhône with the first stone arches of a bridge rising from the water, masons' scaffolding on them, and the rock above Avignon with a small Romanesque church and the town walls; a few sheep grazing on the near bank, under a bright, windy Provençal sky. Simple and trusting; no crowds, no lettering.
face: A Provençal shepherd boy of about fifteen, visibly a boy, beardless, sun-browned and lightly FRECKLED across the nose, with a NARROW, LONG, BONY young face tapering to a small, POINTED chin — a high, narrow forehead, a thin, straight nose, very LARGE, clear hazel eyes, thin straight brows bleached pale by the sun, slightly hollow cheeks, a wide, thin mouth in a faint smile, rather LARGE ears standing out from the head; short, straight, sun-bleached straw-coloured hair cut round in a fringe; the gaze open and earnest, toward us.

subject: St. Julius, Bishop of Rome, half-length, as a fourth-century pope: a white tunic and a full, bell-shaped chasuble of deep crimson, a narrow white pallium with small black crosses over his shoulders; in his right hand a folded letter sealed with a disc of red wax, his letter to the bishops of the East in defence of St. Athanasius, held a little forward as if handing it to a messenger; in his left, a closed book of the Gospels bound in gold. Behind him, Rome across the Tiber: a plain, early brick basilica with a low gabled front and a small porch among red-tiled roofs, cypresses and umbrella pines, the river and an old stone bridge, under a clear, late-afternoon sky. Firm and just; no lettering.
face: A Roman of about sixty with a warm olive complexion and a face that WIDENS DOWNWARD — NARROW temples and a moderate, rounded forehead above a BROAD, BONY, ANGULAR JAW whose corners stand out clearly under the beard, so the face reads as a trapezoid, broad at the base; a long, straight nose ending in a slightly FULL, rounded tip, SMALL, ROUND, dark-brown eyes set CLOSE together under single, smoothly ARCHED dark brows, flat cheeks, a WIDE, THIN-LIPPED, straight mouth; dark-brown hair cut short in a round clerical tonsure, a SHORT, close-trimmed dark-brown beard greying at the chin that follows the angle of the jaw; the gaze steady and direct, toward us.

subject: St. Anicetus, Bishop of Rome, half-length, as a second-century pope: a white tunic and a full, bell-shaped chasuble of deep crimson, a narrow white pallium with small black crosses; a shepherd's staff with a plain curled head in his left hand, a closed book of the Gospels held against his breast with his right. Behind him, second-century Rome by the Tiber: the Aelian bridge and the great round drum of Hadrian's mausoleum across the river, with umbrella pines and cypresses on the far bank, under a warm, golden evening sky. Watchful and fatherly; no Polycarp, no wounds, no lettering.
face: A Syrian of Emesa, about sixty-five, with a warm, olive-brown complexion and a TALL, NARROW, EGG-SHAPED head, broadest across the upper face — a high, SLOPING forehead, a LONG, THIN, gently ARCHED nose with a narrow bridge, LARGE, dark, luminous eyes with HEAVY LOWER LIDS under THICK, black-and-grey brows that ARCH HIGH toward the temples, lean cheeks, NOTICEABLY FULL, wide lips; black-and-grey hair CROPPED VERY SHORT, close to the skull; a long, full, gently curling black beard streaked with grey, falling to the breast; the gaze watchful and grave, toward us.

subject: St. Hermenegild, Visigothic prince, half-length, as a young king's son of sixth-century Spain in his prison: a knee-length tunic of deep blue wool with a broad woven border, a crimson cloak fastened at the shoulder with a round gold brooch, a plain iron fetter on each wrist joined by a short chain; in his right hand a small, plain wooden cross held to his breast, in his left a martyr's palm. Behind him, the round arch of his cell opens onto Seville by night: the broad Guadalquivir, Roman walls and low towers, and from the cell a soft, clear light streaming out into the dark, as the Christians saw it on Easter night. Serene and resolute; no axe, no executioner, no crown on his head, no lettering.
face: A Visigoth of about thirty with a fair, lightly sun-browned complexion and a LONG, FLAT-CHEEKED face that ends in a STRONG, PROJECTING, rounded chin — a broad, smooth forehead, a straight nose with a LOW, FLAT bridge sitting between VERY WIDE-SET, pale green eyes, long, flat cheeks without prominent cheekbones, a BROAD mouth with thin, firm lips; thick, straight reddish-blond hair falling to the shoulders in the Gothic manner, a short, neat reddish-blond beard along the jaw; the gaze calm and far-off, lifted a little above us.

subject: St. Elphege, Archbishop of Canterbury, half-length, as an Anglo-Saxon archbishop of about 1010: a white alb and a full, bell-shaped chasuble of deep green silk with a gold orphrey, the white pallium with black crosses over it, a low white mitre; a plain gilt crozier in his left hand; in the gathered fold of the chasuble at his right side a few smooth grey stones, as he is traditionally shown. Behind him, the Thames at Greenwich: a broad, grey river with a few Danish longships with striped sails moored along the muddy bank, low green hills and a small timber church, under a pale, cloudy spring sky. Gentle and resolute; no blood, no axe, no raiders' violence, no lettering.
face: An Anglo-Saxon of about fifty-eight, CLEAN-SHAVEN, with a fair, pale complexion and a SHORT, WIDE face under a PROMINENT, ROUNDED, forward-bulging brow — WIDE-SET, heavy-lidded pale-blue eyes sheltered beneath it, light, sparse brows, a SHORT, straight nose, broad, smooth cheeks, a small, gentle mouth and a SMALL, TUCKED-IN chin; fine, fair-grey hair in a monk's crown round the tonsure, showing below the mitre; the gaze gentle and forgiving, toward us.

subject: St. Apollonius, Roman senator and philosopher, half-length, as a senator of the age of Commodus: a white tunic with the broad purple stripe of his rank, a white toga draped over his left shoulder and arm; in his left hand a rolled scroll, the defence of the faith he read before the Senate, his right hand raised, open, as one speaking calmly. Behind him, the Roman Forum: the plain brick front of the Senate house with its bronze doors, marble columns and temples, the Capitol rising beyond, under a clear morning sky. Composed and courteous, a philosopher; no sword, no lettering.
face: A Roman of about fifty with a fair olive complexion and a BROAD, SHORT, ROUND-JAWED face like an Antonine portrait bust — a wide, low forehead with the hair growing forward on it, full, rounded cheeks, a SHORT, THICK, straight nose, LARGE, slightly PROMINENT eyes under HEAVY, half-lowered upper lids, giving the dreamy, thoughtful look of the portraits of his day, soft, level brown brows, a small, full mouth; thick, dark-brown hair in short, crisp curls, a SHORT, close, curly dark-brown beard trimmed to the line of the round jaw; the gaze calm and inward, a little to the side.

subject: St. Engratia and St. Optatus, first of the eighteen martyrs of Saragossa, side by side, half-length. ENGRATIA (left, a little forward): a young noblewoman of Roman Hispania in a long gown of deep rose-red with a gold-embroidered border at the neck, a fine white travelling veil over her hair and shoulders, a martyr's palm in her right hand, her left hand on her breast. OPTATUS (right): a mature man of Roman Saragossa in a white tunic and a plain grey-brown cloak, a martyr's palm in his hand. Behind them, a little way back and small, a close group of their companions, men in plain tunics and cloaks, each holding a palm; beyond, the walls and gate of Roman Caesaraugusta on the broad river Ebro, with poplars along the bank, under a clear, bright spring sky. Serene and steadfast; no wounds, no hooks, no soldiers, no fire, no lettering.
face: Two clearly different people of Roman Hispania with warm, light-olive skin. ENGRATIA (left): a young woman of about twenty with a LONG, OVAL face and a FIRM, SQUARE-TIPPED chin — a smooth, high forehead, a STRONG, STRAIGHT, rather long Iberian nose with a HIGH bridge, large, dark-brown eyes under LOW, nearly STRAIGHT dark brows, smooth, flat cheeks, a full, grave mouth; dark-chestnut hair braided and pinned up under the veil; the gaze level and fearless, toward us. OPTATUS (right): a man of about fifty-five with a ROUND, DOMED, BALD head and a SHORT, BROAD face — a BROAD, FLAT nose, small, DEEP-SET, kindly dark eyes under thick grey brows, full cheeks, a wide mouth, SLIGHTLY PROMINENT ears; a fringe of cropped grey hair and a SHORT, CURLY grey beard; the gaze turned toward Engratia.

subject: St. Paternus, hermit and Bishop of Avranches, half-length, as an old sixth-century monk-bishop: a plain dark-brown monastic habit with a hood laid back, over it a simple bishop's chasuble of undyed cream wool with a narrow red border, a plain wooden pastoral staff with a curled head in his left hand; his right hand open, palm out, in a gesture of peace. Behind him, the coast of the Cotentin near Avranches: a wide, silvery tidal bay, dark oak forest running down to the shore, a small wooden chapel with a thatched roof at the forest's edge, and far out in the bay a lone granite rock with no buildings on it, under a soft, grey-blue sea sky. Peaceable and weathered; no temple, no idols, no lettering.
face: A Gallo-Roman of about seventy, weathered by sea wind, with a ruddy, fair complexion and a LONG, SHIELD-SHAPED face — a STRAIGHT, HORIZONTAL line of broad, FLAT cheekbones set HIGH, the sides of the face falling almost PARALLEL below them and curving into a broad, rounded chin; a very HIGH, flat forehead; NARROW, pale-grey eyes, SLANTING slightly upward at the outer corners and creased from squinting at the sea, under thin, straight white brows; a thin, long, straight nose; a small, closed mouth; thin white hair cut short round a bald crown; a LONG, NARROW, straight white beard to the breast; the gaze mild and peaceable, a little to the side.

subject: St. Soter, Bishop of Rome, half-length, as a second-century pope: a white tunic and a full, bell-shaped chasuble of deep crimson, a narrow white pallium with small black crosses; in his right hand a small leather purse of alms held out, in his left a rolled letter tied with a cord, his letter to the Church of Corinth. Behind him, the harbour of Ostia: a stone quay, a Roman merchant ship with a square sail making ready to sail east for Corinth, warehouses of red brick and a lighthouse, under a bright, breezy sky. Fatherly and generous; no lettering.
face: A Roman of Greek family from Fondi, about sixty, with a warm, light-olive complexion and a SOFT, HEART-SHAPED face — a BROAD, smooth forehead and full temples, FULL, soft, rounded cheeks tapering to a SMALL, rounded chin; very LARGE, gentle, dark-brown eyes that TURN DOWN at the outer corners under softly RAISED, curved brows, a SMALL, fine, straight nose, a small, soft mouth in a tender smile; soft, wavy silver-grey hair cut short; a MEDIUM, soft, wavy silver-grey beard, rounded at the tip; the gaze tender and fatherly, toward us.

subject: St. Marcellinus, first Bishop of Embrun, half-length, as a fourth-century missionary bishop: a white tunic, a full chasuble of warm ochre-gold wool with a narrow red border, a plain wooden pastoral staff in his left hand; his right arm extended, pointing up the valley toward the mountains, as when he sent Vincent and Domninus to preach where he could not go. Behind him, the high Alpine valley of the Durance: the rock of Embrun with a small stone chapel and a few houses on it above the green-grey river, pine-dark slopes and snow-capped peaks, under a clear, cold blue sky. Zealous and fatherly; no lettering.
face: A Berber of Africa Proconsularis, about sixty, with a warm, deep olive-bronze complexion and a LONG, FINE-BONED, NARROW face — a high forehead, a NARROW, HIGH-BRIDGED, very STRAIGHT nose, LIGHT HAZEL-GREEN eyes, striking against the dark skin, set rather deep under straight black-and-grey brows, lean cheeks with fine, sharp cheekbones, a firm mouth, a SMALL, NEAT, pointed chin; tightly curled black hair greying at the temples, cut short; a SHORT, close, curly black-and-grey beard; the gaze keen and eager, toward the mountains.

subject: St. Vitalis, a citizen of Milan martyred at Ravenna, half-length: a knee-length Roman tunic of dark green wool with narrow red bands, a heavy cloak of undyed grey-brown wool fastened on the right shoulder with a bronze brooch; a martyr's palm in his right hand, his left hand laid over his heart. Behind him, Ravenna in the Roman age: low brick walls and a gate, a canal with a flat boat among reeds, the flat marshy coast and a dark pine wood by the sea, and near the walls a single tall date palm, the place called the Palm-tree, under a wide, pale, luminous Adriatic sky. Resolute and serene; no rack, no pit, no stones, no judge, no lettering.
face: A Milanese of about fifty with a warm, light-olive complexion and a WEDGE-SHAPED face — a BROAD, SQUARE, flat forehead and wide temples, a HEAVY, STRAIGHT brow ridge, the cheeks falling in STRAIGHT lines to a NARROW, firm chin; a long, straight nose with a strong, SQUARED tip; deep-set, level, dark-grey eyes under thick, straight dark brows; a firm, narrow mouth; short, dense, dark-brown hair cropped close, greying at the temples; a SHORT, trimmed dark beard following the narrow jaw to a blunt point; the gaze steady and resolute, toward us.

subject: St. Hugh, Abbot of Cluny, half-length, as an eleventh-century Benedictine abbot: a full black monastic cowl with wide sleeves and the hood laid back, a plain gold pectoral cross, an abbot's crozier of carved wood and gilt in his left hand; in his right, held against his breast, a small, closed book of the Rule. Behind him, the abbey of Cluny in its valley in Burgundy: the long Romanesque church with its many towers and bell-turrets, part of it still in building with timber scaffolding and cranes, the monastery roofs of red tile, and gentle green hills with vineyards, under a clear, golden late-afternoon sky. Noble, serene and wise; no emperor, no crown, no lettering.
face: A Burgundian noble of about sixty, CLEAN-SHAVEN, with a fair, lightly ruddy complexion and a SQUARE-OVAL face, full-cheeked, marked by a LONG, STRAIGHT, prominent nose that runs from a HIGH ROOT between the brows with almost no dip, like a Greek statue's; a broad, smooth forehead under the tonsure; calm, heavy-lidded grey-blue eyes set level under light, straight brows; smooth, FULL cheeks; a small, firm, closed mouth; a DEEP, rounded chin; greying fair-brown hair in a broad monastic crown; the gaze serene and noble, a little above us.

subject: St. Zita, the servant of Lucca, half-length: a plain thirteenth-century Tuscan working dress of russet-brown wool with the sleeves pushed up to the elbow, a long white linen apron, a white linen kerchief over her hair tied at the nape, a small iron ring of household keys at her belt; in her arms, gathered in a fold of the apron, fresh round loaves of bread for the poor, one hand laid over them. Behind her, Lucca: a narrow street of stone and brick houses with a tall medieval tower-house, and the plain white Romanesque front of the church of San Frediano with a band of gold mosaic high on its gable, early morning light on the stone, a clear, pale sky. Humble, cheerful and quiet; no angels, no master, no lettering.
face: A Tuscan countrywoman of about forty-five with a warm, lightly sun-browned complexion and a MEDIUM OVAL face whose LOWER HALF leads in profile — a gently SLOPING forehead, a SHORT, straight nose with a small, slightly UPTURNED tip, a LONG UPPER LIP over a full, softly FORWARD mouth, a ROUNDED, firm chin, small DIMPLES in flat, narrow cheeks; LARGE, round, bright hazel eyes under straight, soft brown brows; brown hair parted in the middle under the kerchief; the gaze modest and warm, a small smile.

subject: St. Epiphanius, Bishop of Salamis in Cyprus, half-length, as a fourth-century Greek bishop who still wore the monk's habit: a plain dark-brown monastic tunic, and over it a white phelonion and a broad white omophorion with large black crosses on his shoulders; in his left hand a heavy book bound in dark leather, his work against the heresies, held closed against his side; his right hand raised in blessing. Behind him, the coast of Salamis: the blue sea and a low harbour wall, a new basilica of pale stone with a tiled roof, and the ruined columns of the older Roman city among olive trees, under a bright, hot Cypriot sky. Zealous, austere and charitable; no lettering.
face: A Palestinian of about eighty-five, lean and sun-browned, with a SMALL, NARROW face of SHARP, BIRD-LIKE features under a high, POLISHED BALD dome — PINCHED temples, a THIN, SHARP, POINTED nose, SMALL, piercing, CLOSE-SET black eyes under TUFTED, bristling white brows, tight, thin lips; a LONG, straight, silver-white beard to the breast, narrow and combed; the gaze alert and searching, toward us.

subject: St. Marcellinus, Bishop of Rome, half-length, as a pope of the age of Diocletian: a white tunic and a full, bell-shaped chasuble of deep crimson, a narrow white pallium with small black crosses over his shoulders; both hands holding closed against his breast a book of the Gospels in a plain, worn leather binding, kept safe in the persecution. Behind him, the Via Salaria outside Rome at dusk: a dusty road between umbrella pines and cypresses, low tombs along it, and the plain, dark doorway of the catacomb of Priscilla cut into a grassy bank, with the walls of Rome far off, under a heavy, stormy sky breaking to gold at the horizon. Grave and humble; no palm, no soldiers, no idols, no lettering.
face: A Roman of about sixty-five with a pale olive complexion and a SHORT, WIDE, SOFT face — a broad, furrowed forehead running up into a BALD crown with a fringe of short grey hair, HEAVY, FLESHY upper lids half covering sorrowful dark-brown eyes, grey brows that slant UP toward the centre, a SHORT, broad nose with a rounded tip, soft, full cheeks, DEEP vertical lines from the nose past the corners of a WIDE, full-lipped mouth, a short, rounded chin; a SHORT, rounded grey beard; the gaze grave and humble, lowered a little.

subject: St. Mammertus, Bishop of Vienne, half-length, as a fifth-century Gallo-Roman bishop leading the Rogations: a white alb and a full, bell-shaped chasuble of deep violet wool; in his left hand a tall, plain processional cross of gilt bronze, his right hand raised in blessing over the fields. Behind him, a little way back and small, a long procession of clergy and people in plain cloaks walking between green fields of young wheat and vineyards, and beyond, Roman Vienne on the broad Rhône: a small Roman temple with Corinthian columns among red roofs, hills behind, a thin veil of smoke drifting away from the town under a clearing spring sky. Penitent and hopeful; no fire, no wild beasts, no lettering.
face: A Gallo-Roman aristocrat of about sixty-five with a fair olive complexion and a LONG face with a CONVEX, ROMAN profile — a SLOPING forehead flowing into a LARGE, high-bridged, CURVED nose, a slightly receding upper lip and a FIRM, rounded chin; deep-set, dark-brown eyes under strong, arched grey brows; lean cheeks; grey hair cut short with a round clerical tonsure; a SHORT, neatly trimmed grey beard; the gaze earnest and pleading, lifted toward heaven.

subject: St. Leonides of Alexandria, half-length, in his prison: a plain Greek tunic of undyed linen and a philosopher's himation of deep slate-blue wool over his left shoulder, a plain iron fetter on each wrist joined by a short chain; in both hands, held open before him, a small unrolled papyrus letter, his son Origen's letter urging him to be constant. Behind him, a narrow stone window with iron bars and through it Alexandria in the evening: flat white roofs, a colonnaded street, the harbour with its ships and, far out on its island, the tall, stepped lighthouse of Pharos with a fire at its top, under a warm, fading sky. Steadfast and peaceful; no executioner, no sword, no lettering.
face: A Greek of Alexandria of about forty-eight with a warm, light-olive complexion and a SQUARE face as wide as it is long — a FLAT, nearly VERTICAL forehead, a short, straight nose with a narrow bridge, WIDE-SET, clear grey-green eyes under THICK, STRAIGHT black brows set low, flat cheeks, a firm mouth under a DEEP groove of the upper lip, and a strong, SQUARE chin with a marked CLEFT; short, thick, black hair combed forward in a straight fringe, a very SHORT, close-cropped black beard that lets the square jaw and the cleft of the chin show; the gaze calm and level, lowered to the letter in his hands.

subject: St. Antoninus, Archbishop of Florence, half-length, as a Dominican bishop of the fifteenth century: the white habit and scapular of the Friars Preachers under a black cappa, a white woollen pallium with small black crosses over his shoulders; in his right hand a round loaf held out as an alms, in his left a small pair of brass balance scales, for his just counsel; his white mitre set aside on a ledge beside him. Behind him, Florence from across the Arno: the red dome of the cathedral, the tall tower of the Palazzo Vecchio, red-tiled roofs and the old bridge with its shops, the hills of Fiesole beyond with cypresses, under a clear, soft Tuscan sky. Kind, humble and poor; no plate, no riches, no lettering.
face: A small, slight Florentine of about sixty-five, CLEAN-SHAVEN, with a pale olive complexion and a LARGE, HIGH, DOMED, bald cranium over a SHORT face — the face WIDEST at the cheekbones, the cheeks falling in below them; a LONG, straight, narrow nose; LARGE, ROUND, slightly prominent dark eyes under thin brows RAISED high on the forehead, which give him an attentive, listening look; deep lines from the nose to the mouth; a WIDE, THIN-LIPPED mouth; a SHORT, squared chin; a thin ring of short grey hair in the Dominican crown; the gaze attentive and kind, toward us.

subject: St. John the Silent, monk of the laura of St. Sabas, half-length: a coarse black monastic habit and a black hood drawn over his head, a leather belt; his hands folded quietly on his breast over a small wooden cross on a cord. Behind him, the deep, dry gorge of the Kidron in the Judaean desert: tawny cliffs with small monks' cells and a little church built into the rock on terraces, a few palms far below, and high in the clear evening sky a soft, bright cross of light. Silent and recollected, his lips closed; no bishop's vestments, no lettering.
face: An Armenian of about seventy-five with a pale olive complexion and a BROAD-TEMPLED face — a WIDE, HIGH forehead and broad temples, DEEP eye sockets in which LARGE, dark, heavy-lidded eyes rest LOWERED and half closed in recollection, a LONG, strong nose with a gentle HUMP and a tip that points DOWNWARD, LOW, broad cheekbones, a small mouth gently pressed shut; thin white hair under the hood; a LONG, full white beard that widens toward the bottom and ends SQUARE; the gaze inward and still, lowered.

subject: St. Peter of Verona, Dominican friar, half-length: the white habit and white scapular of the Friars Preachers under a black cappa with its black hood laid back; in his left hand an open book held toward us, the Creed he professed; in his right, a martyr's palm. Behind him, the Lombard countryside between Como and Milan: a lonely road running through chestnut woods and green fields, a small wayside shrine, and far off the walls and towers of Milan on the plain, the snowy Alps faint on the horizon, under a bright sky with a single white cloud casting shade. Fearless and ardent; no axe, no knife, no wound, no blood, no assassins, no lettering.
face: A Veronese of about forty-five, CLEAN-SHAVEN, with a warm olive complexion and a COMPACT, SQUARE-ROUND head on a strong neck — a short, broad, rounded forehead, FIRM, full cheeks over a strong, ROUND, muscular jaw and a round chin with a small DIMPLE; a SHORT, straight nose; very DARK, intense, round eyes under THICK, STRAIGHT black brows that nearly MEET over the nose; a firm, full, closed mouth; thick black hair in the Dominican ring of the tonsure, the shaven cheeks blue-shadowed; the gaze fearless and ardent, toward us.

subject: St. Maria of Jesus Santocanale, the Palermo noblewoman who became a Capuchin tertiary and founded the Capuchin Sisters of the Immaculate of Lourdes, half-length in her sisters' Franciscan habit: a plain brown habit girded with a white knotted cord, a black veil over a white wimple and a small white bib, a simple wooden crucifix on her breast; in the crook of her left arm a round loaf of bread in a white cloth for the poor she visited door to door, her right hand laid over it. Behind her, Cinisi in Sicily: white and ochre houses and the dome and bell tower of the mother church at the foot of the grey limestone Monte Pecoraro, and a strip of the blue Tyrrhenian Sea beyond. Tender and grave; no lettering.
face: A tall Palermitan noblewoman of about sixty with a pale olive complexion and a LONG, NARROW, fine-boned face — a smooth, high forehead under the wimple, dark brows that slope DOWN at their outer ends, large dark eyes whose outer corners DROOP a little, giving a gentle, sorrowful look, a LONG, slender nose with a high, straight bridge, a LONG upper lip, lightly hollowed cheeks and hollow temples, a SMALL, full, closed mouth and a narrow, tapering chin; the gaze grave and kind, toward us.

subject: St. María Antonia de Paz y Figueroa, "Mama Antula", the consecrated laywoman of Santiago del Estero who walked barefoot across the viceroyalty to keep the Spiritual Exercises alive after the Jesuits were expelled, half-length in the dress of a Jesuit beata as in her portrait: a black habit and a long black mantle, a white toca (wimple) framing the face and falling over the breast under a black veil; in her right hand a tall, plain wooden cross-staff held upright, and in her left a small closed book, the Exercises. Behind her, a dusty road running through the dry thorn scrub of the Argentine north, tall cardón cacti and a low adobe chapel with a small bell gable, the far blue line of the sierras under a wide, pale sky. Tireless and serene; no lettering.
face: A criolla of Santiago del Estero of about fifty-five with a warm, light-olive complexion and a SMOOTH, LONG OVAL face under a HIGH, rounded forehead — LARGE, WIDE-SET, light-brown almond eyes under fine, HIGH-ARCHED brows, a long, straight, slender nose, smooth, unmarked cheeks, a SMALL, firm mouth with a fuller lower lip, a neat, rounded chin; the gaze calm, steady and direct, toward us.
verdict: rejected: a generic young nun's face, too close to clare_assisi and maria_santocanale; she was about 55

subject: St. Lazarus Devasahayam, the Hindu court official of Travancore who became a Christian, half-length as a martyr in chains, as his traditional image shows him: a plain white cotton veshti (mundu) at the waist and a white cotton shawl drawn across his chest and over one shoulder, a light iron chain hanging loosely from his wrists, his hands joined in prayer before his breast. Behind him, the rocky, scrub-covered hillock of Aralvaimozhy in the far south of India at dusk, a great bare boulder on its crest, palmyra palms below and the blue ridges of the Western Ghats beyond under a warm, glowing sky. Peaceful and steadfast; no wounds, no soldiers, no lettering.
face: A South Indian man of about forty (he died at thirty-nine) with a warm, deep-brown complexion and a BROAD, SQUARE face — a wide, LOW forehead, strong, FLAT cheekbones, a STRAIGHT, broad nose with a LOW bridge and full, rounded nostrils, large, dark, deep-set eyes under THICK, straight black brows that nearly meet, a wide, full-lipped mouth and a strong, square jaw; thick, wavy black hair falling to the shoulders and a FULL, dense black beard trimmed ROUND at the chin; the gaze lifted in prayer. Not a long oval face, not Christ-like.

subject: St. Maria Domenica Mantovani, first superior of the Little Sisters of the Holy Family, half-length in the habit of her photograph: a black habit and a black veil over a narrow white band at the brow, a wide, round, white collar spread over her shoulders and breast, a small oval medal on a cord below it; a rosary held in her joined hands. Behind her, Castelletto di Brenzone on the eastern shore of Lake Garda: a small stone village with its church bell tower among silver olive trees at the water's edge, the calm blue lake, and the long green slopes of Monte Baldo rising above. Homely and motherly; no lettering.
face: A countrywoman of the Lake Garda shore of about sixty with a warm, lightly sun-browned complexion and a PEAR-SHAPED face — narrower at the brow and BROAD and full at the cheeks and jaw, a straight, fairly long nose with a broad, rounded tip, SMALL eyes NARROWED by a smile, with fine crinkles at their corners, under thin, slightly RAISED, arched brows, a WIDE mouth in a warm, closed smile, a broad, rounded chin; the gaze toward us, motherly and a little amused.

subject: St. Carmen Rendiles of Caracas, foundress of the Servants of Jesus, born without a left arm, half-length in the habit of her photographs: a pale grey-blue habit, a WHITE veil drawn back from the dark hair at her brow and falling over her shoulders, a wide, pointed white collar, a small medal on a thin chain at her breast; her right hand laid on her breast, the left side of her figure covered by the fall of the veil and the habit, so that only the right hand shows. Behind her, Caracas in its valley under the tall green wall of El Ávila mountain, red-tiled roofs, royal palms and a white colonial church tower in the warm morning light. Joyful and steadfast; no lettering.
face: A Caraqueña of about sixty with a warm, light-olive complexion and a LONG face with HIGH, prominent cheekbones — dark hair PARTED in the middle and drawn smoothly back under the white veil, a LONG, straight nose with a slight rise at the bridge, dark, bright almond eyes under dark, ARCHED brows, cheeks that fold into long smile creases, a WIDE mouth with a broad, warm, closed-lipped smile, a softly pointed chin; the gaze toward us, affectionate and bright.

subject: St. César de Bus of Cavaillon, the priest who founded the Fathers of Christian Doctrine to teach the catechism to the poor and the country people, half-length as a secular priest of about 1600, as in his portraits: a black soutane buttoned to the throat, a plain white turned-down collar, a black cloak over his shoulders; his hands joined in prayer before his breast, a small closed catechism book held between them. Behind him, Avignon on the Rhône: the broken stone arches of the old bridge running out into the river, the great pale walls and towers of the Palace of the Popes on its rock, cypresses, and the soft hills of Provence under a luminous sky. Humble and luminous; no lettering.
face: A Provençal of about fifty-five with a warm olive complexion and a LONG, RECTANGULAR face under a high forehead, where the dark, grey-streaked hair RECEDES at the temples and is cut short — level dark brows, HEAVY, HALF-LOWERED upper lids over dark eyes cast down (he became blind), a long, straight nose whose tip DIPS a little, flat, hollow-shadowed cheeks below high cheekbones, a FULL lower lip under a thick dark MOUSTACHE that droops at the corners, and a NARROW jaw, the grey-streaked beard trimmed CLOSE on the cheeks and gathered into a SHORT POINT at the chin; the expression inward and peaceful. Not the full, square-jawed beard of camillus.

subject: St. Elena Guerra of Lucca, foundress of the Oblates of the Holy Spirit, who wrote to Pope Leo XIII to have the whole Church pray the novena of Pentecost, half-length in the habit of her photograph: a black habit, a black veil falling to the shoulders, a white collar at the throat, a small black crucifix; she holds a small open prayer book against her breast in her left hand and raises her right hand a little, open, toward a white dove of the Holy Spirit in a soft glow of golden light above her shoulder. Behind her, Lucca: the broad, tree-planted Renaissance walls, red roofs, the Romanesque bell tower of the cathedral of San Martino and the Guinigi tower with its oak trees on top, under a clear sky. Ardent and gentle; no lettering.
face: A Lucchese noblewoman of about sixty-five with a warm, lightly sallow complexion and a LONG, STRONG-BONED face ending in a SQUARE, slightly PROMINENT chin — THICK, dark, STRAIGHT, LEVEL brows set LOW over deep-set, HOODED dark eyes, a LONG, strong nose with a broad, ROUNDED tip, flat cheeks with long creases from the nose to the mouth, a WIDE, thin-lipped mouth with a faint, knowing smile; the gaze direct and earnest.

subject: St. Marie Rivier, the tiny, indomitable foundress who taught the children of the Vivarais after the Revolution, half-length in the habit of her portrait: a black habit, a black hooded veil over a white band framing the face, a black shawl crossed over the breast, and a plain metal cross on a cord; in her hands a small open book, turned toward a little peasant girl in a white cap who stands close at her side, looking up at her. Behind her, Bourg-Saint-Andéol on the Rhône: the broad river, a Romanesque church tower and the old convent walls of pale stone, plane trees, and the low hills of the Ardèche beyond. Warm and resolute; no lettering.
face: A very SMALL, slight woman of about sixty-five from the Ardèche, with a fair, pale complexion and a SOFT, ROUND face falling into gentle JOWLS — a smooth forehead under the white band, HEAVY, DROOPING upper lids over small, bright, kindly eyes, faint, softly arched brows, a LONG nose with a rounded, FLESHY tip, full cheeks, a SMALL mouth drawn up at one corner in a slight smile; the head TILTED a little to one side, as in her portrait. The girl: about seven, round-faced, with short brown hair under a white cap.

subject: St. Marie-Léonie Paradis of Québec, foundress of the Little Sisters of the Holy Family, who keep house for priests and seminaries, half-length in the habit of her photograph of 1906: a black habit and a long black veil, a STIFF white coif closely framing the whole face, a broad white bib over the breast, a silver crucifix hanging on it and a black rosary in her hands. Behind her, Sherbrooke in autumn: the red-brick convent and the twin towers of a stone church on the hill above the Magog river, maples turning red and gold along the bank. Humble and serene; no lettering.
face: A sturdy Québécoise of about sixty-five with a fair complexion and a WIDE, FLAT, RECTANGULAR face closely framed by the coif — a broad, smooth forehead, STRAIGHT, heavy dark brows, small, DEEP-SET, pale, steady eyes, a SHORT, straight nose with a broad base, a notably LONG, FLAT upper lip, a straight, THIN-lipped mouth firmly closed, full, flat cheeks and a broad chin; the gaze level and steady, toward us.

subject: St. Giuseppe Allamano, priest of Turin, rector of the Consolata shrine and founder of the Consolata Missionaries, half-length in a black cassock with a narrow white collar and a small black skullcap, as in his photograph; he holds before his breast a small framed icon of Our Lady Consolata, the dark Byzantine Madonna with the Child, in both hands. Behind him, Turin: the baroque dome and the tall Romanesque bell tower of the Santuario della Consolata, the roofs of the old city, and the snowy Alps on the horizon under a clear morning sky. Cheerful and fatherly; no lettering.
face: A Piedmontese priest of about seventy, clean-shaven, with a fair complexion and a LONG, LEAN face under a HIGH forehead — short, thick WHITE hair brushed back under the skullcap, deep-set, lively eyes CRINKLED with laughter lines under strong, straight brows, a LONG, straight, PROMINENT nose, deep creases running from the nose to the corners of the mouth, a WIDE, warm, closed smile, large, prominent ears and a firm chin; the head turned in three-quarter view, the gaze bright and kindly.

subject: St. María Antonia de Paz y Figueroa, "Mama Antula", the consecrated laywoman of Santiago del Estero who walked barefoot across the viceroyalty to keep the Spiritual Exercises alive after the Jesuits were expelled, half-length in the dress of a Jesuit beata as in her portrait: a black habit and a long black mantle, a white toca (wimple) framing the face and falling over the breast under a black veil; in her right hand a tall, plain wooden cross-staff held upright, and in her left a small closed book, the Exercises. Behind her, a dusty road running through the dry thorn scrub of the Argentine north, tall cardón cacti and a low adobe chapel with a small bell gable, the far blue line of the sierras under a wide, pale sky. Tireless and serene; no lettering.
face: A criolla of Santiago del Estero of about fifty-five, CLEARLY MIDDLE-AGED, not a young nun: a warm, light-olive, sun-weathered complexion and a LONG face with a HIGH, rounded forehead and LEAN cheeks hollowed a little under PROMINENT cheekbones from her years on the road; LARGE, WIDE-SET, light-brown almond eyes with fine lines at their outer corners, under fine, HIGH-ARCHED brows; a long, straight, slender nose; faint lines from nose to mouth; a SMALL, firm mouth with a fuller lower lip; a neat, rounded chin; the gaze calm, steady and direct, toward us.

subject: St. Peter To Rot, the Tolai catechist of Rakunai in New Britain, husband and father, who kept his people praying under the Japanese occupation and died in prison for defending marriage, half-length in a plain white shirt with an open collar, as in his photograph, and a dark laplap wrapped at the waist; on a cord round his neck hangs the plain wooden catechist's cross his bishop gave him, and he holds a small, worn Bible in both hands. Behind him, the village of Rakunai on the Gazelle Peninsula: tall coconut palms, gardens of taro and bananas, a small mission church of timber with an iron roof, and the green volcanic hills of the Rabaul country under a bright tropical sky. Gentle and unafraid; no prison, no soldiers, no lettering.
face: A Tolai man of New Britain of about thirty-three with a deep, dark-brown complexion and a BROAD, SQUARE face — a wide forehead under thick, tightly curled black hair cut short and standing up a little above the brow, STRAIGHT, heavy black brows set LOW over deep-set dark eyes, a BROAD, flat nose with wide nostrils, full cheeks, a WIDE, full-lipped mouth closed firmly, a rounded, strong jaw; clean-shaven; the gaze grave, gentle and direct. Not the long, sculpted face of charles_lwanga.

subject: St. Pier Giorgio Frassati, the Turin student, mountaineer and lay Dominican who served the poor, half-length as a climber of the 1920s, as in his mountain photographs: a white shirt open at the neck under a brown tweed jacket, a coil of hemp rope over one shoulder; his right hand grips the shaft of a wooden ice axe held upright beside him, and from his left hand hangs a rosary. Behind him, the high Alps of the Val di Lanzo above Turin: grey rock ridges with snowfields, a steep path climbing toward the summit, and a clear, deep-blue sky. Joyful, strong and upward-looking; no pipe, no lettering.
face: A young Turinese of twenty-four, clean-shaven, with a warm olive complexion and a BROAD, SQUARE face — a low, wide forehead under thick, glossy black hair brushed UP and back from the brow and cut short at the sides, THICK, straight, nearly level black brows set LOW over deep-set, dark, steady eyes, a strong, straight nose with a broad bridge, broad, flat cheekbones, full lips closed in a slight smile, and a strong, SQUARE chin; the gaze open, frank and cheerful. A sturdy young man, not a soft, slender, beardless youth like aloysius_gonzaga.

subject: The sixteen Discalced Carmelites of Compiègne, guillotined in Paris on 17 July 1794 after offering their lives for peace in the Church and in France, shown by three of them side by side, half-length, as they went to their death: in the brown Carmelite habit and scapular and the long white choir mantle, which they had put on again for the journey to Paris. In the centre, the prioress, Mother Teresa of St. Augustine, in a black veil over a white wimple, holding a small wooden crucifix before her breast. On the left, the youngest, the novice Sister Constance, in a WHITE novice's veil, her hands joined and her lips parted in song. On the right, the eldest, Sister Charlotte of the Resurrection, small and bent, in a black veil, leaning on a plain wooden crutch, a rosary in her other hand. Behind them, the edge of Paris at the Barrière du Trône on a July evening: the two tall stone columns of the tollgate, rows of trees, and a sky turning gold and rose. Serene and joyful; no guillotine, no cart, no crowd, no lettering. Keep all three figures inside the arched window.
face: Three clearly different women. Mother Teresa of St. Augustine (centre): a Parisian of forty-one with a fair complexion and a HEART-SHAPED face — a broad, smooth forehead, WIDE-SET, large grey eyes under fine, high-arched brows, a small, straight nose, a small, firm, pointed chin and a composed, closed mouth; the gaze calm and resolute, lifted a little. Sister Constance (left): a novice of twenty-nine with a ROUND, fresh face — full, rosy cheeks, a short, slightly UPTURNED nose, bright brown eyes, round brows, lips parted as she sings; eager and radiant. Sister Charlotte (right): a small old woman of seventy-eight with a LONG, NARROW, finely lined face — a long nose, deep laughter lines at the eyes and mouth, sunken cheeks, light-blue eyes bright and merry, a wide, thin smile; cheerful and undaunted. None of them the young oval of therese or the square jaw of teresa_benedicta.
verdict: rejected: broken frame: a different border, initial box and floral bands from the set

subject: St. Maria Francesca of Jesus Rubatto of Carmagnola, foundress of the Capuchin Tertiary Sisters of Loano, who nursed the sick poor in their homes and died in Montevideo, half-length in the habit of her photographs: a dark-brown habit, a black veil, a close white wimple and a BROAD white guimpe covering the breast and shoulders, a plain wooden crucifix on a cord; her hands folded over a rosary. Behind her, the bay of Montevideo: the low hill of the Cerro with its small white fortress and lighthouse on the far shore, a steamship at anchor in the calm water, and the roofs and bell towers of the old city on the near side, under a clear southern sky. Strong and motherly; no lettering.
face: A Piedmontese of about fifty-five with a fair complexion and a BROAD, FULL face — rounded cheeks and a soft fullness under the chin, a smooth forehead under the wimple, THICK, dark, straight brows, LARGE, PALE grey eyes set wide, open and calm, a straight nose BROAD at the bridge, a SMALL, full-lipped mouth closed firmly, a rounded chin; the gaze level, strong and kindly. Not the flat, rectangular face with small deep-set eyes and thin mouth of marie_leonie_paradis, nor the long, narrow maria_santocanale.

subject: The eleven Martyrs of Damascus, killed in the Franciscan friary of St. Paul on the night of 9-10 July 1860, shown by three of them side by side, half-length. In the centre, St. Manuel Ruiz, the Spanish guardian of the friary, in the brown Franciscan habit and hood with a white knotted cord, holding before his breast in both hands a small golden ciborium with its veiled lid, the Eucharist he consumed so that it would not be profaned. On the left, St. Francis Massabki, the eldest of the three Maronite brothers, a silk merchant and father of eight, in a long striped silk robe (qumbaz) with a sash and a dark mantle over it, a white turban wound round his head, a rosary in one hand and a green palm in the other. On the right, St. Raphael Massabki, the youngest brother, in a plain dark robe and a dark-red turban, his hands joined over a green palm. Behind them, old Damascus at dusk: flat roofs, courtyards with poplar trees and a small stone church bell tower, and the bare, rose-brown slopes of Mount Qasioun beyond under an amber sky. Peaceful and steadfast; no weapons, no wounds, no fire, no lettering. Keep all three figures inside the arched window.
face: Three clearly different men. Manuel Ruiz (centre): a Castilian friar of fifty-six with a weathered olive complexion and a LONG, BONY face — a bald crown ringed by short grey hair in the Franciscan tonsure, deep-set dark eyes under heavy grey brows, a LONG, slightly AQUILINE nose, hollow cheeks, and a long grey beard narrowing to the breast; the gaze lowered to the ciborium. Francis Massabki (left): a Damascene of about sixty with a warm olive complexion and a BROAD, ROUND face — full cheeks, a short, broad nose, large, kind, dark eyes under thick grey brows, a full mouth, and a short, full, ROUNDED white beard and white moustache; a calm, fatherly look. Raphael Massabki (right): a slighter Damascene of about forty with a NARROW, LONG face — a high forehead, a long, straight, fine nose, large dark almond eyes under fine black brows, a small mouth, a thin black moustache and a short, trim black beard close along the jaw; a quiet, devout look, lifted. None of them Christ-like.

subject: St. Ignatius Choukrallah Maloyan, Armenian Catholic Archbishop of Mardin, martyred in 1915, half-length in the dress of his photograph of 1911: a black cassock and over the head the black, pointed Armenian bishop's hood (veghar) falling in folds over the shoulders, a gold pectoral cross on a chain; he holds a small Gospel book bound in dark red against his breast with both hands, and a green martyr's palm. Behind him, Mardin: honey-coloured stone houses, churches and domes terraced up a steep hillside under the old citadel on its rock, and the wide, pale plain of upper Mesopotamia stretching away below in the evening light. Grave and steadfast; no wounds, no soldiers, no lettering.
face: An Armenian archbishop of about forty-six with a warm, light-olive complexion and a FULL, SOFT OVAL face with rounded cheeks — a high, smooth forehead under the hood, no hair showing, large, dark, HEAVY-LIDDED eyes with a calm, slightly lowered gaze under thick, gently arched black brows, a straight nose with a broad tip, and a LONG, FULL, dense black BEARD, broad and squared at the bottom and reaching to the breast, with a full moustache over a closed mouth; the expression mild and resolute. Not the lean, narrow josaphat, nor the wide-open eyes of gregory_narek.

subject: St. Giovanni Battista Scalabrini, Bishop of Piacenza, founder of the missionaries and sisters for Italian emigrants, half-length in a bishop's black cassock piped and buttoned in purple, a purple sash, a purple zucchetto and a gold pectoral cross on a chain, as in his photographs; his right hand raised in blessing, his left holding a small crucifix against his breast. Behind him, Piacenza: the Romanesque front and tall bell tower of the cathedral, the roofs of the city and the broad river Po; on the road below, very small, a family of emigrants with bundles and a trunk setting out. Fatherly and resolute; no lettering.
face: A bishop of about sixty, clean-shaven, with a fair complexion and a LONG, RECTANGULAR face ending in a strong, SQUARE chin — a HIGH forehead, short grey hair RECEDING at the temples and brushed straight back under the zucchetto, dark, STRAIGHT, level brows, darker than the hair, over deep-set, dark, intent eyes, a LONG, straight, STRONG nose, flat cheeks with firm lines from nose to mouth, a WIDE, thin-lipped mouth set in a faint, resolute smile; the gaze direct and steady. Not the broad, silver-haired, smiling pius_x, nor the lean, white-haired, broadly smiling giuseppe_allamano.

subject: St. Luigi Maria Palazzolo, priest of Bergamo and founder of the Sisters of the Poor (Suore delle Poverelle) for abandoned girls, half-length in a black cassock with a narrow white collar and a black four-cornered biretta, as in his portraits; in his right hand, held against his breast, a small crucifix, as in the Dicastery's portrait; his left hand rests on the shoulder of a little poor girl of about seven in a plain brown dress and a faded shawl, who stands close at his side and looks up at him. Behind him, Bergamo's Città Alta on its hill: the Venetian walls, the domes of Santa Maria Maggiore and the Colleoni Chapel, the tall Campanone tower, and the green foothills of the Alps beyond under a soft evening sky. Fatherly and humble; no lettering.
face: A priest of Bergamo of about fifty-five, clean-shaven, with a fair complexion and a BROAD, HEAVY face that WIDENS toward a full jaw with soft JOWLS — a high forehead, short grey-brown hair RECEDING under the biretta and cropped close at the temples, a LONG, straight nose with a thick, ROUNDED tip, HEAVY upper lids over small grey eyes that glance a little to one side, full cheeks, a WIDE mouth whose corners turn DOWN in repose, softened by a slight, kindly smile; the gaze gentle and shrewd. Not the round, twinkling, broadly smiling face of john_xxiii. The girl: a thin, oval little face, dark hair tied back, large brown eyes.

subject: St. Titus Brandsma, the Frisian Carmelite priest, professor of mysticism and rector of the Catholic University of Nijmegen, who defended the freedom of the Catholic press against the Nazis and died at Dachau, half-length in the brown Carmelite habit and scapular with the WHITE Carmelite cloak and hood over his shoulders, as in his photographs; round steel-rimmed spectacles; he holds a small open book against his breast with one hand, a rosary looped round the fingers of the other. Behind him, Nijmegen on the river Waal: the tall tower of St. Stephen's church above the old town, the broad river with a barge, green dykes and meadows beyond under a wide Dutch sky with piled white clouds. Kind and serene; no camp, no barbed wire, no lettering.
face: A Frisian of about sixty, clean-shaven, with a fair complexion and a LONG face that WIDENS at HIGH, broad cheekbones and narrows to a pointed chin — a high forehead under a thick, springy CREST of wavy grey hair brushed up and back, small, narrowed, smiling eyes with crinkles at the corners behind small ROUND steel-rimmed spectacles, a LONG nose with a slight bump and a rounded tip, lean cheeks folded by smile lines, a thin-lipped, gently smiling mouth; the head a little tilted, the gaze kind and humorous. Not maximilian_kolbe (beard, balding) nor josemaria_escriva (round face, dark rectangular glasses).

subject: St. Giustino Maria Russolillo, parish priest of Pianura in Naples and founder of the Vocationists, who gathered poor boys to become priests, half-length in a black cassock with a short black shoulder cape and a narrow white collar, round wire-rimmed spectacles, as in his portraits; he holds a small open book in his left hand and with his right points gently toward it, as in the painted portrait of his shrine; behind him, a little lower, two boys of about twelve in dark jackets, looking up. Behind them, Pianura on the western edge of Naples: the white houses and the bell tower of the parish church of San Giorgio among vineyards on the green hills of the Campi Flegrei, under a warm, clear sky. Earnest and fatherly; no lettering.
face: A Neapolitan priest of about forty, clean-shaven, with a warm olive complexion and a LONG, NARROW face tapering to a pointed chin — a high forehead, short dark hair parted at the side and brushed back, RECEDING a little at the temples, LARGE ears that stand out, dark, earnest eyes behind small ROUND wire-rimmed spectacles, level dark brows, a long, straight nose, hollowed cheeks, FULL lips closed; the gaze direct and gentle. Not the round, smiling josemaria_escriva, nor the grey-crested titus_brandsma of this batch. The boys: one round-faced with curly black hair, one thin with short straight brown hair.

subject: The sixteen Discalced Carmelites of Compiègne, guillotined in Paris on 17 July 1794 after offering their lives for peace in the Church and in France, shown by three of them side by side, half-length, as they went to their death: in the brown Carmelite habit and scapular and the long white choir mantle, which they had put on again for the journey to Paris. In the centre, the prioress, Mother Teresa of St. Augustine, in a black veil over a white wimple, holding a small wooden crucifix before her breast. On the left, the youngest, the novice Sister Constance, in a WHITE novice's veil, her hands joined and her lips parted in song. On the right, the eldest, Sister Charlotte of the Resurrection, small and bent, in a black veil, leaning on a plain wooden crutch, a rosary in her other hand. Behind them, the edge of Paris at the Barrière du Trône on a July evening: the two tall stone columns of the tollgate, rows of trees, and a sky turning gold and rose. Serene and joyful; no guillotine, no cart, no crowd, no lettering. Keep all three figures inside the arched window.
face: Three clearly different women. Mother Teresa of St. Augustine (centre): a Parisian of forty-one with a fair complexion and a HEART-SHAPED face — a broad, smooth forehead, WIDE-SET, large grey eyes under fine, high-arched brows, a small, straight nose, a small, firm, pointed chin and a composed, closed mouth; the gaze calm and resolute, lifted a little. Sister Constance (left): a novice of twenty-nine with a ROUND, fresh face — full, rosy cheeks, a short, slightly UPTURNED nose, bright brown eyes, round brows, lips parted as she sings; eager and radiant. Sister Charlotte (right): a small old woman of seventy-eight with a LONG, NARROW, finely lined face — a long nose, deep laughter lines at the eyes and mouth, sunken cheeks, light-blue eyes bright and merry, a wide, thin smile; cheerful and undaunted. None of them the young oval of therese or the square jaw of teresa_benedicta.

subject: St. Bartolo Longo, lawyer of Apulia who, converted from spiritualism, became the apostle of the Rosary and built the Shrine of Our Lady of the Rosary at Pompeii with its orphanages, half-length in the dress of his photographs about 1900: a dark frock coat and waistcoat, a high white wing collar and a dark tie, a PINCE-NEZ on a thin black cord; in his hands, held before his breast, a long rosary of dark beads with a small crucifix. Behind him, the Shrine of Pompeii: its white and cream façade with columns and loggia, the tall bell tower, the new town around it, and Vesuvius, grey-violet and softly smoking, across the plain under a clear southern sky. Earnest and devout; no lettering.
face: A southern Italian of about sixty with a fair olive complexion and a LONG face under a HIGH, DOMED forehead — thick, wavy dark hair going grey, RECEDING at the temples and brushed back, standing out in soft waves over the ears; deep-set, earnest dark eyes under heavy brows that rise a little at their inner ends, behind a small oval PINCE-NEZ; a LONG, straight nose; a FULL, BROAD, BUSHY beard, dark and streaked with grey, grown from the cheekbones and reaching to the collar, with a full moustache over a closed mouth; the gaze intent and a little upward. Not the pointed chin beard of cesar_de_bus, nor the round spectacles and narrow pointed beard of maximilian_kolbe.

subject: St. Carlo Acutis, the Milanese teenager who loved the Eucharist, went to Mass daily and used his gift for computers to catalogue the Eucharistic miracles of the world, half-length in the red polo shirt with a white-and-navy collar of his best-known photograph, the straps of a small backpack over his shoulders; in his joined hands, a rosary. Behind him, Assisi, where he loved to stay and where he is buried: the Basilica of St. Francis on its arches, the pale pink stone of the town climbing the slope of Monte Subasio, and in the sky above the hill, small and luminous, a white Host in a golden monstrance. Joyful and open; no computer, no lettering.
face: A Milanese boy of fifteen with a light olive complexion and a SOFT, BROAD OVAL face with FULL, rounded cheeks — a smooth forehead half-covered by a THICK, TOUSLED MOP of dark-brown CURLS, straight, dark brows, warm brown eyes a little narrowed by a smile, a straight nose with a softly rounded tip, a WIDE mouth in an easy, closed-lipped, slightly crooked smile, and a firm, rounded chin; the gaze frank and friendly, toward us. Not the square-jawed pier_giorgio_frassati with his hair brushed up, nor the fine, slender aloysius_gonzaga.

subject: St. Vincenza Maria Poloni of Verona, foundress of the Sisters of Mercy of Verona, who nursed the sick, the old and the orphans of the city's Pio Ricovero, half-length in the habit of her portraits: a black habit, a black veil falling in a deep hood round the face over a narrow white band, a broad, SQUARE white collar spread over the breast, a crucifix on a black cord; her right hand laid flat on her breast, as in her portrait, and in her left a small open book. Behind her, Verona on the river Adige: the old Roman stone bridge (Ponte Pietra), the red roofs and bell towers of the city, and the cypress-covered hill of San Pietro beyond, in soft evening light. Gentle, firm and recollected; no lettering.
face: A Veronese of about fifty with a pale, warm complexion and a LONG, NARROW OVAL face — a high, smooth forehead under the band, a LONG, PROMINENT nose with a high, straight bridge and a slightly DOWNTURNED tip, large dark eyes with HEAVY upper lids glancing a little to one side, thin, finely arched brows, flat cheeks, a SMALL, thin-lipped mouth with a faint, wry smile at one corner, and a small, rounded chin; the gaze quiet, perceptive and kind. Not the sloping, sorrowful brows of maria_santocanale, nor the square chin and wide mouth of elena_guerra.
