subject: St. Maria Troncatti, Salesian Sister (Daughter of Mary Help of Christians) from the Alps of Brescia, nurse in the First World War and for forty-four years missionary nurse among the Shuar of the Ecuadorian Amazon, half-length in the habit of her photographs: a black habit and black veil, a narrow white band at the brow, a broad, ROUNDED white collar covering the breast, a small crucifix on it; round, thin-rimmed spectacles; she holds a rosary in her right hand and with her left a small brown leather nurse's bag, as in the emblem of her canonization. Beside her, a little lower, a Shuar boy of about six in a plain cotton shirt, with straight black hair cut in a fringe, looks up at her. Behind them, the mission of Macas in the valley of the Upano: a small white mission church with a wooden porch, thatched houses among banana plants, the broad, stony river, and the green, cloud-wreathed wall of the Andean foothills and the Amazon forest beyond. Motherly and joyful; no lettering.
face: A woman from the Alpine valleys of Lombardy of about seventy-five, with a fair, weathered, lightly ruddy complexion and a BROAD, ROUNDED-SQUARE face — a wide, low forehead under the white band, FULL, rounded cheeks, a SHORT, broad nose, small, bright, kindly eyes creased at the corners behind ROUND, thin-rimmed spectacles, thin, faint brows, a WIDE mouth in a broad, open, warm smile that lifts the cheeks, and a soft fullness under a rounded chin; the gaze direct and cheerful. Not the small, pointed-chinned, unsmiling teresa_calcutta, nor the flat, thin-lipped marie_leonie_paradis.

subject: St. Charles de Foucauld, French cavalry officer and explorer turned priest and hermit among the Tuareg of the Sahara, half-length in his white gandoura with, sewn on the breast, a red heart surmounted by a red cross, a broad dark leather belt with a long rosary hanging from it, as in his photograph; his hands joined before him. Behind him, the Hoggar mountains at dawn: his small stone hermitage on the Assekrem plateau, and beyond it the dark volcanic peaks and needles of the Atakor rising out of the rose-gold desert under a pale, clear sky. Poor, gentle and at peace; no weapons, no lettering.
face: A Frenchman of about fifty-five, lean and sun-darkened, with a TRIANGULAR face, broad at the temples and cheekbones and narrowing to the chin — a high forehead under dark hair CROPPED very SHORT, deep-set, dark, luminous eyes with fine crow's-feet, straight dark brows, HIGH cheekbones over hollowed cheeks, a straight, strong nose, a SHORT, trimmed dark beard flecked with grey, closer on the cheeks and a little longer at the chin, a short moustache, and a gentle, closed smile; the gaze kind, direct and serene. Not the long, rectangular, lid-lowered cesar_de_bus, nor the full, white beard of an old hermit.

subject: St. José Gregorio Hernández, Venezuelan physician, scientist and professor in Caracas, the 'doctor of the poor', half-length in the dress of his photographs: a black three-piece suit, a white stiff collar and a black tie, a white handkerchief in the breast pocket, and his black felt hat with a wide brim; in his left hand a black doctor's bag, in his right a rosary. Behind him, Caracas in its valley: red-tiled roofs, the white towers of the church of La Candelaria, palms, and the great green wall of the Ávila mountain beyond under a bright tropical sky. Grave, gentle and recollected; no lettering.
face: A Venezuelan of about fifty of Andean and Canarian stock with a warm, light-olive complexion and a SMOOTH, ROUND face, FULL through the cheeks, with a small, rounded chin — large, dark, GENTLE eyes with slightly HEAVY upper lids, dark brows that RISE a little at their inner ends, giving a mild, compassionate look, a short, straight nose, a neat, full, dark MOUSTACHE trimmed straight over a closed mouth, short dark hair under the hat; clean-shaven otherwise; the gaze calm, grave and kind. Not the square, tousled, laughing artemide_zatti of this batch.

subject: Blessed Fulton J. Sheen, Archbishop, who preached the Gospel to millions on radio in The Catholic Hour and on television in Life Is Worth Living, half-length in a bishop's black cassock piped and buttoned in red-purple, the purple zucchetto, and the long purple silk cape (ferraiolo) over his shoulders, as in his photographs of the 1950s; a gold pectoral cross on a chain; his right hand raised a little in a speaker's gesture, his left holding a rosary. Behind him, New York at dusk: the twin white Gothic spires of St. Patrick's Cathedral on Fifth Avenue among the towers of Manhattan, lit windows, and a deep blue evening sky. Radiant, warm and persuasive; no microphone, no camera, no blackboard, no lettering.
face: An American of Irish stock of about sixty with a fair complexion and a LONG, LEAN face with HIGH, sharply MODELLED cheekbones and hollowed cheeks — a high forehead under dark, wavy hair greying at the temples, brushed back from a slight widow's peak under the zucchetto, strong, ARCHED dark brows, LARGE, light, deep-set, INTENSE eyes that seem to look straight through the viewer, a long, straight nose, deep lines from the nose to a WIDE, thin-lipped mouth in a warm, slightly lifted smile, and a firm, narrow chin; the gaze magnetic and kind. Not the square-chinned, level-browed giovanni_battista_scalabrini, nor the white-haired, laughing giuseppe_allamano.
verdict: rejected: drawn with a saint's halo; a Blessed has rays

subject: St. Artemide Zatti, Italian-born Salesian brother who, healed of tuberculosis, gave his life as nurse and pharmacist of the San José hospital at Viedma in Patagonia and went to the sick of the town by bicycle, half-length in a long white hospital coat over a dark waistcoat, a white shirt and a dark tie, as in his photographs; his left hand rests on the handlebar of his black bicycle beside him, and in his right he holds a rosary. Behind him, Viedma on the Río Negro: low white houses and the hospital with its small chapel, the broad river with the town of Patagones on the far bank, and the flat, dry Patagonian steppe under a huge, wind-swept sky. Warm, cheerful and tireless; no lettering.
face: An Emilian-born Argentine of about sixty with a weathered, ruddy-olive complexion and a SQUARE, BROAD face, WIDEST at HIGH, prominent cheekbones — a low forehead under thick, dark hair going grey, TOUSLED and falling in a lock over the brow, deep-set dark eyes narrowed by laughter lines, straight, thick brows, a broad, straight nose, a THICK, BUSHY, DROOPING dark moustache streaked with grey over a WIDE mouth in a broad, generous smile, deep creases from the nose to the corners of the mouth, and a strong, square jaw; clean-shaven otherwise; the gaze warm, lively and direct. Not the smooth, round, grave jose_gregorio_hernandez of this batch, nor the heavy, crowned stephen_hungary.

subject: An ordinary weekday morning Low Mass in a simple parish church. Beyond the altar rail, the priest stands at the altar facing it, AD ORIENTEM, seen from behind, small, in a plain GREEN Roman fiddleback chasuble with the maniple on his left arm, over an amice and a lace-trimmed alb, his hands extended before his breast; one server in cassock and surplice kneels at the step. It is a high altar with gradines: two of the six candles lit on the gradine, a central crucifix, three altar cards, and the tabernacle veiled in green silk; a green frontal; before the tabernacle a sanctuary lamp hangs from the vault, glowing. In the pews, a few faithful kneel, half-length and seen from behind or in profile: a workman with his cap held in his hands, a grey-haired woman in a black lace veil with a rosary, a schoolgirl in a beret with a satchel, a young nurse in her white uniform and white headdress. Clear, cool morning light through plain windows. Quiet and unhurried. Keep everyone inside the arched window.

A weekday morning Low Mass in Christmas Time, at sunrise. Beyond the altar rail, the priest stands at the altar facing it, AD ORIENTEM, seen from behind, small, in a WHITE, gold-orphreyed, Roman fiddleback chasuble with the maniple on his left arm, over an amice and a lace-trimmed alb, his eyes raised to the crucifix and his hands extended before his breast; one server in cassock and surplice kneels at the step. It is a high altar with gradines: two of the six candles lit on the gradine, a central crucifix, three altar cards, and the tabernacle veiled in white silk; a white frontal with gold embroidery, with evergreen boughs and white flowers on the gradine. At the left, small, the church's Christmas crib under its gilded star. A handful of faithful in winter clothes kneel in the front pews, half-length, seen from behind, the women with their heads covered. The first golden rays of the rising sun stream through a tall east window over the altar, lighting the whole sanctuary of stone and gilt. Bright, calm, joyful. Keep everything inside the arched window.
verdict: rejected: broken frame: white initial box lost on the parchment, different vine bands

subject: The Fourth Sunday of Lent: a stone parish church in which, for this one Sunday, the Lenten sobriety lifts a little. Beyond the altar rail, the priest stands at the altar facing it, AD ORIENTEM, seen from behind, small, in a ROSE-coloured, gold-orphreyed, Roman fiddleback chasuble with the maniple on his left arm, over an amice and a lace-trimmed alb, his hands extended before his breast, no higher than his shoulders; two servers kneel at the steps. It is a high altar with gradines: six tall candles lit on the gradine, a central crucifix, three altar cards, and the tabernacle veiled in rose silk; a rose frontal with gold; for the first time in Lent, two vases of pale spring blossom (almond and white lilies) stand on the gradine between the candlesticks. In the organ loft at the side, small, an organist at the pipes. In the foreground, half-length and seen from behind, a congregation in the pews, the women's heads covered, a child looking up at the flowers. Clear spring light, pale rose and gold, through tall windows. Keep everything inside the arched window.

A Sunday morning in Ordinary Time outside a small white village church with a bell tower, its bell swinging. Families in their Sunday clothes walk up the path to the open wooden doors: a grandfather with a cane and his hat in his hand, a young couple with a baby, two children running ahead, a woman in a lace mantilla carrying a hand missal; they are small, half-length or seen from behind. Through the open doors, small and deep inside, beyond the altar rail, a high altar with gradines, its six candles lit, and the priest in a GREEN Roman fiddleback chasuble standing at it with his back to the doors. Around the church, green meadows, a few trees and low hills under a clear blue sky with white clouds; bright, peaceful, ordinary daylight. No lettering. Keep the church and everyone inside the arched window.

The First Sunday of Advent: on a low stand just outside the altar rail, an evergreen Advent wreath of fir and holly with red berries and a few pine cones, holding four tall candles — three violet and one rose — only the first violet candle lit, its small flame steady. Beyond the rail, a sanctuary of stone and gilt and a high altar with gradines: six tall candlesticks, unlit, on the gradine, a central crucifix, three altar cards, and the tabernacle veiled in violet silk; a violet frontal with gold orphreys; no flowers. Above the altar, a round window shows a deep blue pre-dawn sky over a snowy village with a single bright morning star. No people. Quiet, expectant, nocturnal light. Keep everything inside the arched window.

An early weekday Low Mass in Advent, before dawn, in a small stone parish church lit only by candles. At the far end, beyond the altar rail, the priest stands at the altar facing it, AD ORIENTEM, seen from behind, small, in a violet Roman fiddleback chasuble with the maniple on his left arm, over an amice and a lace-trimmed alb, his hands extended before his breast; a young server in black cassock and white surplice kneels on the lowest step at the side. It is a high altar with gradines: two of the six candles lit on the gradine, a central crucifix, three altar cards, and the tabernacle veiled in violet silk; a violet frontal; no flowers. In the foreground, half-length and seen from behind or in profile, a few faithful in winter coats kneel in the wooden pews, each holding a small lit candle: an old woman in a dark headscarf, a young father with his daughter in a knitted bonnet, a nun in a grey habit. The tall windows are still deep blue with the first pale light at their base. Hushed, watchful, warm pools of candlelight in the dark. Keep everyone inside the arched window.

A church's Christmas crib at night during a Sunday of Christmas Time. At the side of the nave, outside the altar rail, a wooden stable with a thatched roof on a bed of straw and moss, with painted carved statues (clearly statues, not living people): the Child in the manger on white linen with arms open, Mary kneeling in blue, Joseph standing with a staff, an ox and a donkey, two shepherds with a lamb; a gilded star hangs above the stable roof. Evergreen boughs, red poinsettias and many small candles glow around it. In front, half-length and seen from behind, a young mother in a Sunday coat, her hair covered with a white lace mantilla, kneels at the crib rail holding her small son, who points at the Child. Behind the crib, beyond the altar rail, a high altar with gradines: six tall candles lit on the gradine, a central crucifix, three altar cards, and the tabernacle veiled in white silk; a white frontal embroidered in gold. Warm golden light in the dark church, deep blue windows with stars. Keep everything inside the arched window.
verdict: rejected: broken frame: white initial box lost on the parchment, different vine bands

subject: A weekday Low Mass in Lent at a side altar in a quiet chapel on a grey early morning. The priest stands at the altar facing it, AD ORIENTEM, seen from behind, small, in a plain VIOLET Roman fiddleback chasuble with the maniple on his left arm, over an amice and a lace-trimmed alb, bowing slightly as he prays; one server in cassock and surplice kneels at the step. The small side altar has a low gradine with a wooden crucifix and two lit candles, an altar card at its centre, a violet antependium, and NO FLOWERS. On the whitewashed wall, a carved wooden Station of the Cross (Jesus falls) without lettering. A few faithful kneel half-length in the foreground, seen from behind or in profile: a man in a worn work jacket with his head bowed, an elderly woman with a black lace veil and a rosary, a young woman in a dark headscarf with joined hands. Cold, soft light from a single high window; bare and sober, but peaceful. Keep everyone inside the arched window.
verdict: rejected: broken frame: florals down the sides, a different border

Beyond the altar rail, a high altar with gradines: six tall candles lit on the gradine, a central crucifix, three altar cards, and the tabernacle veiled in violet silk; a violet frontal, and the altar BARE OF FLOWERS. The priest stands at the altar facing it, AD ORIENTEM, seen from behind, small, in a VIOLET Roman fiddleback chasuble with the maniple on his left arm, over an amice and a lace-trimmed alb, his hands joined, with two servers in cassock and surplice kneeling on the steps at his sides. In the foreground, half-length and seen from behind, a full congregation kneels in the pews, heads bowed: men bareheaded, women in veils and headscarves, children, an old couple. Along the side walls, the small carved Stations of the Cross. Grey-violet morning light through tall windows. Solemn, penitent, still. Keep everyone inside the arched window.
verdict: rejected: broken frame: the window runs into the bottom band, then a different vine style

subject: The Third Sunday of Advent. In the foreground, on a low stand outside the altar rail, the evergreen Advent wreath with three candles lit — two violet and the ROSE one — and one violet candle still unlit. Beyond the rail, in a brighter church of stone and gilt, the priest stands at the altar facing it, AD ORIENTEM, seen from behind, small, in a ROSE-coloured, gold-orphreyed, Roman fiddleback chasuble with the maniple on his left arm, over an amice and a lace-trimmed alb, his hands extended before his breast, no higher than his shoulders; two servers in cassock and surplice kneel at either side of the step. Soft rose-gold morning light falls through the windows. Joyful but restrained. Keep everything inside the arched window.

St. Gemma Galgani, half-length, in the plain black, high-collared dress of her photograph of 1900, no veil, her hands joined at her breast round a small wooden crucifix, her face lifted toward heaven. Just behind her shoulder, faint and gentle, her guardian angel in white with a hand raised over her. Behind them, Lucca seen from a window at dusk: red-tiled roofs, the medieval brick Guinigi tower crowned with its holm oaks, and the white marble front of the cathedral of San Martino under a soft rose-gold sky. A plain gold halo; no visible wounds; no lettering.
face: A young woman of about twenty-two with a pale, clear complexion and a full OVAL face, broad at the cheekbones and tapering to a small, firm, rounded chin — a high smooth forehead, dark, straight, softly sloping brows, large, clear grey-brown eyes raised upward, a straight nose with a broad, rounded tip, a small mouth with full lips, closed; dark-brown hair parted in the centre and drawn smoothly back behind the ears to a knot at the nape, ears showing; the gaze lifted to heaven, rapt and calm.

subject: Our Lady as St. Catherine Labouré saw her on 27 November 1830 in the chapel of the Rue du Bac in Paris, the image of the Miraculous Medal: standing full-length on a globe, her feet crushing a greenish serpent; in a high-necked silk gown of dawn-white with plain, close sleeves ('à la Vierge') and a white veil falling from her head to her feet on either side, no blue mantle; her arms lowered and opened toward the globe, palms outward, her fingers set with jewelled rings from which streams of golden light pour down. Around her, an oval of soft golden light; behind, the dim gold and blue of the chapel sanctuary. Keep the rays and the globe inside the arched window. No lettering: the medal's inscription, the letter M, the cross and the two hearts of the reverse are all left out.
face: Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md, a young woman of about eighteen with a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, softly rounded cheeks, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre, under the white veil; her eyes LOWERED toward the globe, as St. Catherine says they were when the rays fell.

subject: St. Raphael the Archangel as the travelling companion of young Tobias (Tob 5-6), full-length and walking, painted in the same manner as the set's St. Michael and St. Gabriel cards: great white wings, a plain gold halo, a knee-length tunic of soft sage-green with a gold-embroidered neckline, girded high at the waist with a gold cord 'as it were ready to walk' (Tob 5:5), a rose-violet travelling mantle blowing back from one shoulder, laced sandals, a tall pilgrim's staff in his left hand. With his right hand he leads by the hand the boy Tobias, about fourteen, with short dark-brown hair, in a short ochre tunic over a white undertunic, who carries a large silver fish hanging from a cord and looks up at the angel; a small white dog trots at their feet (Tob 6:1). Behind them the green banks of the river Tigris winding through a wide valley, blue hills and a small walled town far off under a clear sky. Calm, protective, unhurried. Keep the whole scene, wings and dog included, inside the arched window; no scroll, no lettering.
face: A radiant youthful angel, beardless and ageless, of the same family as the set's Michael and Gabriel but plainly a different face: a HEART-SHAPED face — a broad, smooth brow tapering to a NARROW, softly pointed chin, a slender straight nose, large warm HAZEL eyes under softly arched AUBURN brows, delicate high cheekbones, a gentle closed smile; thick, short AUBURN (copper-red) curls clustering round the head and over the ears, not reaching the shoulders; the head turned and inclined down toward the boy with a kindly gaze. Not Michael's golden curls and rosy oval face, not Gabriel's long light-brown waves.

subject: The icon of Our Lady of Perpetual Help (Sant'Alfonso all'Esquilino, Rome), painted faithfully as an icon on a burnished gold ground, half-length: Our Lady in a dark-blue maphorion edged and hatched with gold, drawn over her head, a small gold eight-pointed star on the veil above her brow, a dark-red tunic beneath; she holds the Child on her left arm, her right hand open before him. The Child, in a green tunic with a red sash and a golden-ochre mantle, turns his head back over his shoulder toward the angel at the upper right, both his hands clasping his Mother's right thumb; one sandal hangs loose by its strap from his dangling foot. Small half-figures of two angels in the upper corners, hands veiled: St. Michael at the upper left with the lance, the sponge on its reed and the vessel of gall, St. Gabriel at the upper right with the three-barred cross and the nails. The icon's flat, linear Cretan manner, no landscape. No lettering: the Greek abbreviations of the icon are left out.
face: The icon's own face, not the set's Our Lady: a LONG, NARROW Byzantine face — a long, very thin straight nose, large, dark, almond-shaped eyes with heavy lids under long, thin, high-arched brows, a SMALL, closed, dark-red mouth, a long smooth cheek and a small chin; olive skin; the head inclined a little toward the Child and the gaze turned out to the viewer, grave and sorrowful. The Child: a small boy of about three with a round face, short brown hair, his head turned back and up toward the angel with the cross. The angels: small, round, youthful faces with short brown curls.

subject: Sts. Louis and Zélie Martin, the married couple of Alençon, half-length side by side, each with a plain gold halo, in the dress of their photographs of about 1875: Louis on the left in a dark, high-buttoned frock coat with a white shirt collar, Zélie on the right in a dark-brown silk dress buttoned to the throat, with a small brooch at the collar. She holds across her hands a length of fine white Alençon point lace, her trade; he rests one hand on a small open watchmaker's case with a pocket watch, his. Her other hand is laid on his arm. Behind them a street of Alençon with the tall Flamboyant Gothic porch and tower of the church of Notre-Dame under a soft evening sky. Quiet, tender, dignified; no children; no lettering.
face: Two clearly different people from their photographs. Zélie (right): a woman of about forty-four with a BROAD face and a SQUARE, firm jaw — wide cheekbones, level dark brows over steady dark eyes set rather wide, a straight, firm nose, a wide, straight mouth closed in the hint of a smile, a firm chin; dark-brown hair parted in the centre and smoothed flat over the ears into a low knot; no veil; her gaze on the viewer, frank and warm.

subject: The Divine Mercy image as Eugeniusz Kazimirowski painted it under St. Faustina's direction (Vilnius, 1934): the risen Christ standing full-length and stepping toward us, barefoot, in a long, loose white robe with wide sleeves; his right hand raised in blessing at shoulder height, his left hand touching the robe over his breast, where it falls open a little; from the breast two broad rays stream down and widen toward the ground, one pale, translucent white-blue and one red, falling across the robe. A deep night-blue background with a faint pale glow around him and the floor just suggested under his feet. Keep the image's stillness: no landscape, no other figures, rays kept inside the arched window; no lettering, no inscription or banner beneath.
face: Christ as in recurring-figures.md: a man of about thirty-three with a LONG OVAL face narrowing gently to the chin — a high, smooth forehead, a long straight nose with a fine bridge, calm almond-shaped dark-brown eyes under level brown brows, high, softly modelled cheekbones, a quiet closed mouth; chestnut-brown hair parted in the centre and falling in soft waves past the shoulders; a short, full chestnut beard and moustache, lightly parted at the chin; a plain gold halo; the lids a little lowered, the gaze turned gently DOWN toward the viewer as in Kazimirowski's painting. The wounds show only as small, clean marks on the hands and feet.

subject: The Holy Face of Tours: the 'Veronica', as in the facsimile of the veil kept at St. Peter's in Rome that Ven. Léon Dupont venerated at Tours from 1851 with a lamp burning before it. A square linen veil, its two upper corners knotted and hung from two nails, filling most of the arched window against a deep violet ground; on the veil, the imprinted Face of the suffering Christ seen frontally, in warm sepia-brown and soft flesh tones, the veil's lower folds falling loose around it. Below the veil, a small oil lamp burning in a brass holder. No crown of thorns (the facsimile shows none), no angels, no Veronica, no figures; no lettering (the facsimile's Latin caption is left out).
face: The Face is Christ's set face from recurring-figures.md, imprinted on the cloth: a LONG OVAL face narrowing gently to the chin, a high forehead, a long straight nose with a fine bridge, level brows drawn a little together in pain, a quiet closed mouth; chestnut-brown hair parted in the centre and falling long on either side, a short, full beard parted at the chin; the EYES CLOSED, a few drops of blood on the brow and running down from the eyes and lips like tears, as on the Tours facsimile. Sorrowful and peaceful, not gory; no halo.

subject: St. Gerard Majella, the Redemptorist lay brother, half-length in the black Redemptorist habit with its plain white turned-down collar, as in his traditional portrait; he holds a wooden crucifix against his breast with his right hand, his left laid flat over his heart. face: A young man of about twenty-nine, pale from consumption, with a LONG, rather rectangular face — a high, broad forehead, a long straight nose with a rounded tip, light-brown eyes under HEAVY upper lids, raised to heaven, softly arched brows, lightly hollowed cheeks, a small mouth with a fuller lower lip, a rounded chin; thick, STRAIGHT dark-brown hair cut short and combed back from the brow, the ears showing; clean-shaven; the head tilted to his right. subject: Our Lady, Undoer of Knots, after Johann Georg Melchior Schmidtner's altarpiece of about 1700 in St. Peter am Perlach, Augsburg: Our Lady standing full-length as the Woman of the Apocalypse, on a crescent moon on a bank of cloud, her foot on the head of a coiled serpent; a rose-red gown and a deep-blue mantle billowing out from her shoulders, her head bare, twelve small gold stars in a ring above it; with both hands she unties a knot in a long white ribbon. At the left a kneeling angel in a pale robe hands up the knotted end of the ribbon; at the right a winged angel receives the smooth, untied end. Above her head the Holy Spirit as a white dove in a glow of light, and small cherub heads in the clouds about her. Far below, very small on a dark strip of land, an angel walking with a youth (Tobias and Raphael, as in the painting). Warm golden Baroque light; keep all of it inside the arched window; no lettering.
face: The painting's own Madonna, close to the set's face: a young woman of about twenty with a softly OVAL face bent forward and a little to her right — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose, the eyes LOWERED to the knot in her hands under gently arched light-brown brows, softly rounded cheeks, a small closed rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre and falling loose behind her shoulders, no veil. St. Laurence O'Toole, half-length, an Irish archbishop of about 1175: a white alb, a deep-red chasuble of the twelfth century falling in wide, soft folds, a low white mitre; a simple crozier with a curled head in his left hand, his right raised in blessing. Behind him the valley of Glendalough in the Wicklow hills, where he was abbot: a slender stone round tower with a conical cap and small stone churches among the trees beside a still, dark lake, wooded slopes rising steeply on either side under a soft, clouded Irish sky. Grave, prudent and charitable; no wound, no attacker, no lettering.
face: An Irish prince of Leinster of about fifty, TALL and lean, with a fair, lightly weathered complexion and a LONG face with a STRONG, ANGULAR jaw whose corners show clearly — a high, straight forehead, a LONG, HIGH-BRIDGED, gently ARCHED nose, DEEP-SET, steady grey eyes under STRAIGHT, dark brows drawn a little together, flat, lean cheeks, a WIDE, firm, thin-lipped mouth; dark-brown hair greying, cut short below the mitre; a SHORT, CLOSE-TRIMMED dark-brown BEARD streaked with grey, following the angular jaw; the look grave and resolute. Not the clean-shaven, smooth, neat-nosed malachi_armagh, the broad, white-haired columba, the long, flaxen finbarr, the square, snub-nosed gall, the big-boned, red-grey columban or the clean-shaven thomas_becket.

subject: St. Stanislas Kostka, half-length, a Polish Jesuit novice of seventeen in Rome in 1568: a plain black Jesuit cassock buttoned to the throat with a narrow white collar; he holds a small sprig of white lilies against his breast with his crossed hands, a black rosary hanging from his fingers. Behind him the novitiate garden on the Quirinal hill in the August evening: a low wall, cypresses and orange trees, and below, the tiled roofs, towers and domes of Rome in golden light. Young, bright, sweet-tempered and fervent; no angels, no lettering.
face: A Polish youth of seventeen, BEARDLESS, with a fair, fresh complexion and a face BROAD across the EYES and cheekbones, narrowing gently to a small, ROUNDED chin — a smooth, rounded forehead, a LONG, STRAIGHT nose, BROAD at its base, LARGE, dark-brown eyes set WIDE under HEAVY, half-lowered upper lids, dark brows ARCHED HIGH above them, smooth, softly full cheeks, a SMALL, FULL, slightly POUTING mouth with a SHORT upper lip; dark-brown hair cut short and straight across the brow; the look bright and gentle, lifted a little. Not the round, short-nosed boy pancras, the upturned-nosed herman_joseph, the tousle-curled carlo_acutis, the flat-cheeked, low-bridged venantius_camerino, the long, narrow casimir, the triangular peter_luxemburg or the straw-fair, narrow-faced student of john_kanty.

subject: St. Andrew Avellino, half-length, a very old Theatine priest in 1608, vested for Mass: a white alb with a lace border, a gold-and-cream Roman chasuble, a plain maniple; he stands at the foot of the altar with his hands joined before his breast and his head a little bowed, beginning the Mass. Behind him a Neapolitan church interior: the altar with a white cloth, six tall candles and a crucifix, a gilded frame on the wall beyond, the light from a high window falling on him.
