face: A southern Italian of about eighty-eight with a pale, parchment-soft olive complexion and a BROAD, BIG-BONED, SQUARE face — a massive, smooth, BALD DOME with a few wisps of white hair above the ears, a STRONG, straight brow, a SHORT, broad nose with a FLATTENED, rounded tip, SMALL, deep-set, kindly dark eyes under BUSHY, white brows, wide cheekbones with softened hollows below, a wide, firm mouth; a SHORT, FULL, ROUNDED white beard and moustache, neatly kept; the gaze lowered to the altar, patient and gentle. Not his order's founder cajetan (round, soft, dark-bearded), the bald, rectangular, ruddy john_leonardi, the gaunt, hook-nosed laurence_justinian, the soft, long francis_caracciolo, the bony, bald peter_alcantara or the clean-shaven, bald andre_soveral.

subject: St. Hubert, half-length, a Frankish bishop of the early eighth century, bareheaded (no mitre): a white linen alb and over it a wide, plain, moss-green bell-shaped chasuble falling in soft folds; a simple wooden crozier with a curled head in his left hand, his right raised in blessing; an ivory hunting horn on a leather cord hangs at his side, the one sign of the huntsman he had been. Behind him the forest of the Ardennes in autumn: tall oaks and beeches with golden leaves, a small wooden church with a stone cross in a clearing, and between the trees, a little way off, an ordinary red deer stag standing calmly and looking toward him. Kindly, vigorous and at peace; no crucifix between the stag's antlers, no hounds, no weapons, no lettering.
face: A Frank of about sixty-five, broad-shouldered, with a ruddy, weathered outdoor complexion and a face WIDEST at HIGH, ROUNDED, JUTTING cheekbones, tapering below them to a FIRM, fairly narrow chin (a wide inverted egg) — a broad, smooth forehead, a SHORT, straight nose with FLARED nostrils, DEEP-SET, far-seeing pale-blue eyes with deep crow's-feet from years in the open, THICK, TUFTED sandy-grey brows, a wide, good-humoured mouth; thick, WAVY sandy hair going grey, left fairly full; a FULL, ROUNDED, sandy-grey beard of medium length that follows the tapering chin; the gaze warm and direct. Not his master lambert (long, parallel-sided, square-jawed, short dense iron-grey beard), the hawkish, forward-chinned hunter eustachius, the oblong, domed, round-chinned huntsman germanus_auxerre, the broad, snub-nosed boniface or the long, symmetrical remigius.

subject: St. Theodore Tyro, half-length, a young recruit of a Roman legion in the year 306: a red woollen tunic under a shirt of iron ring-mail, a dark-red cloak pinned at the right shoulder, bareheaded; he holds a martyr's palm upright in his right hand, his left resting on the rim of a plain oval shield, and makes no gesture of war. Behind him Amasea in Pontus in winter: the steep river gorge with the royal tombs cut into the cliff face, the small town on the riverbank below, snow on the far hills under a clear, cold sky. Young, steadfast and serene; no fire, no burning temple, no dragon, no lettering, no letters or monogram on the shield.
face: A Greek of the East of about twenty-two, a recruit, with a warm olive complexion and a NARROW, LONG face with a CLASSICAL GREEK PROFILE — the nose continuing the line of the forehead WITHOUT a dip, long and straight, LARGE, dark, ALMOND eyes under HEAVY upper lids and long, level black brows, lean cheeks, a SMALL, full, firmly closed mouth, a NARROW chin; thick, straight, glossy BLACK hair falling in a full bowl OVER the ears; a SHORT, dense, BLACK young beard, as the Painter's Manual has him; the gaze steady and calm. Not the curly young george and sebastian, the hawkish eustachius, the joined-browed romanus_ostiarius, the round, grizzled marcellus_centurion, the smooth, beardless pantaleon or the bell-shaped theodoret_antioch.

subject: St. Edmund of Canterbury, half-length, an English archbishop of about 1238: a white alb, a plain white chasuble with a narrow gold orphrey, a low white mitre; a crozier in his left hand, and in his right an open book resting against his breast, the scholar of Oxford and Paris. Behind him the Cistercian abbey of Pontigny in Burgundy, where he is buried: a long, plain church of pale stone with tall lancet windows and no tower, orchards and meadows, a few white-habited monks small in the distance, a soft, clear sky. Gentle, learned and steadfast; no lettering.
face: An Englishman of about sixty-five, spare from fasting, with a fair, pale complexion and a LEAN, ANGULAR face WIDEST at HIGH, SHARP cheekbones — a TALL, straight forehead, a nose with a pronounced DOWNWARD HOOK at its tip, PALE-GREY, deep-set, kindly eyes under thin, level grey brows, deep vertical lines beside a THIN-LIPPED, gently smiling mouth, a small, POINTED chin; CLEAN-SHAVEN; thin grey hair cut short below the mitre; the gaze mild and thoughtful. Not the long-headed, jutting-chinned, short-bearded anselm, the long, fine-nosed thomas_becket, the triangular, hollow simon_stock, the square-bearded augustine_canterbury, the bulge-browed elphege or the broad, snub-nosed richard_chichester.

subject: St. Leonard, half-length, a Frankish hermit of the sixth century: a plain, dark-brown monk's cowl of rough wool with the hood fallen back; in his right hand he holds up a pair of OPENED iron fetters with a short broken chain, the sign of the prisoners he comforted and set free, and his left hand rests on his breast. Behind him the forest of Noblac near Limoges: chestnut and oak woods, a small stone oratory with a wooden cross beside a clear river, a rocky hillside, soft morning light. Gentle, compassionate and recollected; no prison, no captives, no lettering.
face: A Frank of about fifty with a fair, lightly weathered complexion and a face that is WIDE and FLAT across the EYES — a broad, low forehead, a BROAD, straight nose with a LOW bridge, WIDE-SET, soft brown eyes that SLOPE gently DOWN at their outer corners under thick, low, dark-brown brows, broad, flat cheeks, a WIDE mouth with FULL, gentle lips, a broad, ROUNDED chin; thick dark-brown hair around a monastic tonsure; a SHORT, CURLY dark-brown beard, just touched with grey; the gaze kind and patient. Not the long-headed, close-eyed ludger, the heart-shaped, Irish-tonsured fiaker, the broad, square-jawed lambert, the hooded, triangular anthony_abbot or the wide, short, flat-faced Crispin of crispin_crispinian (clean-shaven).

subject: St. Bertille, half-length, a Frankish abbess of the seventh century: a black Benedictine habit and scapular, a close white wimple and a long black veil; a plain wooden abbess's staff with a simple curved head in her left hand, and in her right a small book of the Rule held against her breast. Behind her the abbey of Chelles by the Marne: a simple stone church with a low tower and a cloister wall, a few nuns small at the gate, poplars along the river and green fields under a soft, pale sky. Grave, humble and steadfast; no lettering.
face: A Frankish noblewoman of about fifty-five, spare from long austerities, with a fair, pale complexion and a LONG face with a LONG, gently DOWN-CURVING, AQUILINE nose — a smooth forehead under the wimple band, DEEP-SET, clear grey-blue eyes under HEAVY, softly arched lids and straight, light-brown brows, clearly marked cheekbones over LEAN, slightly sunken cheeks, a SMALL, FIRM, closed mouth, a NARROW, ROUNDED chin; all hair hidden under the wimple; the gaze lowered and quiet. Not her queen bathildes (round, full, short-nosed), the broad, square-jawed bertha_blangy, the long, slender-nosed young rosalia, the long, square-chinned, low-browed elena_guerra, the drooping-eyed maria_santocanale or the heart-shaped angela_merici.

subject: St. Didacus, half-length, a Spanish Franciscan lay brother of the fifteenth century: a patched grey-brown Franciscan habit with a deep hood lying on the shoulders and a knotted white cord; he holds a plain wooden cross upright against his breast with both hands, embracing it. Behind him the friary of Alcalá de Henares on the Castilian plain: a simple brick-and-stone church with a small bell gable, a friary garden, a few poor folk waiting small at the door, dry golden fields and a pale, high sky. Humble, meek and joyful; no roses, no lettering.
face: An Andalusian of about sixty with a sun-browned olive complexion and a LONG, NARROW, SMOOTH OVAL face after Zurbarán — a high, narrow forehead, a very LONG, THIN, straight nose with a slight DROOP at its tip, SMALL, soft, dark ALMOND eyes under THIN, HIGH-arching black brows, gently hollow cheeks, a SMALL, pursed, closed mouth, a LONG, NARROW chin; CLEAN-SHAVEN; black hair greying at the sides in the Franciscan crown; the gaze turned a little aside, mild and humble. Not the angular, moustached paschal_baylon, the bony, bald peter_alcantara, the round frei_galvao, the broad benedito or the heart-shaped nicholas_tolentino.

subject: St. Willibrord, half-length, an Anglo-Saxon archbishop of about the year 700, bareheaded (no mitre): a white alb, a wide, plain, cream-white bell-shaped chasuble, and the white woollen pallium with small dark crosses that the Pope gave him; a plain wooden crozier in his left hand, a Gospel book held against his breast with his right. Behind him the low, green land of Frisia: a new stone church with a small wooden bell-cote on a mound above the flat meadows, a canal with a moored boat, dunes and a strip of grey North Sea under a wide, bright, cloud-flecked sky, a few Frisian folk in plain wool small on the path. Stately, frank and joyful; no lettering.
face: A Northumbrian of about sixty, stately and 'comely in person', with a fair, fresh, open complexion and a well-proportioned, SQUARE-OVAL face — a broad, smooth forehead, a straight nose of medium length with a slightly BROAD tip, LARGE, bright, LAUGHING blue eyes creased at the corners under fair, gently arched brows, FIRM, full cheeks with DIMPLES in a broad, frank smile that shows a little of the teeth, a STRONG, broad, CLEFT chin; CLEAN-SHAVEN; fair hair gone silver in a neat ring around the tonsure; the look joyous and direct. Not the beak-nosed, long-chinned wilfrid (his master), the long, handsome, unsmiling oswald_worcester, the milk-white, full-oval edward_confessor, the broad, snub-nosed richard_chichester, the smooth, neat-nosed malachi_armagh or the long-headed, prim ludger.

subject: St. Edward the Confessor, half-length, the last Anglo-Saxon king of England, about 1065: a long, deep-blue royal tunic embroidered at the neck, a rich crimson mantle clasped on the right shoulder with a round gold brooch, an open gold crown with trefoil points over his white hair; in his right hand a slender gold sceptre, and in his long, pale left hand, held up a little, a plain gold ring. Behind him, by the broad Thames under a soft English sky, his new Romanesque abbey church of Westminster with its round arches and central tower, pale stone still bright, and at the palace gate a few poor people waiting. Gentle, pure and kingly, eyes lowered; no lettering.
face: An Englishman of about sixty, TALL, with a milk-white complexion and ROSY cheeks, and a FULL, SMOOTH, broad OVAL face as the Vita Aedwardi describes him — a HIGH, smooth, rounded forehead, FULL, rounded, rosy cheeks without hollows, a straight, medium nose with a softly rounded tip, gentle, pale-blue eyes LOWERED under fine, white, gently arched brows, a small, kindly mouth; MILK-WHITE hair falling straight to the nape and a long, MILK-WHITE beard that PARTS into TWO soft points below the chin, as on the Bayeux Tapestry; the gaze cast down, mild and dignified. Not the crowned, grey-bearded stephen_hungary, the brown-bearded henry, the heavy-jowled, weeping gontran, the long-hexagonal ladislas, or the curly, fisherman-faced andrew.

subject: St. Wilfrid, half-length, a Northumbrian bishop of about 680: a wide, bell-shaped chasuble of deep green over a white alb, a white pallium with small dark crosses, bareheaded and tonsured; a plain wooden pastoral staff with a simple curved head in his left hand, a small gilt reliquary casket from Rome held in his right. Behind him, on a green rise above a river in the Yorkshire dales, the small stone church of his Benedictine monastery at Ripon with its round-arched door and a low tower, monks in black at its door, and white clouds moving fast over the moor. Energetic, cheerful and resolute, with the trace of a smile; no lettering.
face: A Northumbrian noble of about fifty, CLEAN-SHAVEN in the Roman manner, with a fair, fresh, wind-coloured complexion and a face whose length is in the LOWER half — a SHORT, low, square forehead, a HIGH-BRIDGED, straight, rather BEAKED nose, bright, quick, pale-grey eyes set deep in a network of SMILE LINES under straight, fair brows, sharp, high cheekbones over lean cheeks, a LONG upper lip and a wide, mobile mouth turning up at the corners, a long, FORWARD-THRUST, rounded chin; fair hair gone silver in a neat ring around the tonsure; a lively, cheerful look, "never a sour face". Not the long, handsome, fair-browed oswald_worcester, the broad, short, snub-nosed richard_chichester, the short-faced, bulging-browed elphege, or the lean, fine-nosed thomas_becket.

subject: Sts. Tarachus, Probus and Andronicus, half-length, side by side, three martyrs of Cilicia in the year 304, each holding a martyr's palm: TARACHUS (centre), the old soldier, in a plain dark-red Roman military tunic and a brown cloak pinned at the shoulder; PROBUS (left), the man of the people, in a coarse undyed wool tunic and a grey-brown mantle; ANDRONICUS (right), the young patrician of Ephesus, in a fine white tunic and a blue mantle with a narrow gold border. Behind them the stone arena of Anazarbus under a rocky crag, empty and quiet, with two wild beasts lying down peacefully at the far edge of the sand, as in the book, and the Taurus mountains beyond. Calm, united and steadfast; no wounds, no chains, no gladiators, no lettering.
face: Three clearly different men of Asia Minor with olive skin of different warmth. TARACHUS (centre), about sixty-five, a veteran: a BROAD, SQUARE, heavy-boned face with a FLAT, wide forehead, a BROKEN, slightly crooked nose with a flattened bridge, small, deep-set, steady grey eyes under thick, straight, grizzled brows, a wide, set mouth, a strong, square chin; close-cropped iron-grey hair and a short, dense, square-cut grey beard. PROBUS (left), about forty, a plebeian of Side: a LONG, LEAN face with its length in the lower half — a LONG upper lip, HOLLOW cheeks, a long, thin nose with a slight hook, large, dark, earnest eyes set CLOSE together under thin, arched black brows, a narrow, ROUNDED chin; short, untidy black hair and a thin, sparse black beard along the jaw. ANDRONICUS (right), about twenty-two, a patrician of Ephesus: BEARDLESS, with a smooth, BROAD-CHEEKED, softly HEXAGONAL face — wide, flat cheekbones, a short, straight Greek nose continuing the line of the brow, large, wide-set, light-brown eyes, a full, well-cut mouth, a firm chin; short, neat, wavy chestnut hair. Not the young, clean-shaven, triangular-faced companion of theban_legion, the brothers of nereus_achilleus or faustinus_jovita, or the two young Palestinians of adrian_eubulus.

subject: St. Ursula, half-length, a young Christian woman of Britain in the fifth century: a long gown of soft rose over a white under-tunic, a wide deep-green mantle lined with ermine-white linen, spread a little on one side as a shelter over two small maidens behind her shoulder; a thin gold circlet on her head; in her right hand a white banner with a red cross on a slender staff, in her left a single arrow held point-down together with a martyr's palm. Behind her the broad Rhine near Cologne, the walls and towers of the Roman city on the far bank, a small ship with a furled sail at the water's edge under a pale morning sky. Pure, courageous and motherly; no wound, no Huns, no lettering.
face: A Romano-British maiden of about nineteen with a fair, clear, lightly freckled complexion and a LONG OVAL face whose length is in a LONG LOWER FACE and a STRONG, ROUNDED chin — a smooth, moderate forehead, a straight GRECIAN nose running on in one line from the brow, LARGE, deep-set, clear grey eyes under STRONG, straight, auburn brows, smooth, lean cheeks, a LONG upper lip and a full, calm, closed mouth; thick COPPER-RED hair in two long plaits over the shoulders under the circlet; the gaze steady and protective. The two maidens behind her are small, one dark-haired and round-faced, one fair and fine-boned, their eyes lowered. Not the young, soft-oval agnes, lucy or cecilia, the short, square margaret_antioch, the long, narrow, golden-haired rosalia, the high-foreheaded euphrasia, or the convex-profiled julia_corsica.

subject: St. Peter of Alcantara, half-length, a Discalced Franciscan friar of about 1560: a short, patched habit of rough brown sackcloth with a knotted white cord and a short, narrow brown cloak, bareheaded as the book says he always went; a plain wooden cross held against his breast in his right hand, an open book of prayer in his left. Behind him a tiny friary of whitewashed stone and a narrow cell door among holm oaks and bare rock on a dry Castilian hillside at dawn, a pale sky with a few birds. Rapt, lean and joyful in prayer, eyes lifted; no skull, no lettering.
face: A Spaniard of Extremadura of about sixty, WORN to the bone by penance, "like the roots of trees", with a dark, weather-browned olive complexion and a LONG face in which every BONE shows — a HIGH, KNOBBED, BALD skull with a narrow ring of short dark-grey hair, PROMINENT BROW BONES, deeply SUNKEN temples and eye sockets, JUTTING cheekbones over DEEP hollows, a LONG, BONY nose with a slight HUMP at the bridge, LARGE, dark, shining eyes LIFTED upward, a WIDE, thin-lipped mouth slightly open, a long, narrow jaw under a SHORT, SPARSE dark-grey beard; rapt and luminous, not grim. Not the emaciated but white-bearded pius_v, the smooth-domed, clean-shaven bernardine_siena or john_capistrano, the long-angular, thick-browed paschal_baylon, or the horse-faced Copt paphnutius.

subject: St. Mello, half-length, a bishop of Gaul at the end of the third century: a full, bell-shaped chasuble of golden-yellow wool over a white alb, a plain white pallium, bareheaded; a simple wooden pastoral staff with a curled head in his left hand, his right hand raised in blessing. Behind him the small Gallo-Roman town of Rotomagus (Rouen) on the Seine, with red-tiled roofs, a plain small church with a wooden cross, and a loop of the wide river among green, wooded hills under a soft grey-blue Norman sky. Peaceful, zealous and fatherly; no lettering.
face: A Briton of about seventy-five, tall and spare, with a fair, weathered, pink complexion and a DISH-SHAPED face in profile — a PROMINENT, rounded brow and a PROMINENT, firm chin with the middle of the face set back between them: a SHORT, slightly SNUB nose, broad, FLAT cheeks, ROUND, bright, pale-blue eyes set rather CLOSE together under long, feathery white brows, a small mouth; long, straight, fine white hair falling to the shoulders, a LONG, full, softly WAVING white beard to the breast; a kindly, serene gaze. Not the pear-shaped, clean-shaven albinus_angers, the shield-shaped paternus_avranches, the long, symmetrical, silver-bearded remigius, the rectangular, dark-grey-bearded lambert, or the square, laughing medard.

subject: St. Mark, Pope, half-length, a Roman bishop of the year 336 in the dress of his age: a long, full white dalmatic with two narrow purple stripes (clavi), over it a plain, deep-red paenula-chasuble falling in soft folds, and a narrow white woollen pallium marked with small dark crosses around his shoulders; no tiara, no mitre, bareheaded. He holds a closed codex of the Gospels bound in plain leather against his breast with both hands. Behind him, under a clear Roman sky, the new brick basilica he built rising among cypresses and umbrella pines outside the city on the Via Ardeatina, its timber roof half on, a few building stones and a wooden ladder at its foot, as in the book's engraving; the Aurelian walls far off. Watchful, humble and steady; no lettering.
face: A Roman of about sixty-five with a warm, light-olive complexion and a ROUND, FIRM face as WIDE as it is long — not fleshy: a ROUND, bald crown ringed at the sides and back by short, CRISP, curly grey hair, a broad, smooth forehead crossed by ONE deep vertical FROWN LINE between the brows, FIRM, apple-round cheekbones, a SHORT, straight nose with a HIGH, narrow bridge, SMALL, keen, DEEP-SET dark-brown eyes under THICK, STRAIGHT, dark-grey brows, deep lines running from the nose to the corners of a small, firm, closed mouth; a SHORT, crisp, curly grey beard following the round line of the jaw to a blunt point; the gaze level, alert and watchful. Not the soft, round, mild-eyed gal_clermont, the flat-featured, flat-nosed zephyrinus, the curl-browed, protruding-eyed felix_i, the heavy-lidded, fleshy marcellinus_pope, or the long, narrow sylvester.

subject: St. Francis Borgia, half-length, the former Duke of Gandia become a Jesuit priest: a plain black Jesuit cassock and a long black mantle, bareheaded; in his left hand, held low, a small ivory skull wearing a little gold ducal crown, the sign of the queen's funeral that turned him from the world, as in the Spanish paintings; his right hand open toward it in a gesture of renunciation. Behind him, through a round arch, the palace of the dukes at Gandia among orange groves on the Valencian plain, and far off the blue sea. Serene, detached and humble; the skull small, clean and ivory, no lettering.
face: A Spanish grandee of about sixty, TALL and gaunt, with a pale, olive complexion and a very LONG face under a HIGH, SMOOTH, egg-shaped BALD DOME with only a narrow fringe of short grey hair above the ears — a tall forehead, a LONG, LARGE nose, straight in the bridge and ending in a FULL, slightly DROOPING tip, dark, gentle eyes that SLANT DOWN at the outer corners under heavy lids, with dark shadows beneath, level grey brows, sharp cheekbones over LONG, HOLLOW cheeks, a NARROW, long jaw; a THIN grey moustache and a SMALL grey tuft on the chin, the cheeks shaven; the gaze lowered, sorrowful and kind. Not the round-faced, dark-bearded ignatius_loyola, the domed but short-faced, round-eyed antoninus_florence, the broad-jawed turibius, or the triangular john_capistrano.

subject: St. Gall, half-length, an Irish hermit-monk of about 620: a plain, coarse black monastic cowl with its hood thrown back, a leather belt and a small leather book satchel on a strap; a long, rough hazel staff in his right hand, a round loaf of bread in his left. Behind him, in a clearing of the dark fir forest above the Steinach near the Lake of Constance, a small fire and a half-built log cell, as in the book's engraving; at the edge of the clearing a small brown bear carrying a log of firewood toward the fire, and the silver lake with snowy Alps far off. Humble, steadfast and kindly; the bear small and tame, no lettering.
face: An Irishman of about seventy, stocky and weathered, with a ruddy, windburnt, freckled complexion and a COMPACT, SQUARE face on a thick neck — the front of the head shaved from ear to ear in the Irish tonsure, leaving a broad, lined forehead, with thick, straight sandy-white hair falling behind the ears to the nape; a SHORT, BROAD, slightly UPTURNED nose, SMALL, bright, deep-set blue eyes creased at the corners under THICK, sandy-white brows, round, ruddy cheekbones, a WIDE, firm mouth, a broad, square chin under a SHORT, thick, BRISTLY sandy-white beard cut square; a steady, warm gaze. Not the long, big-boned, jutting-chinned, red-grey columban, the broad, clean-shaven, white-haired columba, the heart-shaped, dark-bearded fiaker, the long, narrow, flaxen-bearded finbarr, or the hooded, grey-bearded francis_paola.

subject: St. Louis Bertrand, half-length, a Spanish Dominican friar of about 1565: the white Dominican habit and scapular under a black cappa with its black hood drawn up over the head, as in Zurbarán's painting; a plain wooden crucifix raised a little in his right hand as he preaches, his left hand open at his breast. Behind him the Caribbean coast of New Granada at Cartagena: a sandy bay with a few palms, a small whitewashed mission chapel with a wooden cross, and on the shore a group of indigenous people of the coast, small in the distance, listening; a warm, clear tropical light. Grave, gentle and ardent; no chalice, no serpent, no lettering.
face: A Valencian of about forty, lean and grave, with a sallow olive complexion and an INVERTED-TRIANGLE face after Zurbarán's portrait — a BROAD, smooth forehead and wide temples narrowing sharply along FLAT, hollow cheeks to a NARROW, POINTED chin; a LONG, straight nose with a slightly BROADENED tip, HEAVY upper lids LOWERED over dark eyes, STRAIGHT, dark brows set LOW and close above them, a small, thin, downturned mouth; black hair hidden under the hood; a THIN dark moustache and a SMALL, sparse, pointed tuft of beard on the chin; the look withdrawn and recollected. Not the long, full-oval, clean-shaven vincent_ferrer, the soft, heavy-lidded, long-oval thomas_villanova, the square-round peter_verona, or the rectangular, grey-goateed robert_bellarmine.

subject: St. Remigius, half-length, a very tall Gallo-Roman bishop of about 500: a full, bell-shaped white chasuble with a gold orphrey over a white alb, a low white mitre; a plain gilt crosier in his left hand, and in his right a small glass flask of holy chrism, held up before his breast. Behind him, the Gallo-Roman city of Reims: a small early church with a round-arched baptistery, Roman walls and a triumphal arch, the flat Champagne plain and a golden winter sky of Christmas morning. Majestic, gentle and serene; no king, no dove, no lettering.
face: A Gallo-Roman noble of about sixty, UNUSUALLY TALL, with a LONG NECK and a pale, fine complexion and a LONG, NOBLE, symmetrical face — a HIGH, broad, smooth forehead, a LONG, straight, finely cut nose, LARGE, calm grey eyes set LEVEL under LONG, straight silver brows, smooth, LONG cheeks, a small, serene closed mouth, a long, gently rounded chin; silver-grey hair cut short below the mitre; a MEDIUM, neatly combed silver beard, smooth and oval, not full or flowing; the gaze calm and a little lowered, with 'blended majesty and serenity'. Not the lantern-jawed gregory_langres, the square, laughing medard, the square-bearded, domed germanus_auxerre, or the clean-shaven, underbitten germanus_paris.

subject: St. Catherine of Genoa, half-length, a Genoese noblewoman become a widow and servant of the sick: a plain dark-grey woollen gown and a long white linen veil and wimple framing the face, a small wooden crucifix on a cord at her breast; she holds before her, in both hands, a simple earthenware bowl of broth, as she carried it to the sick in the great hospital of Pammatone. Behind her, through a round arch, a whitewashed hospital ward with a row of beds under a vaulted ceiling, and beyond a window the terraced houses and harbour of Genoa on its steep hillside above a bright blue sea. Ardent, recollected and tender; no flames, no purgatory, no lettering.
face: A Genoese noblewoman of about fifty-five with a pale ivory complexion and a DIAMOND-SHAPED face — a NARROW, high forehead under the wimple, the face WIDEST at HIGH, PROMINENT cheekbones with soft hollows beneath, then narrowing along a lean jaw to a NARROW, firm, pointed chin; a LONG, THIN, HIGH-BRIDGED aquiline nose whose tip turns slightly down, LARGE, deep-set grey-green eyes with faint violet shadows beneath, THIN, sharply ARCHED dark brows, a narrow, thin-lipped mouth; hair hidden; the gaze lifted a little, burning and inward. Not the young, oval catherine_siena, the small, short-nosed colette, the moon-faced catherine_ricci, or the broad, square jane_frances_chantal.

subject: St. Placid, half-length, a young Benedictine monk: a plain black monastic habit and cowl, the hood fallen back, hands joined in prayer before his breast, a small wooden cross on a cord. Behind him, the lake of Subiaco in the deep, wooded gorge of the Aniene, with the cliffside cells of St. Benedict's first monasteries on the rocks above, the still water where he once fell in and was drawn out, green holm-oaks and a clear Italian sky. Innocent, obedient and serene; no palm, no martyrdom, no other figures, no lettering.
face: A young Roman patrician of about twenty, BEARDLESS, with a pale olive complexion and a LONG, NARROW OVAL face — a narrow, high forehead, a SLENDER, HIGH-BRIDGED Roman nose, LARGE, ALMOND-SHAPED dark-brown eyes set a little wide under thin, LEVEL dark brows, softly HOLLOW cheeks, a small, full-lipped mouth, a DELICATE, NARROW chin; black hair cut in a thick ring round a monastic tonsure; the gaze lifted, as in Perugino's panel, clear and innocent. Not the round-faced boy pancras, the soft-oval aloysius_gonzaga, or the heart-shaped, older nicholas_tolentino.

subject: St. Firmin, half-length, a missionary bishop of the third century: a simple, full red chasuble over a white alb, a low, plain white mitre, a plain wooden crosier in his left hand; his right hand raised in blessing over the unseen crowd; a martyr's palm tucked in the crook of his arm. Behind him, the green marshes and water-gardens of the Somme at Amiens, reeds and poplars along the river, and on a rise the low stone walls and red-tiled roofs of the small Gallo-Roman town of Samarobriva under a soft, bright northern sky. Zealous, warm and fearless; no cathedral, no wound, no lettering.
face: A Navarrese of Pamplona of about forty, CLEAN-SHAVEN, with a sun-warm olive complexion and a LONG, NARROW face with a STRONG, PROJECTING CHIN — a high, narrow forehead, a LONG, STRAIGHT nose running from the brow with hardly a dip, NARROW-SET, bright black eyes under STRONGLY ARCHED, thick black brows, FLAT cheeks under clean cheekbones, a thin, firm, wide mouth, a long jaw ending in a DEEP, slightly jutting chin; thick, straight black hair cut short below the mitre; the gaze eager and bright, toward his people. Not the fair, long-faced thomas_becket, the young symphorian, or the hawk-nosed, bearded Eustachius of this batch.

subject: St. Thomas of Villanova, half-length, an archbishop who kept the friar's poverty: the plain black habit of the Hermits of St. Augustine with its black leather belt, over it a simple white rochet and a plain dark cope, a low, unadorned white mitre, a simple pectoral cross; in his right hand a small open leather purse from which he gives a coin to a poor barefoot boy who reaches up at his side, in his left a plain crosier. Behind him, the Gothic bell tower of Valencia cathedral (the Micalet), flat roofs and palms, and the blue Mediterranean beyond under a warm Spanish sky. Gentle, grave and generous; no lettering.
face: A Castilian of La Mancha of about sixty-five, CLEAN-SHAVEN, with a warm olive complexion and a LONG, SOFT OVAL face after his Spanish portraits — a high forehead RECEDING at the temples, a LONG, straight nose with a FLESHY, rounded tip, LARGE, dark eyes under HEAVY, DROOPING upper lids, lowered in thought, thick, straight dark brows with a deep vertical CREASE between them, smooth, full cheeks, a FULL lower lip, a soft, rounded jaw with a hint of fullness beneath the chin; short dark hair touched with grey under the mitre; the gaze lowered, gentle and grave. Not the wide, angular, broad-jawed john_sahagun, nor the lean, narrow, fine-nosed thomas_becket.

subject: St. Finbarr, half-length, an Irish monk-bishop of the sixth century: a plain undyed white woollen cowl with a dark-brown mantle, a short Irish crook-headed crosier of bronze-bound wood in his left hand, a small book satchel of tooled leather on a strap across his breast; his right hand raised, teaching. Behind him, the marshy islands of the River Lee where Cork began: a small wooden church and round-roofed wattle cells on a green island among reeds and willows, a few students in white by the water, low wooded hills and a soft, silver Irish sky. Gentle, learned and welcoming; no lettering.
face: An Irishman of about fifty with a fair, pink, lightly freckled complexion and a LONG, NARROW face with a SOFT, gently RECEDING chin — a high, bare forehead under the Irish tonsure shaved from ear to ear, a LONG, straight nose with a NARROW bridge, deep-set, PALE-BLUE eyes whose outer corners SLOPE DOWN, faint, near-white brows, high, FLAT cheekbones, a small, gentle mouth; hair of a striking PALE WHITE-BLOND (the 'fair crest' of his name) falling from behind the ears; a SOFT, pale-flaxen beard of medium length, PARTED into two short forks; the gaze kindly, toward his pupils. Not the broad, open, clean-shaven, white-haired columba, the big-boned, jutting-chinned columban, or the heart-shaped, dark-bearded fiaker.

subject: St. Gerard, half-length, a Benedictine abbot of the tenth century: a plain black monastic cowl with wide sleeves, the hood fallen on the shoulders, a simple wooden abbot's staff in his right hand; in his left, held with care against his breast, a small house-shaped reliquary of gilt copper, the relic of St. Eugene he brought from Saint-Denis. Behind him, the small Romanesque stone abbey church of Brogne with a low square tower, a few monastery roofs and a walled garden, in a green valley of the Namur country with wooded hills and a stream, under a clear morning sky. Sweet-tempered, recollected and joyful; no lettering.
face: A noble of the Namur country of about sixty, once a soldier, CLEAN-SHAVEN, with a fair, ruddy complexion and a SHORT, WIDE, SQUARE-OVAL face with FULL, ROUNDED cheeks — a broad, low forehead under the tonsure, a SHORT, slightly UPTURNED nose with a rounded tip, ROUND, warm brown eyes with deep laughter lines, BUSHY brown-grey brows, a WIDE, kindly mouth set in a DIMPLED half-smile, a short, ROUND chin; greying brown hair in a thick monastic crown; the gaze warm and engaging, toward us, with the 'engaging sweetness of temper' of the book. Not the Greek-nosed hugh_cluny, the white-bearded gal_clermont, or the lean, high-browed benedict_aniane.

subject: St. Lambert, half-length, a Frankish bishop of about 700: a full, bell-shaped red chasuble with a plain gold orphrey over a white alb, a white pallium-like band with small dark crosses, a low white mitre; a plain wooden crosier in his left hand, a martyr's palm held against his breast with his right. Behind him, the abbey of Stavelot in the wooded Ardennes in winter: a small stone church, a tall plain stone cross before its door standing in fresh snow, dark fir-covered hills under a pale, cold dawn sky. Steadfast, humble and calm; no weapons, no wound, no lettering.
face: A Frankish noble of about sixty-five, broad-shouldered and strongly built, with a fair, weathered complexion and a LONG, RECTANGULAR face whose sides run nearly PARALLEL — a WIDE, FLAT, level forehead, a STRAIGHT, SQUARE jaw as wide as the brow, a long, straight nose ending in a BROAD, rounded tip, WIDE-SET, calm hazel eyes under THICK, STRAIGHT, dark-grey brows, a wide, firm mouth with a full lower lip; iron-grey hair cut short under the mitre and a SHORT, DENSE beard, dark-grey streaked with silver, trimmed close and square; the gaze level and composed. Not the broad, flat-planed, snub-nosed boniface, the short, curly-bearded denis, the white-haired, brow-ridged david_wales, or the lantern-jawed gregory_langres.

subject: Three soldiers of the Theban Legion side by side, half-length, as their captain St. Maurice (centre) tells the emperor they will not shed innocent blood: all three in Roman scale armour over short tunics, bareheaded, their helmets laid aside. Maurice wears a deep-red officer's cloak, his right hand on his breast, his left holding his sword reversed, point down, as one who lays it down; Exuperius (left) sets his round shield on the ground; Candidus (right) holds a martyr's palm. Behind them, the narrow valley of the Rhône at Agaunum, the river between towering grey limestone cliffs and green Alpine slopes, the tents of a Roman camp and a long rank of soldiers with lowered spears in the distance. Calm, loyal and unresisting; no blood, no executioner, no lettering.
face: Three clearly different men of Upper Egypt. MAURICE (centre), about forty, with DEEP-BROWN skin as in the Magdeburg statue: a LONG OVAL face with a HIGH, rounded forehead, HIGH, PROMINENT cheekbones, a BROAD, straight nose with rounded nostrils, full, well-drawn lips, large, calm dark eyes under straight black brows, a strong, ROUNDED chin; short, tightly curled black hair and a SHORT, close black beard along the jaw; the gaze steady and serene. EXUPERIUS (left), about fifty-five, warm olive-brown: a SQUARE, heavy-browed face with a strong, HOOKED nose, deep-set dark eyes, a wide, thin mouth and a SHORT, grizzled grey-black beard; close-cropped grey hair. CANDIDUS (right), about twenty-two, light-brown, BEARDLESS: a NARROW, TRIANGULAR face with a small, pointed chin, a straight, fine nose, large almond-shaped dark eyes lifted upward, short, straight black hair. Not the beardless young charles_lwanga, the round benedito, or the old, hooded Egyptians paphnutius and macarius_alexandria.

subject: St. Eustachius, half-length, a Roman general of the second century at the moment of his calling: a bronze muscled cuirass with leather straps over a short red tunic, a deep-red military cloak clasped at the right shoulder, a hunting horn slung at his side; bareheaded, his right hand laid on his breast and his left half-raised in awe. Behind him and a little to one side, in a sunlit clearing of a deep oak forest, a great white stag stands still and turns its head toward him; between its antlers shines a small radiant golden crucifix, the figure on it tiny and serene (Christ as in recurring-figures.md, too small for features). Awed, converted and humble; no hounds attacking, no brazen bull, no fire, no lettering.
face: A Roman of about forty-five with a light-olive, sun-browned complexion and a HAWKISH face — a NARROW, high forehead, a LARGE, PROMINENT, high-bridged AQUILINE nose, keen dark eyes set CLOSE together under strong, ANGLED black brows, LEAN cheeks with deep lines from nose to mouth, a strong, FORWARD-JUTTING chin; short, crisp black hair going grey at the temples; a SHORT, close-trimmed black beard edged with grey along the jaw; the gaze wide-eyed with wonder, fixed on the stag. Not the young, curly george or sebastian, the sandy, cleft-chinned victor_marseilles, or the clean-shaven, old, hook-nosed laurence_justinian.

subject: Blessed Fulton J. Sheen, Archbishop, who preached the Gospel to millions on radio in The Catholic Hour and on television in Life Is Worth Living, half-length in a bishop's black cassock piped and buttoned in red-purple, the purple zucchetto, and the long purple silk cape (ferraiolo) over his shoulders, as in his photographs of the 1950s; a gold pectoral cross on a chain; his right hand raised a little in a speaker's gesture, his left holding a rosary. Behind him, New York at dusk: the twin white Gothic spires of St. Patrick's Cathedral on Fifth Avenue among the towers of Manhattan, lit windows, and a deep blue evening sky. He is a Blessed, not yet canonized: behind his head there is NO halo ring and NO gold disc, only a glory of fine, straight gold RAYS spreading outward from behind the head, with no circle round them. Radiant, warm and persuasive; no microphone, no camera, no blackboard, no lettering.
face: An American of Irish stock of about sixty with a fair complexion and a LONG, LEAN face with HIGH, sharply MODELLED cheekbones and hollowed cheeks — a high forehead under dark, wavy hair greying at the temples, brushed back from a slight widow's peak under the zucchetto, strong, ARCHED dark brows, LARGE, light, deep-set, INTENSE eyes that seem to look straight through the viewer, a long, straight nose, deep lines from the nose to a WIDE, thin-lipped mouth in a warm, slightly lifted smile, and a firm, narrow chin; the gaze magnetic and kind. Not the square-chinned, level-browed giovanni_battista_scalabrini, nor the white-haired, laughing giuseppe_allamano.
verdict: rejected: too realistic a likeness beside the set's painted cards

subject: Two Jesuits in black soutanes on the deck of a sailing ship at sea, half-length. In front, Bl. Ignatius de Azevedo holds up before him with both hands a framed copy of the icon of Our Lady of St. Luke (Salus Populi Romani: the Virgin in a dark blue mantle holding the Child). Just behind his shoulder, one young companion, a teenage Jesuit novice, hands joined in prayer, looking up. Both hold martyrs' palms or have them nearby. Behind them the mast, rigging and a red-cross sail of the ship Santiago, a calm blue Atlantic and the green volcanic cliffs of La Palma (Tazacorte) on the horizon. No weapons, no violence. Keep the scene inside the arched window. They are Blesseds, not yet canonized: behind each head there is NO halo ring and NO gold disc, only a glory of fine, straight gold RAYS spreading outward from behind the head, with no circle round them.
face: Inácio: a noble Portuguese priest of about forty-three with a BROAD, full, rounded-square face and wide cheekbones, a short straight nose, wide-set warm dark eyes under straight dark brows, a full mouth; THICK wavy dark-brown hair with a full hairline (not receding, not balding), and a FULL, ROUNDED dark-brown beard (not pointed, not a goatee); a steady, luminous upward gaze. He must look clearly different from St. Ignatius of Loyola (balding, lean, short pointed beard). The companion: a slender boy of about seventeen with a fresh, broad-cheeked face — a short, slightly upturned nose, large, clear light eyes under straight fair brows, a square, cleft chin and a wide, eager mouth; beardless, with short fair-brown hair and an ardent look.

subject: St. Veronica of Milan, Augustinian lay sister, half-length: a black Augustinian habit with a leather belt, a white linen wimple framing the face and a black veil; a coarse linen alms-sack slung over one shoulder, and in her hands a round loaf of bread begged for her community; a small sprig of olive tucked into the belt. Behind her, a narrow street of old Milan with brick houses and arcades, and in the distance the flat green Lombard fields with rows of poplars where she once worked, under a pale, hazy morning sky. Cheerful, humble and hard-working; no lettering. She is a Blessed, not yet canonized: behind her head there is NO halo ring and NO gold disc, only a glory of fine, straight gold RAYS spreading outward from behind the head, with no circle round them.
face: A Lombard countrywoman of about fifty with a sun-weathered, ruddy complexion and a SHORT, BROAD face under a LOW, WIDE brow — high, round APPLE cheekbones, a short, broad nose with a slightly upturned tip, small, bright, deep-set dark-brown eyes under thick, straight dark brows, a wide mouth with thin lips set in a patient half-smile, a small, firm, square chin; hair hidden by the wimple; her gaze lifted a little, cheerful and willing.

subject: St. Vitus, the boy martyr of Lucania, alone, half-length, a child of about twelve: a knee-length white Roman tunic with two narrow purple stripes, as a noble's son, and a mantle of martyr's red over his left shoulder; in his right hand a green martyr's palm held upright; in the crook of his left arm he carries a small, empty, three-legged bronze CAULDRON, the sign of his martyrdom, held like a token, with no fire, no oil and no torment shown; beside him, on a low stone wall, stands a ROOSTER with a red comb and a bright tail, his old attribute. Behind him, Lucania in southern Italy, where the Martyrology places him: the green plain of the river Sele winding to the blue Tyrrhenian Sea, a small Doric temple like those of Paestum far off on the plain, and wooded mountains under a clear early-morning sky. Young, bright and fearless; no other figures, no lion, no gore, no lettering.
face: A boy of about twelve of Roman southern Italy, visibly a child and not a young man, BEARDLESS, with a fair, rosy complexion and a LONG face that is FULLEST BELOW — a rather HIGH, narrow forehead, long, smooth cheeks widening to a BROAD, softly rounded jaw and a FULL, rounded chin; a LONG, straight nose with a rounded tip; LARGE, wide-open, clear BLUE eyes under faint, fair, high-arched brows; a very SMALL, closed, full-lipped mouth; bright GOLDEN-BLOND hair in thick, tight RINGLETS that stand out round the head and fall to the nape, the curly blond youth of his pictures; the gaze lifted heavenward, calm and unafraid. Not the round, dark-curled pancras, the square, dark cyril_caesarea, the heart-shaped, straight-haired agapetus, the wide, flat venantius_camerino or the narrow, freckled, straw-haired benezet; and not the round-faced, brown-eyed Christ Child of finding_temple with his soft golden-brown curls: Vitus's face is long and full-jawed, his eyes blue, his curls tight and bright blond.

subject: St. Helena alone, half-length, standing as in the book's engraving: her right arm around a tall, plain wooden cross that stands upright beside her, rising out of the window's top edge, her left hand holding three iron nails in her open palm against her breast. Behind her the hills of Jerusalem in soft evening light, and on the rock of Calvary the rising walls and columns of the great basilica she had built, with masons' scaffolding. Grateful and recollected; not the finding scene of discovery_cross (no pit, no three crosses, no sick woman, no bishop), no title board, no lettering.
face: St. Helena as in recurring-figures.md: the empress at about seventy-eight (Eusebius: about eighty at her return from Palestine), a LONG, dignified face narrowing to a FIRM, slightly prominent chin — a high forehead, a STRONG, STRAIGHT ROMAN NOSE running on from the line of the brow, large deep-set grey-brown eyes under thin, arched silver brows, lean cheeks with fine lines at the eyes and mouth; silver-white hair waved back from the brow and gathered in a low bun at the nape, as on her coins, under a white veil and a slender jewelled gold diadem; a white stola bordered in gold and a deep purple imperial mantle.
verdict: rejected: the cross ran over the top border and the vine; the subject now keeps it inside the window

subject: St. Hyacinth, half-length, a Dominican friar in the white habit and scapular under the black cappa, a white Mass stole still crossed at his breast because he left the altar without unvesting: in his right hand, held up before his heart, a small gold ciborium veiled in white silk; in the crook of his left arm, light as a reed, a small white alabaster statue of the Virgin and Child. He walks calmly over the still surface of the broad river Dnieper, the water smooth and silver about him; behind him on the high wooded bank the walls and domed churches of Kiev under a pale morning sky. Serene and unhurried; no Tartars, no fire, no smoke, no lettering.
face: A Pole of about fifty-five with a fair, wind-reddened northern complexion and an OBLONG face with a FLAT-TOPPED crown — a broad, straight forehead, HIGH, ROUNDED cheekbones set wide in the Slavic manner, a SHORT nose with a broad, slightly UPTURNED tip, SMALL, deep-set, pale-blue eyes under slightly heavy lids and straight, fair brows, a WIDE, level mouth, a firm, SQUARISH chin with a shallow CLEFT; CLEAN-SHAVEN, with fair sandy hair turning grey in the Dominican corona; the gaze calm and trusting, lowered to the ciborium. Not the dark, compact peter_verona, the long, full-oval vincent_ferrer, the white-bearded raymund_penyafort or the domed, bald antoninus_florence.

subject: St. Fiaker, half-length, an Irish hermit in a coarse brown hooded habit with a rope girdle, the sleeves pushed back, leaning on the handle of a long wooden spade in his right hand, his left hand holding a bunch of fresh herbs and vegetables. Behind him his garden cleared from the forest of Breuil: neat beds of cabbages, beans and flowering herbs, a wattle fence, his small wooden cell, and the little stone oratory of Our Lady with a bell-cote, the tall oaks of the forest of Brie all around. Quiet, contented labour; no women, no lettering.
face: An Irishman of about fifty-five with a fair, freckled, weather-browned complexion and a HEART-SHAPED face, BROAD at the temples and tapering to a NARROW chin — the front of the head shaved from ear to ear in the Irish tonsure, leaving a high, bare, lined forehead, with dark-brown hair greying and falling from behind the ears to the nape; a long, THIN nose with a KNOBBED, rounded tip, SMALL, bright, dark-grey eyes set CLOSE under SHAGGY dark brows, sharp, high cheekbones over lean cheeks, a small mouth; a SHORT, POINTED dark-brown beard streaked with grey; the gaze kindly and shrewd, toward us. Not the long, big-boned, jutting-chinned, red-grey columban, nor the broad, clean-shaven, white-haired columba.

subject: St. Agapetus, half-length, a youth of Praeneste in a white tunic and the purple-bordered toga praetexta of a freeborn Roman boy, a gold bulla on a cord at his neck, holding a green palm upright in his right hand, his left hand on his heart. Behind him, the town of Praeneste on its steep hillside, olive groves below and the blue Latin hills and the Campagna toward Rome on the horizon. Young, brave and gentle; no beasts, no arena, no sword, no wounds, no lettering.
face: A Roman youth of about fifteen, visibly a boy and not a young man, BEARDLESS, with a fair, lightly sun-warmed complexion and a HEART-SHAPED face — a BROAD, smooth, rounded forehead, wide cheekbones tapering to a SMALL, POINTED chin, a small, straight nose, LARGE, clear GREY eyes under fine, arched light-brown brows, a small, bow-shaped mouth; STRAIGHT light-brown hair, cut short, with one lock falling over the brow; the gaze lifted a little, bright and steady. Not the round, curly pancras, the wide, flat venantius_camerino, the short, wide, bowl-fringed Celsus of nazarius_celsus, or the chubby, curly Martialis of seven_brothers; no curls.
verdict: rejected: the first draft had its own frame; the next two only repeated the red-and-blue initial box of the original aloysius_gonzaga, which belongs to the set

subject: St. Philip Benizi, half-length, in the black habit, scapular and hood of the Servants of Mary with a leather belt, holding a plain wooden crucifix open before him in both hands as one reads a book, his eyes on it. Beside him on a low stone ledge, set aside, a papal tiara he fled from. Behind him a wooded Tuscan hillside with a small stone convent, and far below the valley of the Arno with the walls and towers of medieval Florence. Humble and prayerful; no lettering.
face: A Florentine of about fifty, CLEAN-SHAVEN, with a warm, light-olive complexion and a WIDE, SOFT, ROUND face, after the Renaissance portrait on his Wikipedia page — a small, LOW forehead under a THICK ring of grizzled dark hair in the tonsure (not bald), a LARGE, AQUILINE nose curving down to a HOOKED tip, SMALL, NARROW dark eyes that SLANT DOWN at the outer corners, softly pouched beneath, under thin, arched brows, FULL, soft cheeks and gentle jowls, a SMALL, pursed mouth, a soft, ROUND chin; the gaze lowered to the crucifix, contrite and tender. Not the square-jawed, keen-eyed albert_great, the domed, bald antoninus_florence, or any of the seven servite_founders.

subject: The seven monks of Capsa, half-length, standing close together inside the arched window on the shore near Carthage: plain, undyed wool monastic tunics and dark hooded cloaks, each holding a small green palm. In front, at the centre, the abbot St. Liberatus with a plain wooden abbot's staff; at his right side, a head shorter, the boy Maximus, pressed close to his abbot, the old man's hand on his shoulder; the five others behind and between them, in two rows. Behind them, a calm blue sea, a weathered old wooden boat drawn up on the sand, and on the headland the white walls of Carthage under a clear African sky. Steadfast and peaceful; no fire, no oars raised, no wounds, no chains, no lettering.
face: Seven clearly different North Africans of the Roman province, warm olive-brown to deep-brown skin. LIBERATUS (centre front), the abbot, about sixty-five: a LARGE, BOXY head with a flat crown — a broad, deeply lined forehead, a strong ROMAN nose with a high bridge, grave, HOODED dark-brown eyes, deep lines from nose to mouth, a thin, wide mouth, a SQUARE chin under a short, full WHITE beard cut square; close white hair. MAXIMUS (front, at his right), a boy of about twelve, the darkest-skinned of the group, deep brown: a soft OVAL face with full cheeks, a BROAD, short nose with wide nostrils, very LARGE dark eyes, a full mouth, a softly rounded chin; black hair in short, tight curls close to the head; looking up at his abbot. Not the triangular, big-eared Vitalis or the chubby Martialis of seven_brothers. BEHIND, left to right: BONIFACE, about forty, a ROUND, full face with a short black beard and a broad, kind smile; SERVUS, about thirty, a LONG, NARROW, beardless face with a hooked nose; RUSTICUS, about thirty-five, a BROAD, FLAT face with a snub nose and dark stubble, thick black hair; ROGATUS, about fifty-five, GAUNT, bald on the crown, with a wispy grey beard; SEPTIMUS, about forty-five, a PEAR-SHAPED face, heavy in the jaw, clean-shaven, with short, thick grey-black hair. All gazes calm, some lifted.
verdict: rejected: frame: the first draft had its own border all round, the second no sides to the window

subject: Pope St. Zephyrinus, half-length, an early-third-century bishop of Rome: a white tunic under a full, rust-red paenula, a plain white woollen pallium about his shoulders, no tiara and no mitre; his right hand raised in teaching, his left holding a closed Gospel codex bound in red leather against his breast. Behind him the Via Appia outside Rome, its paving stones and umbrella pines, and a low brick entrance leading down into the cemetery on the Appia he charged his deacon Callistus to make. Grave and fatherly; no other figures, no palm, no lettering.
face: A Roman of about seventy-five with a weathered olive complexion and a BROAD, FLAT-FEATURED face under a ROUND, bald crown with white hair at the sides — a wide, LOW, slightly bulging brow, TUFTED white brows that FLARE UP at their outer ends, SMALL, kind, DOWN-SLANTING grey eyes, a BROAD, FLAT nose with a LOW bridge, wide, flat cheeks, a small mouth; a long, full, WAVY white beard falling to the chest with a white moustache, as in the book's engraving; the gaze grave and gentle, toward us. Not the wide, fringed, square-bearded callistus (his deacon), the round, dark-bearded Pontian of pontian_hippolytus, the heart-shaped soter, or the long-faced fabian and stephen_i.

subject: St. Louis of Toulouse, half-length, a young Franciscan bishop: the rough grey-brown Franciscan habit with its white knotted cord showing beneath a deep-blue cope powdered with small gold fleurs-de-lis and fastened with a gold morse, a white mitre edged in gold, a gold crosier in his left hand; his right hand resting on an open book of the Gospels. Beside him, set aside on a low stone ledge, a small gold royal crown on a red cushion, the kingdom of Naples he gave up. Behind him, the red-brick churches and houses of Toulouse along the wide Garonne under a warm southern sky. Humble and grave; no lettering.
face: A prince of twenty-three, CLEAN-SHAVEN, with a pale, smooth complexion and a face WIDER at the JAW than at the brow, after Simone Martini's fresco at Assisi painted some twenty years after his death — a smooth, moderate forehead, a LONG, STRAIGHT nose with a broad base, SMALL, NARROW, heavy-lidded grey eyes under faint, level brows, full, smooth cheeks, a SMALL, closed mouth, a BROAD, rounded jaw on a thick neck; short, light-brown hair showing below the mitre; the gaze turned a little aside, quiet and withdrawn. Not the long, narrow oval of his great-uncle louis_france, nor the older, pear-shaped stanislaus.

subject: St. Raymund Nonnatus, half-length, a Mercedarian friar in the white habit, white scapular and white hooded cape of the Order of Our Lady of Mercy, the Order's small red-and-gold shield, topped by a cross, hanging on his breast as in the Camón Aznar painting; in his right hand a green palm, in his left, held out, a set of opened iron fetters, the chains of the captives he ransomed. Behind him the white, flat-roofed houses and walls of Algiers climbing from its harbour, a few small ships at anchor on a blue sea. Gentle and fearless; no cardinal's red cape or hat, no padlock, no wounds, no lettering.
face: A Catalan of about thirty-six with a sun-browned olive complexion and a SHORT, BROAD face with a WIDE, gently BULGING forehead and a strong brow — deep-set, intense black eyes under thick, ARCHED black brows, a SHORT, straight nose with a HIGH, narrow bridge, flat cheeks, a WIDE mouth with a full lower lip, a ROUND, prominent chin; a close, short black beard and moustache; black hair in a thin ring round a large tonsure; the gaze direct and steadfast. Not the long, narrow, single-browed romanus_ostiarius, the long, soft-faced francis_caracciolo or the broad, flat-cheeked william_montevergine.

subject: St. Symphorian, half-length, a young Gallo-Roman noble in a white tunic and a plain white toga, walking out through the city gate, a green palm in his right hand, his left hand open at his breast; he looks up and back toward the wall. Behind him, small on the Roman walls of Augustodunum (Autun) above the arched gate, his mother Augusta in a dark-blue mantle and white veil, leaning forward with one arm raised toward him. Wooded Burgundian hills beyond under a clear sky. Brave and serene; no soldiers, no weapons, no idol, no wounds, no lettering.
face: Two figures. SYMPHORIAN, a Gallo-Roman of about twenty, BEARDLESS, with a fair, fresh complexion and a LONG face with a LONG, STRAIGHT jawline ending in a DEEP, SQUARE chin — a high, narrow forehead, a THIN, HIGH-BRIDGED, slightly AQUILINE nose, deep-set, clear BLUE eyes under straight fair brows, lean cheeks, a wide, firm mouth; thick, STRAIGHT fair-blond hair cut short across the forehead, no curls; the gaze lifted, joyful and resolute. AUGUSTA, his mother, small in the distance, about fifty: a long, pale face under the white veil, her mouth open in a call. Not the square, snub-nosed, chestnut-haired Tiburtius of tiburtius_susanna, the curly, olive pantaleon or the long-haired casimir.

Behind her the hills of Jerusalem in soft evening light, and on the rock of Calvary the rising walls and columns of the great basilica she had built, with masons' scaffolding. LIBERATUS (centre front), the abbot, about sixty-five: a LARGE, BOXY head with a flat crown — a broad, deeply lined forehead, a strong ROMAN nose with a high bridge, grave, HOODED dark-brown eyes, deep lines from nose to mouth, a thin, wide mouth, a SQUARE chin under a short, full WHITE beard cut square; close white hair. MAXIMUS (front, at his right), a boy of about twelve, the darkest-skinned of the group, deep brown: a soft OVAL face with full cheeks, a BROAD, short nose with wide nostrils, very LARGE dark eyes, a full mouth, a softly rounded chin; black hair in short, tight curls close to the head; looking up at his abbot. Not the triangular, big-eared Vitalis or the chubby Martialis of seven_brothers. BEHIND, left to right: BONIFACE, about forty, a ROUND, full face with a short black beard and a broad, kind smile; SERVUS, about thirty, a LONG, NARROW, beardless face with a hooked nose; RUSTICUS, about thirty-five, a BROAD, FLAT face with a snub nose and dark stubble, thick black hair; ROGATUS, about fifty-five, GAUNT, bald on the crown, with a wispy grey beard; SEPTIMUS, about forty-five, a PEAR-SHAPED face, heavy in the jaw, clean-shaven, with short, thick grey-black hair. All gazes calm, some lifted.
verdict: rejected: frame: the first draft had its own border all round, the second no sides to the window

subject: St. Agapetus, half-length, a youth of Praeneste in a white tunic and the purple-bordered toga praetexta of a freeborn Roman boy, a gold bulla on a cord at his neck, holding a green palm upright in his right hand, his left hand on his heart. Behind him, the town of Praeneste on its steep hillside, olive groves below and the blue Latin hills and the Campagna toward Rome on the horizon. Young, brave and gentle; no beasts, no arena, no sword, no wounds, no lettering.
face: A Roman youth of about fifteen, visibly a boy and not a young man, BEARDLESS, with a fair, lightly sun-warmed complexion and a HEART-SHAPED face — a BROAD, smooth, rounded forehead, wide cheekbones tapering to a SMALL, POINTED chin, a small, straight nose, LARGE, clear GREY eyes under fine, arched light-brown brows, a small, bow-shaped mouth; STRAIGHT light-brown hair, cut short, with one lock falling over the brow; the gaze lifted a little, bright and steady. Not the round, curly pancras, the wide, flat venantius_camerino, the short, wide, bowl-fringed Celsus of nazarius_celsus, or the chubby, curly Martialis of seven_brothers; no curls.
verdict: rejected: the first draft had its own frame; the next two only repeated the red-and-blue initial box of the original aloysius_gonzaga, which belongs to the set

subject: The seven monks of Capsa, half-length, standing close together inside the arched window on the shore near Carthage: plain, undyed wool monastic tunics and dark hooded cloaks, each holding a small green palm. In front, at the centre, the abbot St. Liberatus with a plain wooden abbot's staff; at his right side, a head shorter, the boy Maximus, pressed close to his abbot, the old man's hand on his shoulder; the five others behind and between them, in two rows. Behind them, a calm blue sea, a weathered old wooden boat drawn up on the sand, and on the headland the white walls of Carthage under a clear African sky. Steadfast and peaceful; no fire, no oars raised, no wounds, no chains, no lettering.

LIBERATUS (centre front), the abbot, about sixty-five: a LARGE, BOXY head with a flat crown — a broad, deeply lined forehead, a strong ROMAN nose with a high bridge, grave, HOODED dark-brown eyes, deep lines from nose to mouth, a thin, wide mouth, a SQUARE chin under a short, full WHITE beard cut square; close white hair. Behind him, the town of Praeneste on its steep hillside, olive groves below and the blue Latin hills and the Campagna toward Rome on the horizon. Young, brave and gentle; no beasts, no arena, no sword, no wounds, no lettering.

subject: St. Maximus of Riez, half-length, a Gallo-Roman bishop of the fifth century who had been a monk, bareheaded: a plain white tunic, a wide, soft chasuble of undyed natural wool over it and a narrow white pallium; a plain wooden pastoral staff with a simple curved head in his left hand, his right hand open and held out in a gentle, welcoming gesture. Behind him the high plateau of Riez in Provence: four tall grey Roman columns still standing in a meadow, a small, square early baptistery with a low dome, olive trees and stone walls, and blue hills beyond, under a clear, warm, luminous sky. Gentle, kindly and fatherly; no lettering.
face: A Gallo-Roman of Provence of about sixty, CLEAN-SHAVEN, with a warm, sun-touched complexion and a gently PEAR-SHAPED face — NARROW at the temples and BROADENING to a WIDE, SOFT, rounded jaw and full lower cheeks, with a small fold under the chin; a LOW, smooth forehead; a SHORT, broad, BLUNT nose; small, kind brown eyes, a little creased at the corners; LOW, heavy, straight dark-grey brows; a wide, gentle mouth in a quiet, fatherly smile; short, thick grey hair in a monk's crown; the gaze warm and fatherly, toward us. Not his abbot honoratus (domed forehead, small lower face), the square-oval, laughing willibrord, the high-browed, jowled luigi_maria_palazzolo, the square, short-faced denis, the flat-faced, bearded leonard_noblac or the round, bearded Peter of Alexandria of this batch.

subject: St. Barbara, half-length, a young noblewoman of the East in the early fourth century: a gown of deep crimson with a white linen veil laid lightly over her hair and shoulders, a thin gold circlet on her head, and a mantle of dark green; in her right hand she holds up a golden chalice with a white Host above it, and in her left a martyr's palm. Behind her, on a rocky hillside, a tall, slender stone tower with THREE narrow arched windows side by side near its top, and beyond it a green valley and far blue hills of Asia Minor under a clear, calm sky. Steadfast, noble and serene; no sword, no lightning, no father, no torments, no lettering.
face: A young noblewoman of about twenty, tall and strongly built, with a warm, creamy complexion and a BROAD, FULL OVAL face with a STRONG, ROUNDED jaw — a HIGH, smooth forehead; a STRAIGHT, strong nose with a firm bridge; LARGE, calm, light-brown eyes under LEVEL, well-marked auburn brows; FULL cheeks; FULL, firm lips; a round, firm chin; thick, wavy AUBURN hair drawn back and gathered up under the veil and circlet; the gaze calm, direct and commanding, toward us. Not the fine-oval catherine_alexandria, the small, square margaret_antioch, the broad, square-jawed, low-browed genevieve, the round dorothy, the long-chinned ursula or Bibiana of this batch (long, pale, eyes lifted).

subject: St. James of the Marches, half-length, an Observant Franciscan friar of the fifteenth century: a coarse grey-brown habit with its hood lying on his shoulders and a knotted white cord; in his right hand he raises a plain golden chalice, and his left hand is laid on his breast. Behind him the hills of the Marche above the Adriatic: the small hill town of Monteprandone with its brick walls and a bell tower, olive groves and ploughed fields falling toward a thin line of blue sea, under a bright, clear sky. Ardent, austere and kind; no serpent, no lettering.
face: An Italian of the Marche of about seventy, gaunt, CLEAN-SHAVEN, with a sun-browned, weathered complexion and a LONG, RECTANGULAR face with deep vertical lines down the cheeks — a HIGH, broad, BALD crown with a thin ring of short grey hair; a LONG, heavy, straight nose with a BROAD, rounded tip; LARGE, round, dark eyes LIFTED upward under straight, dark-grey brows, the lower lids heavy; a WIDE, thin-lipped mouth slightly open as if about to preach; a LONG, broad chin; the gaze lifted and ardent. Not his master bernardine_siena (thin, pointed, sunken-cheeked), the small, triangular john_capistrano, the lantern-jawed patrician gregory_langres, the angular, moustached paschal_baylon, the smooth, narrow didacus or the craggy-browed peter_damian.

subject: St. Odo of Cluny, half-length, a Benedictine abbot of the tenth century: a full black monastic cowl with wide sleeves and the hood fallen back, no mitre; a plain wooden abbot's staff with a simple curved head in his left hand, and in his right, held against his breast, a small book of the Rule. His head is a little bowed and his shoulders a little bent, as his monks knew him. Behind him the Burgundian valley of the Grosne: green wooded hills, and the new abbey church of Cluny rising in pale stone with its wooden scaffolding still on the walls, a few monks small in the cloister garth, under a soft, clear autumn sky. Humble, gentle and quietly cheerful; no lettering.
face: An Aquitanian noble of about sixty, slight and a little stooped, CLEAN-SHAVEN, with a pale, rather sallow complexion and a face shaped like an UPRIGHT EGG — WIDEST at the BROAD, HIGH, rounded forehead under the monastic tonsure and narrowing evenly, with SMOOTH, soft cheeks and no marked cheekbones, to a small, ROUNDED chin; a SHORT, slightly UPTURNED nose; large, ROUND grey eyes under softly rounded lids, LOWERED toward the ground; sparse, straight fair brows; a small, gentle mouth with a quiet hint of humour at the corners; a thin ring of light-brown hair going grey around the tonsure; the gaze cast down, recollected. Not his successor hugh_cluny (square-oval, Greek-nosed), the lean, sharp-cheeked, hook-nosed edmund_canterbury, the long, smooth, long-nosed didacus, the long, domed ludger, the bulge-browed, short, wide elphege, the heart-shaped polycarp or the broad, flat-faced leonard_noblac.

subject: St. Felix of Valois, half-length, a very old hermit and founder: the white habit and white scapular of the Order of the Holy Trinity, a small cross of RED upright and BLUE crossbar on the breast of the scapular, a dark-brown mantle over his shoulders; his hands folded on a small wooden rosary over a closed book. Behind him the forest of Cerfroid near Meaux: tall oaks and beeches, a small hermit's cell of stone with a wooden cross, and a clear spring in a mossy basin at which a white stag stands drinking quietly, under a soft, silvery morning light. Contemplative, gentle and venerable; no cross between the stag's antlers, no captives, no chains, no lettering.
face: A Frenchman of about eighty-five, spare and frail, with a pale, fine, deeply lined complexion and a LONG, NARROW face with HOLLOW temples and cheeks — a HIGH, BALD, smooth dome with a few wisps of white hair at the sides; deep-set, HOODED, heavy-lidded blue-grey eyes looking DOWN and a little to the side; long, feathery white brows that DROOP at their outer ends; a thin, finely ARCHED nose; a small mouth half hidden; a VERY LONG, full, softly WAVY white beard that flows down over the breast to the waist; the gaze meek and inward. Not his companion john_matha (clean-shaven, convex, curved-nosed), the triangular, hooded anthony_abbot, the fine-boned, clean-shaven fabian or the long-bearded athanasius.

subject: St. Gregory Thaumaturgus, half-length, a Greek bishop of the third century, bareheaded: a plain white linen tunic, over it a wide phelonion of warm ochre and a white woollen omophorion with large black crosses lying over his shoulders and breast, as in the old icons; in his left hand a Gospel book bound in dark red leather with a small gold cross, his right hand raised in blessing. Behind him the green valley of the Lycus in Pontus: the river running calmly between its banks under wooded hills, a large, leafy tree growing on the bank where he planted his staff to hold back the flood, and the small walled town of Neocaesarea with a plain early church on a rise, under a clear, soft sky. Wise, grave and kindly; no demons, no vision, no lettering.
face: A Greek of Pontus of about sixty with a warm, light olive complexion and a NARROW face with SUNKEN TEMPLES — a HIGH, BALD crown with a single short CURL of white hair left over the middle of the forehead and thick, short white curls over the ears; a DEEP vertical FURROW between the brows; a LONG, STRAIGHT, NARROW nose running down from it; small, CLOSE-SET, deep-brown eyes under brows that slant gently UP toward the centre in a look of concentration; flat cheeks; a small, tight mouth; a SHORT, CURLY, rounded white beard; the gaze grave and searching, toward us. Not the long-bearded athanasius, the rectangular, square-jawed lambert, the trapezoid hilary, the domed honoratus or the long, symmetrical remigius.

subject: St. Eligius, half-length, the goldsmith who became Bishop of Noyon in the seventh century, bareheaded: a white alb and a wide, bell-shaped chasuble of deep wine-red wool with a narrow gold-embroidered band at the neck; in both hands he holds up a small house-shaped reliquary shrine of gold set with red garnets, his own work; beside him on a stone ledge lie a small goldsmith's hammer and a little anvil. Behind him the valley of the Oise: the small town of Noyon on its low hill with a simple stone church, a river with a mill and green meadows, under a soft northern sky. Honest, prudent and devout; no king, no throne, no lettering.
face: A Gallo-Roman of about fifty-five, TALL, CLEAN-SHAVEN, with a fresh, ROSY complexion and a LONG, smoothly OVAL face, FULL and rounded in the rosy cheeks, with no sharp bones — a smooth, open forehead; a LONG, straight nose with a slightly RAISED, rounded tip; clear hazel eyes, a little NARROWED in a shrewd, PRUDENT, appraising look, under neatly arched brown brows; a small, composed mouth with a SHORT upper lip; a neat, softly rounded chin; a thick head of short, TIGHT, springy chestnut CURLS touched with grey, with a small tonsure; the gaze prudent and kind, toward us. Not the sharp-cheeked edmund_canterbury, the tapering, bearded hubert, the heart-shaped polycarp, the round, apple-cheeked blase or the long, fine remigius.

subject: St. Saturninus, half-length, a Roman missionary bishop of the third century, bareheaded: a white tunic and over it a full, dark-green paenula (the round Roman travelling cloak) with a narrow white pallium; a plain wooden pastoral staff in his left hand and a martyr's palm in his right. Behind him Roman Toulouse on the Garonne: the broad river with a low stone bridge, walls and houses of rose-red brick, and on a rise the columns of the pagan capitol with a long flight of steps, and apart from it a very small, plain house-church with a cross over its door, under a warm, clear southern sky. Fearless, calm and resolute; no bull, no crowd, no wounds, no lettering.
face: A Roman of about fifty-five, tall and lean, with a light olive complexion and a LONG face shaped like a SHIELD — a wide, flat forehead crossed by STRAIGHT, LEVEL black brows, the sides of the face running long and straight and narrowing only at the bottom to a firm, BLUNT chin; a ROMAN nose with a strong HUMP high on the bridge; deep-set, level, steady dark eyes; hollow cheeks under clear cheekbones; a firm, thin mouth; short, cropped, greying black hair combed forward in the Roman way; a SHORT, DENSE, cropped black-and-grey beard close to the jaw; the gaze fearless, toward us. Not the rectangular, square-jawed lambert, the long, jutting-chinned firmin, the broad, square denis, the oblong germanus_auxerre or the long, rectangular cornelius of cornelius_cyprian.

subject: St. Bibiana, half-length, a young Roman woman of the fourth century: a long, softly draped tunic of pale rose linen gathered at the waist with a cord, and a mantle of soft grey-blue over her shoulders and one arm; her right arm rests on a short, plain marble column beside her, and in her left hand she holds a martyr's palm against her breast. Behind her the Esquiline hill in Rome: a garden of green herbs and a few cypresses, the small brick basilica built over her tomb, and the distant domes and towers of the city under a soft, luminous sky. Patient, faithful and serene, her eyes lifted; no scourge, no chains, no wounds, no lettering.
face: A Roman girl of about twenty with a fair, pale complexion and a LONG, graceful neck carrying a LONG OVAL face with a HIGH, softly rounded forehead — a STRAIGHT, classical GREEK nose that continues the line of the forehead with almost no dip; LARGE, WIDE-SET, softly rounded eyes LIFTED toward heaven; fine, softly arched brows; smooth cheeks; a small mouth with the lips just PARTED; a soft, ROUNDED chin; light-brown hair, wavy and loosely parted in the middle, drawn back from the face and caught at the nape, a few waves loose over the ears; the gaze lifted upward, rapt and calm. Not the fine-oval, crowned catherine_alexandria, the diamond-faced anastasia, the round, joyful dorothy, the square margaret_antioch, the triangular christina_bolsena or Barbara of this batch (broad, crowned, auburn).

subject: St. Peter of Alexandria, half-length, a Greek bishop of Egypt of the early fourth century, bareheaded: a white tunic, a wide phelonion of deep crimson, and a white omophorion with small dark crosses over his shoulders; in his left hand a Gospel book bound in plain leather, in his right a martyr's palm. Behind him Alexandria by the sea: the great harbour with a few sailing ships, the tall white Pharos lighthouse on its island, low white houses and a simple early church with a small dome along the shore, a few date palms, under a bright, hazy Egyptian sky. Steadfast, fatherly and wise; no sword, no executioner, no prison, no lettering.
face: An Alexandrian of about sixty-five, sturdy, with a warm olive complexion and a ROUND, FULL face — a broad, rounded forehead with short, thick grey hair receding a little at the temples, FULL, rounded cheeks, a SHORT, broad nose with a ROUNDED tip, LARGE, dark, heavy-lidded eyes under softly ARCHED black-and-grey brows, a small, full mouth; a FULL, ROUNDED grey beard of medium length, curling at the edges; the gaze steady and fatherly, toward us. Not the oblong, high-nosed cyril_alexandria, the bald, long-bearded athanasius, the broad-domed lucian_antioch, or the short-bearded, narrow Gregory Thaumaturgus of this batch.

subject: Blessed Fulton J. Sheen, Archbishop, who preached the Gospel to millions on radio in The Catholic Hour and on television in Life Is Worth Living, half-length in a bishop's black cassock piped and buttoned in red-purple, the purple zucchetto, and the long purple silk cape (ferraiolo) over his shoulders; a gold pectoral cross on a chain; his right hand raised a little in a speaker's gesture, his left holding a rosary. Behind him, New York at dusk: the twin white Gothic spires of St. Patrick's Cathedral on Fifth Avenue among the towers of Manhattan, lit windows, and a deep blue evening sky. He is a Blessed, not yet canonized: behind his head there is NO halo ring and NO gold disc, only a glory of fine, straight gold RAYS spreading outward from behind the head, with no circle round them. Radiant, warm and persuasive; no microphone, no camera, no blackboard, no lettering. The whole figure is PAINTED in the manner of the attached nineteenth-century cards, not copied from a photograph: flat, simplified, idealised, with broad, simple drapery folds, soft even colour and clear outlines; the city behind him is small, simplified and decorative, like the backgrounds of the attached cards. Never a realistic or photographic modern portrait.
face: A PAINTED holy-card face, flat and idealised like the faces on the attached cards: smooth, even skin in soft flat tones, clear outlines, simple almond eyes, no photographic modelling, no individual wrinkles, no sharp highlights. Only these marks tell him apart: a clean-shaven man of about sixty with a LONG, LEAN face and HIGH cheekbones; dark, wavy hair greying at the temples, brushed back from a slight widow's peak under the zucchetto; ARCHED dark brows over LARGE, light, deep-set eyes; a long, straight nose; a wide mouth in a gentle, slightly lifted smile; a firm, narrow chin; the gaze kind and direct. A devotional image of him, not a likeness from a photograph.
verdict: rejected: too realistic a likeness beside the set's painted cards

subject: Blessed Fulton J. Sheen, Archbishop, who preached the Gospel to millions on radio in The Catholic Hour and on television in Life Is Worth Living, half-length in a bishop's black cassock piped and buttoned in red-purple, the purple zucchetto, and the long purple silk cape (ferraiolo) over his shoulders; a gold pectoral cross on a chain; his right hand raised a little in a preacher's gesture, his left holding a rosary; his head inclined a little, as the saints of the attached cards hold theirs. Behind him, small and far off under a soft, pale early-evening sky with light clouds like the skies of the attached cards: the twin white Gothic spires of St. Patrick's Cathedral on Fifth Avenue among the simplified towers of Manhattan. He is a Blessed, not yet canonized: behind his head there is NO halo ring and NO gold disc, only a glory of fine, straight gold RAYS spreading outward from behind the head, with no circle round them. Warm, gentle and recollected; no microphone, no camera, no blackboard, no lettering.
