The whole figure is PAINTED in the manner of the attached nineteenth-century cards, not copied from a photograph: flat, simplified, idealised, with broad, simple drapery folds, soft even colour and clear outlines, no dramatic light, no glowing windows. Never a realistic or photographic modern portrait.
face: A PAINTED holy-card face, flat and idealised like the faces on the attached cards: smooth, even skin in soft flat tones, clear outlines, simply drawn eyes, no photographic modelling, no individual wrinkles, no sharp highlights. Only these marks tell him apart: a clean-shaven man of about sixty with a LONG, LEAN face and HIGH cheekbones; dark, wavy hair greying at the temples, brushed back from a slight widow's peak under the zucchetto; ARCHED dark brows over LARGE, light, deep-set eyes; a long, straight nose; a wide mouth in a gentle, slightly lifted smile; a firm, narrow chin. His eyes are lifted a little upward and aside in prayerful thought, NOT looking at the viewer. A devotional image of him, not a likeness from a photograph.

subject: St. Julia of Carthage, virgin and martyr, half-length, as a household slave of the fifth century: a plain, long-sleeved tunic of undyed wool, a mantle of faded blue and a simple white veil over her hair; in her right hand a small, plain wooden cross held against her breast, in her left a martyr's palm. Behind her, the northern cape of Corsica: a high, dark rock rising straight from the sea with a small village of grey stone houses and a watchtower on its top, a dark shingle beach below, a merchant ship with a square sail at anchor in the bay, and green, scrub-covered mountains beyond, under a warm, clear evening sky. Patient, faithful and serene; no governor, no torments, no lettering.
face: A Carthaginian woman of about twenty-five with a warm, light-brown North African complexion and a face with a softly CONVEX PROFILE — a gently SLOPING forehead, a LONG nose with a soft CURVE to the bridge and a rounded tip, deep-set, dark eyes under HEAVY, dark, nearly straight brows, a WIDE mouth with full lips, and a ROUNDED, PROMINENT chin that carries the curve of the profile; black, curling hair under the veil; the gaze patient and steadfast, toward us.

subject: St. John of Nepomuk, a canon of Prague, half-length, in his traditional image: a black cassock, a white rochet edged with a band of plain lace, a short cape (almuce) of grey-brown fur over his shoulders, a black biretta; a small crucifix held against his breast in his left arm with a martyr's palm, the forefinger of his right hand laid gently on his closed lips in the gesture of silence; five small gold stars ringing his halo. Behind him, Prague at dusk: the broad Vltava, a long stone bridge on many arches with its Gothic bridge tower, and on the hill across the river the castle and the tall Gothic cathedral, a soft light shining on the dark water below the bridge. Gentle, faithful and silent; no king, no river-drowning, no lettering.
face: A Bohemian of about forty-eight with a fair, pale complexion and a SOFT, LONG OVAL face, FULL through the cheeks — a smooth, rounded forehead, a straight nose with a FLESHY, ROUNDED tip, LARGE, MOIST, slightly PROMINENT brown eyes rolled UPWARD in the Baroque manner under HIGH, THIN, arched brows, a SMALL mouth with a FULL lower lip, a soft, rounded chin; straight chestnut-brown hair to the collar under the biretta; a SHORT, soft chestnut beard and moustache following the jaw; the gaze lifted and gentle, the head tilted a little.

subject: St. Venantius of Camerino, a boy martyr of fifteen, half-length: a knee-length white Roman tunic with narrow red bands and a short cloak of deep red wool pinned at the right shoulder; a martyr's palm in his right hand, his left hand raised, blessing a spring of clear water that gushes from a grey rock beside him. Behind him, the green Apennine hills of the Marche: a steep ridge with the walls and towers of Camerino, oak woods and small fields below, blue mountains beyond, under a bright, clear morning sky. Brave, candid and serene; no fire, no lions, no torments, no soldiers, no lettering.
face: A boy of fifteen, visibly a boy and not a young man, BEARDLESS, with a warm light-olive Italian complexion and a face WIDE and FLAT across the cheekbones — a low, straight forehead, a BROAD, STRAIGHT nose with a LOW bridge set between WIDE-SET, slightly HOODED dark eyes, thick, STRAIGHT black brows, flat cheeks, a WIDE, full mouth, a small but FIRM, SQUARE chin; thick, coarse, straight black hair cut in a short, blunt fringe; the gaze candid and steady, toward us.

subject: St. Pachomius, the Egyptian abbot, half-length, as a monk of the fourth century: a plain tunic of coarse, undyed linen, a dark-brown monastic mantle about his shoulders, a small hood fallen back on his neck, a plain leather belt; in both hands, held before his breast, a small rolled scroll tied with a cord, the rule of life the angel gave him. Behind him, Tabenna on the Nile in Upper Egypt: the broad brown river with a reed boat under a square sail, a mud-brick monastery wall enclosing low, flat-roofed cells and a small church, date palms and green fields along the bank, and the pale desert cliffs beyond, under a clear, hot, golden sky. Vigilant and fatherly; no angel, no lettering.
face: A Copt of the Thebaid of about fifty-five, broad-shouldered like the soldier he once was, with a deep-brown, sun-darkened complexion and a LONG, STRAIGHT-SIDED face under a BROAD, HIGH, smooth BALD dome — a STRAIGHT, broad nose with a LOW, FLAT bridge and WIDE, flared nostrils, LARGE, wide-open, dark ALMOND eyes set WIDE apart and rimmed with thick black lashes, like a Fayum portrait's, under straight, thick black-and-grey brows; flat cheeks; FULL, thick lips; a grey-streaked black beard to mid-breast, parted into FIVE narrow, separate POINTS; the gaze direct and vigilant, toward us.

subject: St. Paschal Baylon, Franciscan lay brother, half-length, kneeling in adoration: the coarse, patched brown habit of the reformed Friars Minor with a short hood, a white knotted cord at the waist and a wooden rosary; his hands joined before his breast, his face lifted toward the upper corner of the window, where a small golden monstrance with the white Host shines in a soft radiance among light clouds. Behind him, the dry hills of Aragon: a flock of sheep grazing on a stony slope with a shepherd's crook laid on the ground, and in the valley below a small village church with a bell-cote, under a clear, pale-blue sky. Humble and rapt; no angel figure, no lettering.
face: An Aragonese countryman of about forty-five with a sun-browned olive complexion and a LONG, ANGULAR face — a broad, flat forehead, PROMINENT, BONY cheekbones with shallow hollows under them, DEEP creases from the nose to the corners of the mouth, a LONG, strong, slightly HOOKED nose, deep-set, HEAVY-LIDDED dark eyes under THICK, straight black brows, a WIDE, THIN-LIPPED mouth, a firm chin; black hair cropped short in the Franciscan crown; a thin dark moustache and a small tuft of beard on the chin; the gaze lifted, rapt.

subject: St. Peter Celestine, the hermit of Morrone who was pope for four months, half-length: a coarse, undyed grey-brown woollen hermit's habit with its hood laid back on his shoulders and a plain leather girdle; in his hands, open before him, a small, worn book of the psalms, as at Lauds; beside him on a rock ledge, set aside, the papal tiara of white and gold. Behind him, Monte Morrone in the Abruzzi: a steep, bare limestone mountainside with a tiny hermitage and its small bell-cote built into a cave in the cliff, beech woods below, and far down the green valley of Sulmona, under a clear, high, pale sky. Simple, peaceful and withdrawn; no cardinals, no guards, no lettering.
face: An Abruzzese of about eighty, CLEAN-SHAVEN as in the old fresco, with a pale, weathered, finely wrinkled complexion and a LONG, NARROW, STRAIGHT-SIDED face — a very HIGH forehead, cheekbones barely marked, the cheeks falling flat and parallel to a NARROW, rounded chin; a LONG, STRAIGHT, narrow nose; SMALL, LEVEL, almond-shaped grey eyes set CLOSE together under straight, sparse white brows; a LONG upper lip over a SMALL, gently pursed mouth; thin white hair in a monastic ring; the gaze calm and withdrawn, lowered to the book.

subject: St. Hospitius, the recluse near Nice, half-length: a coarse tunic of dark-brown haircloth, worn and patched, and girded round his body a heavy iron chain; in his open right hand a few dates and a small piece of bread, his left hand laid over his heart. Behind him, the ruins of an old square stone tower overgrown with ivy on a rocky point of the Provençal coast, the deep-blue bay below with a small fishing boat, umbrella pines and wild rosemary on the rocks, and far across the water the green hills above the bay, under a bright, clear Mediterranean sky. Penitent and at peace; no soldiers, no swords, no lettering.
face: A man of about sixty, burned a deep bronze by the sun, with a LEAN face whose HIGH, BROAD, FLAT cheekbones run in a straight line across it — NARROW eyes that SLANT gently DOWN at the outer corners, dark and sorrowful, under thick, level black-and-grey brows, a LONG, THIN, very STRAIGHT nose, SUNKEN cheeks below the cheekbones, a thin mouth; long, unkempt black-and-grey hair to the shoulders; a LONG, dense, rough black-and-grey beard to the breast; the gaze penitent and humble, a little lowered.

subject: Sts. Peter and Dionysia, martyrs of Lampsacus under Decius, half-length and side by side. PETER (left): a young Greek of the third century in a knee-length tunic of undyed wool and a mantle of deep russet-red thrown over his left shoulder; a martyr's palm in his right hand, his left hand laid on his breast in thanksgiving, his face lifted. DIONYSIA (right): a Greek girl in a long tunic of pale blue linen and a white veil drawn over her hair and shoulders, a martyr's palm in her left hand, her right hand at her heart, turned a little toward him. Behind them, Lampsacus on the Hellespont: the narrow, deep-blue strait with a small sailing ship, the hills of the Thracian shore across the water, a small white Greek town with a colonnaded temple and red roofs among vineyards and olive trees on the slope, under a clear, bright sky with a single streak of gold. Joyful and steadfast; no wheel, no sword, no proconsul, no soldiers, no lettering.
face: Two clearly different young Greeks of Asia Minor with warm, light-olive skin. PETER (left): about twenty, BEARDLESS but for a faint dark down on the upper lip, with a face BROAD at the temples that TAPERS in straight lines to a NARROW, POINTED, slightly JUTTING chin — a wide, smooth forehead, a LONG, THIN, gently AQUILINE nose, bright, deep-set dark eyes lifted to heaven, straight dark brows, lean cheeks, a wide mouth in a SMILE (the book's 'smiling countenance'); short, thick, wavy black hair; the gaze lifted, thankful. DIONYSIA (right): about sixteen, with a DIAMOND-SHAPED face, WIDEST at HIGH, rounded cheekbones and narrowing both to a moderate forehead and to a small, soft chin — a SHORT, straight nose, large, dark eyes whose outer corners TILT UP, thick, straight black brows, a WIDE, full mouth, grave and closed; black hair parted in the middle under the veil; the gaze earnest and fearless, turned toward Peter.

subject: Sts. Donatian and Rogatian, brothers of a noble Gallo-Roman family of Nantes, half-length and side by side. ROGATIAN (left, the elder): a long tunic of dark green wool and a heavy cloak of undyed grey-brown wool fastened at the right shoulder with a round bronze brooch; a martyr's palm in his right hand. DONATIAN (right, the younger, who had brought his brother to the faith): a tunic of pale blue and a cloak of deep red fastened with a gilt brooch; in his left hand a small book of the Gospels held against his breast, his right hand laid on his brother's shoulder. Behind them, Roman Nantes on the Loire: the wide, slow river with sandbanks and a flat river boat, a low town wall with a gate, red-tiled roofs, and flat green meadows with poplars along the banks, under a soft, bright, silvery sky. Brotherly, steadfast and at peace; no rack, no lances, no chains, no lettering.
face: Two clearly different Gallo-Roman brothers with fair, lightly ruddy complexions. ROGATIAN (left): about twenty-eight, with a WIDE, FLAT, SQUARE face under a LOW, straight hairline — a SHORT, strong, straight nose, SMALL, deep-set grey eyes under a HEAVY brow and thick, straight brown brows, broad, flat cheeks, a WIDE, firm mouth; thick brown hair cropped short; a SHORT, close-trimmed brown beard that follows the square jaw; the gaze grave and resolute, toward us. DONATIAN (right): about twenty, BEARDLESS, with an open, OVAL face and HIGH, ROUNDED cheekbones — a smooth, high forehead, a straight nose with a slightly UPTURNED tip, LARGE, bright blue eyes under softly arched fair brows, a gentle, smiling mouth, a rounded chin with a small DIMPLE; straight, fair, light-brown hair cut short and close with a short fringe; the gaze warm, turned toward his brother.

subject: St. Yvo Helori, priest and ecclesiastical judge of Brittany, half-length: a long black cassock-like gown with a deep collar and cuffs of brown fur, a black clerical cap; in his left hand a rolled parchment tied with a red cord, a poor man's petition; in his right, held out a little, a small leather purse for the poor. Behind him, the Breton countryside near Tréguier: the tall grey granite cathedral with its spire above a small town, the tidal river with its mudflats and a small boat, green fields bounded by hedges and stone walls, and a thatched stone farmhouse, under a soft, grey-blue sky with drifting clouds. Just, kind and upright; no court, no rich man, no lettering.
face: A Breton of about forty-nine, CLEAN-SHAVEN, with a pale, fair complexion and a LEAN face that is WIDE at the cheekbones and HOLLOW beneath them, narrowing to a LONG, SQUARE-TIPPED chin — a prominent, BONY brow ridge, HOODED, grey eyes cast down, a LONG, straight nose with a LOW-SET, fleshy tip, a small mouth with a full, slightly pouting LOWER lip, deep lines from the nose to the chin; dark-brown hair cut short and round like a bowl beneath the cap; the gaze attentive and grave, lowered to the petition.

subject: Sts. Primus and Felicianus, two aged Roman brothers, half-length side by side, dressed as in their seventh-century mosaic at Santo Stefano Rotondo: long white tunics with narrow dark clavi and white pallia draped over the left shoulder, each with a martyr's palm; Primus (left) holds a small loaf of bread for the prisoners they served, Felicianus (right) lays his hand on his brother's shoulder. Behind them, the Roman Campagna along the Via Nomentana: a paved road with milestones and umbrella pines, a low arched tomb-church by the roadside, and the hill town of Nomentum in the distance under a warm golden evening sky. Gentle, steadfast and brotherly; no lettering, no chains, no torments.
face: Two clearly different old Roman brothers with warm olive complexions. PRIMUS (left), about eighty, as in the mosaic grey-haired with a short grey beard: a LONG, NARROW, HORSE-LONG face with its length in the MIDDLE — eyes set HIGH under a narrow, lined forehead, a LONG, DROOPING nose with a rounded tip, a LONG upper lip, flat, long cheeks, a narrow chin under a SHORT, NEAT silver beard; deep-set, pale hazel eyes; thin silver hair cropped close. FELICIANUS (right), about seventy, as in the mosaic darker-haired: a SHORT, ROUND-OVAL face with a PROMINENT, ROUNDED, BOSSED forehead and a SMALL, slightly RECEDING chin under a full, dark-brown beard streaked with grey — a SMALL, ARCHED nose, BIG, ROUND, dark-brown eyes, softly rounded cheeks, a small, full mouth; thick, short dark-brown hair greying at the sides; both gazes calm and kind.

subject: St. Silverius, Pope, half-length, in exile on a desert island: stripped of his papal vestments, he wears a plain, rough grey-brown monk's habit, and holds a martyr's palm against his breast with his right hand, his left hand resting on a small, plain wooden cross; he looks out to sea toward Rome. Behind him, Palmarola in the Tyrrhenian Sea: steep, bare cliffs of pale volcanic rock with scrub and a few wild flowers, a deep-blue sea, a small fishing boat with a white sail, and the long shape of Ponza on the horizon under a bright, clear sky. Steadfast, patient and serene in privation; no chains, no lettering.
face: A Roman of Campania of about fifty-five, THINNED by hunger, with a light-olive, sun-dried complexion and a ROUND skull with a FULL, CURVED forehead — very PROMINENT, ROUNDED cheekbones standing out over the hollows that hunger has made, SMALL, CLOSE-SET grey-green eyes under thin, slightly slanting grey brows, a SHORT, straight nose with a PINCHED, narrow bridge, a SMALL, softly receding chin under a SHORT, SPARSE, grizzled beard, a small, closed, patient mouth, LARGE ears; close-cropped greying dark hair; the gaze steady and far-off.

subject: St. John Francis Regis, half-length, as a seventeenth-century French Jesuit on a winter mission: a black cassock under a heavy black travelling cloak dusted with snow, a plain wooden walking staff in his left hand; with his right hand he raises a small crucifix toward the mountain villages he goes to preach in. Behind him, the high Vivarais in winter: snow-covered ridges and pine woods, a steep, frozen mountain path, and the small stone village of Lalouvesc with its church on the pass, smoke from the chimneys, under a cold, clear pale-blue sky. Ardent, tireless and meek; no lettering.
face: A Frenchman of Languedoc of about forty-three, lean from labour, with a fair complexion reddened by the cold and a LONG, NARROW, CHISELLED face following his portrait — a HIGH, rounded forehead, HIGH cheekbones with flat hollows beneath, a narrow jaw, a LONG, STRAIGHT, NARROW nose whose tip turns slightly DOWN, LARGE, bright, rather PROMINENT hazel eyes turned sideways toward the villages under thin, arched auburn brows, a small, firm mouth; short AUBURN-CHESTNUT hair, a THIN auburn moustache and a SHORT, POINTED auburn beard on the chin only; the gaze eager and ardent.

subject: St. Columba, Abbot of Iona, half-length, as an old Irish monk: a plain, undyed cream woollen cowl with its hood fallen back, a simple abbot's staff of dark wood in his left hand, and against his breast a Gospel book in a cover of Insular gold interlace (no lettering); a small white dove, for his name, alights near his right shoulder. Behind him, Iona: a low green island of turf and pale rock above white sand and a clear green-blue sea, a few simple monastic buildings and a small church, the Sound with a hide-covered boat, and the blue hills of Mull across the water under a high, luminous northern sky. Glad, serene and full of holy joy; no lettering.
face: An Irishman of about seventy-five, CLEAN-SHAVEN, with a fair, fine-skinned complexion lit by a RUDDY GLOW, the front of the head shaved from EAR TO EAR in the Irish tonsure so that a smooth, bare forehead rises high, and long, fine WHITE hair falls from the back of the head to the shoulders; a BROAD, OPEN face, as WIDE at the jaw as at the cheekbones, with SMOOTH, FULL, glowing cheeks and no hollows — a straight, medium nose with a slightly UPTURNED tip, very LARGE, clear, luminous light-grey eyes set wide apart under faint, high, white brows, a WIDE, generous mouth in a joyful smile, and a firm chin with a distinct CLEFT; the gaze lifted a little, radiant ('angelic in appearance').

subject: St. Etheldreda, Abbess of Ely, half-length, as in her tenth-century image in the Benedictional of St. Æthelwold: a dark veil over a cream wimple, a full mantle of warm ochre and russet over a brown habit; she holds a book against her breast with her right hand and in her left a slender staff that has budded into green, flowering branches; her neck plain, with no jewels. Behind her, the Isle of Ely in the Fens: a low green island rising from wide, still waters, reed beds and willows, a small monastery church of stone and timber on the rise (not the later Norman cathedral), and a vast, pale, cloud-streaked East Anglian sky. Serene, royal and detached; no crown, no king, no lettering.
face: An East Anglian princess of about forty with a fair, clear complexion and a softly PEAR-SHAPED face — NARROW at the temples and widening to FULL lower cheeks and a broad, rounded jaw; a straight nose that continues the line of the forehead in ONE UNBROKEN LINE (a classical profile); LARGE, WIDE-SET, heavy-lidded pale-blue eyes under HIGH, curved fair brows; a SMALL, full, rosebud mouth; a SHORT, rounded chin; the neck plain and unadorned; all hair hidden; the gaze calm and inward.

subject: Sts. Marcus and Marcellianus, twin brothers of a noble Roman family, half-length side by side: long tunics, Marcus's of deep blue and Marcellianus's of dark green, each under a white pallium, each holding a martyr's palm; Marcus (left) has his hand on his heart, Marcellianus (right) holds his palm upright with both hands. Behind them, the Via Ardeatina outside Rome in the late third century: a paved road between cypresses and low tombs, the brick entrance of a catacomb in the green slope, and the walls and roofs of Rome in the distance under a clear, warm, blue sky. Steadfast and brotherly; no pillars, no lances, no lettering.
face: Twin Roman brothers of about thirty-five with fair olive complexions and ONE SHARED bone structure, told apart only by the beard: a face with a BROAD, SQUARE forehead above a NARROWER, V-SHAPED lower face ending in a POINTED chin — a LONG nose with a distinct BUMP at the bridge, LARGE, dark eyes set CLOSE together under THICK, STRAIGHT black brows that nearly meet, clearly PROMINENT ears, a small, full mouth; short, crisp, curly black hair. MARCUS (left) wears a short, close black beard; MARCELLIANUS (right) is clean-shaven, which shows the pointed chin; both gazes grave and steadfast.

subject: St. Avitus, half-length, as a sixth-century Frankish abbot turned recluse: a coarse, dark-brown woollen monastic habit with a deep hood laid back, a rope girdle, a plain, rough wooden abbot's staff in his right hand, his left hand resting on a small wooden cross at his breast. Behind him, the forest of the Dunois on the edge of the Perche: tall oaks and beeches, a clearing with a small hermit's cell of timber and thatch, and beyond the trees a glimpse of a river valley and a hill town under a soft, silvery summer sky. Humble, quiet and recollected; no lettering.
face: A Frank of peasant stock of about sixty-five, weathered by field and forest, with a brown, outdoor complexion and a LEAN, FLAT, WIDE face with a DISHED, CONCAVE profile — a broad, flat forehead, a SHORT, SCOOPED nose with an UPTURNED tip, WIDE-SET, large, mild, pale-green eyes under sparse, straight grey brows, BROAD, FLAT cheekbones with thin cheeks beneath, a wide, thin-lipped mouth, a SMALL, ROUND chin under a SHORT, ROUGH grey-brown beard; grey-brown hair cropped close around a monastic tonsure; the gaze lowered, gentle and patient.

subject: St. Medard, Bishop of Noyon, half-length, as a very old sixth-century Frankish bishop without a mitre: a white alb under a full, bell-shaped chasuble of rose-red edged in gold, a plain wooden pastoral staff in the crook of his left arm; in his right hand he holds out a small wreath of white roses, as for the maiden of Salency whom he crowned for her virtue. Above his head a great brown eagle hovers with wings spread wide like a roof, sheltering him from a shower of rain that falls silver on either side while he stands dry. Behind him, the green, rolling fields and orchards of Picardy, a village with a small church, and the little walled city of Noyon on its hill under a sky of broken rain clouds with sunlight breaking through. Merry, fatherly and warm; no lettering.
face: A Frank of Picardy of about eighty-five, hale and HEAVY-BONED, with a ruddy, weathered complexion and a big, SQUARE face with a strong, BROAD jaw — a high, BALD, DOMED crown with a fringe of short white hair, a LONG, strong, gently HOOKED nose, LARGE ears, eyes squeezed into merry CRESCENTS by laughter under BUSHY white brows lifted at the centre, deep laugh lines, a WIDE mouth OPEN in a hearty laugh that shows a little of the upper teeth (the laughing Medard of tradition), and a SHORT, SQUARE-CUT, close white beard that follows the jaw; the gaze warm and full of joy.

subject: St. Juliana Falconieri, half-length, as an aged Servite foundress of the fourteenth century: the black habit and black mantle of the Servants of Mary with a leather girdle, a black veil over a close white wimple; her hands crossed on her breast, and over her heart on the black habit a small white Host marked with a little cross, as she is always shown. Behind her, Florence on the Arno: red-tiled roofs, stone towers, and the church of the Santissima Annunziata that her father built, under a soft evening sky of rose and gold. Recollected, tender and modest, eyes lowered; no doves, no lettering.
face: A Florentine noblewoman of about sixty-five, thin from long illness, with a pale, finely lined complexion and a face like an INVERTED EGG — a WIDE, SQUARE-set forehead framed tight by the wimple, FLATTISH cheeks, the face narrowing to a firm, slightly JUTTING, rounded chin; a LONG, straight, NARROW nose with a delicate HOOK at the tip; SMALL, deep-set, dark-brown eyes LOWERED, as one who never gazed on a man's face, under thin, STRAIGHT dark brows; a small, thin, gently compressed mouth; all hair hidden.

subject: St. John of Sahagún (the book's 'of St. Fagondez'), half-length, as a fifteenth-century Augustinian friar: the black habit of the Hermits of St. Augustine with its wide sleeves, black hood and leather belt; in his right hand he raises a gold chalice with a white Host above it surrounded by soft golden rays, as in his traditional image, his left hand open on his breast. Behind him, Salamanca in golden sandstone: the Old Cathedral's tower and ribbed dome over the roofs, and the long Roman bridge over the river Tormes, under a clear, deep-blue Castilian sky. Peaceful, grave and luminous; no assassins, no lettering.
face: A Castilian of about forty-nine, CLEAN-SHAVEN with a faint blue shadow of beard, a sun-darkened olive complexion and a WIDE, ANGULAR face whose JAW is BROADER than its forehead — a short, flat forehead under a full ring of black hair in the monastic tonsure, a straight nose with a BROAD bridge and FLARED nostrils, LARGE, calm, steady dark eyes set WIDE apart under THICK, straight black brows that angle slightly DOWN toward the nose, FLAT cheeks, a WIDE, straight, closed mouth, and a PROMINENT, ROUNDED chin; the gaze fixed peacefully on the Host.

subject: St. Victor, half-length, as a Roman army officer of the late third century: a muscled bronze cuirass over a russet tunic, leather shoulder straps, a deep-blue military cloak pinned at the right shoulder, no helmet; he holds a green palm in his right hand, his left resting on the rim of a small round stone hand-mill millstone set upright beside him. Behind him, Marseilles: the long harbour inlet with moored Roman ships, the white limestone hills, and on the rocky slope across the water a cave-mouth among pines where the Christians buried him. Resolute, cheerful and brave; no wounds, no lettering.
face: A Gallo-Roman of Massilia of about thirty-five, weathered by service, with a fair, sun-reddened complexion and a strong, ANGULAR face — a broad, straight forehead, SHARPLY CUT cheekbones, the sides running straight down to a BROAD, FLAT-BOTTOMED chin with a vertical CLEFT; a SHORT nose with a slight BREAK at the bridge; deep-set, bright blue-grey eyes under thick, LOW, straight sandy brows; a wide, thin-lipped mouth; thick, straight sandy-brown hair cut short, a short, close sandy beard; the gaze frank and steady.

subject: St. John Gualbert, half-length, as the founder-abbot of Vallombrosa: the ash-grey Benedictine habit of the early Vallombrosans with a full cowl and hood lying on the shoulders, a plain wooden abbot's staff in his left hand; in his right he holds up a small wooden crucifix, the Christ on it with head gently bowed toward him, recalling the crucifix of San Miniato. Behind him, the shady valley of Vallombrosa in the Tuscan Apennines: tall dark firs, a small stone monastery with a bell-cote, a stream, and far below the Arno valley toward Florence in blue haze. Humble, forgiving and serene; no lettering.
face: A Florentine of about seventy, lean from austerity, with a fair, lightly weathered complexion and a face BROADEST ACROSS HIGH, JUTTING CHEEKBONES, the cheeks falling FLAT beneath them to a NARROW, SQUARE-TIPPED chin; a medium straight nose with a slightly BULBOUS tip, WIDE-SET, pale grey eyes under sparse, ARCHED grey brows, a small, firm mouth under a pronounced upper-lip groove; a short, close, silver-grey beard following the jaw, grey hair in a monastic crown; the gaze lowered to the crucifix, gentle.

subject: St. Simon Stock, half-length, in the Carmelite habit: a brown tunic and brown scapular, a white mantle over the shoulders, the hood fallen back. He holds out in both hands, as if showing it, a brown scapular of two small plain rectangles of brown wool joined by cords (no lettering, no emblem), his eyes lifted toward a soft golden light at the upper corner of the window (no figure in it). Behind him, a thirteenth-century English friary of grey stone with a small chapel and cloister, beside a quiet river among willows and green fields, under a pale summer sky. Humble, grateful and full of trust; no lettering.
face: St. Simon Stock as on `mount_carmel`: an Englishman of about seventy, clean-shaven, with a gaunt TRIANGULAR face — broad temples narrowing to a small pointed chin, hollow cheeks, a long, thin, slightly aquiline nose, deep-set pale blue eyes lifted in wonder under sparse white brows, a thin-lipped mouth slightly open; white hair in a narrow ring around a wide tonsure.
verdict: rejected: frame: its own border and a round-topped window, and a face too photographic

subject: St. James of Nisibis, half-length, as a fourth-century Syrian bishop who had been a mountain hermit: a coarse, dark goat-hair tunic, and over it a white wool omophorion with small dark crosses worn round the neck and falling in front; no mitre. He stands on the top of a square stone tower of the city walls of Nisibis, his right hand raised in prayer toward heaven, his left resting on the parapet. Below and far off, the Mesopotamian plain under a hot sky with the Persian camp: tents, a few small elephants and horsemen, and a faint dark haze of gnats drifting over them; behind the tower, the flat roofs and a small early church of Nisibis. Grave and prayerful, not wrathful; no battle, no lettering.
face: A Syrian of Mesopotamia of about seventy, sun-darkened and weathered from years in the open air, with a SQUARE, BIG-BONED face — a HEAVY, FLAT BROW RIDGE running straight across, a BROAD, FLAT-BRIDGED nose with wide nostrils, SMALL, DEEP-SET, very dark eyes under bushy black-and-grey brows, HIGH, FLAT cheekbones, a WIDE, straight mouth; a very long, dense black beard heavily streaked with grey, falling in one mass to the chest; thick, rough grey-black hair cut short; the gaze lifted, intent.

subject: St. Alexius, half-length, as a poor beggar sheltering in his father's house: a threadbare, patched tunic of undyed grey-brown wool with a rope belt and a worn dark cloak; he sits in a dim nook beneath a marble stairway of a Roman palace, a small wooden bowl and a pilgrim's staff beside him, and holds against his breast a small folded parchment (nothing legible). Through an archway beyond the stairs, the gardens and the church of the Aventine hill and the roofs of Rome in soft morning light. Poor, hidden, patient and peaceful; no lettering.
face: A Roman patrician worn down by seventeen years of beggary, about fifty-five, with a pale olive complexion and a SMALL, NARROW, TALL face — LONG, FLAT cheeks, a FINE, STRAIGHT nose with a slightly squared tip, LARGE, soft brown eyes whose outer corners SLOPE DOWN, fine, straight brows, a small, soft mouth above a SMALL, RECEDING chin; dark-brown hair roughly cropped short and greying, a sparse, patchy dark beard; the gaze lowered, gentle and hidden.

subject: St. Pantaleon, half-length, as a young Greek physician of Nicomedia: a white chiton with narrow purple bands and a rose-red chlamys pinned at the right shoulder; he holds a small open wooden box of medicines against his side with his left hand and a slender long-handled silver spoon in his right, a green palm tucked into the crook of his arm. Behind him, Nicomedia on its gulf: a colonnaded street climbing the hill, a domed building, cypresses, and the blue water of the Sea of Marmara. Compassionate, grave and gentle; no lettering.
face: A Bithynian Greek of about twenty-nine, BEARDLESS, with a warm olive complexion and a LONG, SMOOTH face — a HIGH, NARROW forehead under a low cap of short, TIGHT dark-brown curls, a LONG, THIN, straight nose with slightly flared nostrils, large ALMOND-SHAPED dark eyes set rather CLOSE under finely arched dark brows, smooth, lean cheeks, a SMALL, full, closed mouth, a LONG, narrow, rounded chin; the gaze direct and compassionate.

subject: St. Felicitas and her seven sons, grouped half-length inside the arched window: Felicitas in the centre, a little taller than the rest, a noble Roman widow in a deep plum-violet stola with a dark-grey palla drawn over her head as a veil, her right arm round the shoulders of her youngest son and her left hand raised toward heaven; the seven sons around her in graded heights, the three eldest standing behind at her right and left, the four younger in front, all in plain Roman tunics of white, saffron, sage-green and russet wool with short mantles, several holding green palms. Behind them, second-century Rome from the Via Salaria: umbrella pines and cypresses, a low brick tomb-chapel over a catacomb entrance, the walls and roofs of the city in warm evening light. Grave, tender and steadfast; no wounds, no instruments, no lettering. Keep all eight figures inside the arched window, eight clearly separate faces.
face: Eight clearly different people of one Roman family, fair-olive skin. FELICITAS (centre), about fifty-five: a LONG face with HIGH, FLAT cheekbones and a STRONG, SQUARE, slightly prominent chin; a long, straight nose whose tip turns a little down, deep-set grey-brown eyes under thick, straight dark brows, a firm, wide mouth with fine lines at its corners; dark hair greying at the temples under the veil; her gaze lifted, fearless. The SONS: (1) JANUARIUS, the eldest, about twenty-four, behind at her right: a LONG, NARROW face, a thin, AQUILINE nose, deep-set dark eyes, a short, close black beard. (2) FELIX, about twenty-two, behind at her left: a BROAD, SQUARE face, a SHORT, BLUNT nose, wide-set brown eyes, clean-shaven, thick straight black hair. (3) PHILIP, about twenty, behind beside Felix: a HEART-SHAPED face, a fine straight nose, large dark eyes, a faint first moustache, wavy brown hair. (4) SILVANUS, about eighteen, front left: a ROUND face, a small SNUB nose, a few freckles, light-brown curls. (5) ALEXANDER, about sixteen, front: an OVAL face with his mother's long, straight nose, straight dark hair with a fringe. (6) VITALIS, about fourteen, front: a small TRIANGULAR face with a pointed chin, prominent ears, cropped black hair. (7) MARTIALIS, the youngest, about twelve, under her arm: a chubby child's face with full round cheeks and tight black curls, looking up at her.

subject: St. Eugenius, Bishop of Carthage, half-length, as a fifth-century African bishop without a mitre: a white tunic under a full, bell-shaped paenula of deep wine-red, a white wool pallium with small dark crosses, a plain wooden staff in the crook of his left arm; with his right hand he gives a round loaf of bread to an unseen poor man at the edge of the window (only the reaching hand shows). Behind him, Carthage by the sea: the round naval harbour, white-walled houses and a colonnaded basilica on the Byrsa hill, date palms, the blue gulf with the mountains of Cape Bon beyond. Generous, steadfast and kind; no lettering.
face: A Carthaginian of Roman Africa of about sixty-five, with a warm olive-brown complexion and a LONG face with DEEPLY SUNKEN TEMPLES and a TALL, ROUNDED crown; a strongly ARCHED, bony nose, LARGE, gentle dark eyes under HEAVY LIDS, thick, curved black-grey brows, full lips in a WIDE, generous mouth, a short, TIGHTLY CURLED white beard close along the jaw, close-cropped curly white hair; the gaze turned kindly toward the poor man.

subject: St. Margaret, half-length, as a young Christian girl of Pisidia: a long-sleeved tunic of pale green under a warm rust-red mantle, a narrow white veil laid back over braided hair; she holds up a small plain wooden cross in her right hand and a green martyr's palm in her left, against her shoulder. Behind her, the upland pastures of Pisidia with a few grazing sheep, low limestone hills, and the walls of Antioch on a far slope under a clear sky. Pure, fearless and gentle; no dragon, no torments, no lettering.
face: A Greek girl of Asia Minor of about sixteen, with a warm, light olive complexion and a SHORT, SQUARE face — a broad, STRAIGHT jaw ending in a small SQUARE chin, WIDE, FLAT cheekbones, a SHORT, straight nose with a broad bridge, very LARGE, WIDE-SET dark eyes under STRONG, straight, nearly level dark brows, a WIDE mouth with a full lower lip; black hair in two thick braids; the gaze direct and steady.

subject: St. Christina, half-length, as a young girl of a rich Roman family: a long white tunic, a sky-blue mantle edged in gold, a thin gold circlet in her hair; she holds a green palm and two plain arrows crossed in her right hand, her left hand on her breast; a small round millstone rests at her side. Behind her, the lake of Bolsena: calm blue water with its two small wooded islands, the town of Bolsena with its castle on the hill, olive groves and vineyards on the green shore. Innocent, calm and unafraid; no wounds, no torments, no lettering.
face: An Etruscan-Roman girl of about thirteen, visibly a young girl, with a fair, rosy complexion and a face like a small INVERTED TRIANGLE — a HIGH, ROUNDED, PROMINENT forehead over a SHORT lower face and a small, POINTED chin; a tiny, UPTURNED nose; large, ROUND, light-brown eyes set FAR APART under fine, pale, high-arched brows; a small, bow-shaped mouth; wavy fair-auburn hair falling to the shoulders; the gaze lifted, candid and serene.

subject: St. Simon Stock, half-length, in the Carmelite habit: a brown tunic and brown scapular, a white mantle over the shoulders, the hood fallen back. He holds out in both hands, as if showing it, a brown scapular of two small plain rectangles of brown wool joined by cords (no lettering, no emblem), his eyes lifted toward a soft golden light at the upper corner of the window (no figure in it). Behind him, a thirteenth-century English friary of grey stone with a small chapel and cloister, beside a quiet river among willows and green fields, under a pale summer sky. Humble, grateful and full of trust; no lettering.
face: St. Simon Stock as on `mount_carmel`: an Englishman of about seventy, clean-shaven, with a gaunt TRIANGULAR face — broad temples narrowing to a small pointed chin, hollow cheeks, a long, thin, slightly aquiline nose, deep-set pale blue eyes lifted in wonder under sparse white brows, a thin-lipped mouth slightly open; white hair in a narrow ring around a wide tonsure.

subject: St. Romanus, half-length, as a Roman soldier newly baptised: a brown leather cuirass with bronze fittings over a white tunic, a dark-red military cloak pinned at the shoulder, no helmet; he holds a plain clay water pitcher against his side with his left arm and a green palm in his right hand. Behind him, the inside of a Roman prison: rough stone walls, a small high barred window with daylight, an oil lamp in a niche, and an open iron-bound door through which the sunlit roofs of Rome can be seen. Humble, newly converted and brave; no weapons drawn, no lettering.
face: A Roman soldier of about twenty-seven with a dark olive complexion and a LONG, NARROW head — thick, straight black brows that MEET over the nose in one line, deep-set hazel eyes, a thin, STRAIGHT nose with a sharp bridge, HOLLOW cheeks above a LEAN, NARROW jaw, a WIDE mouth, a slightly jutting narrow chin, EARS that stand out; black hair cropped very short; a short, dense black beard trimmed close to the jaw; the gaze lifted, wondering. Not the sandy, cleft-chinned victor_marseilles, the blocky Nereus, or the beardless, curly pantaleon.

subject: Pope St. Stephen I, half-length, seated on a plain stone chair in a chamber of the Roman catacombs: a third-century bishop in a white tunic with narrow purple stripes and a full, rust-red paenula, no tiara and no mitre; an open codex of the Gospels on his knee, his right hand raised in blessing over the faithful, who are not shown. Behind him, the tufa walls of the catacomb with arched burial niches, a painted Good Shepherd on the vault, small clay oil lamps burning, and a narrow shaft of daylight from a light-well. Patient, gentle and firm; no soldiers, no sword, no blood, no lettering.
face: A Roman of about fifty-five, CLEAN-SHAVEN as on the Speyer reliquary head, with a pale olive complexion and a LONG, NARROW face under a PROMINENT, ROUNDED forehead that bulges over the brows — SUNKEN temples, LARGE, DEEP-SET dark eyes in shadowed sockets under thin, straight brows, a LONG, STRAIGHT, NARROW nose running on from the brow line, FLAT cheeks, a SMALL, soft, closed mouth, a SHORT, POINTED chin; close-cropped dark hair touched with grey, cut straight across the forehead; a patient, forbearing look. Not the bald, hook-nosed sixtus_ii, nor the fine-boned, hump-nosed fabian.

subject: St. Eusebius of Rome, half-length, as a fourth-century Roman priest confined to his room: a plain white tunic and a dark-brown paenula, his hands joined in prayer, kneeling behind a simple wooden prayer-desk with an open codex on it. Behind him, a bare whitewashed room of his house on the Esquiline: a heavy, closed wooden door with iron studs, a small high window with a glimpse of Roman roofs and a cypress, an oil lamp in a niche. Patient, unbowed and prayerful; no chains, no guards, no lettering.
face: A Roman priest of about fifty, pale from confinement, with a face BROADEST AT THE BROW — a WIDE, SQUARE forehead, CLOSE-SET, intense black eyes under thick, straight black brows, a nose with a HIGH, SHARP bridge, THIN, drawn cheeks, a LONG, NARROW chin, a thin-lipped mouth; very short black hair receding to a point at the brow; CLEAN-SHAVEN with a dark shadow on the jaw; the eyes raised in prayer. Not the heavy-browed, curly-bearded eusebius_vercelli.

subject: St. Radegundes, half-length, as the queen who became a nun: a dark-grey religious habit, a white wimple and a black veil, a slender gold crown resting over the veil, and a royal-blue mantle with a gold border slipping from her shoulders; in both hands she holds a small gold reliquary cross set with a few garnets, the relic of the True Cross she obtained for her abbey. Behind her, Poitiers on its hill above the river Clain: the walls of the Merovingian abbey of the Holy Cross, a small stone church with a bell-cote, poplars along the river under a soft sky. Humble, recollected and royal; no lettering.
face: A Thuringian princess of about fifty with a fair, fine complexion and a SHORT, WIDE face — a LOW forehead framed by the wimple, HIGH, ROUNDED cheekbones that make the eyes look narrow and slightly UPWARD-SLANTING, hooded dark-blue eyes under straight, dark-blonde brows, a SHORT, straight nose, a WIDE, full-lipped mouth, a FIRM, ROUNDED chin; her gaze lowered to the cross. Not the long oval of hedwig and margaret_scotland, the broad square-jawed maud, or the triangular, wide-eyed cunegundes.

subject: Sts. Tiburtius and Susanna side by side, half-length, inside the arched window, as in the book's engraving: Tiburtius at the left, a young Roman subdeacon in a white alb with a gold-bordered pale tunicle, holding a green palm; Susanna at the right, a young Roman noblewoman in a dusty-rose stola with a white palla drawn over her head as a veil, holding a white lily and a green palm. Behind them, the Via Labicana outside Rome: two tall laurel trees beside the road, a small brick chapel, the Campagna with a distant aqueduct under a soft morning sky. Gentle and steadfast; no wounds, no swords, no lettering.
face: Two clearly different young Romans with fair-olive skin. TIBURTIUS (left), about twenty-two, BEARDLESS: a SQUARE face with a WIDE, flat forehead and a BROAD, BLUNT jaw — a short, UPTURNED nose, round, lively grey eyes under curved light-brown brows, a wide mouth with a faint smile, thick, wavy chestnut hair to the ears. SUSANNA (right), about twenty: a LONG, NARROW face — a high forehead, a long, fine, gently AQUILINE nose, HEAVY-LIDDED dark almond eyes under straight dark brows, narrow cheeks, a small, closed mouth, a small POINTED chin; black hair parted in the centre under the veil; her gaze lowered. Not the soft oval of the virgin martyrs (agnes, cecilia).

subject: St. Peter Favre, half-length, as a sixteenth-century Jesuit priest: a plain black cassock and a black cloak, a black three-cornered biretta; he holds a small open book of the Spiritual Exercises in his left hand and lays his right hand on his breast. Behind him, the high valley of his Savoyard childhood: green alpine pastures with a few sheep, a wooden chalet with a stone roof, pine woods and snowy peaks under a clear sky. Gentle, recollected and warm; no lettering.
face: A Savoyard of about forty with a fair, lightly weathered mountain complexion and a BROAD, FULL face, as in his old portraits — a WIDE forehead, WIDE cheekbones, LARGE, WIDE-SET, clear dark-brown eyes, slightly PROMINENT, under thick, softly arched dark brows, a straight nose with a BROAD, rounded tip, FULL lips, a BROAD, rounded chin under a full, short, ROUNDED dark-brown beard and moustache; dark-brown hair under the biretta; a gentle, open, attentive gaze. Not the oval, curly-haired francis_xavier, the bald ignatius_loyola or the grey peter_canisius.

subject: St. Germanus of Auxerre, half-length, as a fifth-century Gallic bishop: a white linen alb and over it a deep moss-green paenula (the old round chasuble) with a narrow gold border, no mitre; a plain wooden crozier with a simple curled head in his left hand, his right hand raised open in blessing and command. Behind him, a green river valley between rounded hills in Britain, a small timber church with a thatched roof on the bank, and far off a crowd of newly baptised Britons in white, small and peaceful. Strong, fatherly and unafraid; no battle, no weapons, no lettering.
face: A Gallo-Roman noble of about sixty-five, once a soldier and a huntsman, with a weathered, ruddy complexion and an OBLONG face under a BROAD, DOMED forehead — WIDE, FLAT cheekbones, a BROAD, ROUNDED chin, a short, straight nose with a wide bridge, SMALL, keen, pale-grey eyes with deep crow's-feet from years in the open, thick, level, BRISTLING iron-grey brows, a wide, straight, firm mouth; iron-grey hair cropped short round a tonsured crown; a short, CLIPPED iron-grey beard cut SQUARE at the chin; a commanding, far-seeing gaze. Not the clean-shaven, bald, underbitten germanus_paris.

subject: Sts. Nazarius and Celsus side by side, half-length, inside the arched window: Nazarius at the left, a travelling preacher in a white wool tunic under a brown hooded travelling cloak, holding a small closed Gospel codex against his chest with his right hand and a green palm in his left; Celsus at the right, a little shorter, a boy in a plain undyed short tunic with a russet mantle, holding a green palm and looking up at his master. Behind them, a walled garden outside the Roman walls of Milan: cypresses and a fig tree, a low stone wall, the brick walls and a gate-tower of the city beyond, and the Alps faint and blue on the horizon. Calm and steadfast; no soldiers, no swords, no wounds, no lettering.
face: Two clearly different figures, both olive-skinned. NAZARIUS (left), a Roman of about forty-five, CLEAN-SHAVEN in the Roman manner with a dark shadow on the jaw: a TALL, RECTANGULAR face with a LONG MIDFACE — a high, straight forehead, a LONG nose with a pronounced BUMP high on the bridge, HOODED grey eyes set LOW under straight, heavy dark brows, a LONG UPPER LIP over a wide, thin-lipped mouth, a squared chin; close-cropped black hair greying at the temples; a calm, resolute gaze forward. CELSUS (right), a boy of about fourteen: a SHORT, WIDE face — a broad, low forehead under a thick, STRAIGHT black fringe cut round like a bowl, a short nose with a wide, flat bridge, big, round, dark eyes set wide under low, straight brows, full cheeks, a WIDE mouth, a small, rounded chin; looking up at Nazarius with trust. No curls on the boy.

subject: Three martyrs side by side, half-length, inside the arched window: in the centre St. Cyriacus, a Roman deacon, in a white alb and a deep-red dalmatic with two gold clavi, holding a closed Gospel book and a green palm; at the left St. Largus, an older man in a grey-brown tunic and dark mantle, a palm in his hand; at the right St. Smaragdus, a young man in a sage-green tunic and russet mantle, a palm held upright. Behind them, the Roman Campagna along the Via Ostiensis: umbrella pines, a low brick tomb by the road, a farmhouse among vines, and the Tiber in the distance under evening light. Serene and steadfast; no soldiers, no wounds, no lettering. Three clearly separate faces.
face: Three clearly different Romans. CYRIACUS (centre), about forty, CLEAN-SHAVEN, with a light-olive complexion and a FULL, SOFT, SQUARE face — a broad, smooth forehead, LARGE, luminous hazel eyes set WIDE apart under dark, arched brows, a SHORT, WIDE nose with rounded nostrils, full cheeks, a WIDE, full-lipped mouth, a squared, softly padded chin; short, thick, straight dark-brown hair; a serene, upward gaze. LARGUS (left), about sixty: a LONG, HEAVY face whose features DROOP — long ear lobes, a big, fleshy nose, heavy, pouched dark eyes under drooping grey brows, loose cheeks, a grey-stubbled jaw, thin grey hair combed forward; a patient, weary kindness. SMARAGDUS (right), about twenty-five: a NARROW, FOX-LIKE face — a sharp, slightly upturned nose, narrow, slanting green eyes, high thin brows, a pointed chin, a light first beard along the jaw, wavy reddish-brown hair; an eager look.

subject: The opening of St. Stephen's tomb at Caphargamala in 415, in the arched window: in the centre, Bishop John of Jerusalem, standing, in a white sticharion and a deep-blue phelonion with a white wool omophorion marked with dark crosses, no mitre, his hands raised open in wonder and thanksgiving; at the left, the old priest Lucian kneeling beside the tomb, in a plain dark-brown robe, his hands joined; in front of them a plain stone chest in the dug earth, its lid slid half aside, a soft golden light rising from within (no bones shown); a young labourer with a spade seen in profile at the right, small. Behind, the terraced hills of Judaea with olive trees, a heap of small stones, a small stone church with a tiled roof, and a few villagers approaching. Awed and joyful; no lettering.
face: Two principal figures, clearly different. BISHOP JOHN (centre), a Greek of about sixty with a warm olive complexion and a LONG, NARROW face — a high, lined forehead, a LONG nose with a HUMPED bridge, large, heavy-lidded dark eyes under thick, curved black-and-grey brows, lean cheeks, a small mouth; grey-black hair to the nape and a LONG, full grey-black beard cut SQUARE at the end; the eyes raised in wonder. LUCIAN (kneeling, left), a Palestinian priest of about seventy: a SMALL, NARROW, sharp-featured face — a high, BALD forehead, a THIN, BEAKED nose, small, bright dark eyes, SUNKEN cheeks, a narrow chin under a SHORT, SPARSE grey beard; wisps of grey hair at the sides; the gaze lowered to the tomb. The labourer: a beardless youth seen in profile, brown and lean.

subject: St. Robert, first abbot of Newminster, half-length, as a Cistercian of the twelfth century: the white cowl of undyed wool with wide, deep sleeves over a white habit, a black scapular just showing at the neck, the monastic tonsure; a plain wooden abbot's staff in his left hand; in his right hand, held a little forward, a plain wooden plate with a loaf of bread sweetened with honey, the food he sent untouched to the poor at the gate. Behind him, Newminster in Northumberland: the pale stone church and cloister of the new abbey in the green valley of the Wansbeck, woods on the slopes and a stone bridge over the river, under a soft, grey-and-gold northern sky. Gentle, abstinent and fatherly; no angel, no lettering.
face: A Yorkshireman of about fifty-five, CLEAN-SHAVEN, with a fair, weathered, lightly ruddy complexion and a face that TAPERS from a WIDE forehead and broad temples under the tonsure to a SMALL, ROUND, DIMPLED chin — a SHORT, straight nose with a small BUMP on the bridge, WIDE-SPACED, clear grey eyes with deep crow's-feet, level, sandy-grey brows, flat cheeks, a WIDE, thin-lipped, gentle mouth with a LONG upper lip; a narrow ring of sandy-grey hair around the tonsure; the gaze mild and merciful, toward us.

subject: St. Germanus, Bishop of Paris, half-length, as an aged sixth-century Gallo-Roman bishop without a mitre: a white alb under a full, bell-shaped chasuble of deep blue, a narrow white pallium-like band over his shoulders, a plain wooden pastoral staff resting in the crook of his left arm; with his right hand he holds out a round loaf of bread toward the lower edge, where the small, lifted hands of a poor man reach up for it ('the Father of the Poor'). Behind him, Paris in the sixth century: the Seine with a flat boat, the walled island city with a few red roofs, and on the green meadows of the left bank the new stone basilica of St. Vincent with its bell-cote (the later Saint-Germain-des-Prés), under a soft, pearly morning sky. Fatherly, frugal and kind; no king, no lettering.
face: A Gallo-Roman of Autun of about eighty, worn thin by penance, CLEAN-SHAVEN as in the old engraving, with a pale, finely wrinkled complexion and a LONG face whose LOWER JAW is HEAVY and PROTRUDES a little beyond the upper, the lower lip fuller and set forward (a slight underbite) — a flat, SLOPING forehead running back into a BALD crown with a thin fringe of fine white hair, a LONG, THIN, straight nose, SMALL, deep-set, pale-blue eyes under DROOPING white brows, HOLLOW cheeks with long smile lines, a long, strong, rounded chin; the gaze lowered kindly toward the poor man's hands.

subject: St. Francis Caracciolo, founder of the Clerics Regular Minor, half-length: the plain black cassock and black mantle of a clerk regular, a white collar-band; his right hand laid on his heart, his left hand resting on an open book of the rule; before him, above and to one side, a golden sunburst monstrance with the white Host shining softly on a cloud, toward which his face is turned. Behind him, a quiet side chapel in Naples: a small altar with candles and a tabernacle veiled in white, a plain arched window, and through it the bay of Naples with Vesuvius faint in the haze, under a warm afternoon light. Ardent and adoring; no bishop's mitre, no rays from his face, no lettering.
face: A Neapolitan noble of about forty-four with a warm, light-olive complexion and a LONG, SOFT-contoured face — a HIGH forehead made higher by a RECEDING hairline, HEAVY, PUFFY upper eyelids over large, dark eyes lifted toward the Host, a LONG nose with a ROUNDED, FLESHY tip, full, softly rounded cheeks, a FULL mouth slightly parted, a soft, rounded jaw; short, dark-brown hair; a thin dark moustache and a SHORT, dark, rounded beard close along the jaw; the gaze upturned, rapt.

subject: St. Petronilla, a consecrated virgin of Rome in the age of the apostles, half-length: a long, full-sleeved dalmatic of pale ivory wool with two narrow purple bands (clavi) falling from the shoulders, as in the old catacomb paintings, and a light white veil over her hair and shoulders; a small, closed book of the Scriptures held against her breast in both hands, a sprig of white lilies laid across it. Behind her, the Via Ardeatina outside Rome: a grassy slope with the low, plain entrance of the catacomb of Domitilla, cypresses and umbrella pines, a small early church of brick on the rise, and the Alban hills blue in the distance under a clear, early-morning sky. Serene, recollected, luminous; no crown, no palm, no lettering.
face: A Roman woman of about twenty with a fair olive complexion and a LONG, RECTANGULAR face with SOFT corners — a smooth forehead with the dark hair growing to a small WIDOW'S PEAK at its centre, a LONG, STRAIGHT nose, DEEP-SET, calm dark-brown eyes under LOW, STRAIGHT dark brows, flat cheeks, a SHORT upper lip over a small, full, closed mouth, a small, SQUARE chin; dark hair parted from the peak and drawn back under the veil; the gaze level and recollected, toward us.

subject: St. Cyril, the boy martyr of Caesarea in Cappadocia, half-length: a knee-length tunic of plain, undyed wool with a narrow brown border, belted with a cord, a short cloak of faded blue thrown back over one shoulder, barefoot like the boy turned out of his father's house; a martyr's palm in his right hand, his left hand laid open on his breast, his face lifted as one 'hastening to his home'. Behind him, Caesarea in Cappadocia under snow-streaked Mount Argaeus: a small Roman town of pale stone and flat roofs on a high, dry plain, poplars along a stream, the great cone of the mountain white against a clear, deep-blue sky with a band of gold above it. Joyful and eager; no fire, no judge, no father, no lettering.
face: A Cappadocian Greek boy of about twelve, visibly a child, BEARDLESS, with a light-olive, sun-warmed complexion and a SQUARE, FLAT-PLANED face — a broad, flat forehead with a LEVEL hairline, a STRAIGHT nose with a HIGH bridge unusual in a child, DEEP-SET grey-green eyes under thin, LEVEL dark brows that nearly MEET, flat cheeks, a WIDE, thin-lipped mouth open in a glad smile, a firm, SQUARE little chin; thick, short, tousled dark-brown curls; the gaze lifted, eager and fearless.

subject: The martyrs of Lyons of the year 177, four figures half-length and close together, each holding a martyr's palm. POTHINUS (centre left, in front): the aged first bishop of Lyons, in a white tunic and a full, bell-shaped chasuble of deep red with a plain white pallium, a small book of the Gospels held to his breast. BLANDINA (centre right, in front): a young slave woman, small and slight, in a plain tunic of coarse, undyed brown wool and a pale linen head-cloth, her hands crossed on her breast over her palm, her face lifted with a quiet joy. Behind them, their heads between and above theirs: SANCTUS (left), the deacon of Vienne, in a white dalmatic; ATTALUS (right), a citizen of Pergamum, in a white Roman toga. Behind the group, Lugdunum at the meeting of the Rhône and the Saône: the Roman town of red roofs, temples and an aqueduct on the steep hill of Fourvière, the two rivers joining below, under a luminous, gold-streaked sky. Joyful and steadfast; no beasts, no amphitheatre, no stake, no gridiron, no soldiers, no lettering.
face: Four clearly different people. POTHINUS: a Greek of Asia of about ninety, frail, with a pale, papery complexion and a face shaped like an INVERTED TRIANGLE — a very WIDE, BALD, domed head and broad temples narrowing sharply to a SMALL, pointed chin; a LARGE, BONY, BEAKED nose; small eyes sunk deep under overhanging white brows; hollow temples and cheeks; a THIN, WISPY, silky white beard falling to the breast; the gaze gentle and far-off. BLANDINA: a young woman of about twenty, small and slight, with a fair, lightly freckled complexion and a ROUND-CHEEKED, PLAIN, open face — a LOW, broad forehead, a SHORT, SNUB nose, small, dark, DEEP-SET, shining eyes, a WIDE mouth in a small, glad smile, a full, ROUND chin; brown hair under the head-cloth; the gaze lifted upward. SANCTUS: a man of about thirty-five, CLEAN-SHAVEN, with a HEAVY, SQUARE face — a broad, FLATTENED nose, small, level grey eyes, a wide jaw and a deep CLEFT in the chin; close-cropped black hair; the gaze steady. ATTALUS: a man of about fifty with a TALL, NARROW, aristocratic face — HIGH, sharp cheekbones, a long AQUILINE nose, thin lips, a close-trimmed grey beard and short grey hair; the gaze grave and proud.

subject: St. Claude, Archbishop of Besançon who became a monk and abbot of St. Oyend in the Jura, half-length, in the black Benedictine habit and cowl with the hood fallen back; an abbot's crozier of plain dark wood with a simple curled head in his left hand; in his right hand, held against his breast, an open Bible; a bishop's white mitre set down on a stone ledge at his side, the dignity he laid aside. Behind him, the Jura: the narrow, deeply wooded valley of Condat where two mountain streams meet, the stone church and cloister of the abbey among fir forests, limestone cliffs above, under a clear, cool mountain sky. Humble, silent and serene; no lettering.
face: A Burgundian of great age, about ninety, CLEAN-SHAVEN as in the old glass, with a fair, weathered complexion and a SHORT, WIDE, rounded-square face — a broad, low, lined forehead running into a BALD crown with a thin white fringe, a FLAT, SNUB nose, small, bright, deep-set blue eyes in a web of fine wrinkles, sparse white brows, broad, flat cheeks, a WIDE, thin-lipped mouth drawn slightly inward with age, a soft, loose fold beneath the chin; the gaze peaceful and kindly, a little downward.

subject: St. Clotilda, Queen of the Franks, half-length, as a widowed queen of the sixth century given to prayer: a long gown of deep violet wool with a gold-embroidered border at the neck, a white widow's veil and wimple, and over the veil a slender, plain gold circlet, not a tall crown; her hands joined in prayer, a small alms purse hanging from her girdle. Behind her, Tours on the Loire: the broad, shining river with a stone bridge, the walled town and the tall early basilica over the tomb of St. Martin, where she spent her widowhood, poplars along the bank, under a gentle, silvery evening sky. Recollected and gentle; no king, no army, no lettering.
face: A Burgundian queen of about sixty-five with a fair, pale complexion softened by age and a LEAN, LONG face — HIGH, ROUNDED cheekbones with SOFT HOLLOWS beneath them, a smooth, broad forehead, a long, straight, fine nose, LARGE grey eyes whose outer corners DROOP gently, as in sorrow, under faint, arched fair-grey brows, a SMALL, firm, closed mouth, a softly rounded chin with a first slackness beneath it; grey-blonde hair hidden under the veil; the gaze lowered in prayer.

subject: St. Felix I, Bishop of Rome, half-length, as a third-century pope: a white tunic and a full, bell-shaped chasuble of deep crimson, a narrow white pallium with small black crosses over his shoulders; in his left hand a rolled letter sealed with a small red seal, his letter on the unity of Christ's Person; his right hand raised in blessing. Behind him, the Via Appia outside Rome: the paved road between umbrella pines and cypresses, the low brick entrance to the catacomb of Callixtus in a grassy bank, the walls of Rome far off, under a warm evening sky of gold and rose. Grave and fatherly; no palm, no sword, no emperor, no lettering.
face: A Roman of about sixty with a warm olive complexion and a BROAD, SHORT face whose width is in the FLARING, fleshy cheekbones — a LOW forehead crossed by one DEEP horizontal crease, thick, tight, grizzled CURLS growing low on it, LARGE, slightly PROTRUDING dark eyes under HIGH, thick, ARCHED brows that give a searching look, a SHORT, WIDE, straight nose with round nostrils, FULL, curving lips, a full, CURLY, rounded grey-black beard of medium length; the gaze direct and earnest.

subject: St. Pamphilus, priest and scholar of Caesarea in Palestine, half-length, as a learned man of about the year 300: a long tunic of undyed linen and a plain dark-grey pallium draped over his left shoulder; in his hands a large, open parchment codex of the Scriptures in neat columns, a reed pen held between the fingers of his right hand, a martyr's palm leaning against the shelf beside him. Behind him, his library at Caesarea: wooden pigeon-hole shelves stacked with scrolls and codices, an ink-pot on a stone ledge, and through an arched window Caesarea Maritima on the sea: the white harbour mole, a lighthouse and a ship at anchor on a bright, blue Mediterranean under a clear sky. Studious, humble and steadfast; no hooks, no fire, no governor, no lettering.
face: A Phoenician of Berytus of about fifty with a warm, olive-brown Levantine complexion and a LONG face, NARROW in the jaw, whose chin thrusts FORWARD under the beard, beneath a TALL, BULGING scholar's forehead lined with three horizontal creases — a LARGE, HIGH-BRIDGED, arched nose; small, CLOSE-SET, keen dark eyes NARROWED in a scholar's short-sighted squint, crow's-feet at their corners; DEEPLY HOLLOW cheeks; thin, firm lips; short black hair greying and RECEDING at the temples; a SMALL, close-trimmed black beard and moustache, as the Painter's Manual has it; the gaze lifted from the page toward us.

subject: St. Frumentius, half-length, a bishop of the fourth century: a white linen tunic, a plain saffron-gold paenula, and a white woollen pallium marked with dark crosses around his shoulders, bareheaded; he holds a Gospel book bound in plain leather with a small cross on it against his breast and raises his right hand in blessing. Behind him the highland city of Axum: tall, carved granite stelae standing among acacia trees, stone buildings, green terraced hills and a few Aksumite people in white cotton robes, small in the distance, under a high, clear sky. Kindly, wise and steadfast; no lettering.
face: A Phoenician of Tyre of about fifty-five with a warm, olive-bronze complexion and a WIDE, LOW, FLAT-CHEEKED face — a BROAD, low forehead, WIDE, flat cheek planes and a WIDE jaw, THICK, black brows ARCHED high and full, LARGE, dark, slightly PROMINENT eyes with a kind, direct look, a nose with a strong, gentle CURVE and a FLESHY, rounded tip, a FULL, wide mouth; thick, wavy black hair touched with grey at the temples, falling to the neck; a full, thick black beard, rounded at the bottom; the gaze warm and steady. Not the tall, egg-shaped anicetus, the round, soft severianus_scythopolis, the short, domed lucian_antioch or the Copts pachomius and macarius_alexandria.
verdict: rejected: frame: its own border and initial box, not the set's

subject: St. Magloire, half-length, an aged Breton bishop and abbot of the sixth century: a plain dark monastic cowl with its hood fallen back, and over it a simple white pallium-like stole of a Celtic bishop; a plain wooden crozier with a curved head in his left hand, his right raised in blessing. Behind him a small, rocky island in the Channel with steep green cliffs, a cluster of small stone cells and a tiny chapel on its top, a grey-blue sea with white surf and a single fishing boat, a soft, bright, cloudy sky. Venerable, kindly and serene; no mitre, no lettering.
face: A Briton of about seventy-five, spare and upright, with a fair, wind-reddened complexion and a TALL, NARROW face that is LONGEST between the eyes and the mouth — a high, BALD, smooth DOME with a fringe of white hair at the back, a LONG, THIN, straight nose that ENDS in a slightly DROOPING tip, WIDE-SET, clear, light-blue eyes under THIN, level white brows, HIGH, NARROW cheekbones with flat planes below, a LONG upper lip and a small mouth, LARGE ears; a long, STRAIGHT, silver-white beard that TAPERS to a single narrow point on the breast; the gaze calm and benevolent, toward us. Not the dish-profiled, snub-nosed, wavy-bearded mello, the heavy-browed, broad david_wales, the shield-shaped paternus_avranches, the trapezoid, broad-bearded hilary, the long, symmetrical remigius, or the round, bald, flat-featured zephyrinus.

subject: St. Hilarion, half-length, an aged hermit of the fourth century: a rough shirt of undyed sackcloth and over it a small, worn cloak of brown skins (the one St. Antony gave him), bareheaded; in his hands a half-woven basket of rushes resting against his breast, his fingers still at the weaving. Behind him the sandy desert inland from Gaza: low dunes, a few date palms, a tiny, low cell of reeds and clay, hardly taller than a man, and far off a thin blue line of the Mediterranean under a pale evening sky. Gentle, humble and at peace; no skull, no scroll, no lettering.
face: A Palestinian of about eighty, worn thin by fasting, with a dry, sun-browned olive complexion and a face whose PROFILE is CONVEX — a forehead that SLOPES BACK from a knotted brow, a LONG, gently CURVED nose that projects far forward, and a SMALL, RECEDING chin, so that the face seems drawn forward to a point at the nose; narrow temples, flat, lined cheeks, SMALL, almond-shaped, soft brown eyes under HEAVY, half-lowered lids and wispy grey brows, deep crow's-feet; thin, dry, rough-cut hair, BROWN streaked with grey, short about the ears; a long, thin, BROWN, rush-like beard, streaked with grey and divided into THREE narrow points, as the Painter's Manual has it; the gaze lowered, meek. Not the triangular, hooded anthony_abbot, the long-tapering, bald, wide-eyed paul_hermit, the small, chiselled, two-point-bearded simeon_stylites, the elfin john_egypt, the horse-like paphnutius, the diamond-shaped porphyry_gaza or the rounded-square macarius_alexandria.

subject: St. Evaristus, half-length, the bishop of Rome about the year 105 in the plain dress of his time: a long white tunic and a wide, cream woollen pallium (the Greek mantle) draped over the left shoulder, bareheaded, no tiara, no mitre; he holds a small scroll of the Scriptures in his left hand and lifts his right a little as if assigning a task. Behind him, under a clear Roman sky, the Vatican hill with its cypresses and tombs, where St. Peter lies buried, and beyond the Tiber the roofs of Trajan's Rome. Grave, recollected and fatherly; no lettering.
face: A Greek of Jewish family from Bethlehem, about sixty-five, with a warm, olive-bronze complexion and a face DOMINATED by a LARGE, STRONGLY ARCHED, high-bridged nose — a LOW forehead under a WIDOW'S PEAK of thick, WAVY grey hair brushed back and still full, HOODED, dark-brown eyes that SLANT DOWN at the outer corners under thick, level, black-and-grey brows, HIGH cheekbones over LEAN cheeks, a deep groove above a thin-lipped mouth, a NARROW chin; a MEDIUM, black-and-grey beard cut SQUARE across the bottom; the gaze inward and grave. Not the round, bald, crisp-bearded mark_pope, the tall, egg-shaped anicetus, the soft, heart-shaped soter, the hexagonal linus, the bony, two-pointed cletus, the diamond-faced clement_i or the long, narrow sylvester.

subject: St. Marcellus the Centurion, half-length, a Roman centurion of the year 298: a red woollen tunic and a scale-mail cuirass, a red cloak pinned at the shoulder, bareheaded; he has UNBUCKLED his military belt and holds it out with his sword in its scabbard in his right hand, as if laying them down, while his left hand rests on his breast; his vine staff lies at his feet. Behind him the legion's camp on the emperor's birthday: rows of leather tents, the standards with their eagles and garlands, a smoking altar and small, distant soldiers feasting, under a hot, hazy sky with dry hills. Resolute, calm and clear-eyed; no wounds, no executioner, no lettering.
face: A veteran of about forty-five with a sun-browned, ruddy olive complexion and a ROUND, SHORT face as wide as it is long on a THICK neck — a broad, rounded forehead, FULL, firm, ROUNDED cheeks, a SHORT, slightly UPTURNED nose, ROUND, light-brown eyes, frank and steady, under STRAIGHT, thick brown brows, a WIDE, good-humoured mouth, a round chin with a DIMPLE; brown hair going grey, cut very short in the soldier's fashion; a SHORT, close-trimmed grizzled beard; the look firm and open. Not the angular, cleft-chinned victor_marseilles, the long-headed, joined-browed romanus_ostiarius, the square, broken-nosed Tarachus of tarachus_companions, the dark, long-oval Maurice of theban_legion, or george and sebastian.

subject: St. Malachi, half-length, an Irish archbishop of about 1140: a white alb, a plain green chasuble of the twelfth century falling in wide, soft folds, a low white mitre; a simple crozier with a curled head in his left hand, his right raised in blessing. Behind him a green hill in Ireland with a small stone church, low stone walls and a churchyard with a few crosses, soft Irish light after rain. Grave, cheerful and gentle; no lettering.
face: An Irishman of about fifty with a fair, fresh, lightly ruddy complexion and a smooth, UNLINED, OVAL face somewhat LONGER than wide — a high, ROUNDED forehead, a SHORT, straight nose with a slightly UPTURNED, neat tip, LARGE, clear, grey-blue eyes set WIDE apart, their lower lids lifted by a quiet smile, soft, arched brown brows, FIRM, smooth cheeks, a small, calm, closed mouth turned up at the corners, a SMALL, rounded chin; CLEAN-SHAVEN; brown hair greying a little, cut short in a Roman round tonsure; the gaze grave but joyful. Not the broad, white-haired, Irish-tonsured columba, the long, flaxen finbarr, the heart-shaped fiaker, the square, snub-nosed gall, the big-boned columban, the long, handsome oswald_worcester, or the clean-shaven, beak-nosed wilfrid.

subject: St. Narcissus, half-length, the bishop of Jerusalem about the year 200, very old and a little stooped: a white tunic and a plain, deep-blue paenula with a white woollen pallium marked with dark crosses, bareheaded; he holds up in both hands a small clay oil lamp burning with a clear flame, the lamp of the Paschal vigil whose water he turned to oil. Behind him the hills of Jerusalem at dusk, the city's pale stone walls and roofs, a few olive trees and the first stars in a deep-blue evening sky. Serene, patient and full of trust; no mitre, no lettering.
face: A man of great age, well past a hundred, with a soft, pale, parchment-fine complexion and a SMALL, ROUND, SHRUNKEN face in which the mouth has FALLEN IN, bringing a small, HOOKED nose and a small, forward-CURVING chin close together (a gentle 'nutcracker' profile) — a round, BALD crown with a few wisps of fine white hair at the sides, small, soft, watery-blue eyes deep in folds of skin, puffed, softly drooping lids, sparse, long white brows, rounded, sunken cheeks; a SHORT, SPARSE, soft white beard that shows the chin's shape beneath; the gaze mild and trusting, the lips in a faint smile. Not the long, hatchet-faced simeon_jerusalem, the rosy, heart-shaped, full-haired polycarp, the long, tapering paul_hermit, the broad, flat-planed theodosius_cenobiarch or the round, flat-featured, long-bearded zephyrinus.

subject: St. Theodoret, half-length, a priest of Antioch in the year 362: a long white linen tunic and over it a plain, dark-red paenula falling in soft folds, bareheaded; he holds a martyr's palm in his right hand and presses a small silver chalice, one of the church's sacred vessels he kept, against his breast with his left. Behind him Antioch on the Orontes: colonnaded streets and tiled roofs climbing the slope of Mount Silpius, a closed church door in the foreground street, a warm late-afternoon light. Steadfast, grave and fearless; no ropes, no wounds, no lettering.
face: A Syrian of Antioch of about forty-five with a warm, olive complexion and a face shaped like a BELL — NARROW at the temples and the low forehead, WIDENING down to a BROAD, ANGULAR jaw with marked corners; a strong nose with a distinct BUMP on the bridge and a straight, slightly down-turned tip, deep-set, dark, steady eyes under thick black brows ARCHED HIGH at their middle, flat cheeks, a firm mouth with a FULL lower lip; short, thick, black curly hair cropped close to the skull; a SHORT, dense, curly black beard that follows the wide jaw closely; the look direct and unafraid. Not the short, domed-browed lucian_antioch, the square-jawed, full-cheeked Cosmas of cosmas_damian, the long-headed, joined-browed romanus_ostiarius or the broad-browed, clean-shaven eusebius_rome.

subject: St. Quintin, half-length, a young Roman of senatorial family preaching in Gaul about 287: a white tunic with the broad purple stripe of a senator's son and a white toga-like pallium draped over the shoulder, bareheaded; a martyr's palm in his right hand, his left open toward the listeners. Behind him Roman Amiens on the Somme: a wooden bridge over the river, reed-marshes and poplars, tiled roofs and a small forum, a few Gallic townspeople in hooded cloaks listening, under a soft, grey-blue northern sky. Young, ardent and gentle; no nails, no chains, no wounds, no lettering.
face: A Roman patrician of about thirty, CLEAN-SHAVEN, fair-skinned with a light flush, with a LONG, RECTANGULAR face and a STRONG, FLAT-BOTTOMED jaw as wide as the cheekbones — a high, broad forehead, a Roman nose with a HIGH bridge and a slight HOOK, DEEP-SET, grey-green eyes under straight, fair-brown brows, flat cheeks, a WIDE, thin-lipped mouth, a long neck; short, TIGHT, close-cropped fair curls; the gaze eager and bright. Not the smooth-oval, fringe-haired alexander, the round-faced boy pancras, the angular, cleft-chinned victor_marseilles, the long-headed romanus_ostiarius, or the heart-shaped youngest of forty_martyrs_sebaste.

subject: Sts. Crispin and Crispinian, side by side, half-length, two brothers of a noble Roman family working as shoemakers in Gallo-Roman Soissons about 285: plain belted tunics of undyed wool with leather aprons, sleeves pushed up; Crispin (left) holds a finished leather sandal and a martyr's palm, Crispinian (right) a shoemaker's awl and a wooden last with a palm resting in the crook of his arm. Behind them their small workshop open to the street: a work bench with leather, thread and a hanging row of sandals, an oil lamp burning for the night's work, and through the doorway the tiled roofs of Roman Soissons and a few townspeople listening. Two brothers who are clearly different men; humble, cheerful, devout; no swords, no millstones, no lettering.
face: Two brothers who must read as different men, NOT twins. CRISPIN (left), the elder, about forty, with a ruddy olive complexion and a WIDE, SHORT, FLAT face — a broad, low forehead under a STRAIGHT, low hairline of short, thick black hair, WIDE, FLAT cheekbones, a SHORT, BROAD nose with a low bridge, small, bright, dark eyes creased by a ready smile under thick, straight black brows, a WIDE mouth, a strong, rounded chin; CLEAN-SHAVEN with a dark shadow on the jaw, a thick neck. CRISPINIAN (right), about thirty, paler, with a TRIANGULAR face — BROAD temples and a high, smooth forehead tapering past lean cheeks to a NARROW, POINTED chin; a thin, straight nose, LARGE, grey-green eyes set wide, fine, arched light-brown brows, a small, thoughtful mouth; soft, wavy, light-brown hair to the ears and a SPARSE, short light-brown beard only on the chin; the gaze earnest. Not the olive twins of cosmas_damian, nor the pairs john_paul_martyrs, faustinus_jovita or romanus_lupicinus.
