subject: St. Frumentius, half-length, a bishop of the fourth century: a white linen tunic, a plain saffron-gold paenula, and a white woollen pallium marked with dark crosses around his shoulders, bareheaded; he holds a Gospel book bound in plain leather with a small cross on it against his breast and raises his right hand in blessing. Behind him the highland city of Axum: tall, carved granite stelae standing among acacia trees, stone buildings, green terraced hills and a few Aksumite people in white cotton robes, small in the distance, under a high, clear sky. Kindly, wise and steadfast; no lettering.
face: A Phoenician of Tyre of about fifty-five with a warm, olive-bronze complexion and a WIDE, LOW, FLAT-CHEEKED face — a BROAD, low forehead, WIDE, flat cheek planes and a WIDE jaw, THICK, black brows ARCHED high and full, LARGE, dark, slightly PROMINENT eyes with a kind, direct look, a nose with a strong, gentle CURVE and a FLESHY, rounded tip, a FULL, wide mouth; thick, wavy black hair touched with grey at the temples, falling to the neck; a full, thick black beard, rounded at the bottom; the gaze warm and steady. Not the tall, egg-shaped anicetus, the round, soft severianus_scythopolis, the short, domed lucian_antioch or the Copts pachomius and macarius_alexandria.

subject: St. Giles, half-length, an old hermit-abbot in a plain black Benedictine cowl with its hood fallen back, a small black skullcap on his head, a simple wooden abbot's staff in the crook of his left arm; his right hand rests gently on the neck of a slender red-brown hind that nestles against his side, her head lifted to him, unafraid. Behind them, the deep oak and holm-oak forest near Nîmes, a spring among mossy rocks and the mouth of a small cave, shafts of soft light through the leaves. Peaceful and tender; no hunters, no arrow, no wound, no lettering.
face: A Greek of about seventy, lean and gentle, with a fair olive complexion and an OVAL face that is WIDEST at soft, rounded cheekbones — a smooth, high forehead running into a BALD crown under the skullcap, a LONG, STRAIGHT 'Greek' nose continuing the line of the brow without a dip, LARGE, dark, HEAVY-LIDDED almond eyes under thin, level grey brows, soft, slightly sunken cheeks, a WIDE, gentle, thin-lipped mouth, a small rounded chin; a thin fringe of grey hair above the ears and a THIN, WISPY grey beard falling to a soft point; the gaze lowered to the hind, tender. Not the broad, round-headed Benedict with his long full white beard, nor the triangular, hooded anthony_abbot.

subject: St. Eleutherius, half-length, an old abbot in a plain black monastic cowl and hood thrown back, a simple wooden abbot's staff in his left hand, the book of the Gospels held to his breast with his right; he prays with tears. Behind him, the small Romanesque stone church and cloister of the abbey of St. Mark outside Spoleto, cypresses and the green Umbrian hills with the town on its height beyond. Humble, simple and contrite; no demon, no child, no lettering.
face: An Umbrian of about seventy with a soft, pale-pink complexion and a MOON-ROUND face — a low, rounded forehead, FULL, SOFT cheeks, a SMALL, SNUB nose, SMALL, ROUND light-brown eyes with REDDENED rims, moist with tears, under thin white brows lifted and DRAWN TOGETHER in the middle in compunction, a small, soft, trembling mouth, a soft double chin; white hair cut close round a monastic tonsure and a SHORT, SOFT, rounded white beard; the gaze lifted, simple and tearful. Not the long-bearded benedict, nor the square-faced Bonfilius or snub-nosed, dark-bearded Bonajuncta of servite_founders.

subject: St. Guy of Anderlecht, half-length, a poor Brabant peasant returned as a pilgrim: a rough, faded red woollen tunic belted with a cord, a brown cloak, a broad-brimmed pilgrim's hat hanging at his back, a pilgrim's staff in his right hand and a small scrip at his side; his left hand holds a small bronze altar-bell, for he was the sacristan of Laeken. Beside him the head of a patient brown ox. Behind him, flat green fields and pollarded willows of Brabant, and the small stone chapel of Our Lady at Laeken with its low tower under a pale, luminous northern sky. Poor, penitent and content; no lettering.
face: A Brabant countryman of about fifty, CLEAN-SHAVEN, with a ruddy, weather-reddened complexion and a BROAD, SQUARE face with STRONG JAW CORNERS, after the Book of Hours miniature — a LOW, broad forehead, a SHORT, BROAD nose with a ROUNDED tip, SMALL, DEEP-SET blue-grey eyes under HEAVY, STRAIGHT brown brows, wide, weathered cheeks with deep smile-lines, a WIDE, straight mouth, PROMINENT ears; thick brown hair with the first grey, cut in a straight fringe across the brow and short over the ears; the gaze humble and kindly. Not the wedge-faced Cloud of this batch, nor the fair, flat-topped hyacinth.
verdict: rejected: frame: its own border and a round-topped window, and a face too photographic

subject: St. Omer, half-length, an old bishop of the seventh century in a full, bell-shaped red-gold chasuble over a white alb, a low white mitre, a plain gilt crosier held firmly in his left hand; his right hand raised in blessing. His eyes are closed, for he is blind, yet his face is turned toward his people. Behind him, the flat green country of Artois with its marshes and waterways, and on a low rise the small stone church of Our Lady at Sithiu with a few monastery roofs. Gentle and fatherly; no lettering.
face: A Frank of about seventy with a pale, weathered complexion and a HEXAGONAL face of FLAT PLANES — a BROAD, FLAT forehead crossed by deep level lines, ANGULAR cheekbones set WIDE, a LONG, fleshy nose ending in a ROUNDED, BULBOUS tip, a LONG upper lip, a BROAD, FLAT chin; the EYES gently CLOSED under heavy lids, for he is blind, with thick, straight white brows; a short, CLOSE-TRIMMED white beard following the jaw; white hair showing below the mitre; the face serene and listening. Not the round, soft Eleutherius of this batch, nor the white-bearded nicholas with his full curled beard.

subject: St. Rosalia, half-length, a young hermit in a plain brown woollen hermit's robe with a rough cord, a white linen veil fallen back on her shoulders; on her long, loose hair a small crown of pink and white roses; a white lily in her right hand, her left hand laid on her breast. She stands at the mouth of her limestone cave high on Monte Pellegrino, ivy and wild rock-roses about the entrance; far below, the city of Palermo and its golden bay under a clear blue Sicilian sky. Recollected and serene; no skull, no plague, no lettering.
face: A Norman-Sicilian noblewoman of about thirty with a fair, lightly sun-touched complexion and a LONG, NARROW face — a high, rounded forehead, a SLENDER, HIGH-BRIDGED nose with a delicate, slightly downturned tip, WIDE-SET grey-green eyes lifted toward heaven under fine, high-arched golden brows, smooth, flat cheeks, a small, full, rosy mouth, a SMALL, POINTED chin; long, loose, wavy GOLDEN-RED hair falling past the shoulders; the gaze upturned and rapt, as in van Dyck's Palermo pictures. Not the round, dark rose_lima under her rose crown; no dark hair.

subject: St. Cloud, half-length, a young Merovingian prince become a monk and priest: a plain dark-brown monastic habit with a white linen amice at the neck, a small wooden cross on a cord; in his right hand a small gold chalice held before his breast; with his left he lays aside, on a low stone ledge beside him, a slender gold Frankish crown on a fold of purple cloth. Behind him, a green wooded hill above a wide bend of the Seine, a small stone church and a few monks' huts on the slope, fishermen's boats on the river and Paris far off on the horizon. Calm and resolved; no uncles, no swords, no lettering.
face: A Frank of about thirty-five, CLEAN-SHAVEN, with a fair, fresh complexion and an INVERTED-TRIANGLE face with a CLEFT chin — a WIDE, HIGH, smooth forehead and broad temples narrowing along a lean, straight jaw to a NARROW chin marked by a clear CLEFT; a thin, straight nose with a narrow bridge; DEEP-SET, pale-blue eyes under straight, fair brows; flat, lean cheeks; a thin, WIDE mouth; ash-blond hair cut SHORT round a monastic tonsure, the long royal locks gone; the gaze level, clear and resolved. Not the pale, jaw-heavy young louis_toulouse, nor the lean, long-faced grandmother clotilda.

subject: St. Nicholas of Tolentino, half-length, an Augustinian friar in the full black habit of the Hermits of St. Augustine with its wide sleeves and black leather belt, the hood fallen on his shoulders; on his breast a small radiant golden star; in his right hand a white lily and a small crucifix held together, in his left a small plain round loaf marked with a cross. Behind him, the cloister arcade of the friary at Tolentino and, beyond, the green hills of the Marche with the town's walls and bell tower. Gentle, mortified and joyful; no purgatory, no flames, no lettering.
face: An Italian of the Marche of about fifty-five, CLEAN-SHAVEN, with a pale olive complexion thinned by fasting and a HEART-SHAPED face — a BROAD, smooth forehead tapering over HOLLOW cheeks to a SMALL, POINTED chin, a small, STRAIGHT, fine nose, LARGE, gentle dark-brown eyes set a little close under softly arched dark brows, a SMALL, sweet mouth; black hair touched with grey cut in a thick ring round a full tonsure; the gaze lowered, tender and humble. Not the round, big-nosed philip_benizi, nor the dark, compact, brow-joined peter_verona.

subject: St. Eulogius, half-length, a patriarch of about 600 as the Menologion of Basil II shows him: a dark-brown phelonion over a white sticharion, a white omophorion with large black crosses over his shoulders, a jewelled book of the Gospels held in his left hand, his right hand raised in blessing; beside him on a small table a few scrolls and a reed pen, for his writings against the heresies. Behind him, through a colonnade, the harbour of Alexandria with the tall white Pharos lighthouse and sailing ships on a bright blue sea. Learned, serene and firm; no lettering.
face: A Syrian of Antioch of about sixty-five with a warm olive complexion and an OBLONG face under a HIGH, BALD, DOMED forehead — a LONG, fine, straight nose, NARROW-SET dark eyes under STRAIGHT, HEAVY black-and-grey brows that nearly meet, FLAT cheeks, a small, firm mouth; short grey hair at the sides and back; a FULL, ROUNDED grey beard of medium length, as in the Menologion; the gaze direct and thoughtful. Not the hair-hidden, high-bridged cyril_alexandria, the egg-headed, long-black-bearded anicetus, or the broad-browed, short-faced lucian_antioch.

subject: St. Paphnutius, half-length, an old Egyptian bishop of the fourth century: a plain undyed linen tunic and a dark-brown monk's mantle with the hood drawn up over the head, and over it a white woollen omophorion with dark crosses about his shoulders; he leans on a plain wooden staff in his right hand, for he is lame, and holds a small book of the Gospels against his breast with his left. Behind him, the Nile winding between green fields and golden desert cliffs of the Upper Thebaid, palms along the bank under a hot, clear sky. Steadfast and venerable; no wounds shown, no blood, no lettering.
face: A Copt of about seventy-five with a deep-brown, sun-dark complexion and a LONG, HORSE-LIKE face — a HIGH, NARROW, deeply lined forehead under the hood, a LONG, BROAD-BASED nose with flared nostrils, the RIGHT EYE CLOSED under a smooth, long-healed lid, the LEFT eye large, dark and steady under a thick grey brow, LONG, FLAT cheeks, a WIDE, FULL-LIPPED mouth, a long jaw; a LONG, SQUARE-CUT grey-white beard; the gaze grave and unbowed. Not the wide, low, rounded-square macarius_alexandria, the square, big-boned james_nisibis, the bald, long-tapering paul_hermit, or the triangular anthony_abbot.

subject: St. Laurence Justinian, half-length and turned three-quarters to the left, as in Gentile Bellini's portrait: a close black skullcap covering the head, the plain white habit of a canon regular with a high black collar, a simple gold pectoral cross on a cord; in his hands a small closed book of the Gospels held against his breast. Behind him, through a round-arched window, the still, silver-blue Venetian lagoon with low islands and slender bell towers under a hazy morning sky. Austere, humble and at peace; no mitre, no pomp, no lettering.
face: A Venetian of about seventy-four, CLEAN-SHAVEN, with a sallow, parchment-pale complexion and a very LONG, GAUNT face after Gentile Bellini's portrait — a high forehead SLOPING back under the skullcap, a MASSIVE, HIGH-BRIDGED, strongly HOOKED nose, SMALL, keen, heavy-lidded dark eyes set DEEP in their sockets under a jutting brow ridge, a SHARP cheekbone over a deeply SUNKEN cheek, THIN, tightly closed lips, and a LONG, strongly JUTTING chin under a lean jaw; no hair showing; the gaze level and inward. Not the youngish, fine-nosed charles_borromeo in cardinal's red, nor the white-haired, bearded alphonsus_liguori.

subject: St. Guy of Anderlecht, half-length, a poor Brabant peasant returned as a pilgrim: a rough, faded red woollen tunic belted with a cord, a brown cloak, a broad-brimmed pilgrim's hat hanging at his back, a pilgrim's staff in his right hand and a small scrip at his side; his left hand holds a small bronze altar-bell, for he was the sacristan of Laeken. Beside him the head of a patient brown ox. Behind him, flat green fields and pollarded willows of Brabant, and the small stone chapel of Our Lady at Laeken with its low tower under a pale, luminous northern sky. Poor, penitent and content; no lettering.
face: A Brabant countryman of about fifty, CLEAN-SHAVEN, with a ruddy, weather-reddened complexion and a BROAD, SQUARE face with STRONG JAW CORNERS, after the Book of Hours miniature — a LOW, broad forehead, a SHORT, BROAD nose with a ROUNDED tip, SMALL, DEEP-SET blue-grey eyes under HEAVY, STRAIGHT brown brows, wide, weathered cheeks with deep smile-lines, a WIDE, straight mouth, PROMINENT ears; thick brown hair with the first grey, cut in a straight fringe across the brow and short over the ears; the gaze humble and kindly. Not the wedge-faced Cloud of this batch, nor the fair, flat-topped hyacinth.

subject: St. Finian, half-length, an old Irish monk-bishop of the sixth century: a white linen tunic under a hooded, dark-grey woollen cloak fastened at the breast with a simple bronze brooch; a short wooden crook-headed crozier in his left hand and a Gospel book bound in plain leather held against his breast with his right. Behind him Clonard on the river Boyne: a green meadow with small round wattle-and-daub cells and a little wooden church, young monks with books sitting on the grass as at a school, the slow river with alders, under a soft, grey-and-silver Irish sky. Tender, compassionate and learned; no lettering.
face: A Leinsterman of about eighty with a fair, pink, soft complexion and a SHORT, BROAD face, ROUND at the jaw — the front of the head shaved from ear to ear in the Irish tonsure, leaving a broad, high forehead, with fine white hair falling behind the ears; a BROAD, fleshy nose with a ROUNDED tip, WIDE-SET, moist, gentle blue-grey eyes whose inner brows are LIFTED in COMPASSION, soft, full cheeks, a small, tender mouth; a FULL, SOFT, WAVY WHITE beard reaching the breast; the look of one who weeps with those who weep. Not columba (clean-shaven, broad and ruddy), the long, narrow, receding-chinned finbarr, the long, big-boned columban, the compact, square gall, the heavy-browed david_wales, the smooth, clean-shaven malachi_armagh or valery on the same day (lean, narrow, short brown beard).

subject: St. Nicasius, half-length, a Gallo-Roman bishop of the early fifth century, bareheaded (no mitre): a white alb and a wide, plain, deep-red bell-shaped chasuble; a martyr's palm in his right hand, and in his left a Gospel book held against his breast. Behind him Rheims: the tall triple arch of the Roman gate, a new stone church with a plain facade and a small bell-cote, the city's roofs and a strip of the Champagne plain beyond, under a clear, pale, morning sky with a few smoke-grey clouds on the horizon. Fatherly, solicitous and brave; no severed head, no barbarians, no swords, no lettering.
face: A Gallo-Roman of about fifty-five with a fair complexion and a FULL, SOFT, OVAL face, fleshy at the jowls — a broad, smooth forehead with a few worried lines, a BROAD, LOW-bridged nose with a ROUND tip, LARGE, ROUND, pale-grey eyes under brows RAISED at their inner ends in fatherly concern, full cheeks, full lips; a THICK, CURLED, chestnut-grey beard cut ROUND, and short, CURLY chestnut-grey hair; the look anxious for his flock yet steadfast. Not his successor remigius (very tall, long, noble and smooth), the broad, short, square-jawed, tight-curled denis, the lantern-jawed gregory_langres, the Roman-nosed mammertus or the long, parallel-sided lambert.

subject: St. Mesmin, half-length, a Frankish abbot of about the year 515: a plain black woollen monastic habit and cowl, the hood down; a simple wooden abbot's staff in his left hand, and in his right a round loaf of bread, a full sheaf of golden wheat resting in the crook of his arm. Behind him the abbey of Micy on the Loire near Orleans: a low stone church and granary among poplars, sacks of grain stacked at the door and a few poor folk with baskets small in the distance, the broad, shining river with sandbanks under a soft, pale sky. Generous, humble and serene; no serpent, no king, no lettering.
face: A Frank of Verdun of about forty-five with a fair, ruddy complexion and a face WIDE at the BROW and NARROW at the JAW — a broad, high forehead, a LONG, THIN, gently AQUILINE nose, CLOSE-SET, bright hazel eyes creased by a ready smile under straight, dark-brown brows, lean cheeks, a wide, generous mouth, a NARROW, pointed chin under a SHORT, NEAT chestnut beard; thick chestnut hair around a monastic tonsure; the look warm and open-handed. Not avitus (also of Micy: lean, flat, wide, snub-nosed), the concave-profiled, clean-shaven eucherius_orleans of the same city, the round, small-featured gal_clermont, the hexagonal omer or the elfin john_egypt.

subject: St. Olympias, half-length, a noble widow of Constantinople about the year 400, a deaconess of its church: a plain, dark-brown woollen dress of good cut and over it a long deep-red mantle drawn over her head as a veil, no jewels; she holds folded white altar linen against her breast with both hands, the duty of her office. Behind her Constantinople: the long stone colonnade and bronze doors of a great timber-roofed basilica, beyond it the roofs of the city and the blue water of the Bosphorus with a few sails, under a warm, golden evening sky. Noble, recollected and generous; no lettering.
face: A Greek noblewoman of about forty with a pale, ivory complexion and a SQUARE-OVAL face with a BROAD, STRAIGHT JAW — a smooth, broad forehead, a straight nose with a slight AQUILINE bump high on the bridge, VERY LARGE, dark, DEEP-SET, luminous eyes under THICK, dark brows that nearly MEET over the nose, cheeks a little thinned by fasting, a FULL, closed mouth, a firm, rounded chin; dark hair hidden under the veil but for a parting; the look calm and self-possessed. Not the old, heart-shaped marcella, the round, full bathildes, the short, wide radegundes, the lean, droop-eyed clotilda helena (long face, Roman nose) or the young, full-oval, light-eyed barbara.

subject: St. Valery, half-length, a Frankish monk-abbot of the early seventh century: a plain, undyed grey-brown woollen cowl with the hood down, a leather belt; a simple wooden abbot's staff in his left hand and an open book held in his right, as the book's engraving shows him reading. Behind him the mouth of the Somme on the Channel coast: a small wooden monastery with a thatched chapel at the edge of a wood, a great solitary oak on a rise above the shore, salt meadows, a strip of grey sea and gulls under a wide, bright, windy sky. Mild, humble and patient; no king, no apparition, no lettering.
face: An Auvergnat of about fifty-five, 'lean and tall', with a fair, wind-reddened complexion and a LONG, NARROW face with a LONG, STRAIGHT, NARROW JAW — a smooth, fairly low forehead, a straight nose of medium length with a small, ROUNDED tip, MILD, wide-open, light-brown eyes with SOFT lower lids under thin, gently curved brown brows, FLAT, lean cheeks, a small, gentle mouth with the corners lifted, a long, narrow, rounded chin under a SHORT, thin, brown beard going grey that follows the jaw; brown hair cropped short around a monastic tonsure; the look meek and patient. Not his master columban (big-boned, jutting-chinned, Irish tonsure), the concave-profiled eucherius_orleans, the tall, dome-headed magloire, the long, droop-nosed wulfran, the hexagonal, blind omer or finian_clonard on the same day (white-bearded, Irish tonsure).

subject: St. Sabas, half-length, a very old abbot of the Judaean desert in the early sixth century: a coarse dark-brown monastic tunic and over it a wide, dark olive-green mantle, the hood of a black monastic cowl fallen back on his shoulders; in his left hand a plain wooden staff with a small cross-piece at the top, in his right an unrolled parchment scroll held against his breast. Behind him the gorge of the brook Cedron in the wilderness of Judah: steep, bare, honey-coloured cliffs pierced with the openings of hermits' caves, a small stone church and a few cells clinging to the rock, the thin line of the brook far below, under a hot, pale sky. Venerable, austere and fatherly; no lion, no lettering.
face: A Cappadocian Greek of about eighty-five, still upright, with a dry, sun-browned olive complexion and a TALL, OVAL face — a HIGH, ROUNDED forehead crossed by fine lines under THICK white hair brushed straight back to the nape (NOT bald), a LONG, straight nose with a sharply CHISELLED, slightly HOOKED tip, deep-set, keen grey eyes under high, ARCHED white brows, HOLLOW cheeks below clear cheekbones, a thin, firm mouth; a LONG white beard reaching the breast and DIVIDED at the end into TWO POINTS, as the Painter's Manual has him; the gaze searching and kind. Not the bald, broad, flat-faced theodosius_cenobiarch, his disciple john_silent (broad-templed, hump-nosed, eyes lowered), the convex-profiled, receding-chinned hilarion, the long, rectangular, furrow-browed john_climacus or the hooded, triangular anthony_abbot.

subject: St. Leocadia, half-length, a young Christian woman of Roman Toledo in the year 304: a plain, long-sleeved white linen tunic and over it a mantle of soft dusty blue drawn up over her head as a veil; she holds a martyr's palm in her left hand and a small, plain wooden cross against her breast with her right, her eyes lifted in longing prayer. Behind her Toledo on its rocky hill above the deep bend of the river Tagus: the plain stone walls and tiled roofs of the Roman town on the heights, the green river far below in its gorge, olive trees on the far bank, a clear, late-afternoon sky. Gentle, yearning and at peace; no prison, no chains, no lettering.
face: A Hispano-Roman woman of about twenty with a warm olive complexion and a SOFT, WIDE, HEART-SHAPED face — a broad, smooth forehead, FULL, rounded cheeks tapering to a SMALL, ROUND chin, a SHORT, softly ROUNDED nose, LARGE, dark-brown eyes under HEAVY lids, lifted upward, under thick dark brows ARCHED HIGH, a small, full mouth, lips just parted in prayer; dark-brown hair parted in the middle under the veil; the look of one who longs for heaven. Not her friend eulalia_merida (a narrow, bold girl of twelve), the long, square-chinned Engratia of saragossa_martyrs, the short, square-faced margaret_antioch, the inverted-triangle christina_bolsena the convex-profiled julia_corsica or the broad, strong-jawed barbara.

subject: St. Gatian, half-length, a missionary bishop from Rome in third-century Gaul, bareheaded (no mitre): a plain white tunic and over it a wide, undyed cream woollen travelling cloak like a bell chasuble; a simple wooden staff in his left hand, and in his right a plain silver chalice held before his breast. Behind him a cave in the pale limestone cliffs above the Loire at Tours: inside it a small stone altar with a lamp and a few kneeling Christians in rough wool, and beyond the mouth of the cave the broad river and wooded banks under a soft dawn sky. Patient, watchful and undaunted; no pagans, no idols, no lettering.
face: A Roman of about seventy with a sallow olive complexion and a DIAMOND-shaped face — a NARROW, BALD crown with short grey hair at the sides and back, WIDE, SHARP cheekbones, a NARROW, firm chin; a SHORT, straight nose, SMALL, DEEP-SET, watchful dark eyes under HEAVY grey brows, deep lines from the nose to a thin, patient mouth; a SHORT, POINTED grey beard; the look of a man long used to hiding and never afraid. Not his companion denis (broad, short, square, curly-haired), the long, noble remigius, the clean-shaven, long-chinned firmin, the heavy-jawed gregory_langres, the long, shield-faced saturninus_toulouse or the forked-bearded sabas.

subject: St. Nemesion, half-length, an Egyptian Christian layman of Alexandria in the year 250: a plain, knee-length white linen tunic with two narrow dark-red stripes from the shoulders and a light brown cloak over one shoulder; he holds a martyr's palm upright in his right hand and lays his left hand flat on his breast. Behind him Alexandria: the Great Harbour with its long stone mole, the tall white lighthouse of Pharos on its island, the colonnades and flat roofs of the city, palm trees, the blue sea under a bright, hot sky. Innocent, calm and joyful; no fire, no stake, no thieves, no lettering.
face: An Egyptian of Alexandria of about forty with a warm, deep-bronze complexion and a LEAN, ANGULAR face with a strong, SQUARE jaw — a straight, fairly narrow forehead, HIGH, SHARP cheekbones over HOLLOW cheeks, a LONG, straight nose with a slightly flared base, deep-set, dark eyes under THICK, straight black brows, FULL lips, a square chin; thick, tightly CURLED black hair cropped short; a SHORT, CLOSE-TRIMMED, curly black beard along the jaw; the look calm and unashamed. Not peter_alexandria (round, full, grey, short-nosed), the old desert monks macarius_alexandria, pachomius (long, bald), john_egypt and paphnutius, the round, fleshy severianus_scythopolis, the bald, domed eulogius_alexandria or the veteran Tarachus of tarachus_companions (square, broken-nosed).

subject: St. Eulalia, half-length, a girl of twelve of Roman Mérida in the year 304, visibly a child: a simple white woollen tunic with a narrow red border and a short rose-red mantle over her shoulders; she holds a martyr's palm upright in her right hand, and a small white dove rests on her left hand, raised before her breast. Behind her Emerita Augusta in winter: the long Roman stone bridge over the wide river Guadiana, the tall arches of the aqueduct beyond, the town's walls and tiled roofs, a light dusting of snow on the ground under a clear, cold sky. Brave, frank and innocent; no fire, no torches, no hooks, no idol, no lettering.
face: A Hispano-Roman girl of twelve, clearly a child, with a fair olive complexion and a LONG, NARROW, OVAL face — a HIGH, smooth forehead, a SHORT, straight, SLENDER nose, large, dark ALMOND eyes with a BOLD, DIRECT gaze under STRAIGHT, level dark brows, smooth, lean cheeks, a small, FIRM mouth set in resolve, a narrow, pointed chin; long, straight black hair loose over her shoulders, held back by a plain white band; the look of a child who is not afraid. Not leocadia (a soft, heart-shaped young woman), the inverted-triangle, upturned-nosed christina_bolsena, the short, square-faced margaret_antioch, the long-oval, square-chinned Engratia of saragossa_martyrs the round-cheeked maria_goretti or bibiana (a young woman with a long oval face and a Greek nose).
verdict: rejected: a doll-like, big-eyed modern illustration face, not the set's painting
